The word for “than” is مِنْ. This form does not change for masculine or feminine: الْغُرْفَة أَكْبَر مِنَ الْمَكْتَب, وَالصَّفّ أَكْبَر مِنَ الْمَكْتَب.

explanations.title: Comparing two things
explanations.body: Put the two things on each side of the comparative: A + أَفْعَل + مِنْ + B. When the second thing has ال, مِنْ and ال join into مِنَ الْ.

examples.text: هَذَا الصَّفّ أَكْبَر مِنَ الصَّفّ الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: hādhā aṣ-ṣaff ʾakbar mina aṣ-ṣaff al-qadīm. — This classroom is bigger than the old classroom.
al-maktaba ʾaqrab mina al-maṭʿam. — The library is nearer than the restaurant.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الطَّابِعَة أَحْدَث مِنَ الطَّابِعَة الْأُخْرَى.
examples.translation: hādhihi aṭ-ṭābiʿa ʾaḥdath mina aṭ-ṭābiʿa al-ʾukhrā. — This printer is newer than the other printer.

examples.text: نَافِذَة الصَّفّ أَوْسَع مِنْ نَافِذَة الْمَكْتَب.
examples.translation: nāfidha aṣ-ṣaff ʾawsaʿ min nāfidha al-maktab. — The classroom window is wider than the office window.
aṭ-ṭāwila al-qaṣīra ʾaqṣar mina al-kursiyy. — The short table is shorter than the chair.
baytī ʾabʿad min bayt ʾakhī. — My house is farther than my brother’s house.

exercises.prompt: What is the comparative of كَبِير?
What is the comparative of قَرِيب?
What is the comparative of طَوِيل?
Does the comparative change for a feminine noun?
exercises.explanation: أَفْعَل is the same for both.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The library is nearer than the restaurant”?

exercises.promptTranslation: My house is farther than my brother’s house.
This classroom is bigger than the old classroom.
The classroom window is wider than the office window.

lessons.title: 185. More comparatives: doubled letters and special forms
lessons.subtitle: أَقَلّ · أَشَدّ · أَهَمّ · أَقْوَى · أَغْلَى · أَفْضَل · أَسْوَأ

explanations.title: Doubled letters and final و / ي
explanations.body: Some adjectives have a doubled root letter (قَلِيل: ق-ل-ل). In the comparative the two letters join into one doubled letter: أَقَلّ. A root ending in a weak letter ends in ـَى: قَوِيّ → أَقْوَى, غَالِي → أَغْلَى. The others follow the pattern you know.

explanations.title: Comparing in practice
explanations.body: For “better”, أَفْضَل (or أَحْسَن) is used, and for “worse” أَسْوَأ. أَكْثَر means “more” and أَقَلّ means “less”, both with مِنْ.

examples.text: هَذَا الْحَاسُوب أَغْلَى مِنَ الْحَاسُوب الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: hādhā al-ḥāsūb ʾaghlā mina al-ḥāsūb al-qadīm. — This computer is more expensive than the old computer.
hādhihi al-mirwaḥa ʾaqwā min tilka. — This fan is stronger than that one.

examples.text: الدَّرْس الثَّانِي أَهَمّ مِنَ الدَّرْس الْأَوَّل.
examples.translation: ad-dars ath-thānī ʾahamm mina ad-dars al-ʾawwal. — The second lesson is more important than the first lesson.
ʿindī waqt ʾaqall min ʾams. — I have less time than yesterday.

examples.text: الْمَطْعَم الْجَدِيد أَفْضَل مِنَ الْمَطْعَم الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: al-maṭʿam al-jadīd ʾafḍal mina al-maṭʿam al-qadīm. — The new restaurant is better than the old restaurant.

examples.text: فِي الصَّفّ طُلَّاب أَكْثَر مِنْ أَمْس.
examples.translation: fī aṣ-ṣaff ṭullāb ʾakthar min ʾams. — There are more students in the class than yesterday.

exercises.prompt: What is the comparative of قَلِيل?
What is the comparative of مُهِمّ?
What is the comparative of قَوِيّ?
exercises.explanation: A final weak letter gives ـَى.

exercises.promptTranslation: This computer is more expensive than the old computer.
I have less time than yesterday.
The new restaurant is better than the old restaurant.

lessons.title: 186. Older than me, taller than you
lessons.subtitle: أَخِي أَكْبَر مِنِّي · أَنْتَ أَطْوَل مِنْهُ · هِيَ أَصْغَر مِنْكِ

explanations.title: Than me, than you: مِنِّي · مِنْكَ · مِنْهُ
explanations.body: After مِنْ, a pronoun is attached as an ending. The one for “me” is special: مِنْ + ـِي becomes مِنِّي. The same endings you used with عِنْدَ and مَعَ (عِنْدِي, مَعَكَ) are used here.

explanations.title: Age and the difference
explanations.body: To say how much older or younger, add بِ and the difference: بِسَنَة (by a year), بِسَنَتَيْن (by two years). The Arabic for “my elder / younger brother” is أَخِي الْأَكْبَر / أَخِي الْأَصْغَر.

examples.translation: ʾakhī ʾakbar minnī bisanatayn. — My brother is two years older than me.
ʾukhtī ʾaṣghar minnī bisana. — My sister is a year younger than me.
hal ʾanta ʾakbar min ʾakhīka? — Are you older than your brother? (to a man)

examples.text: أَنَا أَقْصَر مِنْهُ وَهُوَ أَطْوَل مِنِّي.
examples.translation: ʾanā ʾaqṣar minhu wahuwa ʾaṭwal minnī. — I am shorter than him and he is taller than me.
ʾanti ʾasraʿ minnī yā sāra. — You are faster than me, Sara. (to a woman)
ʾakhī al-ʾakbar muhandis. — My older brother is an engineer.

exercises.prompt: Which means “My brother is older than me by two years”?
Which means “We are stronger than them”?

exercises.promptTranslation: I am shorter than him and he is taller than me.
My sister is a year younger than me.
You are faster than me, Sara.

lessons.title: 187. The biggest, the tallest: the superlative
lessons.subtitle: الْأَكْبَر · الْأَطْوَل · أَكْبَر مَدِينَة · أَطْوَل نَهْر

explanations.title: Two ways to say “the most”
explanations.body: The same pattern gives the superlative in two ways. (1) With ال after a noun, or alone: الطَّالِب الْأَطْوَل, هُوَ الْأَطْوَل. (2) Without ال, in front of a singular noun without ال: أَطْوَل نَهْر, أَكْبَر مَدِينَة (“a longest river”, meaning “the longest river”). A place is added with فِي or مِنْ: فِي الصَّفّ, مِنْ بَيْن الطُّلَّاب.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Some feminine superlatives have their own form, for example الْكُبْرَى (the greatest) in the name الصَّحْرَاء الْكُبْرَى (the Sahara). In everyday speech the one form الْأَكْبَر is usual.

examples.translation: mani al-ʾaṭwal fī aṣ-ṣaff? — Who is the tallest in the class?
an-nīl ʾaṭwal nahr fī ʾafrīqiyā. — The Nile is the longest river in Africa.

examples.text: الْمُحِيط الْهَادِئ أَكْبَر مُحِيط فِي الْعَالَم.
examples.translation: al-muḥīṭ al-hādiʾ ʾakbar muḥīṭ fī al-ʿālam. — The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean in the world.
hādhihi ʾakbar qāʿa fī al-madrasa. — This is the biggest hall in the school.
khālid huwa al-ʾaṣghar fī aṣ-ṣaff. — Khalid is the youngest in the class.
hādhā ʾafḍal maṭʿam fī al-madīna. — This is the best restaurant in the city.

exercises.explanation: أَفْعَل + a singular noun without ال.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “the longest river”?
Which means “Who is the tallest in the class?”
Which means “Khalid is the youngest in the class”?
What does the word فِي mean in “the best restaurant IN the city”?

exercises.promptTranslation: This is the best restaurant in the city.
The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
Khalid is the youngest in the class.

lessons.title: 188. Colours, and “redder than”
lessons.subtitle: أَحْمَر · أَخْضَر · أَزْرَق · أَكْثَر اِحْمِرَارًا مِنْ

explanations.title: Colours agree with the noun
explanations.body: Most basic colours use the pattern أَفْعَل for a masculine noun and a pattern ending in ـَاء for a feminine one: بَاب أَحْمَر, سَيَّارَة حَمْرَاء. Colours that end in ـِيّ (بُنِّيّ, رَمَادِيّ) take ـِيَّة for the feminine.

explanations.title: More or less of a colour
explanations.body: A colour cannot take the أَفْعَل pattern again, so Arabic says “more of the colour”: أَكْثَر + the noun of the colour with ـًا, followed by مِنْ. The nouns are: اِحْمِرَار (redness), خُضْرَة (greenness), زُرْقَة (blueness), اِصْفِرَار (yellowness), بَيَاض (whiteness). For “less”, use أَقَلّ.

examples.text: لَوْن الْجُدْرَان أَبْيَض وَلَوْن الْبَاب بُنِّيّ.
examples.translation: lawn al-judrān ʾabyaḍ walawn al-bāb bunniyy. — The colour of the walls is white and the colour of the door is brown.
ʿindī sayyāra ḥamrāʾ. — I have a red car.

examples.text: هَذَا الْقَمِيص أَكْثَر اِحْمِرَارًا مِنَ الْقَمِيص الْآخَر.
examples.translation: hādhā al-qamīṣ ʾakthar iḥmirāran mina al-qamīṣ al-ʾākhar. — This shirt is redder than the other shirt.

examples.text: السَّمَاء الْيَوْم أَكْثَر زُرْقَةً مِنْ أَمْس.
examples.translation: as-samāʾ al-yawm ʾakthar zurqatan min ʾams. — The sky today is bluer than yesterday.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الْحَدِيقَة أَكْثَر خُضْرَةً مِنَ الْحَدِيقَة الْأُخْرَى.
examples.translation: hādhihi al-ḥadīqa ʾakthar khuḍratan mina al-ḥadīqa al-ʾukhrā. — This garden is greener than the other garden.

examples.text: الْحَائِط الْقَدِيم أَقَلّ بَيَاضًا مِنَ الْحَائِط الْجَدِيد.
examples.translation: al-ḥāʾiṭ al-qadīm ʾaqall bayāḍan mina al-ḥāʾiṭ al-jadīd. — The old wall is less white than the new wall.

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine of أَحْمَر?
exercises.explanation: The feminine pattern ends in ـَاء.

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine of أَزْرَق?

exercises.explanation: Feminine noun, feminine colour, colour after the noun.

exercises.promptTranslation: The colour of the walls is white and the colour of the door is brown.
I have a red car.
The sky today is bluer than yesterday.

lessons.title: 189. Places around the school
lessons.subtitle: الْبَوَّابَة · الْمَكْتَبَة · الْمَسْجِد · الْكَنِيسَة · الْمَلْعَب · مَكْتَب الْبَرِيد

explanations.title: A school and what is around it
explanations.body: A big school or campus has places for study, food, sport and prayer. The names with two nouns are the iḍāfa you know: مَكْتَب الْبَرِيد is “the office of the post”, so the first noun has no ال: مَكْتَب الْبَرِيد, not الْمَكْتَب الْبَرِيد.

explanations.title: Where is it?
explanations.body: Use the place words you know to say where each building is.

examples.translation: al-bawwāba ʾamām al-madrasa. — The gate is in front of the school.
al-maktaba bijānib al-masjid. — The library is next to the mosque.
al-kanīsa qarība mina as-sāḥa. — The church is near the courtyard.
al-malʿab khalf al-markaz ar-riyāḍiyy. — The field is behind the sports centre.
maktab al-barīd bayna al-ʿiyāda wal-matjar. — The post office is between the clinic and the shop.
ʾataghaddā fī al-maṭʿam kull yawm. — I have lunch in the restaurant every day.

exercises.prompt: Which place is for prayer for Christians?
Which place would you go to for football?

exercises.explanation: The first noun of an iḍāfa has no ال.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The library is next to the mosque”?

exercises.promptTranslation: The field is behind the sports centre.
The post office is between the clinic and the shop.
I have lunch in the restaurant every day.

lessons.title: 190. A place where…: what is it for?
lessons.subtitle: مَكَان يَلْعَب فِيهِ الْأَوْلَاد · مَكَان نَشْتَرِي مِنْهُ

explanations.title: Describing a place with a verb
explanations.body: To say “a place where…”, put a verb sentence straight after the word مَكَان, with no word for “where”. A pronoun then points back to the place: فِيهِ (in it), مِنْهُ (from it). مَكَان يَلْعَب فِيهِ الْأَوْلَاد = “a place in which the children play”. The verb stays singular before a plural subject.

rows: a place where we buy things

explanations.title: Riddles: “I am a place…”
explanations.body: Answer these riddles with a place from the last lesson.

examples.translation: ʾanā makān fīhi kutub kathīra. — I am a place with many books in it. (the library)

examples.text: أَنَا مَكَان يَلْعَب فِيهِ الْأَوْلَاد كُرَة الْقَدَم.
examples.translation: ʾanā makān yalʿab fīhi al-ʾawlād kura al-qadam. — I am a place where the boys play football. (the field)
ʾanā makān yaʾkul fīhi an-nās. — I am a place where people eat. (the restaurant)
ʾanā makān yuṣallī fīhi al-masīḥiyyūn. — I am a place where Christians pray. (the church)
ʾanā makān nursil minhu risāla. — I am a place from which we send a letter. (the post office)

examples.text: أَنَا مَكَان يَدْخُل مِنْهُ الطُّلَّاب وَيَخْرُجُون.
examples.translation: ʾanā makān yadkhul minhu aṭ-ṭullāb wayakhrujūn. — I am a place through which the students enter and leave. (the gate)

exercises.prompt: What does فِيهِ mean in مَكَان فِيهِ كُتُب?
What does مِنْهُ mean in مَكَان نُرْسِل مِنْهُ رِسَالَة?
Which place is “a place where children play”?
Which place is “a place where people eat”?
Which means “a place where Christians pray”?
exercises.explanation: A verb, فِيهِ, then the people.

exercises.prompt: Why is the verb يَلْعَب singular in يَلْعَب فِيهِ الْأَوْلَاد?
options: A verb before its subject stays singular
exercises.explanation: The verb comes first, so it stays singular.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am a place with many books in it.

exercises.explanation: A place in which people eat.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am a place where people eat.
I am a place from which we send a letter.

lessons.title: 191. Using services: post, cash, clinic
lessons.subtitle: أُرِيد أَنْ أُرْسِل طَرْدًا · أَسْحَب نُقُودًا · مَفْتُوح / مُغْلَق

explanations.title: What you do at each place
explanations.body: Each service has its own verb. Notice that the post office and the bank machine use verbs you can put after أُرِيد أَنْ (“I want to…”).

explanations.title: At the counter
explanations.body: To ask whether a place is open, use هَلْ and مَفْتُوح / مَفْتُوحَة. Opening hours use مِنَ السَّاعَة … إِلَى السَّاعَة …

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أُرْسِل رِسَالَة إِلَى أُمِّي.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾursil risāla ʾilā ʾummī. — I want to send a letter to my mother.
kam thaman hādhā aṭ-ṭābiʿ? — How much does this stamp cost?
ʾasḥab nuqūdan mina aṣ-ṣarrāf al-ʾāliyy. — I take out money from the cash machine.
hali al-ʿiyāda maftūḥa al-yawm? — Is the clinic open today?

examples.text: مَكْتَب الْبَرِيد مَفْتُوح مِنَ السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة إِلَى الْخَامِسَة.
examples.translation: maktab al-barīd maftūḥ mina as-sāʿa at-tāsiʿa ʾilā al-khāmisa. — The post office is open from nine to five.
al-matjar mughlaq yawm al-jumʿa. — The shop is closed on Friday.

exercises.prompt: Which place do you use to send a parcel?
Which means “Is the clinic open today?” (a feminine noun)
Which means “I want to send a letter to my mother”?
options: أُرِيد أَنْ أَقْرَأ رِسَالَة مِنْ أُمِّي
أُرِيد أَنْ أُرْسِل رِسَالَة إِلَى أُمِّي

exercises.prompt: What does the question كَمْ ثَمَن هَذَا الطَّابِع؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: The shop is closed on Friday.
The post office is open from nine.
I withdraw money from the cash machine.

lessons.title: 192. The genitive case: after a preposition and in the iḍāfa
lessons.subtitle: فِي الْبَيْتِ · بَابُ الْبَيْتِ · مِنْ مَدِينَةٍ

explanations.title: Three cases, three endings
explanations.body: In careful Arabic the last letter of a noun shows its job in the sentence. The subject takes ـُ (nominative), the object takes ـَ (accusative) and a noun after a preposition takes ـِ (genitive). A noun without ال adds a nunation sign (tanwīn): ـٌ, ـً, ـٍ. Until now this course has left these endings out, as Arabic speakers do when they pause. From here on you will see them in some lessons, so that you can read fully vowelled texts.

explanations.title: Where the genitive appears
explanations.body: Two places put a noun in the genitive. First, a noun after a preposition (فِي, مِنْ, عَلَى, إِلَى, عَنْ, مَعَ). Second, the owner in an iḍāfa: the first noun has no ال and no tanwīn, and the second noun is genitive. An adjective copies the case of its noun.

examples.translation: al-kitābu fī al-bayti. — The book is in the house.
al-qalamu ʿalā al-maktabi. — The pen is on the desk.
ʾanā min madīnatin kabīratin. — I am from a big city.
bābu al-bayti kabīrun. — The door of the house is big.
kitābu aṭ-ṭālibi jadīdun. — The student’s book is new.
maktabu al-mudīri fī al-bayti al-qadīmi. — The director’s desk is in the old house.

exercises.prompt: Which case does a noun take after a preposition such as فِي?
exercises.explanation: Prepositions are followed by the genitive.

exercises.prompt: Which is the genitive of الْبَيْتُ?
Which is the genitive of بَيْتٌ (without ال)?
Which means “the door of the house”?
exercises.explanation: First noun: no ال, no tanwīn. Second noun: genitive.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct? “The book is in the house.”
In كِتَابُ الطَّالِبِ, which word is in the genitive?
Why does كِتَابُ have no tanwīn in كِتَابُ الطَّالِبِ?
options: it is the first noun of an iḍāfa
exercises.explanation: The first noun of an iḍāfa takes no tanwīn and no ال.
The owner in an iḍāfa is genitive and has ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: The student’s book is new.
The pen is on the desk.

lessons.title: 193. The genitive of the dual and the plural
lessons.subtitle: مَعَ الطَّالِبَيْنِ · مِنَ الْمُهَنْدِسِينَ · بَيْتُ الْمُدَرِّسَاتِ

explanations.title: Two forms, not three
explanations.body: The dual and the sound masculine plural have only two forms. The subject form is ـَانِ (dual) or ـُونَ (plural). After a preposition, as the second noun of an iḍāfa and as an object, the form is ـَيْنِ (dual) or ـِينَ (plural). You have met these forms in earlier units. Now you know why they change.

explanations.title: The sound feminine plural
explanations.body: The sound feminine plural (ـَات) has two forms too. The subject form ends in ـَاتُ. After a preposition, and as an object, it ends in ـَاتِ with a kasra, not a fatḥa.

examples.translation: ʾanā maʿa aṭ-ṭālibayni fī al-maktabati. — I am with the two students in the library.
ar-risālatu mina al-muhandisīna. — The letter is from the engineers.
al-kutubu ʿalā maktabi al-mudarrisayni. — The books are on the two teachers’ desk.
al-kurrāsatu ʿalā ṭāwilati aṭ-ṭālibatayni. — The notebook is on the two female students’ table.
baytu al-mudarrisāti qarībun mina al-jāmiʿati. — The female teachers’ house is near the university.
ʾanā fī aṣ-ṣaffi maʿa aṭ-ṭālibāti. — I am in class with the female students.

exercises.prompt: Which is the dual of طَالِب after a preposition?
Which is the plural of مُهَنْدِس after a preposition?
Which means “The letter is from the engineers”?
Which ending does the sound feminine plural take after a preposition?
Why is the ending ـَيْنِ in مَكْتَبُ الْمُدَرِّسَيْنِ?
options: the second noun of an iḍāfa is genitive

exercises.promptTranslation: The letter is from the two engineers.
I am in class with the students.

exercises.explanation: Two female students; second noun of an iḍāfa.
exercises.promptTranslation: The notebook is on the two female students’ table.

lessons.title: 194. An afternoon off: activities and feelings
lessons.subtitle: أَشْعُر بِالرَّاحَة · نَظَّفْتُ الْغُرْفَة · غَسَلْتُ الْمَلَابِس

explanations.title: How do you feel?
explanations.body: Feelings are adjectives, so they agree with the person: add ـَة for a woman. For “I feel…” Arabic says أَشْعُر بِـ + a noun, with بِ joined to the noun: أَشْعُر بِالسَّعَادَة (“I feel happiness”).

explanations.title: What I did
explanations.body: On a day off you can talk about what you did with the past tense you know, in the first person ـْتُ.

examples.translation: naẓẓaftu al-ghurfa waghasaltu al-malābis. — I cleaned the room and washed the clothes.
shāhadtu fīlman hādiʾan fī al-masāʾ. — I watched a quiet film in the evening.
zurtu ṣadīqī baʿda aẓ-ẓuhr. — I visited my friend in the afternoon.
ʾanā murtāḥ liʾanna al-yawm ʿuṭla. — I am relaxed because today is a holiday.
ʾashʿur bish-shawq ʾilā ʾummī. — I miss my mother.
sāra ghāḍiba waʾaḥmad ṣāmit. — Sara is angry and Ahmad is silent.

explanations.title: A short email (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: Here is a short email from Sara to her friend Ahmad. Read it line by line.

examples.translation: ʿazīzī ʾaḥmad, — Dear Ahmad,
kāna al-yawm yawm rāḥa. — Today was a day of rest.
naẓẓaftu al-ghurfa waghasaltu al-malābis. — I cleaned the room and washed the clothes.
thumma shāhadtu fīlman hādiʾan. — Then I watched a quiet film.

examples.text: أَشْعُر بِالرَّاحَة، وَأَشْعُر أَيْضًا بِالشَّوْق إِلَى أَهْلِي.
examples.translation: ʾashʿur bir-rāḥa, waʾashʿur ʾayḍan bish-shawq ʾilā ʾahlī. — I feel at ease, and I also miss my family.
maʿa taḥiyyātī, sāra — With my greetings, Sara

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine of غَاضِب?
Which is the feminine of مُرْتَاح?
Which sentence means “I miss my mother”?

exercises.promptTranslation: Sara is happy because today is a holiday.
I miss my family.
Yesterday I watched a quiet film.

explanations.title: Two easy ways to say “how”
explanations.body: (1) بِـ + a noun: بِسُرْعَة (“with speed”) means “quickly”. (2) An adjective with the accusative nunation ـًا: جَيِّدًا (“well”), سَرِيعًا (“fast”). Both go after the verb.

explanations.title: In what state?
explanations.body: An adjective with ـًا can also describe the state of a person while he does something: دَخَلَ مُبْتَسِمًا (“he came in smiling”). This one must agree with the person it describes in gender and number, and it stays accusative: ـًا (one man), ـَةً (one woman), ـَيْنِ (two), ـِينَ (men).

examples.translation: yatakallam al-mudarris bihudūʾ. — The teacher speaks calmly.
taʿmal ʾukhtī jayyidan. — My sister works well.
dakhala al-mudarris mubtasiman. — The teacher came in smiling.
dakhalati al-mudarrisa mubtasimatan. — The female teacher came in smiling.
dakhala aṭ-ṭālibāni mubtasimayni. — The two students came in smiling.
dakhala aṭ-ṭullāb mubtasimīna. — The students came in smiling.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The teacher came in smiling”?
Which means “The female teacher came in smiling”?
The state word in دَخَلَ مُبْتَسِمًا agrees with the person in…
exercises.explanation: It matches the person: one man, one woman, two or several.

exercises.promptTranslation: The students came in smiling.
The teacher speaks calmly.
My sister works well.

lessons.title: 196. This and that: demonstratives
lessons.subtitle: هَذَا · هَذِهِ · هَذَانِ · هَاتَانِ · هَؤُلَاءِ · ذَلِكَ · تِلْكَ · أُولَئِكَ

explanations.title: “This” and “these”
explanations.body: The word for “this” depends on the noun: masculine هَذَا, feminine هَذِهِ. There are also forms for two things and for several people. The dual changes like any dual: one form for the subject and one after a preposition.

explanations.title: “That” and “those”, and how to use them
explanations.body: For something farther away, use ذَلِكَ (masculine), تِلْكَ (feminine) and أُولَئِكَ (people). With a noun that has ال, the demonstrative comes first and means “this …” or “that …”: هَذَا الْكِتَاب. With a noun that has no ال, it makes a sentence: هَذَا كِتَاب (“This is a book”). Several things (not people) take the feminine singular: هَذِهِ الْكُتُب مُفِيدَة.

examples.text: هَذَا الْكِتَاب جَدِيد وَذَلِكَ الْكِتَاب قَدِيم.
examples.translation: hādhā al-kitāb jadīd wadhālika al-kitāb qadīm. — This book is new and that book is old.
hādhā kitāb. — This is a book.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَة كَبِيرَة وَتِلْكَ الْمَدِينَة صَغِيرَة.
examples.translation: hādhihi al-madīna kabīra watilka al-madīna ṣaghīra. — This city is big and that city is small.
hādhāni aṭ-ṭālibāni fī aṣ-ṣaff. — These two students are in the class.
ʾanā maʿa hātayni aṭ-ṭālibatayni. — I am with these two female students.

examples.text: هَؤُلَاءِ الطُّلَّاب مِنْ كَنَدَا وَأُولَئِكَ الطُّلَّاب مِنَ الْأُرْدُنّ.
examples.translation: hāʾulāʾ aṭ-ṭullāb min kanadā waʾulāʾika aṭ-ṭullāb mina al-ʾurdunn. — These students are from Canada and those students are from Jordan.
hādhihi al-kutub mufīda. — These books are useful.

exercises.explanation: Without ال it is a full sentence.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct? “This city is big.”
Which goes with “the two female students” as the subject?

exercises.explanation: Several things take the feminine singular.

exercises.promptTranslation: This book is new and that book is old.
I am with these two female students.
These students are from Canada.

lessons.title: 197. Review: the classroom and comparing
lessons.subtitle: صَفِّي الْجَدِيد أَكْبَر مِنَ الصَّفّ الْقَدِيم

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: To compare, use أَفْعَل + مِنْ. After مِنْ a pronoun is attached (مِنِّي, مِنْكَ, مِنْهُ). For “the most”, put أَفْعَل in front of a singular noun without ال, or use الْأَفْعَل on its own. A colour agrees with its noun.

explanations.title: A letter from a new student (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: Read these lines from a student’s letter. Notice how each one compares two things.

examples.text: صَفِّي الْجَدِيد أَكْبَر مِنَ الصَّفّ الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: ṣaffī al-jadīd ʾakbar mina aṣ-ṣaff al-qadīm. — My new classroom is bigger than the old classroom.
fīhi nawāfidh ʾakthar waḍawʾ ʾaqwā. — It has more windows and a stronger light.

examples.text: الْكُرْسِيّ الْجَدِيد أَغْلَى مِنَ الْكُرْسِيّ الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: al-kursiyy al-jadīd ʾaghlā mina al-kursiyy al-qadīm. — The new chair is more expensive than the old chair.
al-maktaba al-jadīda ʾaqrab min baytī. — The new library is nearer than my house.

examples.text: أَنَا أَصْغَر مِنْ أَخِي بِسَنَتَيْن وَهُوَ أَقْصَر مِنِّي.
examples.translation: ʾanā ʾaṣghar min ʾakhī bisanatayn wahuwa ʾaqṣar minnī. — I am two years younger than my brother and he is shorter than me.
hādhā ʾafḍal ṣaff fī al-madrasa. — This is the best classroom in the school.

exercises.prompt: Which means “My new classroom is bigger than the old one”?
options: صَفِّي الْجَدِيد أَصْغَر مِنَ الصَّفّ الْقَدِيم
صَفِّي الْجَدِيد أَكْبَر مِنَ الصَّفّ الْقَدِيم
صَفِّي الْقَدِيم أَكْبَر مِنَ الصَّفّ الْجَدِيد

exercises.prompt: Which means “the best classroom in the school”?
Which is correct for “a red car” (a feminine noun)?

exercises.promptTranslation: The new chair is more expensive than the old chair.
I am two years younger than my brother.
He is shorter than me.

lessons.title: 198. Review: school places, the genitive, manner, this and that
lessons.subtitle: هَذِهِ مَدْرَسَتِي · تِلْكَ الْقَاعَة · دَخَلَ بِهُدُوء

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: After a preposition and as the owner in an iḍāfa a noun is genitive: فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ, بَابُ الْمَكْتَبَةِ. The dual and the plural use ـَيْنِ and ـِينَ there. To say how, use بِ + noun or an adjective with ـًا that agrees with the person. Use هَذَا / هَذِهِ for “this”, ذَلِكَ / تِلْكَ for “that”, هَؤُلَاءِ for “these” and أُولَئِكَ for “those”.

explanations.title: A tour of the school (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: A guide shows a visitor around. The sentences mix everything from this part of the unit.

examples.translation: hādhihi madrasatī al-jadīda. — This is my new school.

examples.text: تِلْكَ الْقَاعَة أَكْبَر مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَاعَة.
examples.translation: tilka al-qāʿa ʾakbar min hādhihi al-qāʿa. — That hall is bigger than this hall.
al-kutubu fī maktabati al-madrasati. — The books are in the school library.
dakhala al-mudīr al-qāʿa bihudūʾ. — The director entered the hall calmly.

examples.text: هَؤُلَاءِ الطُّلَّاب مَعَ الْمُدَرِّسَيْنِ فِي الْمَلْعَبِ.
examples.translation: hāʾulāʾ aṭ-ṭullāb maʿa al-mudarrisayni fī al-malʿabi. — These students are with the two teachers on the playground.
dakhala aṭ-ṭullāb mubtasimīna. — The students came in smiling.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct for “the door of the library”?
exercises.explanation: The first noun has no ال; the owner is genitive.

exercises.prompt: Which means “This is my new school”?
exercises.explanation: مَدْرَسَة is feminine and singular: هَذِهِ.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct? “The students came in smiling.”

exercises.explanation: The owner in an iḍāfa is genitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: The books are in the school library.
That hall is bigger than this hall.
These students are with the two teachers on the playground.

units.title: الْمَدِينَة وَالطُّرُق: sights, transport, directions and hollow verbs

lessons.title: 199. Sights of a seaside town
lessons.subtitle: الْمَتْحَف · الْفَنَار · الشَّاطِئ · الرَّصِيف · مَرْكَز الشُّرْطَة

explanations.title: Places to see
explanations.body: A visitor to a town looks for its landmarks (مَعَالِم, the plural of مَعْلَم). Here are common places in a town by the sea. Many of them are an iḍāfa (“the station of the police”), so the first noun has no ال.

explanations.title: Describing a town
explanations.body: Use the nominal sentences you know: a place + فِي + the town, or a place + قَرِيب مِنْ (near) another. Use فِيهِ / فِيهَا for “in it”: فِيهِ means “in it” for a masculine noun and فِيهَا for a feminine noun.

examples.translation: fī al-madīna as-sāḥiliyya maʿālim kathīra. — There are many sights in the coastal town.
al-matḥaf qarīb mina ash-shāṭiʾ. — The museum is near the beach.
yushāhid az-zāʾir al-fanār min baʿīd. — The visitor sees the lighthouse from far away.

examples.text: عَلَى الرَّصِيف مَطَاعِم كَثِيرَة وَفِيهِ مَتْجَر لِلْهَدَايَا.
examples.translation: ʿalā ar-raṣīf maṭāʿim kathīra wafīhi matjar lil-hadāyā. — On the pier there are many restaurants and in it there is a gift shop.
maktab al-istiʿlāmāt fī wasaṭ al-madīna. — The information office is in the middle of the town.
markaz ash-shurṭa qarīb mina al-mustashfā. — The police station is near the hospital.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of مَعْلَم (landmark)?

exercises.explanation: The first noun of an iḍāfa has no ال.

exercises.promptTranslation: The museum is near the beach.
The information office is in the middle of the town.

exercises.prompt: عَلَى الرَّصِيف مَطَاعِم كَثِيرَة وَ___ مَتْجَر لِلْهَدَايَا.
exercises.explanation: رَصِيف is masculine: in it = فِيهِ.
exercises.promptTranslation: On the pier there are many restaurants and in it there is a gift shop.

lessons.title: 200. What can you do there?
lessons.subtitle: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَمْشِي عَلَى الشَّاطِئ · تُحِبّ زِيَارَة الْمَتْحَف

explanations.title: You can…
explanations.body: To say what is possible, use يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ (“you can”, to a man) or يُمْكِنُكِ أَنْ (to a woman), then a present verb. To say what you like, use أُحِبّ and a verbal noun (a noun made from a verb): زِيَارَة الْمَتْحَف (“visiting the museum”). When the verbal noun is followed by its object, it is the first noun of an iḍāfa and has no ال.

explanations.title: Suggestions for a visitor
explanations.body: With إِذَا (“if”) you can say what to do when you like something: إِذَا كُنْتَ تُحِبّ … فَ …

examples.text: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَمْشِي عَلَى الشَّاطِئ فِي الصَّبَاح.
examples.translation: yumkinuka ʾan tamshī ʿalā ash-shāṭiʾ fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — You can walk on the beach in the morning.

examples.text: يُمْكِنُكِ أَنْ تَأْكُلِي السَّمَك الطَّازَج فِي الْمَطْعَم.
examples.translation: yumkinuki ʾan taʾkulī as-samak aṭ-ṭāzaj fī al-maṭʿam. — You can eat fresh fish at the restaurant. (to a woman)

examples.text: إِذَا كُنْتَ تُحِبّ الْمَتَاحِف فَزُرِ الْمَتْحَف الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: ʾidhā kunta tuḥibb al-matāḥif fazuri al-matḥaf al-qadīm. — If you like museums, visit the old museum.

examples.text: أُحِبّ مُشَاهَدَة غُرُوب الشَّمْس مِنَ الرَّصِيف.
examples.translation: ʾuḥibb mushāhada ghurūb ash-shams mina ar-raṣīf. — I like watching the sunset from the pier.

examples.text: فِي الْمَسَاء مَنْظَر جَمِيل عَلَى الْخَلِيج.
examples.translation: fī al-masāʾ manẓar jamīl ʿalā al-khalīj. — In the evening there is a beautiful view over the bay.
yumkinukum ʾan tarkabū safīna ṣaghīra. — You can take a small boat. (to several people)

exercises.prompt: Which means “You can walk on the beach”? (to a man)
Which is the form for a woman?
What does مُشَاهَدَة غُرُوب الشَّمْس mean?
Which means “If you like museums, visit the old museum”?
options: إِذَا كُنْتَ تُحِبّ الْمَتَاحِف فَلَا تَزُرِ الْمَتْحَف
إِذَا كُنْتَ تُحِبّ الْمَتَاحِف فَزُرِ الْمَتْحَف الْقَدِيم

exercises.prompt: The verbal noun in أُحِبّ مُشَاهَدَة غُرُوب الشَّمْس has…
exercises.explanation: It is the first noun of an iḍāfa.

exercises.promptTranslation: You can eat the fresh fish. (to a woman)

exercises.explanation: A verbal noun with no ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: I like watching the sunset from the pier.

exercises.prompt: إِذَا ___ تُحِبّ الْمَتَاحِف فَزُرِ الْمَتْحَف الْقَدِيم.
exercises.promptTranslation: If you like museums, visit the old museum.

explanations.title: Words you meet in a brochure
explanations.body: A brochure speaks to “you” (the reader) in the present tense and uses many verbal nouns. These words help you read it.

explanations.title: Read the brochure (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: The text is invented for practice. A travel company describes a weekend by the sea.

examples.text: تُنَظِّم لَكَ شَرِكَتُنَا رِحْلَات رَائِعَة إِلَى الشَّاطِئ.
examples.translation: tunaẓẓim laka sharikatunā riḥlāt rāʾiʿa ʾilā ash-shāṭiʾ. — Our company organises wonderful trips to the beach for you.

examples.text: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَسْتَمْتِع بِالْمَهْرَجَان السَّنَوِيّ لِلْمُوسِيقَى.
examples.translation: yumkinuka ʾan tastamtiʿ bil-mahrajān as-sanawiyy lil-mūsīqā. — You can enjoy the annual music festival.

examples.text: إِذَا كُنْتَ تُحِبّ الْأَسْوَاق الْقَدِيمَة فَسَتَجِد أَشْيَاء كَثِيرَة.
examples.translation: ʾidhā kunta tuḥibb al-ʾaswāq al-qadīma fasatajid ʾashyāʾ kathīra. — If you like old markets, you will find many things.

examples.text: تَجِد الْمَزِيد مِنَ الْمَعْلُومَات فِي مَكْتَب الِاسْتِعْلَامَات.
examples.translation: tajid al-mazīd mina al-maʿlūmāt fī maktab al-istiʿlāmāt. — You find more information at the information office.

examples.text: كُلّ هَذِهِ الْمَرَاكِز تَجْعَل إِقَامَتَكَ آمِنَة وَمُمْتِعَة.
examples.translation: kull hādhihi al-marākiz tajʿal ʾiqāmataka ʾāmina wamumtiʿa. — All these centres make your stay safe and enjoyable.
natamannā laka riḥla saʿīda. — We wish you a happy trip.

exercises.prompt: What does نَتَمَنَّى لَكَ رِحْلَة سَعِيدَة mean?
options: We organise a trip for you
We wish you a happy trip

exercises.prompt: What does تَجِد الْمَزِيد مِنَ الْمَعْلُومَات mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Our company organises wonderful trips for you.

exercises.prompt: كُلّ هَذِهِ الْمَرَاكِز تَجْعَل إِقَامَتَكَ آمِنَة ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: All these centres make your stay safe and enjoyable.
You can enjoy the festival.

lessons.title: 202. Hollow verbs in the present: قَالَ → يَقُول
lessons.subtitle: قَالَ يَقُول · زَارَ يَزُور · عَاشَ يَعِيش · نَامَ يَنَام · بَاعَ يَبِيع

explanations.title: A long ā in the middle of the past
explanations.body: Some verbs have a long ā in the middle of the he-form of the past: قَالَ, زَارَ, عَاشَ, بَاعَ, نَامَ. They are called hollow verbs, because the middle of the root is a weak letter, wāw or yāʾ, hidden inside the ā. In the present tense the weak letter comes back: يَقُول (wāw), يَبِيع (yāʾ). When the present has a long ā (يَنَام), the weak letter is not visible, so look the verb up in a dictionary.

explanations.title: Present tense in sentences
explanations.body: The prefixes are the same as for sound verbs (أَ, نَ, تَ, يَ). Only the middle changes, and the long vowel stays long.

examples.translation: ʾaqūl ṣabāḥ al-khayr lil-mudarris. — I say good morning to the teacher.
ʾazūr jaddī kull ʾusbūʿ. — I visit my grandfather every week.
yaʿīsh ʾakhī fī madīna sāḥiliyya. — My brother lives in a coastal town.
yabīʿ aṣ-ṣayyād as-samak ʿalā ar-raṣīf. — The fisherman sells fish on the pier.
tanām ʾukhtī mubakkiran. — My sister goes to sleep early.
ʾabī yaqūd as-sayyāra bibuṭʾ. — My father drives the car slowly.

exercises.prompt: Which is the present (he) of قَالَ?
Which is the present (he) of بَاعَ?
Which is the present (he) of عَاشَ?
Why are verbs like قَالَ and بَاعَ called hollow?
options: they end in a long vowel
the middle of the root is a weak letter
exercises.explanation: The weak letter hides inside the ā.

exercises.promptTranslation: My brother lives in a coastal town.
I visit my grandfather every week.
The fisherman sells fish on the pier.

explanations.title: Three verbs, the whole present
explanations.body: Learn the three patterns once. The long vowel stays long in all persons with a vowel ending, and with the endings ـِين, ـُون and ـَان nothing else changes.

explanations.title: The short forms for women in the plural
explanations.body: With the plural “they / you (all women)”, the long vowel becomes short and a sukūn comes before the ending ـْنَ: يَقُلْنَ, تَقُلْنَ, يَبِعْنَ, يَنَمْنَ. The past tense does this for I, you and we, too: قُلْتُ, بِعْتُ, نِمْتُ. In these forms, ā disappears.

examples.translation: hal taqūlīn dhālika liʾummiki? — Do you say that to your mother? (to a woman)
nabīʿ as-samak kull yawm. — We sell fish every day.
al-ʾawlād yanāmūn fī al-ghurfa al-kabīra. — The boys sleep in the big room.
al-banāt yaqulna marḥaban. — The girls say hello.
qultu lahu dhālika ʾams. — I told him that yesterday.
biʿtu sayyāratī al-qadīma. — I sold my old car.

exercises.prompt: What happens to the long vowel in يَقُلْنَ?
exercises.explanation: Before ـْنَ the vowel is short.
In the past, I = ـْتُ and ā disappears.

exercises.promptTranslation: Do you say that to your mother?
The boys sleep in the big room.
Yesterday I sold my old car.

lessons.title: 204. Hollow verbs in conversation
lessons.subtitle: هَلْ تَعِيش هُنَا؟ · مَاذَا تَقُولِين؟ · لَا أَبِيعُهَا

explanations.title: Questions and answers
explanations.body: Hollow verbs are very frequent in speech. Here are short exchanges that use them. The question and the answer use the same verb in a different person: you → I, you → we.

examples.translation: hal taʿīsh fī al-madīna? — Do you live in the city?
naʿam, ʾaʿīsh hunā maʿa ʾusratī. — Yes, I live here with my family.
mādhā taqūlīn liṣadīqatiki? — What do you say to your friend? (to a woman)
ʾaqūl lahā shukran. — I say thank you to her.
matā tanāmūn? — When do you all sleep?
nanām fī as-sāʿa al-ʿāshira. — We go to sleep at ten.

explanations.title: Who does what?
explanations.body: With a negative, put لَا before the present verb: لَا أَبِيعُهَا (“I do not sell it”). An object pronoun is attached to the verb as an ending.

examples.translation: man yaqūd as-sayyāra? — Who drives the car?
ʾabī yaqūd waʾummī tanām. — My father drives and my mother sleeps.
hal tabīʿ sayyārataka? — Are you selling your car? (to a man)
lā, lā ʾabīʿuhā. — No, I am not selling it.
ʾukhtī tazūr jaddatī kull jumʿa. — My sister visits my grandmother every Friday.
hum lā yaʿīshūn baʿīdan ʿannā. — They do not live far from us.

exercises.prompt: How do you answer هَلْ تَعِيش هُنَا؟ with “Yes, I live here”?

options: What do you say? (to a woman)

exercises.prompt: Which means “We go to sleep at ten”?
Which means “I do not sell it”?
Which means “They do not live far from us”?

exercises.promptTranslation: My father drives the car and my mother sleeps.
My sister visits my grandmother every Friday.
When do you all sleep?

explanations.title: How do you get there?
explanations.body: The general word for transport is مُوَاصَلَات. Most means of transport are feminine nouns. The train, قِطَار, is masculine, and so are مَطَار (airport) and مَوْقِف (stop). To say “by bus”, use بِـ: بِالْحَافِلَة.

explanations.title: Verbs of travel
explanations.body: Four verbs are useful for any journey. وَصَلَ (to arrive) has a missing و in the present: يَصِل.

examples.translation: ʾarkab al-ḥāfila ʾilā al-maḥaṭṭa. — I take the bus to the station.

examples.text: أَنْزِل مِنَ الْقِطَار فِي الْمَحَطَّة الْأَخِيرَة.
examples.translation: ʾanzil mina al-qiṭār fī al-maḥaṭṭa al-ʾakhīra. — I get off the train at the last station.
yaṣil al-qiṭār fī as-sāʿa ath-thālitha. — The train arrives at three o’clock.
tughādir aṭ-ṭāʾira al-maṭār fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The plane leaves the airport in the morning.

examples.text: آخُذ سَيَّارَة أُجْرَة مِنَ الْمَطَار إِلَى الْفُنْدُق.
examples.translation: ʾākhudh sayyāra ʾujra mina al-maṭār ʾilā al-funduq. — I take a taxi from the airport to the hotel.
al-mawqif ʾamāma al-maḥaṭṭa. — The stop is in front of the station.

exercises.prompt: What does تُغَادِر الطَّائِرَة الْمَطَار mean?
options: The plane arrives at the airport
The plane is in the airport

exercises.prompt: Which means “I get off the train”?

exercises.promptTranslation: I take the bus to the station.

exercises.explanation: Taxi: an iḍāfa with no ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: I take a taxi from the airport.

exercises.explanation: Something that arrives at a station.
exercises.promptTranslation: The train arrives at three o’clock.

lessons.title: 206. Which is faster? Comparing transport and journey times
lessons.subtitle: الطَّائِرَة أَسْرَع مِنَ الْقِطَار · تَسْتَغْرِق الرِّحْلَة سَاعَتَيْن

explanations.title: Faster, slower, cheaper
explanations.body: You already know the pattern أَفْعَل + مِنْ. Use it to compare ways of travelling. The pattern for “slow” is أَبْطَأ (slower).

explanations.title: How long does it take?
explanations.body: To say how long a journey takes, use تَسْتَغْرِق (“takes”) and a length of time. The numbers 3–10 take the opposite gender of the noun: سَاعَة is feminine, so ثَلَاث سَاعَات. Two is a dual: سَاعَتَيْن.

examples.translation: aṭ-ṭāʾira ʾasraʿ mina al-qiṭār. — The plane is faster than the train.
al-qiṭār ʾarkhaṣ mina aṭ-ṭāʾira. — The train is cheaper than the plane.
al-ḥāfila ʾabṭaʾ mina al-qiṭār. — The bus is slower than the train.
tastaghriq ar-riḥla bil-qiṭār sāʿatayn. — The trip by train takes two hours.
tastaghriq ar-riḥla bil-ḥāfila thalāth sāʿāt. — The trip by bus takes three hours.

examples.text: أَفْضَل وَسِيلَة إِلَى الْمَطَار هِيَ سَيَّارَة الْأُجْرَة.
examples.translation: ʾafḍal wasīla ʾilā al-maṭār hiya sayyāra al-ʾujra. — The best way to the airport is a taxi.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The plane is faster than the train”?
Which means “The train is cheaper than the plane”?

exercises.explanation: سَاعَة is feminine: opposite gender, ثَلَاث.

exercises.prompt: What does تَسْتَغْرِق الرِّحْلَة سَاعَتَيْن mean?
options: The trip left two hours ago
The trip is two hours late

exercises.promptTranslation: The bus is slower than the train.
The trip by bus takes three hours.

exercises.prompt: أَفْضَل ___ إِلَى الْمَطَار هِيَ سَيَّارَة الْأُجْرَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The best way to the airport is a taxi.

lessons.title: 207. Road signs
lessons.subtitle: مَمْنُوع الدُّخُول · مَمْنُوع الْوُقُوف · اِتِّجَاه وَاحِد

explanations.title: Signs that forbid
explanations.body: مَمْنُوع means “forbidden”. After it comes a verbal noun (a noun made from a verb) with ال, or مُرُور (“passing”) + the thing that may not pass. Other signs are just short noun phrases.

explanations.title: Reading signs in sentences
explanations.body: A sign is usually a short phrase without a verb. In a sentence you can explain it: هَذِهِ الْعَلَامَة تَعْنِي …

examples.translation: hādhihi al-ʿalāma taʿnī mamnūʿ ad-dukhūl. — This sign means no entry.
aṭ-ṭarīq mughlaq, falā tadkhul. — The road is closed, so do not enter.
ʿinda ʾishāra al-murūr qif. — At the traffic light, stop.
hādhā aṭ-ṭarīq as-sarīʿ ittijāh wāḥid. — This highway is one way.

examples.text: أَقْصَى سُرْعَة فِي الْمَدِينَة أَقَلّ مِنْ أَقْصَى سُرْعَة عَلَى الطَّرِيق السَّرِيع.
examples.translation: ʾaqṣā surʿa fī al-madīna ʾaqall min ʾaqṣā surʿa ʿalā aṭ-ṭarīq as-sarīʿ. — The maximum speed in the city is less than the maximum speed on the highway.

examples.text: مَمْنُوع مُرُور الشَّاحِنَات فِي شَوَارِع الْمَدِينَة.
examples.translation: mamnūʿ murūr ash-shāḥināt fī shawāriʿ al-madīna. — Trucks may not pass in the city streets.

exercises.prompt: What does قِفْ mean on a sign?

exercises.promptTranslation: Trucks may not pass in the city streets.
The road is closed, so do not enter.
This sign means no entry.

lessons.title: 208. Rules of the road: must and must not
lessons.subtitle: يَجِب أَنْ تَقِف · لَا يَجُوز أَنْ تَقُود بِسُرْعَة

explanations.title: Must, may and may not
explanations.body: To say “you must”, use يَجِب أَنْ + a present verb (or عَلَيْكَ أَنْ). To say “it is not allowed”, use لَا يَجُوز أَنْ. The verb after أَنْ is the present form, but the endings ـِين and ـُون lose their final ن: تَقِفِي, تَقُودُوا. Some roads have their own rules.

explanations.title: The driver’s rules
explanations.body: Notice that قَادَ (to drive) is a hollow verb: تَقُود. Another useful verb is وَقَفَ (to stop, to stand), which loses its first و in the present: تَقِف.

examples.text: يَجِب أَنْ تَقِف عِنْدَ إِشَارَة الْمُرُور.
examples.translation: yajib ʾan taqif ʿinda ʾishāra al-murūr. — You must stop at the traffic light.
yajib ʾan taqūd biḥadhar. — You must drive carefully.

examples.text: لَا يَجُوز أَنْ تَقُود بِسُرْعَة كَبِيرَة فِي الْمَدِينَة.
examples.translation: lā yajūz ʾan taqūd bisurʿa kabīra fī al-madīna. — You may not drive at a high speed in the city.

examples.text: عَلَيْكِ أَنْ تَقُودِي بِبُطْء فِي الشَّارِع الْمُزْدَحِم.
examples.translation: ʿalayki ʾan taqūdī bibuṭʾ fī ash-shāriʿ al-muzdaḥim. — You must drive slowly in the crowded street. (to a woman)
yajib ʾan taʾkhudh rukhṣa al-qiyāda. — You must get a driving licence.

examples.text: لَا يَجُوز الْوُقُوف أَمَامَ مَوْقِف الْحَافِلَات.
examples.translation: lā yajūz al-wuqūf ʾamāma mawqif al-ḥāfilāt. — Stopping in front of the bus stop is not allowed.

exercises.prompt: Which means “You must stop at the light”?
options: يَجِب أَنْ تَسِير عِنْدَ إِشَارَة الْمُرُور
لَا يَجُوز أَنْ تَقِف عِنْدَ إِشَارَة الْمُرُور
يَجِب أَنْ تَقُول عِنْدَ إِشَارَة الْمُرُور
يَجِب أَنْ تَقِف عِنْدَ إِشَارَة الْمُرُور

exercises.prompt: What does لَا يَجُوز أَنْ تَقُود بِسُرْعَة mean?
Which is the form for a woman: “you drive”?
Which is the present “you stop” (to a man)?

exercises.promptTranslation: You must drive carefully.
You may not drive at a high speed.

exercises.explanation: An iḍāfa: no ال on the first noun.
exercises.promptTranslation: You must stop at the traffic light.

lessons.title: 209. Commands with hollow verbs: قُلْ · سِرْ · نَمْ
lessons.subtitle: قُلْ · زُرْ · دُرْ · سِرْ · بِعْ · نَمْ · كُنْ

explanations.title: Two steps
explanations.body: To make a command to one man from a hollow verb, take the present form and (1) drop the prefix يَـ, (2) delete the long vowel in the middle, (3) put the vowel of that long vowel on the first root letter: ُ for يَقُول, ِ for يَبِيع and َ for يَنَام. The last letter gets a sukūn.

explanations.title: Commands in use
explanations.body: When the next word starts with ال, a short kasra joins the two words: قُدِ السَّيَّارَة, نَمِ الْآن. To forbid, use لَا and the present with a sukūn: لَا تَقُلْ (“do not say”), لَا تَنَمْ.

examples.translation: qul lī ʾayna al-maḥaṭṭa. — Tell me where the station is.
dur ʾilā al-yamīn ʿinda al-ʾishāra. — Turn right at the light.
sir ʾilā nihāya ash-shāriʿ. — Go to the end of the street.
qudi as-sayyāra bibuṭʾ. — Drive the car slowly.
nami al-ʾān, fal-waqt mutaʾakhkhir. — Go to sleep now, it is late.
lā taqul dhālika liʾaḥad. — Do not say that to anyone.

exercises.prompt: Which is the command (to a man) from يَقُول?
exercises.explanation: Delete the middle, ُ on the first letter, sukūn at the end.

exercises.prompt: Which is the command from يَبِيع?
Which is the command from يَنَام?
Which is the command from يَدُور?
Why is it نَمِ الْآن, with a kasra?
options: to join the sukūn to ال

exercises.promptTranslation: Go to the end of the street. (to a man)
Tell me where the station is. (to a man)
Do not say that to anyone.

lessons.title: 210. Commands to a woman and to a group
lessons.subtitle: قُولِي · سِيرِي · نَامِي · قُولُوا · سِيرُوا · لَا تَقُولُوا

explanations.title: Women and groups
explanations.body: For a woman add ـِي to the command stem, and for a group of men add ـُوا. Because the ending is a long vowel, the middle vowel comes back and is long again: قُولِي, قُولُوا. Only the form for one man is short.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: The negative command also changes: لَا تَقُلْ (man), لَا تَقُولِي (woman), لَا تَقُولُوا (group).

examples.translation: kūnī hunāka fī al-khāmisa tamāman. — Be there at exactly five. (to a woman)
qūlī dhālika liʾabīki. — Tell that to your father. (to a woman)
bīʿī as-sayyāra al-qadīma. — Sell the old car. (to a woman)
sīrū khalfī. — Walk behind me. (to a group)
nāmū mubakkirīn. — Go to bed early. (to a group)
lā taqūlū dhālika. — Do not say that. (to a group)

exercises.prompt: Which is the command “Tell it!” to a woman?
Which is the command to a group from يَسِير?
Which is the command to a woman from يَنَام?
Which means “Sell the car” (to a woman)?
Which means “Do not say that” (to a group)?
In قُولِي, why does the vowel come back long?
options: the ending is a long vowel
exercises.explanation: Only the one-man form is short.

exercises.promptTranslation: Walk behind me.
Be there at five.
Do not say that to your father.

lessons.title: 211. Giving directions: go straight, turn, continue
lessons.subtitle: سِرْ مُسْتَقِيمًا · دُرْ إِلَى الْيَسَار · اِسْتَمِرّ حَتَّى النِّهَايَة

explanations.title: Words for finding the way
explanations.body: Directions are made of commands plus a few place words. The command for a man is also used when you speak to one person and do not know whether it is a man or a woman.

explanations.title: A set of directions
explanations.body: To say where something will be, use عَلَى يَمِينِكَ / عَلَى يَسَارِكَ (“on your right / left”), with the ending for “you”. To say what you will see, use سَتَجِد or سَتَرَى (“you will find”, “you will see”).

examples.text: اِسْتَمِرّ عَلَى هَذَا الطَّرِيق حَتَّى نِهَايَة الشَّارِع.
examples.translation: istamirr ʿalā hādhā aṭ-ṭarīq ḥattā nihāya ash-shāriʿ. — Continue on this road to the end of the street.
ʿinda al-muftaraq dur ʾilā al-yasār. — At the junction turn left.

examples.text: سِرْ مُسْتَقِيمًا ثُمَّ دُرْ إِلَى الْيَمِين.
examples.translation: sir mustaqīman thumma dur ʾilā al-yamīn. — Go straight and then turn right.
satarā lāfita kabīra qabla al-makhraj. — You will see a big sign before the exit.
satajid maḥaṭṭa banzīn ʿalā yasārika. — You will find a petrol station on your left.

examples.text: اِبْقَ عَلَى الْيَمِين وَتَوَقَّفْ عِنْدَ الْإِشَارَة.
examples.translation: ibqa ʿalā al-yamīn watawaqqaf ʿinda al-ʾishāra. — Stay on the right and stop at the light.

exercises.prompt: Which means “on your left” (to a man)?

exercises.promptTranslation: At the junction turn left. (to a man)
You will find a petrol station on your left.
Continue to the end of the street.

lessons.title: 212. A route, step by step
lessons.subtitle: أَوَّلًا · ثُمَّ · بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ · حَتَّى · مُبَاشَرَةً

explanations.title: Linking the steps
explanations.body: A route has an order. These small words put the steps in sequence. After حَتَّى (“until”) the verb is in the present with the same form you use after أَنْ.

explanations.title: At the hotel desk (an invented practice dialogue)
explanations.body: A visitor asks how to reach a fish restaurant. To ask for directions, use كَيْفَ أَصِل إِلَى … (“How do I get to…?”) or هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تُعْطِينِي بَعْض الْإِرْشَادَات؟

examples.translation: kayfa ʾaṣil ʾilā maṭʿam as-samak? — How do I get to the fish restaurant?

examples.text: أَوَّلًا غَادِرِ الْفُنْدُق وَسِرْ إِلَى الْيَمِين.
examples.translation: ʾawwalan ghādiri al-funduq wasir ʾilā al-yamīn. — First leave the hotel and go to the right.

examples.text: ثُمَّ اِسْتَمِرّ حَتَّى تَصِل إِلَى الْإِشَارَة.
examples.translation: thumma istamirr ḥattā taṣil ʾilā al-ʾishāra. — Then continue until you reach the traffic light.
baʿda dhālika dur ʾilā al-yasār. — After that turn left.

examples.text: الْمَطْعَم عَلَى يَمِينِكَ بَعْدَ مَحَطَّة الْبَنْزِين مُبَاشَرَةً.
examples.translation: al-maṭʿam ʿalā yamīnika baʿda maḥaṭṭa al-banzīn mubāsharatan. — The restaurant is on your right, right after the petrol station.
shukran jazīlan. — Thank you very much.

exercises.prompt: Which means “How do I get to the restaurant?”
What does مُبَاشَرَةً add in بَعْدَ مَحَطَّة الْبَنْزِين مُبَاشَرَةً?
Which is the command to a man, “leave the hotel”?

exercises.promptTranslation: First leave the hotel and go right.
Continue until you reach the traffic light.
The restaurant is on your right after the petrol station.

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Hollow verbs keep a long vowel in the present (يَقُول, يَبِيع, يَنَام) and drop it in short forms (قُلْتُ, يَقُلْنَ, قُلْ). A command to one man is short (قُلْ, سِرْ, نَمْ). To a woman it ends in ـِي (قُولِي) and to a group in ـُوا (قُولُوا).

explanations.title: A father’s advice (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: A father speaks to his son and daughter before a trip. Read the commands and notice who each one is for.

examples.text: يَا بُنَيَّ، قُدِ السَّيَّارَة بِحَذَر وَكُنْ مُنْتَبِهًا دَائِمًا.
examples.translation: yā bunayya, qudi as-sayyāra biḥadhar wakun muntabihan dāʾiman. — My son, drive the car carefully and always be alert.

examples.text: عِنْدَمَا تَصِل إِلَى الْمَدِينَة زُرْ عَمَّكَ.
examples.translation: ʿindamā taṣil ʾilā al-madīna zur ʿammaka. — When you reach the city, visit your uncle.

examples.text: وَأَنْتِ يَا بِنْتِي، كُونِي بِجَانِبِهِ وَقُولِي لَهُ لَا تُسْرِعْ.
examples.translation: waʾanti yā bintī, kūnī bijānibihi waqūlī lahu lā tusriʿ. — And you, my daughter, be beside him and tell him not to hurry.
sīrū fī an-nahār fahādhā ʾafḍal. — Travel in the daytime, that is better. (to both)
lā tanāmū fī as-sayyāra. — Do not sleep in the car. (to both)
waʾanā ʾanām murtāḥan ʾidhā waṣaltum. — And I will sleep easy if you arrive.

exercises.prompt: Which is a command to a woman?
Which is a command to a group?
Which means “Do not sleep in the car” (to a group)?

exercises.explanation: A form of address to a boy.

exercises.promptTranslation: My son, drive the car carefully.
And you, my daughter, be beside him.
Travel in the daytime, that is better.

lessons.title: 214. Review: a day out in a seaside city
lessons.subtitle: الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة مَدِينَة عَلَى الْبَحْر

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: This lesson brings together places and sights, transport, journey times and directions. Remember: أَفْعَل + مِنْ to compare, تَسْتَغْرِق + a time for how long, a command for directions, and حَتَّى + a present verb.

rows: The train is faster than the bus.
سِرْ مُسْتَقِيمًا ثُمَّ دُرْ إِلَى الْيَمِين
sir mustaqīman thumma dur ʾilā al-yamīn

explanations.title: A day in Alexandria (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: Alexandria (الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة) is a large port city in Egypt on the Mediterranean Sea. The story below is invented for practice.

examples.text: الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة مَدِينَة كَبِيرَة عَلَى الْبَحْر الْأَبْيَض الْمُتَوَسِّط فِي مِصْر.
examples.translation: al-ʾiskandariyya madīna kabīra ʿalā al-baḥr al-ʾabyaḍ al-mutawassiṭ fī miṣr. — Alexandria is a large city on the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt.

examples.text: تَسْتَغْرِق الرِّحْلَة بِالْقِطَار مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة نَحْوَ ثَلَاث سَاعَات.
examples.translation: tastaghriq ar-riḥla bil-qiṭār mina al-qāhira naḥwa thalāth sāʿāt. — The trip by train from Cairo takes about three hours.

examples.text: وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْمَحَطَّة وَأَخَذْنَا سَيَّارَة أُجْرَة إِلَى الْفُنْدُق.
examples.translation: waṣalnā ʾilā al-maḥaṭṭa waʾakhadhnā sayyāra ʾujra ʾilā al-funduq. — We arrived at the station and took a taxi to the hotel.

examples.text: قَالَ لَنَا مُوَظَّف الِاسْتِقْبَال سِيرُوا إِلَى نِهَايَة الشَّارِع ثُمَّ دُورُوا إِلَى الْيَمِين.
examples.translation: qāla lanā muwaẓẓaf al-istiqbāl sīrū ʾilā nihāya ash-shāriʿ thumma dūrū ʾilā al-yamīn. — The receptionist told us, “Walk to the end of the street, then turn right.”
raʾaynā lāfita kabīra qabla al-maṭʿam. — We saw a big sign before the restaurant.
kunnā jāʾiʿīn faʾakalnā as-samak aṭ-ṭāzaj. — We were hungry, so we ate fresh fish.

exercises.prompt: Where is Alexandria, according to the text?
options: on the Red Sea in Jordan
on the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt

exercises.prompt: Which means “The trip takes about three hours”?
Which means “We arrived at the station”?

options: Walk to the end of the street

exercises.prompt: Which means “We saw a big sign”?
قَالَ لَنَا الْمُوَظَّف ___ إِلَى نِهَايَة الشَّارِع.
exercises.promptTranslation: The employee told us, “Walk to the end of the street.”
The trip by train takes about three hours.
The train is faster than the bus.

units.title: الْجُغْرَافِيَا: terrain, climate, “still” and Measure V

lessons.title: 215. Landforms: mountains, valleys, lakes
lessons.subtitle: جَبَل · وَادِي · سَهْل · صَحْرَاء · بُحَيْرَة · غَابَة · سَاحِل

explanations.title: The shape of the land
explanations.body: Geography begins with the words for the land. The plural of جَبَل is جِبَال, and a line of mountains is a سِلْسِلَة جِبَال (an iḍāfa: “a chain of mountains”). The top of a mountain is a قِمَّة.

explanations.title: Describing a landscape
explanations.body: Use the nominal sentence and adjectives you know. A plural of things (not people) takes a feminine singular adjective: جِبَال عَالِيَة (“high mountains”).

examples.translation: fī al-gharb silsila jibāl ʿāliya. — In the west there is a high mountain range.
ʿalā qimma al-jabal thalj kathīr. — On the mountain top there is a lot of snow.
buḥayra kabīra fī wasaṭ al-ghāba. — A big lake is in the middle of the forest.
yamurr nahr ṭawīl fī as-sahl. — A long river runs through the plain.
ʿalā as-sāḥil shawāṭiʾ jamīla. — On the coast there are beautiful beaches.
aṣ-ṣaḥrāʾ wāsiʿa wajāffa. — The desert is wide and dry.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of جَبَل?
Which means “On the coast there are beautiful beaches”?
Why is it جِبَال عَالِيَة, with a feminine adjective?
options: plural things take a feminine singular adjective
exercises.explanation: A plural of things behaves like a feminine singular.

exercises.promptTranslation: The desert is wide and dry.

exercises.explanation: In the middle of the forest.
exercises.promptTranslation: A big lake is in the middle of the forest.

exercises.explanation: Range = iḍāfa, first noun without ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the west there is a high mountain range.

lessons.title: 216. Where is it? تَقَع · تَمْتَدّ · تَشْتَهِر
lessons.subtitle: تَقَع الْمَدِينَة عَلَى السَّاحِل · تَمْتَدّ الْجِبَال

explanations.title: Four verbs for a geography text
explanations.body: A text about a place uses a few verbs again and again. They are mostly in the “she” form, because the subject is usually a feminine noun (مَدِينَة, مِنْطَقَة, جَزِيرَة, سِلْسِلَة). For a masculine subject, use يَـ.

explanations.title: A paragraph about a place
explanations.body: These are invented sentences for practice. Read them aloud and notice the preposition after each verb.

examples.translation: taqaʿ al-madīna ʿalā sāḥil al-baḥr. — The city is located on the sea coast.

examples.text: تَمْتَدّ الْجِبَال مِنَ الشَّمَال إِلَى الْجَنُوب.
examples.translation: tamtadd al-jibāl mina ash-shamāl ʾilā al-janūb. — The mountains extend from north to south.
tashtahir al-minṭaqa bil-buḥayrāt. — The region is famous for its lakes.
yaḥudd al-baḥr al-balad mina al-gharb. — The sea borders the country on the west.
yaqaʿ al-matḥaf qarīban mina an-nahr. — The museum is located near the river.
tatamayyaz al-jazīra bish-shawāṭiʾ al-jamīla. — The island is distinguished by its beautiful beaches.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The mountains extend from north to south”?
options: تَمْتَدّ الْجِبَال مِنَ الشَّمَال إِلَى الْجَنُوب
تَمْتَدّ الْجِبَال مِنَ الْجَنُوب إِلَى الشَّمَال
تَقَع الْجِبَال مِنَ الشَّمَال إِلَى الْجَنُوب

exercises.prompt: Why تَقَع and not يَقَع in تَقَع الْمَدِينَة?
exercises.explanation: A feminine subject takes the تَـ form.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The sea borders the country on the west”?

exercises.promptTranslation: The city is located on the sea coast.
The region is famous for its lakes.
The museum is located near the river.

explanations.title: The four directions
explanations.body: Each direction has a noun and an adjective (ending in ـِيّ, like the nationality words). Use the noun after فِي or مِنْ and the adjective after a noun: فِي شَمَال الْبَلَد (“in the north of the country”), السَّاحِل الشَّرْقِيّ (“the eastern coast”).

explanations.title: On the map
explanations.body: To say a place lies in a direction from another, use فِي شَمَال / جَنُوب / شَرْق / غَرْب + the place. For a compass, the word is بَوْصَلَة.

examples.translation: taqaʿ al-madīna fī shamāl al-balad. — The city is in the north of the country.

examples.text: الْجِبَال فِي الْغَرْب وَالْبَحْر فِي الشَّرْق.
examples.translation: al-jibāl fī al-gharb wal-baḥr fī ash-sharq. — The mountains are in the west and the sea is in the east.
taqaʿ al-madīna ʿalā as-sāḥil al-gharbiyy. — The city is on the western coast.

examples.text: الشَّمْس تَطْلُع مِنَ الشَّرْق وَتَغْرُب فِي الْغَرْب.
examples.translation: ash-shams taṭluʿ mina ash-sharq wataghrub fī al-gharb. — The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
nastakhdim al-bawṣala limaʿrifa al-ittijāh. — We use the compass to know the direction.

examples.text: الْمَدِينَة الْجَنُوبِيَّة أَكْبَر مِنَ الْمَدِينَة الشَّمَالِيَّة.
examples.translation: al-madīna al-janūbiyya ʾakbar mina al-madīna ash-shamāliyya. — The southern city is bigger than the northern city.

exercises.explanation: The sun rises in the east.

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine of شَمَالِيّ?

exercises.explanation: An iḍāfa: no ال on the first noun.
exercises.promptTranslation: The city is in the north of the country.
The southern city is bigger than the northern city.
The sun rises in the east.

lessons.title: 218. Climate and the seasons
lessons.subtitle: حَارّ · بَارِد · مُعْتَدِل · جَاف · رَطْب · مُمْطِر

explanations.title: Words for the weather
explanations.body: مُنَاخ is the climate of a place and طَقْس is the weather of a day. Most weather words are adjectives. The names of the four seasons are nouns.

explanations.title: Talking about the climate
explanations.body: The climate and the weather are masculine, so their adjectives are masculine. Rain and snow are said with يَسْقُط (“falls”): يَسْقُط الثَّلْج, يَسْقُط الْمَطَر.

examples.translation: munākh al-minṭaqa muʿtadil. — The climate of the region is mild.
aṣ-ṣayf ḥārr wajāf fī aṣ-ṣaḥrāʾ. — The summer is hot and dry in the desert.

examples.text: فِي الشِّتَاء يَسْقُط الثَّلْج عَلَى الْجِبَال.
examples.translation: fī ash-shitāʾ yasquṭ ath-thalj ʿalā al-jibāl. — In winter snow falls on the mountains.
aṭ-ṭaqs al-yawm dāfiʾ wamumṭir. — The weather today is warm and rainy.
al-munākh fī al-jazīra istiwāʾiyy waraṭb. — The climate on the island is tropical and humid.
ar-rabīʿ jamīl fī al-ghāba. — Spring is beautiful in the forest.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The climate of the region is mild”?

exercises.promptTranslation: The summer is hot and dry in the desert.
In winter snow falls on the mountains.
The weather today is warm and rainy.

lessons.title: 219. A weather report
lessons.subtitle: الطَّقْس غَدًا · دَرَجَة الْحَرَارَة · الرِّيَاح قَوِيَّة

explanations.title: Comparing weather
explanations.body: Weather reports compare days and regions. Use the patterns you know: أَفْعَل + مِنْ. Warm: دَافِئ → أَدْفَأ; cold: بَارِد → أَبْرَد; hot: حَارّ → أَحَرّ (two identical letters join). Two comparatives come from other words: أَعْلَى (higher) and أَقَلّ (lower, less).

explanations.title: An invented weather report
explanations.body: Read this short report. The place names are left out so you can apply it to any country.

examples.text: الطَّقْس الْيَوْم فِي الشَّمَال بَارِد وَمُمْطِر.
examples.translation: aṭ-ṭaqs al-yawm fī ash-shamāl bārid wamumṭir. — The weather today in the north is cold and rainy.

examples.text: فِي الْجَنُوب الْجَوّ أَدْفَأ مِنْهُ فِي الشَّمَال.
examples.translation: fī al-janūb al-jaww ʾadfaʾ minhu fī ash-shamāl. — In the south the weather is warmer than in the north.

examples.text: فِي الشَّرْق رِيَاح قَوِيَّة عَلَى السَّاحِل.
examples.translation: fī ash-sharq riyāḥ qawiyya ʿalā as-sāḥil. — In the east there are strong winds on the coast.
daraja al-ḥarāra munkhafiḍa fī al-jibāl. — The temperature is low in the mountains.
yakhtalif al-munākh ḥasab al-minṭaqa. — The climate differs according to the region.
ghadan sayakūn aṭ-ṭaqs ʾaḥsan. — Tomorrow the weather will be better.

exercises.prompt: Which is the comparative of بَارِد?
Which is the comparative of حَارّ?
Which is the comparative of دَافِئ?
Which means “Tomorrow the weather will be better”?
What does يَخْتَلِف الْمُنَاخ حَسَب الْمِنْطَقَة mean?
options: the climate is the same everywhere

exercises.prompt: فِي الْجَنُوب الْجَوّ ___ مِنْهُ فِي الشَّمَال.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the south the weather is warmer than in the north.
In the east there are strong winds on the coast.
Tomorrow the weather will be better.

lessons.title: 220. Time zones
lessons.subtitle: مِنْطَقَة زَمَنِيَّة · فَرْق التَّوْقِيت · هُنَا الْعَاشِرَة وَعِنْدَكُمُ السَّابِعَة

explanations.title: When it is ten here…
explanations.body: A large country has more than one time zone (مِنْطَقَة زَمَنِيَّة). The difference between two zones is the فَرْق التَّوْقِيت. To compare clocks, use عِنْدَ with an ending: عِنْدَنَا (“at our place”), عِنْدَكُمْ (“at your place”).

explanations.title: Comparing the clocks
explanations.body: These sentences are invented for practice. Practise them with other numbers.

examples.text: الْبِلَاد الْكَبِيرَة فِيهَا أَكْثَر مِنْ مِنْطَقَة زَمَنِيَّة.
examples.translation: al-bilād al-kabīra fīhā ʾakthar min minṭaqa zamaniyya. — Large countries have more than one time zone.

examples.text: فَرْق التَّوْقِيت بَيْنَ الْمَدِينَتَيْن ثَلَاث سَاعَات.
examples.translation: farq at-tawqīt bayna al-madīnatayn thalāth sāʿāt. — The time difference between the two cities is three hours.
hunā al-ʿāshira waʿindakumu as-sābiʿa. — Here it is ten and at your place it is seven.
tatbaʿ al-madīna tawqīt as-sāḥil al-gharbiyy. — The city follows the time of the western coast.

examples.text: لِذَلِكَ أَتَّصِل بِكَ فِي التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً.
examples.translation: lidhālika ʾattaṣil bika fī at-tāsiʿa masāʾan. — That is why I call you at nine in the evening.
lā tansa farq at-tawqīt. — Do not forget the time difference.

options: at our place it is seven
at your place it is seven

exercises.prompt: Which means “Do not forget the time difference”?
Which means “Here it is ten and at your place it is seven”?
Which means “three hours” (the noun is feminine)?

exercises.promptTranslation: The time difference between the two cities is three hours.
Here it is ten and at your place it is seven.
That is why I call you at nine in the evening.

lessons.title: 221. A phone call across the time zones
lessons.subtitle: هَلِ اِتَّصَلْتَ بِصَدِيقِنَا؟ · نَسِيتُ فَرْق التَّوْقِيت

explanations.title: Calling a friend
explanations.body: Calling someone is اِتَّصَلَ بِـ (past) and يَتَّصِل بِـ (present). The person you call comes after بِـ with an ending: بِهِ (him), بِكَ (you). Read the conversation below. It is invented for practice.

examples.translation: hali ittaṣalta biṣadīqinā khālid? — Did you call our friend Khalid?

examples.text: لَا، سَأَتَّصِل بِهِ فِي التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً.
examples.translation: lā, saʾattaṣil bihi fī at-tāsiʿa masāʾan. — No, I will call him at nine in the evening.
lākinna al-waqt al-ʾān al-ʿāshira hunāka. — But the time there is now ten.
ʾāh, nasītu farq at-tawqīt. — Ah, I forgot the time difference.

examples.text: إِذَنْ اِتَّصِلْ بِهِ غَدًا فِي الصَّبَاح.
examples.translation: ʾidhan ittaṣil bihi ghadan fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — Then call him tomorrow morning.
ḥasanan, shukran ʿalā at-tadhkīr. — Fine, thanks for the reminder.

exercises.prompt: Which means “Did you call our friend?” (to a man)
Which means “Call him tomorrow morning”? (to a man)
Why does the speaker decide to call tomorrow morning instead?
Which means “But the time there is now ten”?

exercises.promptTranslation: Did you call our friend Khalid?
Ah, I forgot the time difference.
Then call him tomorrow morning.

explanations.title: A TV vocabulary
explanations.body: A television channel is a قَنَاة. A programme is a بَرْنَامَج (plural بَرَامِج), and a list of programmes is a جَدْوَل. To say that something is shown, use يُعْرَض, the passive of عَرَضَ (“to show”).

explanations.title: Reading a programme guide
explanations.body: These are invented entries. Notice يَبْدَأ (begins) and يَنْتَهِي (ends), with مِنَ السَّاعَة … إِلَى السَّاعَة … for times.

examples.translation: yuʿraḍ al-barnāmaj al-wathāʾiqiyy yawm al-ʾaḥad. — The documentary programme is shown on Sunday.

examples.text: نَشْرَة الْأَخْبَار عَلَى هَذِهِ الْقَنَاة فِي السَّابِعَة مَسَاءً.
examples.translation: nashra al-ʾakhbār ʿalā hādhihi al-qanāh fī as-sābiʿa masāʾan. — The news bulletin is on this channel at seven in the evening.

examples.text: يَبْدَأ الْمُسَلْسَل فِي الثَّامِنَة وَيَنْتَهِي فِي التَّاسِعَة.
examples.translation: yabdaʾ al-musalsal fī ath-thāmina wayantahī fī at-tāsiʿa. — The series begins at eight and ends at nine.
hunāka barnāmaj ʿani al-jibāl wal-ʾanhār. — There is a programme about mountains and rivers.
nuḥibb mushāhada al-ʾaflām al-wathāʾiqiyya. — We like watching documentary films.
jadwal al-barāmij ʿalā mawqiʿ al-qanāh. — The programme schedule is on the channel’s website.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of بَرْنَامَج?
Which means “The series begins at eight and ends at nine”?
options: يَبْدَأ الْمُسَلْسَل فِي التَّاسِعَة وَيَنْتَهِي فِي الثَّامِنَة
يَبْدَأ الْمُسَلْسَل فِي الثَّامِنَة وَيَنْتَهِي فِي التَّاسِعَة

exercises.prompt: Which preposition means “about” in بَرْنَامَج عَنِ الْجِبَال?

exercises.promptTranslation: The documentary programme is shown on Sunday.

exercises.prompt: نَشْرَة ___ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْقَنَاة فِي السَّابِعَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The news bulletin is on this channel at seven.
The series begins at eight.

lessons.title: 223. Choosing a programme from a schedule
lessons.subtitle: مِنَ السَّاعَة الرَّابِعَة إِلَى الْخَامِسَة · بَعْدَ الدِّرَاسَة

explanations.title: A schedule (invented)
explanations.body: Here is an invented schedule. Read each line and decide when you can watch. School ends at half past three.

explanations.title: Choosing
explanations.body: To say what fits your day, use يُنَاسِبُنِي (“it suits me”) and بَعْدَ الدِّرَاسَة (“after school”).

examples.translation: ad-dirāsa tantahī fī ath-thālitha wan-niṣf. — School ends at half past three.

examples.text: بَرْنَامَج الْجِبَال يُنَاسِبُنِي لِأَنَّهُ بَعْدَ الدِّرَاسَة.
examples.translation: barnāmaj al-jibāl yunāsibunī liʾannahu baʿda ad-dirāsa. — The mountains programme suits me because it is after school.

examples.text: فِيلْم الصَّحْرَاء لَا يُنَاسِبُنِي لِأَنَّهُ قَبْلَ نِهَايَة الدِّرَاسَة.
examples.translation: fīlm aṣ-ṣaḥrāʾ lā yunāsibunī liʾannahu qabla nihāya ad-dirāsa. — The desert film does not suit me because it is before the end of school.
saʾushāhid al-barnāmaj yawm al-ʾaḥad. — I will watch the programme on Sunday.
wayawm al-ʾarbiʿāʾ ʾushāhid al-musalsal. — And on Wednesday I watch the series.
ʾayy qanāh taʿriḍ al-ʾakhbār? — Which channel shows the news?

exercises.prompt: According to the schedule, which programme is on Sunday?

options: on Monday at seven in the evening

exercises.prompt: School ends at half past three. Which programme is too early?
options: the desert documentary on Tuesday (three to four)
exercises.explanation: It starts at three, before school ends.

exercises.prompt: Which means “Which channel shows the news?”

exercises.promptTranslation: The mountains programme suits me because it is after school.

exercises.explanation: On Sunday = يَوْم الْأَحَد, with no preposition.
exercises.promptTranslation: I will watch the programme on Sunday.
School ends at half past three.

lessons.title: 224. Still: مَا زَالَ
lessons.subtitle: مَا زِلْتُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَة · مَا زَالَتْ سَارَة هُنَاكَ

explanations.title: How to say “still”
explanations.body: Arabic says “still” with the verb زَالَ and the word مَا before it: مَا زَالَ. The word مَا makes it negative in form, but the meaning is positive: مَا زِلْتُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَة means “I am still in the library”. The verb is conjugated like a hollow verb: the long ā becomes short before the endings ـتُ, ـتَ, ـنَا and ـنَ. The short vowel is a kasra (زِلْتُ), where قَالَ has a ḍamma (قُلْتُ).

explanations.title: With a place
explanations.body: The simplest use is with a place or time. Put the place after the verb. To ask “Are you still…?”, put هَلْ before مَا زِلْتَ.

examples.translation: mā ziltu fī al-maktaba. — I am still in the library.
hal mā zilta hunā? — Are you still here? (to a man)
mā zālat sāra fī al-jāmiʿa. — Sara is still at the university.
mā zilnā fī aṭ-ṭarīq. — We are still on the way.
aṭ-ṭullāb mā zālū fī aṣ-ṣaff. — The students are still in the classroom.
mā zāla ʾakhī fī al-funduq. — My brother is still in the hotel.

exercises.prompt: What does مَا زِلْتُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَة mean?
options: I am not in the library
I was not in the library
I am still in the library

exercises.prompt: Which means “Sara is still at the university”?
To which verb is زَالَ conjugated like?
exercises.explanation: The ā shortens before ـتُ, ـنَا.

exercises.promptTranslation: Sara is still at the university.
The students are still in the classroom.
We are still on the way.

lessons.title: 225. Still, with a noun or an adjective after it
lessons.subtitle: مَا زَالَ الطَّقْس بَارِدًا · مَا زَالَتْ مَسْرُورَةً

explanations.title: The second part goes into the accusative
explanations.body: A nominal sentence has a subject and a predicate: الطَّقْس بَارِد. After مَا زَالَ the subject stays as it is, but the predicate changes into the accusative case. For one man it adds ـًا; for one woman ـَةً; for two ـَيْنِ; for several men ـِينَ.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Remember that a helping kasra joins مَا زَالَتْ to ال: مَا زَالَتِ الْمُدَرِّسَة. The subject after مَا زَالَ keeps its normal nominative form (for example the dual الْوَلَدَانِ); only the predicate changes.

examples.translation: mā zāla aṭ-ṭaqs bāridan. — The weather is still cold.
mā zālati al-mudarrisa masrūratan. — The teacher is still happy.
mā zāla al-waladāni mujtahidayni. — The two boys are still hard-working.
mā zāla aṭ-ṭullāb mujtahidīna. — The students are still hard-working.
hal mā zālati al-maktaba maftūḥatan? — Is the library still open?
mā ziltu mutʿaban baʿda ar-riḥla. — I am still tired after the trip.

exercises.prompt: What case is the predicate in after مَا زَالَ?
exercises.explanation: The predicate takes an accusative ending.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The weather is still cold”?
exercises.explanation: The predicate takes an accusative ending.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The teacher (f.) is still happy”?
Which ending shows the accusative of a dual predicate?
Which ending shows the accusative of a sound masculine plural predicate?
Why is it مَا زَالَتِ with a kasra in مَا زَالَتِ الْمُدَرِّسَة?
options: to join the sukūn to ال

exercises.promptTranslation: The students are still hard-working.
The teacher is still happy.

exercises.explanation: One man or thing, masculine, accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: The weather is still cold.

lessons.title: 226. Still doing something: مَا زِلْتُ أَدْرُس
lessons.subtitle: مَا زِلْتُ أَدْرُس · لَا يَزَال يَعِيش هُنَا · مَا زِلْنَا نُفَكِّر

explanations.title: A verb after مَا زَالَ
explanations.body: To say “still doing”, put the present verb after مَا زَالَ. Both verbs agree with the person: مَا زِلْتُ أَدْرُس (“I am still studying”), مَا زَالُوا يَدْرُسُون. The present-tense twin of مَا زَالَ is لَا يَزَال (“he is still”), which means the same.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: With لَا يَزَال, the predicate is accusative too: لَا تَزَال الْمَكْتَبَة مَفْتُوحَةً.

examples.translation: mā ziltu ʾadrus al-ʿarabiyya. — I am still studying Arabic.

examples.text: مَا زَالَ أَخِي يَعِيش فِي الْمَدِينَة.
examples.translation: mā zāla ʾakhī yaʿīsh fī al-madīna. — My brother still lives in the city.
lā tazāl al-maktaba maftūḥatan. — The library is still open.
lā yazālūn yantaẓirūn al-ḥāfila. — They are still waiting for the bus.
hal mā zilti tataʿallamīn as-sibāḥa? — Are you still learning to swim? (to a woman)
mā zilnā nufakkir fī ar-riḥla. — We are still thinking about the trip.

exercises.prompt: Which means “he is still” (the present twin)?
Which means “We are still thinking about the trip”?
Which means “They are still waiting for the bus”?
Which means “Are you still learning?” (to a woman)
What case is the predicate in لَا تَزَال الْمَكْتَبَة مَفْتُوحَةً?

exercises.promptTranslation: My brother still lives in the city.
The library is still open.
We are still thinking about the trip.

lessons.title: 227. Measure V in the past: تَعَلَّمَ · تَخَرَّجَ · تَوَقَّفَ
lessons.subtitle: تَعَلَّمْتُ · تَخَرَّجَ أَخِي · تَوَقَّفَتِ الْحَافِلَة

explanations.title: Measure II + تَـ = Measure V
explanations.body: You know Measure V from Unit 10. To make it, put تَـ in front of a Measure II verb: عَلَّمَ (he taught) → تَعَلَّمَ (he learned). Measure V often says that the action is carried out by the subject itself, or that a result is reached. In the past, the doubled middle letter keeps a fatḥa: تَفَعَّلَ.

explanations.title: The past tense of Measure V
explanations.body: The endings are the same as for every past tense. Practise them with تَعَلَّمَ.

examples.translation: taʿallama aṭ-ṭullāb kathīran fī al-madrasa. — The students learned a lot at school.
takharraja ʾakhī mina al-jāmiʿa. — My brother graduated from the university.
tadarraba al-walad ʿalā qiyāda ad-darrāja. — The boy practised riding the bicycle.
tawaqqafati al-ḥāfila ʾamāma al-maḥaṭṭa. — The bus stopped in front of the station.
taʾakhkhara al-qiṭār niṣf sāʿa. — The train was half an hour late.
taghayyara aṭ-ṭaqs fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The weather changed in the morning.

exercises.prompt: Which is Measure V of عَلَّمَ?
Which means “The train was half an hour late”?

exercises.explanation: The subject comes first, so the verb agrees: they (men).
exercises.promptTranslation: The students learned a lot at school.
I learned a lot from my teacher.
She graduated from the university.

lessons.title: 228. Measure V verbal nouns: التَّعَلُّم · التَّوَقُّف
lessons.subtitle: تَعَلَّمَ ← تَعَلُّم · تَخَرَّجَ ← تَخَرُّج · تَوَقَّفَ ← تَوَقُّف

explanations.title: From the verb to the noun
explanations.body: A verbal noun (masdar) names the action: “learning”, “stopping”. For Measure V, take the past verb and change the fatḥa on the doubled letter into a ḍamma, then drop the last fatḥa: تَعَلَّمَ → تَعَلُّم. The result has the pattern تَفَعُّل. As with other verbal nouns, ال is added when you mean “the learning”.

explanations.title: Verbal nouns in use
explanations.body: Verbal nouns often follow another noun in an iḍāfa (حَفْلَة التَّخَرُّج, “the graduation ceremony”) or follow مَمْنُوع on a sign.

examples.translation: mamnūʿ at-tawaqquf ʿalā aṭ-ṭarīq as-sarīʿ. — Stopping on the highway is forbidden.
sayaḥḍur al-mudīr ḥafla at-takharruj. — The director will attend the graduation ceremony.

examples.text: يَبْدَأ التَّدَرُّب الصَّبَاحِيّ فِي الْخَامِسَة وَالنِّصْف.
examples.translation: yabdaʾ at-tadarrub aṣ-ṣabāḥiyy fī al-khāmisa wan-niṣf. — The morning training begins at half past five.
iʿtadhara ʿani at-taʾakhkhur. — He apologised for the delay.
at-taghayyur fī aṭ-ṭaqs sarīʿ. — The change in the weather is fast.
at-taʿallum muhimm likull ṭālib. — Learning is important for every student.

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of تَعَلَّمَ?
exercises.explanation: تَفَعُّل: ḍamma on the doubled letter.

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of تَوَقَّفَ?
What is the verbal noun of تَخَرَّجَ?
How does the pattern تَفَعُّل differ from the verb تَفَعَّلَ?
options: the doubled letter has a ḍamma

exercises.promptTranslation: Stopping on the highway is forbidden.
The director will attend the graduation ceremony.
He apologised for the delay.

lessons.title: 229. A country profile
lessons.subtitle: تَقَع مِصْر فِي شَمَال إِفْرِيقِيَا وَعَاصِمَتُهَا الْقَاهِرَة

explanations.title: The parts of a profile
