explanations.body: An area study follows a fixed order: where the country is, its capital, its neighbours and seas, and its language. These words build the profile. Use the verbs from this unit (تَقَع, يَحُدّ, تَشْتَهِر) and an ending for “its”: ـهَا for a feminine country, ـهُ for a masculine one.

explanations.title: Three short profiles (simple facts)
explanations.body: These sentences state well-known facts in short form. Read them aloud, then write a profile for another country.

examples.text: تَقَع مِصْر فِي شَمَال إِفْرِيقِيَا وَعَاصِمَتُهَا الْقَاهِرَة.
examples.translation: taqaʿ miṣr fī shamāl ʾifrīqiyā waʿāṣimatuhā al-qāhira. — Egypt is in the north of Africa and its capital is Cairo.

examples.text: يَمُرّ نَهْر النِّيل فِي مِصْر وَالسُّودَان.
examples.translation: yamurr nahr an-nīl fī miṣr was-sūdān. — The Nile flows through Egypt and Sudan.

examples.text: اللُّغَة الرَّسْمِيَّة فِي مِصْر هِيَ اللُّغَة الْعَرَبِيَّة.
examples.translation: al-lugha ar-rasmiyya fī miṣr hiya al-lugha al-ʿarabiyya. — The official language in Egypt is Arabic.

examples.text: يَقَع الْأُرْدُنّ فِي غَرْب آسِيَا وَعَاصِمَتُهُ عَمَّان.
examples.translation: yaqaʿ al-ʾurdunn fī gharb ʾāsiyā waʿāṣimatuhu ʿammān. — Jordan is in west Asia and its capital is Amman.

examples.text: يَحُدّ الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر السُّعُودِيَّة مِنَ الْغَرْب.
examples.translation: yaḥudd al-baḥr al-ʾaḥmar as-suʿūdiyya mina al-gharb. — The Red Sea borders Saudi Arabia on the west.
ʿāṣima as-sūdān hiya al-khurṭūm. — The capital of Sudan is Khartoum.

exercises.prompt: Which is the capital of Egypt, according to the lesson?
Which country has the capital عَمَّان?
exercises.explanation: Amman is the capital of Jordan.
A noun and an adjective with ال.

exercises.prompt: Which means “The Nile flows through Egypt and Sudan”?
options: يَمُرّ نَهْر النِّيل فِي مِصْر وَالسُّودَان
يَقَع نَهْر النِّيل فِي الْأُرْدُنّ وَالسُّودَان

exercises.prompt: Why عَاصِمَتُهُ for Jordan and عَاصِمَتُهَا for Egypt?
options: الْأُرْدُنّ is masculine, مِصْر is feminine

exercises.promptTranslation: Egypt is in the north of Africa.

exercises.prompt: يَقَع الْأُرْدُنّ فِي غَرْب آسِيَا وَ___ عَمَّان.
exercises.promptTranslation: Jordan is in west Asia and its capital is Amman.

exercises.explanation: The sea in the west of Saudi Arabia.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Red Sea borders Saudi Arabia on the west.

lessons.title: 230. Review: still, Measure V, climate and place
lessons.subtitle: مَا زِلْتُ أَدْرُس · تَخَرَّجْتُ · مَا زَالَ الطَّقْس بَارِدًا

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: مَا زَالَ (“still”) is conjugated like a hollow past verb and puts its predicate into the accusative: مَا زَالَ الطَّقْس بَارِدًا. Before a verb: مَا زِلْتُ أَدْرُس. Measure V = تَـ + Measure II; the past is تَفَعَّلَ and the verbal noun is تَفَعُّل.

explanations.title: A letter from a student (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: A student writes to a friend about school, the weather and a trip. Read the sentences and find every use of “still” and every Measure V verb.

examples.translation: takharrajtu mina al-madrasa wataʿallamtu kathīran. — I graduated from school and I learned a lot.
mā ziltu ʾadrus fī al-jāmiʿa. — I am still studying at the university.

examples.text: تَغَيَّرَ الْمُنَاخ فِي الشَّمَال وَلَا يَزَال الْجَوّ مُمْطِرًا.
examples.translation: taghayyara al-munākh fī ash-shamāl walā yazāl al-jaww mumṭiran. — The climate in the north changed and the weather is still rainy.

examples.text: مَا زَالَ الطَّقْس بَارِدًا فِي الشِّتَاء.
examples.translation: mā zāla aṭ-ṭaqs bāridan fī ash-shitāʾ. — The weather is still cold in winter.

examples.text: تَوَقَّفَتِ الْحَافِلَة وَمَا زِلْنَا فِي الطَّرِيق.
examples.translation: tawaqqafati al-ḥāfila wamā zilnā fī aṭ-ṭarīq. — The bus stopped and we are still on the way.
mamnūʿ at-taʾakhkhur ʿani al-mawʿid. — Being late for the appointment is not allowed.

exercises.prompt: Which means “I am still studying at the university”?
Which means “The weather is still cold in winter”?
options: مَا زَالَ الطَّقْس بَارِدٌ فِي الشِّتَاء
مَا زَالَ الطَّقْس بَارِدًا فِي الشِّتَاء

exercises.prompt: Which is the Measure V verb in the lesson text for “I graduated”?
What is the verbal noun of تَأَخَّرَ?
Which means “still” in the present twin form (he)?
تَغَيَّرَ الْمُنَاخ فِي الشَّمَال وَلَا ___ الْجَوّ مُمْطِرًا.
exercises.promptTranslation: The climate in the north changed and the weather is still rainy.
Being late for the appointment is not allowed.
The bus stopped and we are still on the way.

units.title: الْعَرَب فِي أَمْرِيكَا: communities, media and verbal nouns

lessons.title: 231. Arab communities in big cities
lessons.subtitle: تَعِيش جَالِيَة عَرَبِيَّة فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَة

explanations.title: Words for communities
explanations.body: People who move to another country to live there are مُهَاجِرُون (immigrants). The move itself is هِجْرَة. A group of people from one country who live together abroad is a جَالِيَة (community). A state inside a country such as the United States is a وِلَايَة, and a neighbourhood is a حَيّ.

explanations.title: Talking about where people live
explanations.body: The verb عَاشَ means “to live”. Its present is يَعِيش (he lives), أَعِيش (I live), تَعِيش (she lives or you live). Use مِنْ to say where a family comes from and فِي to say where it lives.

examples.text: يَعِيش كَثِير مِنَ الْعَرَب فِي الْمُدُن الْكَبِيرَة.
examples.translation: yaʿīsh kathīr mina al-ʿarab fī al-mudun al-kabīra. — Many Arabs live in big cities.

examples.text: فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَة حَيّ عَرَبِيّ قَدِيم.
examples.translation: fī hādhihi al-madīna ḥayy ʿarabiyy qadīm. — In this city there is an old Arab neighbourhood.

examples.text: أَصْل عَائِلَتِي مِنْ لُبْنَان وَأَنَا أَعِيش هُنَا.
examples.translation: ʾaṣl ʿāʾilatī min lubnān waʾanā ʾaʿīsh hunā. — My family’s origin is Lebanon, and I live here.
waṣala al-muhājirūn al-judud fī aṣ-ṣayf. — The new immigrants arrived in the summer.

examples.text: تَعِيش الْجَالِيَة الْعَرَبِيَّة فِي هَذِهِ الْوِلَايَة مُنْذُ سَنَوَات.
examples.translation: taʿīsh al-jāliya al-ʿarabiyya fī hādhihi al-wilāya mundhu sanawāt. — The Arab community has lived in this state for years.
al-hijra qarār kabīr. — Emigrating is a big decision.

exercises.explanation: A group from one country living together abroad.
Someone who moves to live in another country.

exercises.prompt: What does يَعِيش كَثِير مِنَ الْعَرَب فِي الْمُدُن الْكَبِيرَة mean?
options: Few Arabs live in big cities
Many Arabs live in big cities

exercises.explanation: I live: the prefix is أ.
exercises.promptTranslation: I live in a big city.

exercises.explanation: A plural noun to go with the plural adjective الْجُدُد.
exercises.promptTranslation: The new immigrants arrived in the summer.

exercises.explanation: A neighbourhood is part of a city.
exercises.promptTranslation: In this city there is an old Arab neighbourhood.

lessons.title: 232. Most, many, some: أَغْلَب · كَثِير · بَعْض
lessons.subtitle: أَغْلَب الطُّلَّاب · كَثِير مِنَ النَّاس · بَعْض الْجِيرَان

explanations.title: Words for “how many”
explanations.body: These words come before a definite plural noun. أَغْلَب (most), مُعْظَم (most), بَعْض (some), جَمِيع and كُلّ (all) are joined to the noun like an iḍāfa: the noun after them has ال. The words كَثِير (many) and قَلِيل (few) usually take مِنْ: كَثِير مِنَ الطُّلَّاب.

explanations.title: Majority and minority
explanations.body: The majority is أَغْلَبِيَّة and a minority is أَقَلِّيَّة. After words like أَغْلَب and كَثِير, a verb about people is usually plural: يَدْرُسُون.

examples.text: أَغْلَب الطُّلَّاب فِي صَفِّي يَدْرُسُون الْعَرَبِيَّة.
examples.translation: ʾaghlab aṭ-ṭullāb fī ṣaffī yadrusūn al-ʿarabiyya. — Most of the students in my class study Arabic.

examples.text: بَعْض الْجِيرَان عَرَب وَبَعْضُهُم مِنْ بُلْدَان أُخْرَى.
examples.translation: baʿḍ al-jīrān ʿarab wabaʿḍuhum min buldān ʾukhrā. — Some of the neighbours are Arabs and some are from other countries.
kathīr mina al-ʾaṭfāl yatakallamūn lughatayn. — Many of the children speak two languages.
al-ʾaghlabiyya tuḥibb hādhā al-maṭʿam. — The majority like this restaurant.
hādhihi ʾaqalliyya ṣaghīra fī al-madīna. — This is a small minority in the city.

examples.text: قَلِيل مِنَ النَّاس يَعْرِفُون هَذَا الْحَيّ.
examples.translation: qalīl mina an-nās yaʿrifūn hādhā al-ḥayy. — Few people know this neighbourhood.

exercises.prompt: What does قَلِيل مِنَ النَّاس mean?

exercises.explanation: “Many of” takes مِنَ; أَغْلَب and مُعْظَم do not.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many of the children speak two languages.

exercises.explanation: No مِنْ after أَغْلَب: the noun follows it directly.
exercises.promptTranslation: Most of the students in my class study Arabic.

exercises.prompt: ___ الْجِيرَان عَرَب وَبَعْضُهُم مِنْ بُلْدَان أُخْرَى.
exercises.promptTranslation: Some of the neighbours are Arabs and some are from other countries.

explanations.title: Papers and permission
explanations.body: Four words are useful for life abroad: جِنْسِيَّة (nationality or citizenship), إِقَامَة (residence), وَثِيقَة (a document; plural وَثَائِق) and جَوَاز سَفَر (passport). A permanent residence permit is إِقَامَة دَائِمَة. An embassy is سِفَارَة.

explanations.title: Getting something
explanations.body: To say “got” or “obtained”, use حَصَلَ عَلَى. Its past tense is regular: حَصَلْتُ (I got), حَصَلَ (he got), حَصَلَتْ (she got).

examples.translation: jinsiyyatī miṣriyya. — My nationality is Egyptian.
ḥaṣala ʾakhī ʿalā al-jinsiyya al-jadīda. — My brother obtained the new citizenship.

examples.text: عِنْدِي إِقَامَة دَائِمَة فِي هَذَا الْبَلَد.
examples.translation: ʿindī ʾiqāma dāʾima fī hādhā al-balad. — I have permanent residence in this country.
hal ḥaṣalti ʿalā al-ʾiqāma? — Did you get the residence permit? (to a woman)
taṭlub as-sifāra wathāʾiq kathīra. — The embassy asks for many documents.
ʾayna jawāz safarī? — Where is my passport?

exercises.prompt: What does حَصَلَ أَخِي عَلَى الْجِنْسِيَّة mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I got the residence permit.
She obtained the citizenship.
The embassy asks for many documents.

lessons.title: 234. Work in the community: shops and free business
lessons.subtitle: أَبِي صَاحِب مَحَلّ صَغِير · أُمِّي طَبِيبَة

explanations.title: Working for yourself
explanations.body: Many people work for a company: مُوَظَّف (employee). Others own a business: صَاحِب مَحَلّ (shop owner) or تَاجِر (merchant). Work that you run yourself is الْعَمَل الْحُرّ (free work, self-employment). The word حُرّ means “free”.

explanations.title: Describing a family’s work
explanations.body: Use a simple sentence without “is”: أَبِي صَاحِب مَحَلّ. The verb فَتَحَ (he opened) is also useful, and its object takes tanwīn with fatḥa: فَتَحَ مَحَلًّا. Ask “Do you have a job?” with عِنْدَك وَظِيفَة؟

examples.translation: ʾabī ṣāḥib maḥall ṣaghīr. — My father owns a small shop.
ʾummī ṭabība fī mustashfā kabīr. — My mother is a doctor in a big hospital.

examples.text: فَتَحَ جَارِي مَحَلًّا صَغِيرًا فِي الْحَيّ.
examples.translation: fataḥa jārī maḥallan ṣaghīran fī al-ḥayy. — My neighbour opened a small shop in the neighbourhood.
yufaḍḍil khālid al-ʿamal al-ḥurr. — Khalid prefers self-employment.
ʾukhtī muwaẓẓafa fī sharika kabīra. — My sister is an employee in a big company.
hal ʿindak waẓīfa? — Do you have a job? (to a man)

exercises.prompt: What does فَتَحَ جَارِي مَحَلًّا mean?
What does هَلْ عِنْدَك وَظِيفَة؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: My mother is a doctor in a big hospital.
My father owns a small shop.

exercises.explanation: Object: tanwīn with fatḥa, and masculine to match صَغِيرًا.
exercises.promptTranslation: My neighbour opened a small shop in the neighbourhood.

lessons.title: 235. Shops in the neighbourhood: grocery, butcher, bakery
lessons.subtitle: أَشْتَرِي الْخُبْز مِنَ الْمَخْبَز الْقَرِيب

explanations.title: Who sells what
explanations.body: The pattern فَعَّال, with a doubled middle letter, names a seller (جَزَّار); with ـَة it often names the shop (بَقَّالَة). Words that start with مَـ often name a place where something is done: مَخْبَز is the place where bread (خُبْز) is baked, and مَطْعَم is where you eat.

explanations.title: Shopping sentences
explanations.body: The verb بَاعَ (he sold) is a hollow verb. Its present is يَبِيع (he sells). To say where you buy something, use مِنْ: أَشْتَرِي الْخُبْز مِنَ الْمَخْبَز.

examples.translation: ʾashtarī al-khubz mina al-makhbaz al-qarīb. — I buy the bread from the nearby bakery.
yabīʿ al-jazzār al-laḥm. — The butcher sells meat.

examples.text: أَبِي يَذْهَب إِلَى الْبَقَّالَة كُلّ يَوْم.
examples.translation: ʾabī yadhhab ʾilā al-baqqāla kull yawm. — My father goes to the grocery store every day.
fī al-ḥayy maṭʿam wamakhbaz wabaqqāla. — In the neighbourhood there is a restaurant, a bakery and a grocery store.
al-baqqāla qarība min baytinā. — The grocery store is near our house.
yaftaḥ al-makhbaz fī as-sādisa ṣabāḥan. — The bakery opens at six in the morning.

exercises.prompt: What does يَبِيع الْجَزَّار اللَّحْم mean?
What does يَفْتَح الْمَخْبَز فِي السَّادِسَة صَبَاحًا mean?
options: The bakery closes at six in the evening
The bakery opens at six in the morning

exercises.explanation: The place where bread is made.
exercises.promptTranslation: I buy the bread from the nearby bakery.
The butcher sells meat.
My father goes to the grocery store every day.

explanations.title: Places of worship and festivals
explanations.body: Arab communities abroad often have both a مَسْجِد (mosque) and a كَنِيسَة (church), because Arab communities include Muslims, Christians and others. The leader of the prayer in a mosque is an إِمَام. A holiday is عِيد, and a public festival is مَهْرَجَان. The Christmas holiday is عِيد الْمِيلَاد.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Two things together take a dual adjective: مَسْجِد وَكَنِيسَة قَرِيبَان (a mosque and a church, both near). Use يَوْم الْجُمْعَة for “on Friday” and كُلّ سَنَة for “every year”.

examples.translation: fī al-ḥayy masjid wakanīsa qarībān. — In the neighbourhood there are a mosque and a church, both nearby.

examples.text: يُصَلِّي أَبِي فِي الْمَسْجِد يَوْم الْجُمْعَة.
examples.translation: yuṣallī ʾabī fī al-masjid yawm al-jumʿa. — My father prays at the mosque on Friday.

examples.text: تَزُور عَائِلَتِي الْكَنِيسَة فِي عِيد الْمِيلَاد.
examples.translation: tazūr ʿāʾilatī al-kanīsa fī ʿīd al-mīlād. — My family visits the church at Christmas.

examples.text: يَتَكَلَّم الْإِمَام مَعَ النَّاس بَعْد الصَّلَاة.
examples.translation: yatakallam al-ʾimām maʿa an-nās baʿd aṣ-ṣalāh. — The imam talks with people after the prayer.

examples.text: يَحْضُر كَثِير مِنَ النَّاس الْمَهْرَجَان الْعَرَبِيّ كُلّ سَنَة.
examples.translation: yaḥḍur kathīr mina an-nās al-mahrajān al-ʿarabiyy kull sana. — Many people attend the Arab festival every year.
ʿīd saʿīd! — Happy holiday!

exercises.prompt: Why is قَرِيبَان in the dual in “مَسْجِد وَكَنِيسَة قَرِيبَان”?
What does يَحْضُر النَّاس الْمَهْرَجَان mean?

exercises.explanation: Friday prayer is at the mosque.
exercises.promptTranslation: My father prays at the mosque on Friday.
My family visits the church at Christmas.

exercises.prompt: يَحْضُر كَثِير مِنَ النَّاس ___ الْعَرَبِيّ كُلّ سَنَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many people attend the Arab festival every year.

explanations.title: Words for missing home
explanations.body: Your homeland is وَطَن and your family and relatives are أَهْل. الْغُرْبَة is the feeling of being a stranger far from home. The verb اِشْتَاقَ إِلَى means “to long for” or “to miss”. Its present tense is أَشْتَاق (I miss), يَشْتَاق (he misses).

explanations.title: Feelings and contact
explanations.body: To say “I feel …”, use أَشْعُر بِ + noun: أَشْعُر بِالْغُرْبَة. To stay in touch you can call or talk: أُكَلِّم أُمِّي بِالْهَاتِف.

examples.translation: ʾashtāq ʾilā ʾahlī fī al-waṭan. — I miss my family in my homeland.
ʾashʿur bil-ghurba fī al-ʾayyām al-ʾūlā. — I feel homesick in the first days.

examples.text: أَنَا بَعِيد عَنْ وَطَنِي، لَكِنْ قَلْبِي هُنَاكَ.
examples.translation: ʾanā baʿīd ʿan waṭanī, lākin qalbī hunāka. — I am far from my homeland, but my heart is there.
ʾukallim ʾummī bil-hātif kull ʾusbūʿ. — I talk to my mother on the phone every week.

examples.text: الْأَيَّام الْأُولَى فِي بَلَد جَدِيد صَعْبَة.
examples.translation: al-ʾayyām al-ʾūlā fī balad jadīd ṣaʿba. — The first days in a new country are hard.
yashtāq jaddī ʾilaynā. — My grandfather misses us.

exercises.prompt: What does أَشْتَاق إِلَى أَهْلِي mean?
What does أَنَا بَعِيد عَنْ وَطَنِي mean?
options: I am far from my homeland
the feeling of being far from home

exercises.prompt: What does أُكَلِّم أُمِّي بِالْهَاتِف mean?
options: I buy my mother a phone
I talk to my mother on the phone

exercises.promptTranslation: I miss my family.

exercises.explanation: I talk to: the prefix is أُ.
exercises.promptTranslation: I talk to my mother every week.
I feel homesick in the first days.

explanations.title: Ways to get the news
explanations.body: The media are وَسَائِل الْإِعْلَام. The singular وَسِيلَة means “a means” and إِعْلَام means “informing”. Each medium has its own word. A plural of things (such as وَسَائِل) is treated as a feminine singular, so the adjective is feminine: وَسَائِل الْإِعْلَام مُهِمَّة.

explanations.title: What people do with them
explanations.body: You watch (شَاهَدَ) television, listen to (سَمِعَ) the radio, and read (قَرَأَ) a paper or a magazine. A channel presents (تُقَدِّم) programmes.

examples.translation: tuqaddim hādhihi al-qanāh barāmij ʿarabiyya. — This channel presents Arabic programmes.
ʾasmaʿ al-ʾidhāʿa fī as-sayyāra. — I listen to the radio in the car.
yaqraʾ ʾabī al-jarīda kull ṣabāḥ. — My father reads the newspaper every morning.
nashtarī al-majalla kull shahr. — We buy the magazine every month.
ʾaqraʾ al-ʾakhbār ʿalā al-mawqiʿ. — I read the news on the website.
wasāʾil al-ʾiʿlām muhimma. — The media are important.

exercises.prompt: Where do you listen to the news by voice only?
What does تُقَدِّم هَذِهِ الْقَنَاة بَرَامِج عَرَبِيَّة mean?
Why is مُهِمَّة feminine in وَسَائِل الْإِعْلَام مُهِمَّة?
options: a plural of things takes a feminine singular adjective

exercises.promptTranslation: My father reads the newspaper every morning.
I listen to the radio in the car.

exercises.explanation: A plural of things → feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: The media are important.

lessons.title: 239. In the newspaper: sections and headlines
lessons.subtitle: أَبْدَأ بِصَفْحَة الرِّيَاضَة

explanations.title: The sections
explanations.body: A newspaper is divided into sections, each with a صَفْحَة (page). The usual ones are السِّيَاسَة (politics), الرِّيَاضَة (sport), الِاقْتِصَاد (economy), الثَّقَافَة (culture) and الطَّقْس (weather). An article is مَقَال, a headline is عُنْوَان, and a single piece of news is خَبَر (plural أَخْبَار).

explanations.title: Reading the paper
explanations.body: Pages are named with an iḍāfa: صَفْحَة الرِّيَاضَة (the sports page). The second word has ال and no tanwīn. The article “about” a subject uses عَنْ.

examples.translation: ʾabdaʾ biṣafḥa ar-riyāḍa. — I start with the sports page.
ʿunwān al-maqāl ṭawīl. — The headline of the article is long.
yaktub al-kātib maqālan ʿani al-iqtiṣād. — The writer writes an article about the economy.
fī aṣ-ṣafḥa al-ʾūlā ṣūra kabīra. — On the first page there is a big picture.
hādhā khabar muhimm ʿani aṭ-ṭaqs. — This is an important piece of news about the weather.
tuḥibb ʾukhtī ṣafḥa ath-thaqāfa. — My sister likes the culture page.

exercises.prompt: Which section would tell you about the rain tomorrow?
What does يَكْتُب الْكَاتِب مَقَالًا عَنِ الِاقْتِصَاد mean?
options: The writer writes an article about the economy
The writer reads a book about sport

exercises.explanation: In an iḍāfa the second word keeps ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: I start with the sports page.

exercises.explanation: One picture, feminine to match كَبِيرَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: On the first page there is a big picture.

exercises.explanation: One piece of news; masculine to match مُهِمّ.
exercises.promptTranslation: This is an important piece of news about the weather.

lessons.title: 240. News bulletins and live broadcasts
lessons.subtitle: تَبْدَأ نَشْرَة الْأَخْبَار فِي التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً

explanations.title: On the air
explanations.body: A news bulletin is نَشْرَة الْأَخْبَار. A programme sent live is بَثّ مُبَاشِر. The person who reads the news is the مُذِيع (announcer), and the person who reports from the field is the مُرَاسِل (correspondent). A report is تَقْرِير, and an advertisement is إِعْلَان.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Notice the time expression التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً (at nine in the evening) and the verb شَاهَدَ (he watched), whose past with “I” is شَاهَدْتُ.

examples.text: تَبْدَأ نَشْرَة الْأَخْبَار فِي التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً.
examples.translation: tabdaʾ nashra al-ʾakhbār fī at-tāsiʿa masāʾan. — The news bulletin starts at nine in the evening.
hādhā bathth mubāshir mina al-madīna. — This is a live broadcast from the city.
yaqraʾ al-mudhīʿ al-ʾakhbār. — The announcer reads the news.
al-murāsil fī al-maṭār al-ʾān. — The correspondent is at the airport now.
baʿd al-ʾiʿlān yabdaʾ al-barnāmaj. — After the advertisement the programme starts.
shāhadtu taqrīran ʿani al-mahrajān. — I watched a report about the festival.

exercises.prompt: Who reads the news on television?
Who reports from outside the studio?

exercises.explanation: The bulletin starts at a time.
exercises.promptTranslation: The news bulletin starts at nine in the evening.

exercises.explanation: He reads the news in the studio.
exercises.promptTranslation: The announcer reads the news.
This is a live broadcast from the city.

lessons.title: 241. In order to: لِـ and كَيْ
lessons.subtitle: جِئْنَا لِنَتَعَلَّم · ذَهَبُوا كَيْ يَلْعَبُوا

explanations.title: Saying the purpose
explanations.body: To say why someone does something, put لِـ (in order to) or كَيْ (so that) before a present verb. Both are followed by the shortened present that you know from أَنْ and لَنْ. A final ن of ـُونَ, ـِينَ and ـَانِ falls away, and ـُوا gets a silent alif. The women’s plural ـْنَ keeps its ن. لِـ is joined to the verb: لِ + يَلْعَبُوا = لِيَلْعَبُوا. كَيْ stands alone.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: The first verb says what is or was done, and the second verb gives the purpose.

examples.translation: ʾadrus kathīran liʾanjaḥ fī al-imtiḥān. — I study a lot in order to pass the exam.
jiʾnā ʾilā hunā linataʿallam al-ʿarabiyya. — We came here to learn Arabic.
dhahaba al-ʾaṭfāl ʾilā al-malʿab liyalʿabū. — The children went to the playground to play.
jāʾa al-waladān kay yadrusā maʿan. — The two boys came to study together.

examples.text: تَجْلِس الْبِنْت قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمُدَرِّسَة كَيْ تَسْمَع جَيِّدًا.
examples.translation: tajlis al-bint qarīban mina al-mudarrisa kay tasmaʿ jayyidan. — The girl sits near the teacher so that she hears well.

examples.text: ذَهَبَتِ الْبَنَات إِلَى الْمَقْهَى لِيَشْرَبْنَ الْقَهْوَة.
examples.translation: dhahabati al-banāt ʾilā al-maqhā liyashrabna al-qahwa. — The girls went to the café to drink coffee.

exercises.prompt: What does لِـ + a present verb often mean?
Which means “We came here to learn Arabic”?
exercises.explanation: لِنَتَعَلَّم = in order that we learn.

exercises.prompt: What happens to the ن of يَلْعَبُون after لِـ?
Which means “so that she hears well”?
Which is correct for “the two boys … so that they study”?
Which one keeps its ن after لِـ?
exercises.explanation: The women’s plural ـْنَ keeps its ن.
They (men): ـُوا with a silent alif.
exercises.promptTranslation: The children went to the playground to play.
We came here to learn Arabic.

exercises.explanation: The two boys: ـَا without ن.
exercises.promptTranslation: The two boys came to study together.

lessons.title: 242. With ن or without ن? A summary
lessons.subtitle: يَكْتُبُون · لَنْ يَكْتُبُوا · لَمْ يَكْتُبُوا · سَيَكْتُبُون

explanations.title: Where the ن goes
explanations.body: A present verb with the endings ـِينَ, ـَانِ and ـُونَ keeps its ن in a plain statement or question, and after سَـ, لَا and هَلْ. The ن falls away after أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ and لِـ, and also after لَمْ (“did not”). The women’s plural ـْنَ never changes. So you only have to remember one shortened form for all five words.

headers: After أَنْ · لَنْ · كَيْ · لِـ · لَمْ

explanations.title: The same verb in six sentences
explanations.body: Compare what happens to the ending. After سَـ and هَلْ the ن stays; after لَنْ, لَمْ and أَنْ it is gone.

examples.translation: sayaktubūn ar-risāla ghadan. — They will write the letter tomorrow.
lan yaktubū ar-risāla ghadan. — They will not write the letter tomorrow.
lam yaktubū ar-risāla ʾams. — They did not write the letter yesterday.
hal taktubīn ar-risāla? — Are you writing the letter? (to a woman)
ʾurīd ʾan taktubī ar-risāla. — I want you to write the letter. (to a woman)
lā yaktubān al-wājib fī al-masāʾ. — The two of them do not write the homework in the evening.

exercises.prompt: Which word keeps the ن of ـُونَ?
Which means “They will not write the letter”?
Which means “They did not write the letter”?
Which is correct after أَنْ for “you (woman) write”?
Which one never loses its ن?
Which means “Are you writing the letter?” (to a woman)

exercises.explanation: After لَنْ the ن falls away.
exercises.promptTranslation: They will not write the letter tomorrow.
Are you writing the letter? (to a woman)

exercises.explanation: After لَمْ the ن falls away.
exercises.promptTranslation: They did not write the letter yesterday.

lessons.title: 243. Verbal nouns of Measure I: دُخُول · كِتَابَة · فَتْح
lessons.subtitle: دَخَلَ ← دُخُول · كَتَبَ ← كِتَابَة · فَتَحَ ← فَتْح

explanations.title: A noun for the action
explanations.body: A verbal noun (maṣdar) names an action, like “entering”, “writing” or “reading”. English uses -ing for this. In Arabic it is a real noun: it can have ال, take an adjective, and be the subject of a sentence. For Measure I verbs there is no single rule, so learn the verbal noun together with the verb. Several patterns are common.

explanations.title: Verbal nouns as subjects
explanations.body: A verbal noun can start a sentence, and any adjective after it is singular and masculine or feminine to match the noun. Most of the nouns ending in ـَة are feminine.

examples.translation: al-kitāba bil-ʿarabiyya ṣaʿba fī al-bidāya. — Writing in Arabic is hard at the beginning.
al-qirāʾa mufīda. — Reading is useful.
ad-dukhūl mamnūʿ. — Entering is forbidden.
al-khurūj mina al-madrasa fī ath-thālitha. — Leaving school is at three o’clock.
as-sibāḥa riyāḍa jamīla. — Swimming is a beautiful sport.
ziyāra al-matḥaf mumtiʿa. — Visiting the museum is enjoyable.

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of كَتَبَ?
What is the verbal noun of دَخَلَ?
What is the verbal noun of قَرَأَ?
What is the verbal noun of زَارَ?
What does السِّبَاحَة رِيَاضَة جَمِيلَة mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Writing in Arabic is hard at the beginning.

exercises.explanation: The action of reading; feminine to match مُفِيدَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: Reading is useful.

exercises.explanation: A verbal noun at the start of an iḍāfa.
exercises.promptTranslation: Visiting the museum is enjoyable.

lessons.title: 244. Using verbal nouns: after prepositions and instead of أَنْ
lessons.subtitle: أُحِبّ الْقِرَاءَة · بَعْد الْوُصُول · مَمْنُوع الْجُلُوس

explanations.title: Two ways to say the same thing
explanations.body: After verbs like أُحِبّ (I like), أُرِيد (I want) and يَجِب (it is necessary), you can use أَنْ + verb or a verbal noun. The verbal noun is shorter and sounds more formal. If the verbal noun has an object, join them in an iḍāfa: أُحِبّ قِرَاءَة الْجَرِيدَة. The second word is genitive, but in our spelling no ending shows.

explanations.title: After a preposition
explanations.body: After بَعْد (after), قَبْل (before), عَنْ (about) and لِـ (for), Arabic uses a verbal noun where English uses -ing. A sign like مَمْنُوع (forbidden) is followed by a verbal noun too.

examples.text: بَعْد الْوُصُول إِلَى الْفُنْدُق نَامَ الْجَمِيع.
examples.translation: baʿd al-wuṣūl ʾilā al-funduq nāma al-jamīʿ. — After arriving at the hotel everyone slept.
qabl al-khurūj ʾaghliqi al-bāb. — Before going out, close the door.
mamnūʿ al-julūs hunā. — No sitting here.
ʾuḥibb dirāsa al-lughāt. — I like studying languages.
sabab najāḥihi huwa ad-dirāsa. — The reason for his success is studying.
adh-dhahāb ʾilā al-maṭār bil-qiṭār sarīʿ. — Going to the airport by train is quick.

exercises.prompt: Which says the same as أُحِبّ أَنْ أَقْرَأ?
exercises.explanation: The verbal noun replaces أَنْ + verb.

exercises.prompt: What does بَعْد الْوُصُول إِلَى الْفُنْدُق mean?
Which says the same as أُرِيد أَنْ أَذْهَب إِلَى الْمَطَار?
What does أُحِبّ دِرَاسَة اللُّغَات mean?

exercises.explanation: A verbal noun joined to its object in an iḍāfa.
exercises.promptTranslation: I like studying languages.
No sitting here.
After arriving at the hotel everyone slept.

lessons.title: 245. Verbal nouns of Measures II and III
lessons.subtitle: عَلَّمَ ← تَعْلِيم · شَاهَدَ ← مُشَاهَدَة

explanations.title: Measure II: تَفْعِيل
explanations.body: These two measures have fixed patterns, so they are easy. For Measure II, the verbal noun is تَفْعِيل: put تَـ in front, a sukūn on the first root letter and a long ī (ـِي) before the last one. عَلَّمَ becomes تَعْلِيم. If the last radical is hamza, the pattern is تَفْعِلَة: هَنَّأَ becomes تَهْنِئَة.

explanations.title: Measure III: مُفَاعَلَة
explanations.body: For Measure III, the verbal noun is مُفَاعَلَة. Put مُـ in front of the stem, keep the long ā, and end in ـَة: شَاهَدَ becomes مُشَاهَدَة.

examples.translation: taʿlīm al-ʾaṭfāl muhimm. — Teaching children is important.
yabdaʾ at-tadrīb fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The training begins in the morning.
ʾuḥibb mushāhada al-ʾakhbār. — I like watching the news.
baʿd al-muqābala ḥaṣala ʿalā al-waẓīfa. — After the interview he got the job.
shukran ʿalā al-musāʿada. — Thank you for the help.
mughādara al-funduq qabl aẓ-ẓuhr. — Hotel check-out is before noon.

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of عَلَّمَ?
What is the verbal noun of دَرَّبَ?
What is the verbal noun of شَاهَدَ?
What is the verbal noun of غَادَرَ?
What is the verbal noun of هَنَّأَ?

exercises.promptTranslation: I like watching the news.
Teaching children is important.
Thank you for the help.

lessons.title: 246. Verbal nouns of Measures IV and VI
lessons.subtitle: أَغْلَقَ ← إِغْلَاق · تَبَادَلَ ← تَبَادُل

explanations.title: Measure IV: إِفْعَال
explanations.body: For Measure IV, the verbal noun is إِفْعَال. The verb أَغْلَقَ (he closed) gives إِغْلَاق. If the middle radical is weak, a ـَة ending is added and the weak letter becomes a long ā: أَقَامَ becomes إِقَامَة.

explanations.title: Measure VI: تَفَاعُل
explanations.body: For Measure VI, the verbal noun is تَفَاعُل. Compare the verb تَبَادَلَ (he exchanged) with تَبَادُل: the ā stays, the vowel before the last letter becomes ḍamma. Measure VI usually describes something done between two or more sides.

examples.translation: ʾighlāq al-maḥall fī at-tāsiʿa. — The shop closes at nine.
shukran ʿalā ʾirsāl ar-risāla. — Thank you for sending the letter.
al-ʾiʿlān ʿani al-mahrajān fī al-jarīda. — The announcement of the festival is in the newspaper.
at-taʿāwun bayna al-jīrān muhimm. — Cooperation between neighbours is important.
badaʾnā tabādul ar-rasāʾil. — We started exchanging letters.
at-tanāfus bayna al-farīqayn qawiyy. — The competition between the two teams is strong.

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of أَغْلَقَ?
What is the verbal noun of أَرْسَلَ?
What is the verbal noun of أَقَامَ?
What is the verbal noun of تَعَاوَنَ?
What is the verbal noun of تَنَافَسَ?
What does التَّعَاوُن بَيْنَ الْجِيرَان مُهِمّ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Thank you for sending the letter.
The competition between the two teams is strong.
We started exchanging letters.

lessons.title: 247. A map of verbal nouns: Measures I to VI
lessons.subtitle: تَعْلِيم · مُشَاهَدَة · إِغْلَاق · تَعَلُّم · تَبَادُل

explanations.title: One picture of all six
explanations.body: Every measure from II to VI has its own pattern, and Measure I has several. If you know the verb’s measure, you can build the verbal noun.

explanations.title: Saying it with a verbal noun
explanations.body: A verbal noun can replace أَنْ + verb. When the action belongs to a person, a pronoun ending goes on the verbal noun: بَعْد وُصُولِنَا (after our arrival). A verbal noun can have its own object: مُغَادَرَة الْفُنْدُق (leaving the hotel).

examples.translation: ʾurīd mughādara al-funduq ghadan. — I want to leave the hotel tomorrow.
yajib ʾighlāq al-maḥall fī at-tāsiʿa. — The shop must close at nine.

examples.text: بَعْد وُصُولِنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَة زُرْنَا الْمَتْحَف.
examples.translation: baʿd wuṣūlinā ʾilā al-madīna zurnā al-matḥaf. — After our arrival in the city we visited the museum.
at-taʿallum wat-taʿlīm muhimmān lil-jāliya. — Learning and teaching are important for the community.
ʾuḥibb mushāhada al-ʾakhbār waqirāʾa al-jarīda. — I like watching the news and reading the newspaper.
qabl muqābala al-mudīr ʾaqraʾ al-wathāʾiq. — Before meeting the director I read the documents.

exercises.prompt: Which verbal noun belongs to Measure IV?
Which verbal noun belongs to Measure VI?
Which verbal noun belongs to Measure III?
Which says the same as أُرِيد أَنْ أُغَادِر الْفُنْدُق?
How do you say “after our arrival”?
Which measure has the verbal noun pattern تَفَعُّل?

exercises.promptTranslation: The shop must close at nine.
Before meeting the director I read the documents.
Learning and teaching are important for the community.

lessons.title: 248. Review: community life, media and verbal nouns
lessons.subtitle: رِسَالَة مِنْ سَلْمَى: أَعِيش فِي مَدِينَة كَبِيرَة

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: This lesson brings together community words, the media, the ن rule and verbal nouns. Remember: the ن of ـُونَ, ـِينَ and ـَانِ falls away after أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ, لِـ and لَمْ; and a verbal noun can replace أَنْ + verb.

rows: Many of the children speak two languages.
They will not write the letter.
The news bulletin starts at nine.

explanations.title: A letter from Salma (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: Salma is an invented character who lives far from her family’s homeland. The text is made up for practice.

examples.text: أَنَا سَلْمَى، أَعِيش فِي مَدِينَة كَبِيرَة مُنْذُ ثَلَاث سَنَوَات.
examples.translation: ʾanā salmā, ʾaʿīsh fī madīna kabīra mundhu thalāth sanawāt. — I am Salma, and I have lived in a big city for three years.
ʾaṣl ʿāʾilatī mina al-ʾurdunn. — My family’s origin is Jordan.
fī ḥayyinā makhbaz wabaqqāla wamasjid. — In our neighbourhood there is a bakery, a grocery store and a mosque.

examples.text: أَشْتَاق إِلَى أَهْلِي، لَكِنْ أُكَلِّم أُمِّي كُلّ أُسْبُوع.
examples.translation: ʾashtāq ʾilā ʾahlī, lākin ʾukallim ʾummī kull ʾusbūʿ. — I miss my family, but I talk to my mother every week.
ʾuḥibb qirāʾa al-jarīda al-ʿarabiyya. — I like reading the Arabic newspaper.

examples.text: وَأُحِبّ مُشَاهَدَة نَشْرَة الْأَخْبَار فِي الْمَسَاء.
examples.translation: waʾuḥibb mushāhada nashra al-ʾakhbār fī al-masāʾ. — And I like watching the news bulletin in the evening.

exercises.prompt: Where does Salma’s family come from?
How long has Salma lived in the city?
What does Salma do every week?
Which is correct after لَنْ for “they (men) write”?
In which newspaper section would you find the forecast?

exercises.explanation: A verbal noun joined to its object.
exercises.promptTranslation: I like reading the Arabic newspaper.
Are you writing the letter now? (to a woman)
The bakery, the grocery store and the mosque are in the neighbourhood.

units.title: الْمُجْتَمَع وَالْأَعْلَام: people, generations and review

lessons.title: 249. Where were you born? وُلِدْتُ
lessons.subtitle: وُلِدْتُ فِي مَدِينَة كَبِيرَة · وُلِدَتْ أُمِّي فِي قَرْيَة

explanations.title: “Was born”
explanations.body: To talk about a person’s life, you need the verb وُلِدَ (he was born). It is a passive verb: the first letter has a ḍamma and the second a kasra. You do not need the rest of the passive for now, only these forms. The endings are the same as for any past verb.

explanations.title: Where and when
explanations.body: Use فِي for a place, a season or a month. To ask “Where were you born?”, put أَيْنَ first.

examples.translation: wulidtu fī madīna kabīra. — I was born in a big city.
ʾayna wulidta? — Where were you born? (to a man)
wulidat ʾummī fī qarya ṣaghīra. — My mother was born in a small village.
wulida ʾabī fī aṣ-ṣayf. — My father was born in the summer.

examples.text: وُلِدْنَا فِي أَمْرِيكَا، لَكِنْ أَصْل عَائِلَتِنَا مِنْ لُبْنَان.
examples.translation: wulidnā fī ʾamrīkā, lākin ʾaṣl ʿāʾilatinā min lubnān. — We were born in America, but our family’s origin is Lebanon.
wulidū fī shahr māris. — They were born in the month of March.

exercises.prompt: What does وُلِدَتْ أُمِّي فِي قَرْيَة صَغِيرَة mean?
options: My mother was born in a small village
My father was born in a village
My mother visited a small village
My mother lives in a small village

exercises.promptTranslation: I was born in a big city.
My mother was born in a small village.
We were born in America.

lessons.title: 250. Grandparents and generations
lessons.subtitle: هَاجَرَ جَدِّي إِلَى أَمْرِيكَا · أَنَا مِنَ الْجِيل الثَّانِي

explanations.title: Family history words
explanations.body: A grandfather is جَدّ and a grandmother is جَدَّة. A generation is جِيل. The first generation (الْجِيل الْأَوَّل) is the people who moved to the new country, and the second generation (الْجِيل الثَّانِي) is their children who grew up there. Grandchildren are أَحْفَاد.

explanations.title: Telling a family story
explanations.body: The verb هَاجَرَ (he emigrated) is followed by إِلَى and the new country. Use فِي to say where a family settled.

examples.translation: hājara jaddī ʾilā ʾamrīkā. — My grandfather emigrated to America.
istaqarra jaddī fī madīna ṣaghīra. — My grandfather settled in a small town.
jaddatī taʿīsh maʿanā. — My grandmother lives with us.

examples.text: الْجِيل الْأَوَّل مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِين عَمِلَ كَثِيرًا.
examples.translation: al-jīl al-ʾawwal mina al-muhājirīn ʿamila kathīran. — The first generation of immigrants worked a lot.
ʾanā mina al-jīl ath-thānī. — I am of the second generation.

examples.text: جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي يَتَكَلَّمَان الْعَرَبِيَّة مَعَ الْأَحْفَاد.
examples.translation: jaddī wajaddatī yatakallamān al-ʿarabiyya maʿa al-ʾaḥfād. — My grandparents speak Arabic with the grandchildren.

exercises.prompt: What does هَاجَرَ جَدِّي إِلَى أَمْرِيكَا mean?
options: My grandfather was born in America

exercises.prompt: Why is يَتَكَلَّمَان dual in “جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي يَتَكَلَّمَان”?

exercises.promptTranslation: My grandfather emigrated to America.
I am of the second generation.
My grandmother lives with us.

explanations.title: Degrees and subjects
explanations.body: A degree or certificate is شَهَادَة. The main university degrees are الْبَكَالُورْيُوس (bachelor’s), الْمَاجِسْتِير (master’s) and الدُّكْتُورَاه (doctorate). You study a subject with دَرَسَ + the subject, you graduate with تَخَرَّجَ مِنْ + the university, and you receive a degree with حَصَلَ عَلَى.

explanations.title: A student’s history
explanations.body: Put the facts in the order they happened: studied, graduated, received a degree. The verb حَصَلَ is followed by عَلَى.

examples.text: دَرَسَ أَخِي الْهَنْدَسَة فِي جَامِعَة مَعْرُوفَة.
examples.translation: darasa ʾakhī al-handasa fī jāmiʿa maʿrūfa. — My brother studied engineering at a well-known university.

examples.text: تَخَرَّجَتْ لَيْلَى مِنَ الْجَامِعَة الْعَام الْمَاضِي.
examples.translation: takharrajat laylā mina al-jāmiʿa al-ʿām al-māḍī. — Laila graduated from the university last year.
ḥaṣala ʿādil ʿalā shahāda al-mājistīr. — Adel received a master’s degree.
tadrus salmā aṭ-ṭibb. — Salma studies medicine.
baʿd at-takharruj ʿamila fī sharika. — After graduating he worked in a company.

examples.text: سَتَحْصُل عَلَى شَهَادَة الدُّكْتُورَاه بَعْد سَنَتَيْن.
examples.translation: sataḥṣul ʿalā shahāda ad-duktūrāh baʿd sanatayn. — She will receive the doctorate in two years.

exercises.prompt: What does تَخَرَّجَتْ مِنَ الْجَامِعَة mean?
What does حَصَلَ عَادِل عَلَى شَهَادَة mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: My brother studied engineering at a well-known university.
Adel received a master’s degree.
She graduated from the university last year.

explanations.title: Working as…
explanations.body: To say “worked as a manager”, put the job after عَمِلَ with tanwīn fatḥa: عَمِلَ مُدِيرًا. A job or position is مَنْصِب, a general manager is مُدِير عَامّ, and to retire is تَقَاعَدَ (a Measure VI verb). The verbal noun is التَّقَاعُد (retirement).

rows: he will work as an engineer

explanations.title: A career story
explanations.body: Use ثُمَّ (then) and بَعْد (after) to put events in order.

examples.text: عَمِلَ أَبِي مُدِيرًا فِي شَرِكَة كَبِيرَة.
examples.translation: ʿamila ʾabī mudīran fī sharika kabīra. — My father worked as a manager in a big company.

examples.text: عَمِلَتْ أُمِّي طَبِيبَةً فِي مُسْتَشْفَى الْمَدِينَة.
examples.translation: ʿamilat ʾummī ṭabībatan fī mustashfā al-madīna. — My mother worked as a doctor in the city hospital.
hādhā huwa al-manṣib al-jadīd. — This is the new position.
taqāʿada jaddī qabl sanatayn. — My grandfather retired two years ago.

examples.text: بَعْد التَّقَاعُد يُحِبّ جَدِّي قِرَاءَة الْجَرِيدَة.
examples.translation: baʿd at-taqāʿud yuḥibb jaddī qirāʾa al-jarīda. — After retirement my grandfather likes reading the newspaper.

examples.text: سَيَعْمَل أَخِي مُهَنْدِسًا فِي شَرِكَة مَعْرُوفَة.
examples.translation: sayaʿmal ʾakhī muhandisan fī sharika maʿrūfa. — My brother will work as an engineer in a well-known company.

exercises.prompt: What does عَمِلَ أَبِي مُدِيرًا mean?
options: My father worked as a manager

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of تَقَاعَدَ?
Which means “she worked as a doctor”?
Which means “he will work as an engineer”?

exercises.explanation: Job after عَمِلَ, with tanwīn fatḥa.
exercises.promptTranslation: My father worked as a manager in a big company.
My grandfather retired two years ago.
After retirement my grandfather likes reading the newspaper.

lessons.title: 253. Winning a prize: فَازَ بِـ
lessons.subtitle: فَازَ الْفَرِيق بِالْمُبَارَاة · فَازَتْ سَلْمَى بِجَائِزَة

explanations.title: A hollow verb: فَازَ
explanations.body: The verb فَازَ (he won) is hollow, like قَالَ: the middle letter is و. Before the endings ـتُ, ـتَ, ـتِ, ـنَا and ـنَ the long ā drops and the first letter takes a ḍamma: فُزْتُ (I won), فُزْنَا (we won). The present is يَفُوز (he wins), أَفُوز (I win). After فَازَ the prize takes بِـ: فَازَ بِجَائِزَة.

explanations.title: Winners
explanations.body: A prize is جَائِزَة. The Nobel Prize is جَائِزَة نُوبِل. As a real example, the Egyptian-American scientist أَحْمَد زُوَيْل won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry near the end of the twentieth century. Other sentences below are invented.

examples.translation: fāza al-farīq bil-mubārāh. — The team won the match.
fāzat salmā bijāʾiza fī al-madrasa. — Salma won a prize at school.

examples.text: فَازَ الْعَالِم أَحْمَد زُوَيْل بِجَائِزَة نُوبِل فِي الْكِيمِيَاء.
examples.translation: fāza al-ʿālim ʾaḥmad zuwayl bijāʾiza nūbil fī al-kīmiyāʾ. — The scientist Ahmed Zewail won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
fuznā bil-mubārāh al-ʾūlā. — We won the first match.
sanafūz ghadan. — We will win tomorrow.
lan yafūzū bihādhihi al-jāʾiza. — They will not win this prize.

exercises.prompt: What does فَازَ الْفَرِيق بِالْمُبَارَاة mean?

exercises.explanation: ـنَا = we; the long ā drops and the first letter takes a ḍamma.

exercises.promptTranslation: I won the prize.
The team will win tomorrow.
Salma won a prize at school.

explanations.title: Creative people
explanations.body: A poet is شَاعِر, a painter is رَسَّام, an artist is فَنَّان, a man of letters is أَدِيب (a woman: أَدِيبَة) and a scientist is عَالِم. Famous is مَشْهُور and well-known is مَعْرُوف. To say what someone is famous for, use بِـ: مَشْهُور بِرِوَايَاتِهِ (famous for his novels).

explanations.title: A famous example
explanations.body: Khalil Gibran (جُبْرَان خَلِيل جُبْرَان) is a well-known real example: a poet and painter from Lebanon who lived in America and wrote in both Arabic and English. The other sentences are invented for practice.

examples.text: جُبْرَان خَلِيل جُبْرَان شَاعِر وَرَسَّام مِنْ لُبْنَان.
examples.translation: jubrān khalīl jubrān shāʿir warassām min lubnān. — Khalil Gibran is a poet and painter from Lebanon.

examples.text: عَاشَ فِي أَمْرِيكَا وَكَتَبَ بِالْعَرَبِيَّة وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة.
examples.translation: ʿāsha fī ʾamrīkā wakataba bil-ʿarabiyya wal-ʾinjilīziyya. — He lived in America and wrote in Arabic and English.
hādhihi al-ʾadība mashhūra biriwāyātihā. — This woman writer is famous for her novels.
huwa fannān maʿrūf fī al-madīna. — He is a well-known artist in the city.
kataba ash-shāʿir qaṣīda jamīla. — The poet wrote a beautiful poem.
ʾuḥibb hādhā ar-rassām. — I like this painter.

exercises.prompt: What does عَاشَ فِي أَمْرِيكَا وَكَتَبَ بِالْعَرَبِيَّة وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة mean?
options: He was born in America and sang in English
He studied in America and worked in Arabic
He visited America and read English
He lived in America and wrote in Arabic and English

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine of أَدِيب?

exercises.promptTranslation: This woman writer is famous for her novels.
The poet wrote a beautiful poem.
He is a well-known artist in the city.

lessons.title: 255. Entertainment and sport: actors, singers, players
lessons.subtitle: هُوَ مُمَثِّل مَعْرُوف · غَنَّى الْمُطْرِب فِي حَفْل كَبِير

explanations.title: People of the stage and the pitch
explanations.body: An actor is مُمَثِّل, a film director is مُخْرِج, a singer is مُطْرِب, and a player is لَاعِب. A film is فِيلْم, a concert or party is حَفْل, and music is مُوسِيقَى. The word أَفْضَل (best) can stand before a singular noun: أَفْضَل مُمَثِّل (best actor).

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: The verb غَنَّى means “he sang”. It is a Measure II verb whose last letter is ى, so it ends in a long ā: غَنَّى.

examples.translation: huwa mumaththil maʿrūf. — He is a well-known actor.
shāhadnā fīlman jadīdan. — We watched a new film.
ghannā al-muṭrib fī ḥafl kabīr. — The singer sang at a big concert.
yalʿab al-lāʿib fī farīq maʿrūf. — The player plays in a well-known team.

examples.text: حَصَلَ الْمُمَثِّل عَلَى جَائِزَة أَفْضَل مُمَثِّل.
examples.translation: ḥaṣala al-mumaththil ʿalā jāʾiza ʾafḍal mumaththil. — The actor received the prize for best actor.
al-mukhrij al-jadīd shābb. — The new director is a young man.

exercises.prompt: What does غَنَّى الْمُطْرِب فِي حَفْل كَبِير mean?
options: The singer left a big concert
The actor watched a big film
The singer sang at a big concert
The player won a big prize

exercises.prompt: Which means “We watched a new film”?

exercises.promptTranslation: He is a well-known actor.
The player plays in a well-known team.
The singer sang at a big concert.

lessons.title: 256. Review: this and that, with people and the genitive
lessons.subtitle: هَذَا الشَّاعِر وَتِلْكَ الْأَدِيبَة · كُتُب هَؤُلَاءِ الْكُتَّاب

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Demonstratives agree with the noun: هَذَا and ذَلِكَ for masculine singular, هَذِهِ and تِلْكَ for feminine singular, هَؤُلَاءِ and أُولَئِكَ for people in the plural. The noun after a demonstrative has ال. After a preposition, or after the first noun of an iḍāfa, the next noun is genitive (no ending shows in our spelling).

explanations.title: In use
explanations.body: A demonstrative can come before a definite noun (هَذَا الشَّاعِر, “this poet”) or stand alone as the subject: هَذَا شَاعِر (this is a poet).

examples.text: هَذَا الشَّاعِر مِنْ لُبْنَان وَتِلْكَ الْأَدِيبَة مِنْ مِصْر.
examples.translation: hādhā ash-shāʿir min lubnān watilka al-ʾadība min miṣr. — This poet is from Lebanon and that woman writer is from Egypt.
man hāʾulāʾ al-ʿulamāʾ? — Who are these scientists?

examples.text: أُولَئِكَ الْفَنَّانُون مَشْهُورُون فِي الْعَالَم الْعَرَبِيّ.
examples.translation: ʾulāʾika al-fannānūn mashhūrūn fī al-ʿālam al-ʿarabiyy. — Those artists are famous in the Arab world.
ʾuḥibb kutub hādhā al-kātib. — I like the books of this writer.
qaraʾtu qiṣṣa dhālika al-ʾadīb. — I read the story of that man of letters.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الرِّوَايَة جَمِيلَة وَتِلْكَ الْقَصِيدَة قَصِيرَة.
examples.translation: hādhihi ar-riwāya jamīla watilka al-qaṣīda qaṣīra. — This novel is beautiful and that poem is short.

exercises.prompt: What does كُتُب هَذَا الْكَاتِب mean?
What does مَنْ هَؤُلَاءِ الْعُلَمَاء؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: This poet is from Lebanon.
I read the story of that man of letters.
Those artists are famous in the Arab world.

lessons.title: 257. Review: the most famous, the best, older than
lessons.subtitle: أَشْهَر شَاعِر · أَفْضَل لَاعِب · أَكْبَر مِنِّي

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: The comparative أَفْعَل is followed by مِنْ for “than”: أَكْبَر مِنِّي (older than me). For the superlative there are two ways. With an indefinite singular noun, the أَفْعَل word comes first: أَشْهَر شَاعِر (the most famous poet). With ال, it comes after the noun: الشَّاعِر الْأَشْهَر.

rows: the oldest member of the family

explanations.title: About people
explanations.body: Remember that the superlative stays singular and masculine before an indefinite noun, even when the person is a woman: أَشْهَر أَدِيبَة. To say “the most famous of the poets”, put the superlative before a definite plural noun: أَشْهَر الشُّعَرَاء.

examples.translation: huwa ʾashhar shāʿir fī al-madīna. — He is the most famous poet in the city.
hiya ʾakbar min ʾakhī. — She is older than my brother.
huwa ʾafḍal lāʿib fī al-farīq. — He is the best player in the team.
hādhihi ar-riwāya ʾajmal min tilka. — This novel is more beautiful than that one.
jaddī ʾakbar fard fī al-ʿāʾila. — My grandfather is the oldest member of the family.
hiya ʾashhar ʾadība fī al-qarya. — She is the most famous woman writer in the village.

exercises.prompt: What does هِيَ أَكْبَر مِنْ أَخِي mean?
options: She is smaller than my brother
My brother is older than she
She is older than my brother

exercises.prompt: Which means “This novel is more beautiful than that one”?
exercises.explanation: تِلْكَ = that one (f.), because الرِّوَايَة is feminine.

exercises.prompt: What does جَدِّي أَكْبَر فَرْد فِي الْعَائِلَة mean?
options: My grandfather is the family’s only member
My grandfather is the tallest man
My grandfather is older than the family
My grandfather is the oldest member of the family

exercises.promptTranslation: He is the most famous poet in the city.
This novel is more beautiful than that one.
She is older than my brother.

lessons.title: 258. Review: hollow verbs and verbal nouns
lessons.subtitle: عَادَ ← عَوْدَة · فَازَ ← فَوْز · زَارَ ← زِيَارَة

explanations.title: Verb to noun
explanations.body: Hollow verbs (verbs with و or ي in the middle) are common in biographies. Their verbal nouns often have the pattern فَعْل, فَعْلَة or فِعَالَة, with the weak letter showing as و or ي: عَادَ → عَوْدَة, فَازَ → فَوْز, سَارَ → سَيْر, نَامَ → نَوْم, قَالَ → قَوْل, زَارَ → زِيَارَة, قَادَ → قِيَادَة.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: A verbal noun can take a pronoun ending: عَوْدَتُهُ (his return), and can follow بَعْد: بَعْد عَوْدَتِهِ (after his return).

examples.text: بَعْد عَوْدَتِهِ إِلَى لُبْنَان كَتَبَ كِتَابًا.
examples.translation: baʿd ʿawdatihi ʾilā lubnān kataba kitāban. — After his return to Lebanon he wrote a book.
fariḥnā bifawz al-farīq. — We rejoiced at the team’s win.
ziyāra al-jadda kull ʾusbūʿ jamīla. — Visiting grandmother every week is lovely.
an-nawm muhimm lil-ʾaṭfāl. — Sleep is important for children.

examples.text: زَارَ الشَّاعِر قَرْيَتَهُ وَعَادَ إِلَى أَمْرِيكَا.
examples.translation: zāra ash-shāʿir qaryatahu waʿāda ʾilā ʾamrīkā. — The poet visited his village and returned to America.

examples.text: فَازَ الْفَرِيق، وَقَالَ الْمُدَرِّب كَلِمَة جَمِيلَة.
examples.translation: fāza al-farīq, waqāla al-mudarrib kalima jamīla. — The team won, and the coach said a nice word.

exercises.prompt: What is the verbal noun of عَادَ?
What is the verbal noun of فَازَ?
What is the verbal noun of زَارَ?
What does النَّوْم مُهِمّ لِلْأَطْفَال mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: After his return to Lebanon he wrote a book.

exercises.prompt: زَارَ الشَّاعِر قَرْيَتَهُ وَ___ إِلَى أَمْرِيكَا.
exercises.promptTranslation: The poet visited his village and returned to America.
We rejoiced at the team’s win.

lessons.title: 259. Asking for biographical information
lessons.subtitle: أَيْنَ وُلِدْتِ؟ · مَاذَا دَرَسْتِ؟ · لِمَاذَا هَاجَرْتِ؟

explanations.title: Questions for a life story
explanations.body: A question word comes first, then the past verb with the ending for “you”. To a man the ending is ـتَ, to a woman ـتِ. The answer uses ـتُ for “I”. Compare: أَيْنَ دَرَسْتِ؟ (Where did you study? to a woman) and دَرَسْتُ فِي جَامِعَة مَعْرُوفَة.

explanations.title: An interview (an invented practice dialogue)
explanations.body: A journalist asks a made-up writer about her life. The questions are to a woman.

examples.translation: ʾayna wulidti? — Where were you born?

examples.text: وُلِدْتُ فِي قَرْيَة صَغِيرَة فِي لُبْنَان.
examples.translation: wulidtu fī qarya ṣaghīra fī lubnān. — I was born in a small village in Lebanon.
mādhā darasti fī al-jāmiʿa? — What did you study at university?

examples.text: دَرَسْتُ الْأَدَب ثُمَّ هَاجَرْتُ لِأَدْرُس فِي أَمْرِيكَا.
examples.translation: darastu al-ʾadab thumma hājartu liʾadrus fī ʾamrīkā. — I studied literature and then emigrated to study in America.
mādhā katabti baʿd dhālika? — What did you write after that?
katabtu riwāyatayn waqaṣīda ṭawīla. — I wrote two novels and a long poem.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks “Where were you born?” (to a woman)
Which question asks “What did you study?” (to a woman)
Which ending is the answer for “I”?

exercises.promptTranslation: What did you write after that?
I studied literature.
Where were you born?

lessons.title: 260. Review: the life of Hind
lessons.subtitle: حَيَاة هِنْد: وُلِدَتْ فِي قَرْيَة صَغِيرَة

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: This lesson brings together the vocabulary of life stories: وُلِدَ (was born), هَاجَرَ (emigrated), دَرَسَ and تَخَرَّجَ (studied, graduated), عَمِلَ + job (worked as), فَازَ بِـ (won), تَقَاعَدَ (retired). Verbal nouns such as التَّخَرُّج and التَّقَاعُد can follow بَعْد.

rows: She was born in a village.

explanations.title: The life of Hind (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: Hind is an invented character. Her story is made up for practice.

examples.text: وُلِدَتْ هِنْد فِي قَرْيَة صَغِيرَة فِي لُبْنَان.
examples.translation: wulidat hind fī qarya ṣaghīra fī lubnān. — Hind was born in a small village in Lebanon.

examples.text: هَاجَرَ جَدُّهَا إِلَى أَمْرِيكَا وَاسْتَقَرَّ فِي مَدِينَة كَبِيرَة.
examples.translation: hājara jadduhā ʾilā ʾamrīkā wastaqarra fī madīna kabīra. — Her grandfather emigrated to America and settled in a big city.

examples.text: دَرَسَتْ هِنْد الطِّبّ فِي جَامِعَة مَعْرُوفَة وَتَخَرَّجَتْ بَعْد سِتّ سَنَوَات.
examples.translation: darasat hind aṭ-ṭibb fī jāmiʿa maʿrūfa watakharrajat baʿd sitt sanawāt. — Hind studied medicine at a well-known university and graduated after six years.

examples.text: بَعْد التَّخَرُّج عَمِلَتْ طَبِيبَةً فِي مُسْتَشْفَى كَبِير.
examples.translation: baʿd at-takharruj ʿamilat ṭabībatan fī mustashfā kabīr. — After graduating she worked as a doctor in a big hospital.

examples.text: فَازَتْ بِجَائِزَة لِأَنَّهَا سَاعَدَتْ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاس.
examples.translation: fāzat bijāʾiza liʾannahā sāʿadat kathīran mina an-nās. — She won a prize because she helped many people.

examples.text: تَقَاعَدَتْ هِنْد وَهِيَ الْآن تَكْتُب رِوَايَة.
examples.translation: taqāʿadat hind wahiya al-ʾān taktub riwāya. — Hind has retired and is now writing a novel.

options: In a big city in America
In a small village in Lebanon
exercises.explanation: وُلِدَتْ فِي قَرْيَة صَغِيرَة فِي لُبْنَان.

exercises.prompt: Why did she win a prize?
بَعْد ___ عَمِلَتْ طَبِيبَةً فِي مُسْتَشْفَى كَبِير.
exercises.promptTranslation: After graduating she worked as a doctor in a big hospital.
Hind was born in a small village.
Hind won a prize.

units.title: الْمَطَار وَالسَّفَر: flights, plural things, assimilated verbs and instructions

lessons.title: 261. At the airport: places, people, papers
lessons.subtitle: مَطَار · طَائِرَة · رِحْلَة · تَذْكِرَة · جَوَاز سَفَر

explanations.title: Words you will see and hear
explanations.body: At an airport you meet a small set of words again and again. A passenger is رَاكِب (plural رُكَّاب). The passport is جَوَاز سَفَر, literally “a pass of travel”.

explanations.title: Short sentences
explanations.body: These sentences use only words and patterns you already know.

examples.translation: ʾanā fī al-maṭār al-ʾān. — I am at the airport now.
aṭ-ṭāʾira kabīra wajadīda. — The plane is big and new.
maʿī ḥaqība ṣaghīra wajawāz safar. — I have a small bag and a passport.
al-muwaẓẓaf yaṭlub al-jawāz wat-tadhkira. — The official asks for the passport and the ticket.
ar-rukkāb fī ṣāla al-mughādara. — The passengers are in the departure hall.
ʾayna bawwāba riḥlatī? — Where is the gate for my flight?

exercises.prompt: What does الْمُوَظَّف يَطْلُب الْجَوَاز وَالتَّذْكِرَة mean?
options: The official sells the passport and the ticket
The official asks for the passport and the ticket
The passenger loses the passport and the ticket

exercises.prompt: What does مَعِي حَقِيبَة صَغِيرَة mean?
options: I am in a small hall

exercises.prompt: What does أَيْنَ بَوَّابَة رِحْلَتِي؟ ask?
options: Where is the gate for my flight?

exercises.promptTranslation: The passengers are in the departure hall.
I am at the airport now.
The official asks for the passport and the ticket.

lessons.title: 262. Flights: leaving, arriving, delays
lessons.subtitle: تُغَادِر الرِّحْلَة فِي الثَّامِنَة · تَصِل فِي الْعَاشِرَة

explanations.title: Departure and arrival
explanations.body: Flights are announced with a few nouns: مُغَادَرَة (departure), وُصُول (arrival), إِقْلَاع (take-off), هُبُوط (landing) and تَأْخِير (delay). A flight without a stop is a رِحْلَة مُبَاشِرَة. The verbs are تُغَادِر (it leaves) and تَصِل (it arrives); the subject رِحْلَة is feminine, so the verb starts with تـ.

explanations.title: Reading a flight board
explanations.body: The board gives the time after فِي. Add صَبَاحًا (in the morning) or مَسَاءً (in the evening) when the hour could be either.

examples.translation: tughādir ar-riḥla fī ath-thāmina ṣabāḥan. — The flight leaves at eight in the morning.
taṣil ar-riḥla fī al-ʿāshira masāʾan. — The flight arrives at ten in the evening.
hādhihi riḥla mubāshira ʾilā al-qāhira. — This is a direct flight to Cairo.
hunāk taʾkhīr fī ar-riḥla. — There is a delay in the flight.
raqm al-bawwāba sabʿa. — The gate number is seven.

examples.text: الْإِقْلَاع فِي الْوَاحِدَة وَالْهُبُوط فِي الرَّابِعَة.
examples.translation: al-ʾiqlāʿ fī al-wāḥida wal-hubūṭ fī ar-rābiʿa. — The take-off is at one and the landing at four.

exercises.prompt: What does تُغَادِر الرِّحْلَة فِي الثَّامِنَة صَبَاحًا mean?
options: The flight is late by eight hours
The flight leaves at eight in the morning
The flight arrives at eight in the evening

exercises.prompt: Why does تَصِل start with تـ in تَصِل الرِّحْلَة؟
What does هُنَاك تَأْخِير فِي الرِّحْلَة mean?
options: There is a delay in the flight

exercises.promptTranslation: The flight arrives at ten in the evening.
This is a direct flight to Cairo.

exercises.prompt: الْإِقْلَاع فِي الْوَاحِدَة وَ___ فِي الرَّابِعَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The take-off is at one and the landing at four.

lessons.title: 263. Booking a ticket
lessons.subtitle: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز تَذْكِرَة ذَهَاب وَإِيَاب

explanations.title: One way or return
explanations.body: To book is حَجَزَ (he booked), present يَحْجِز: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز تَذْكِرَة (I want to book a ticket). A one-way ticket is تَذْكِرَة ذَهَاب and a return ticket is تَذْكِرَة ذَهَاب وَإِيَاب. The class of seat is دَرَجَة: الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى is first class.

rows: I want to book a ticket

explanations.title: At the booking desk
explanations.body: These are the questions and answers you need most.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز تَذْكِرَة إِلَى عَمَّان.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾaḥjiz tadhkira ʾilā ʿammān. — I want to book a ticket to Amman.
hal turīd dhahāban faqaṭ? — Do you want to go one way only?
lā, ʾurīd tadhkira dhahāb waʾiyāb. — No, I want a return ticket.
kam siʿr at-tadhkira? — How much is the ticket?

examples.text: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مَقْعَد فِي الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى؟
examples.translation: hal ʿindakum maqʿad fī ad-daraja al-ʾūlā? — Do you have a seat in first class?
ḥajaztu maqʿadan ʿinda an-nāfidha. — I booked a seat by the window.

exercises.explanation: ذَهَاب وَإِيَاب = going and coming back.

exercises.prompt: What does كَمْ سِعْر التَّذْكِرَة؟ ask?

lessons.title: 264. A verb before things in the plural
lessons.subtitle: تَصِل الرِّحْلَات · تُغَادِر الطَّائِرَات

explanations.title: The rule
explanations.body: You already know that a verb at the start of a sentence agrees with its subject in gender only and stays singular, even before a dual or plural subject: وَصَلَ الرُّكَّاب (the passengers arrived). When the subject is a plural of things (planes, flights, bags, and also animals), the verb is feminine singular, however many there are.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Notice that the verb starts with تـ before these plurals: رِحْلَات (flights), طَائِرَات (planes), حَقَائِب (bags). The same goes for the past: وَصَلَتِ الرِّحْلَات.

examples.text: تَصِل الرِّحْلَات مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة كُلّ يَوْم.
examples.translation: taṣil ar-riḥlāt mina al-qāhira kull yawm. — Flights arrive from Cairo every day.
tughādir aṭ-ṭāʾirāt al-maṭār fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The planes leave the airport in the morning.
waṣalati al-ḥaqāʾib fī waqtihā. — The bags arrived on time.

examples.text: تَبْدَأ الرِّحْلَات إِلَى عَمَّان فِي الْخَامِسَة.
examples.translation: tabdaʾ ar-riḥlāt ʾilā ʿammān fī al-khāmisa. — The flights to Amman begin at five.
yaṣil ar-rukkāb ʾilā al-bawwāba. — The passengers arrive at the gate.
taqif aṭ-ṭāʾirāt qurb al-bawwābāt. — The planes stand near the gates.

exercises.prompt: Which verb fits: ___ الرِّحْلَات مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة؟
exercises.explanation: Things in the plural → feminine singular.

exercises.prompt: Which verb fits: ___ الرُّكَّاب إِلَى الْبَوَّابَة؟
exercises.explanation: A group of men or a mixed group → masculine singular.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct for “The planes leave”?
What does وَصَلَتِ الْحَقَائِب فِي وَقْتِهَا mean?
What does تَبْدَأ الرِّحْلَات فِي الْخَامِسَة mean?

exercises.explanation: Bags are things; the others are people.

exercises.promptTranslation: The planes stand near the gates.
The flights to Amman begin at five.

exercises.explanation: A masculine singular verb goes with people.
exercises.promptTranslation: The passengers arrived at the airport.

explanations.title: What adverts promise
explanations.body: Adverts are full of verbs in front of plural things. Read the pattern: the verb is feminine singular, the plural noun follows it, and any adjective after the plural noun is feminine singular too (رِحْلَات يَوْمِيَّة, daily flights).

explanations.title: An invented advert
explanations.body: This advert is made up for practice; the company does not exist.

examples.text: شَرِكَة «النَّجْمَة» تُقَدِّم رِحْلَات يَوْمِيَّة إِلَى عَمَّان وَالْكُوَيْت.
examples.translation: sharika «an-najma» tuqaddim riḥlāt yawmiyya ʾilā ʿammān wal-kuwayt. — The company “Star” offers daily flights to Amman and Kuwait.
tughādir aṭ-ṭāʾirāt fī al-waqt al-munāsib. — The planes leave at the right time.
al-maqāʿid wāsiʿa wal-ʾasʿār munkhafiḍa. — The seats are wide and the prices are low.
tabdaʾ al-ʾasʿār min miʾa dīnār. — Prices start from a hundred dinars.

examples.text: تَصِل الطَّائِرَات إِلَى الْمَطَار قَبْل الْمَسَاء.
examples.translation: taṣil aṭ-ṭāʾirāt ʾilā al-maṭār qabl al-masāʾ. — The planes reach the airport before evening.
iḥjiz tadhkirataka al-yawm! — Book your ticket today! (to a man)

exercises.explanation: Plural of things → feminine singular adjective.

explanations.title: Words at the desk
explanations.body: Customs is الْجَمَارِك. The officer does a تَفْتِيش (inspection). Tax is ضَرِيبَة. Something forbidden is مَمْنُوع, and a gift is هَدِيَّة (plural هَدَايَا).

explanations.title: A short conversation (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: The officer talks to a traveller. Read it line by line.

tafaḍḍal. — Here you are.
hal maʿaka shayʾ mamnūʿ? — Do you have anything forbidden?
lā, maʿī hadāyā faqaṭ. — No, I only have gifts.
iftaḥ hādhihi al-ḥaqība min faḍlik. — Open this bag, please. (to a man)

examples.text: هَلْ أَدْفَع ضَرِيبَة؟ لَا، لَا تَدْفَع شَيْئًا.
examples.translation: hal ʾadfaʿ ḍarība? lā, lā tadfaʿ shayʾan. — Do I pay tax? No, you do not pay anything.

Open this bag, please. (to a man)
Do I pay tax?

explanations.title: Listen for these
explanations.body: Gate announcements repeat the same few phrases. A boarding pass is بِطَاقَة الصُّعُود. Boarding is عَمَلِيَّة الصُّعُود. The announcer gives commands in the plural: اِذْهَبُوا (go!). Listen for the number after رَقْم.

explanations.title: What you might hear
explanations.body: These announcements are invented for practice.

idhhabū ʾilā al-bawwāba raqm sitta. — Go to gate number six. (to a group)
ar-riḥla ʾilā al-kuwayt taʾakhkharat sāʿa. — The flight to Kuwait has been delayed by an hour.
raqm ar-riḥla khamsūn. — The flight number is fifty.

exercises.explanation: A feminine subject gives تْ in the past.

lessons.title: 268. Assimilated verbs: the و that disappears
lessons.subtitle: وَصَلَ ← يَصِل · وَقَفَ ← يَقِف · وَجَدَ ← يَجِد

explanations.title: A verb whose first root letter is و
explanations.body: Some verbs begin with the root letter و. In the past they look normal: وَصَلَ (he arrived), وَقَفَ (he stood). In the present the و disappears: يَصِل, يَقِف. Grammarians call these assimilated verbs (the first letter “melts away”). Most take a kasra on the second letter in the present, and a few take a fatḥa (يَضَع).

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: The present loses the و (and so does the command, which you will meet soon). The past keeps it, and so do nouns such as وُصُول, “arrival”.

examples.translation: waṣala ʾakhī ʾams. — My brother arrived yesterday.
yaṣil ʾakhī ghadan. — My brother arrives tomorrow.
waqaftu fī aṣ-ṣaff. — I stood in the line.
yaqif ar-rukkāb ʾamāma al-bawwāba. — The passengers stand in front of the gate.
wajadtu jawāzī. — I found my passport.
ʾajid maqʿadī bisuhūla. — I find my seat easily.

exercises.prompt: What happens to the و of وَصَلَ in the present?
Which is the present of وَقَفَ?
Which is the present of وَجَدَ?
Which sentence is in the present?

exercises.promptTranslation: The passengers stand in front of the gate.

exercises.explanation: I find: the و is gone.
exercises.promptTranslation: I find my seat easily.
My brother arrived yesterday.

lessons.title: 269. Assimilated verbs in the present: the main persons
lessons.subtitle: أَصِل · تَصِل · تَصِلِين · يَصِلُون

explanations.title: One pattern for every person
explanations.body: After the و has dropped, the present behaves like any other verb: the prefix shows the person, and the same endings are added. Learn يَصِل once and you know the rest.

explanations.title: The past is regular
explanations.body: In the past the و stays, and the endings are the ones you know: وَصَلْتُ (I arrived), وَصَلْنَا (we arrived), وَصَلُوا (they arrived).

examples.translation: ʾaṣil ʾilā al-maṭār fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — I arrive at the airport in the morning.
taṣilīn ʾilā al-bayt qabl al-masāʾ. — You arrive home before evening. (to a woman)
naqif ʾamāma al-jamārik. — We stand in front of customs.
yajidūn ḥaqāʾibahum bisurʿa. — They find their bags quickly.
waṣalnā ʾams fī al-ʿāshira. — We arrived yesterday at ten.
waṣalū mutaʾakhkhirīn. — They arrived late.

exercises.prompt: What does يَجِدُون حَقَائِبَهُمْ بِسُرْعَة mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I arrive at the airport in the morning.
We stand in front of customs.
They find their bags quickly.

explanations.title: The و stays away
explanations.body: The future, the negations with لَا and لَنْ, and the past negation with لَمْ all use the present stem. So the و never comes back. After لَمْ the ending is cut short: لَمْ يَصِلْ.

explanations.title: In use
explanations.body: Use سَـ or سَوْفَ for the future, and watch the time word: غَدًا (tomorrow) goes with the future, أَمْس (yesterday) with لَمْ.

examples.translation: saʾaṣil ʾilā al-kuwayt ghadan. — I will arrive in Kuwait tomorrow.
sawfa taṣil ar-riḥla fī ath-thāniya. — The flight will arrive at two.
lan ʾaqif fī aṣ-ṣaff al-yawm. — I will not stand in line today.
lā yajid ar-rukkāb ḥaqāʾibahum. — The passengers do not find their bags.
lam ʾajid jawāzī ʾams. — I did not find my passport yesterday.
lam taṣil ḥaqībatī. — My bag did not arrive.

exercises.prompt: What does لَمْ أَجِدْ جَوَازِي أَمْس mean?
options: I did not find my passport yesterday
I will not find my passport tomorrow
I do not find my passport

exercises.prompt: What does سَوْفَ تَصِل الرِّحْلَة فِي الثَّانِيَة mean?
options: The flight did not arrive at two
The flight will arrive at two

exercises.prompt: Which time word goes with لَنْ?

exercises.promptTranslation: I will not stand in line today.
My bag did not arrive.

exercises.explanation: A singular verb before the subject; لَا + present = does not.
exercises.promptTranslation: The passengers do not find their bags.

explanations.title: Take the present stem and drop the prefix
explanations.body: The command is easy for assimilated verbs: take the present stem and drop the prefix, with no helping alif. يَقِف becomes قِفْ, and يَضَع becomes ضَعْ. The endings are the usual ones: nothing (with a sukūn) for a man, ـِي for a woman, ـُوا for a group.

tables.title: Two irregular verbs: the hamza at the start also drops in the command (learn them as they are)
tables.note: أَخَذَ and أَكَلَ begin with hamza, not و, but they also drop their first letter in the command.

explanations.title: In use
explanations.body: Before a word with ال, a command that ends in a sukūn takes a helping kasra: ضَعِ الْحَقِيبَة. To forbid, use لَا + the short present: لَا تَقِفْ.

examples.translation: qif hunā min faḍlik. — Stand here, please. (to a man)
qifī ʾamāma al-bawwāba. — Stand in front of the gate. (to a woman)
ḍaʿi al-ḥaqība ʿalā aṭ-ṭāwila. — Put the bag on the table. (to a man)
ḍaʿū al-jawāzāt hunā. — Put the passports here. (to a group)
khudh tadhkirataka yā ʾakhī. — Take your ticket, brother.
lā taqif ʾamāma al-bāb. — Do not stand in front of the door. (to a man)

exercises.prompt: Which is the command “stand!” to a man?
Which is the command “put!” to a man?
What does لَا تَقِفْ أَمَامَ الْبَاب mean?
options: I did not stand in front of the door
Stand in front of the door
Do not stand in front of the door

exercises.explanation: A man is spoken to; the sukūn becomes kasra before ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: Put the bag on the table. (to a man)
Stand in front of the gate, Salma.

exercises.explanation: Forbid with لَا + the short present.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do not stand in front of the door. (to a man)

lessons.title: 272. Using a machine: step by step
lessons.subtitle: ضَعِ الْعُمْلَة · اِضْغَطِ الزِّرّ · خُذِ الْمَشْرُوب

explanations.title: Steps use commands
explanations.body: Instructions on machines use commands, one for each step, joined by أَوَّلًا (first), ثُمَّ (then) and أَخِيرًا (finally). The commands here are all to a man (or to anyone, on a sign). Each one that comes before ال ends in a kasra.

rows: put the coin in the machine

explanations.body: The same pattern works for a cash machine (ATM).

thumma ḍaʿi al-biṭāqa fī al-ʾāla. — Then put the card in the machine.
thumma uktubi ar-raqm. — Then write the number.

intaẓir daqīqa wāḥida. — Wait one minute.
ʾakhīran khudhi al-biṭāqa wal-māl. — Finally take the card and the money. (to a man)

explanations.body: On a plane the crew speaks to the whole cabin, so the commands end in ـُوا. The safety belt is حِزَام الْأَمَان (literally “the belt of safety”).

lessons.title: 274. Good manners for a guest: do and don’t
lessons.subtitle: اِخْلَعْ حِذَاءَكَ · لَا تَضَعْ قَدَمَيْكَ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة

explanations.title: Advice with commands
explanations.body: A friend might give advice to a guest with short commands. The advice here is general and simple. Customs differ from country to country and from family to family, so treat it as a starting point, not a rule. In many Arab homes guests take off their shoes at the door, and in many places people greet first and ask about the family before getting down to business.

rows: قِفْ عِنْدَمَا يَدْخُل ضَيْف كَبِير فِي السِّنّ
qif ʿindamā yadkhul ḍayf kabīr fī as-sinn

explanations.title: A friend explains (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: Notice that a positive command and a negative one use different forms of the same verb: خُذْ but لَا تَأْخُذْ, ضَعْ but لَا تَضَعْ.

examples.text: اِخْلَعْ حِذَاءَكَ عِنْدَ الْبَاب، فَهَذَا مُنَاسِب فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْبُيُوت.
examples.translation: ikhlaʿ ḥidhāʾaka ʿinda al-bāb, fahādhā munāsib fī kathīr mina al-buyūt. — Take off your shoes at the door; this is suitable in many homes.
lā taḍaʿ qadamayka ʿalā aṭ-ṭāwila. — Do not put your feet on the table.
