lessons.title: 275. Weather and delays on the board
lessons.subtitle: بِسَبَب الضَّبَاب تَأَخَّرَتِ الرِّحْلَات

explanations.title: Why flights are late
explanations.body: Weather words: الطَّقْس (weather), الضَّبَاب (fog), الْمَطَر (rain), عَاصِفَة رَمْلِيَّة (sandstorm). The reason comes after بِسَبَب (because of). A flight can be مُتَأَخِّرَة (late), مُؤَجَّلَة (postponed), مُلْغَاة (cancelled) or فِي الْمَوْعِد (on time).

explanations.title: What the announcer says
explanations.body: The verbs تَأَخَّرَ (it was late) and تَوَقَّفَ (it stopped) take the feminine singular form before a plural of things, exactly as you learned: تَأَخَّرَتِ الرِّحْلَات (not تَأَخَّرَ). These sentences are invented.

examples.translation: aṭ-ṭaqs sayyiʾ al-yawm. — The weather is bad today.
bisabab aḍ-ḍabāb taʾakhkharati ar-riḥlāt. — Because of the fog the flights were late.
tawaqqafati ar-riḥlāt bisabab al-ʿāṣifa. — The flights stopped because of the storm.
hunāk ʿāṣifa ramliyya fī al-madīna. — There is a sandstorm in the city.
sataṣil aṭ-ṭāʾira baʿd sāʿatayn. — The plane will arrive in two hours.

examples.text: رِحْلَتِي فِي الْمَوْعِد وَلَيْسَ هُنَاك تَأْخِير.
examples.translation: riḥlatī fī al-mawʿid walaysa hunāk taʾkhīr. — My flight is on time and there is no delay.

exercises.prompt: What does بِسَبَب الضَّبَاب تَأَخَّرَتِ الرِّحْلَات mean?
options: Because of the fog the flights were late
Because of the flights the fog was late

exercises.prompt: Why does the verb end in تِ in تَأَخَّرَتِ الرِّحْلَات؟
options: a plural of things takes feminine singular
exercises.explanation: Rule: things in the plural → feminine singular.
Things in the plural → feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: Because of the fog the flights were late.
The weather is bad today.
The plane will arrive in two hours.

lessons.title: 276. Review: a journey to Kuwait
lessons.subtitle: رِحْلَتِي إِلَى الْكُوَيْت: حَجَزْتُ · وَصَلْتُ · وَقَفْتُ

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Three ideas from this chapter. First, before a plural of things the verb is feminine singular: تَأَخَّرَتِ الرِّحْلَات. Second, an assimilated verb loses its و in the present (يَصِل, يَقِف, يَضَع) and in the command (صِلْ, قِفْ, ضَعْ). Third, the future and the negations keep the short stem: سَأَصِل, لَنْ أَصِل, لَمْ أَصِلْ.

rows: Put the bag here! (to a man)
I will not arrive before the evening.

explanations.title: My journey (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: A traveller tells the story of one day. The person and the story are made up.

examples.text: حَجَزْتُ تَذْكِرَة ذَهَاب وَإِيَاب إِلَى الْكُوَيْت.
examples.translation: ḥajaztu tadhkira dhahāb waʾiyāb ʾilā al-kuwayt. — I booked a return ticket to Kuwait.

examples.text: وَصَلْتُ إِلَى الْمَطَار فِي السَّادِسَة صَبَاحًا.
examples.translation: waṣaltu ʾilā al-maṭār fī as-sādisa ṣabāḥan. — I arrived at the airport at six in the morning.
waqaftu fī aṣ-ṣaff ʾamāma al-muwaẓẓaf. — I stood in line in front of the official.
qāla al-muwaẓẓaf: ḍaʿi al-ḥaqība hunā. — The official said: put the bag here.
bisabab aḍ-ḍabāb taʾakhkharati ar-riḥlāt sāʿatayn. — Because of the fog the flights were two hours late.
saʾaṣil ʾilā al-funduq baʿd aẓ-ẓuhr. — I will arrive at the hotel in the afternoon.

exercises.prompt: When did the traveller reach the airport?
Which is correct for “The flights arrived”?
exercises.explanation: Things in the plural → feminine singular.

exercises.promptTranslation: I stood in line in front of the official.
Put the bag here, please. (to a man)

exercises.explanation: Things in the plural → feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: Because of the fog the flights were late.

units.title: الْجُغْرَافِيَا وَالتَّارِيخ: relative pronouns, the passive and Measure VII

lessons.title: 277. “Who” and “which”: الَّذِي and الَّتِي
lessons.subtitle: الرَّجُل الَّذِي يَعْمَل هُنَا · الْمَرْأَة الَّتِي تَسْكُن هُنَا

explanations.title: Joining two sentences
explanations.body: A relative pronoun links a describing clause to a noun that is already definite (it has ال, or it is a name). English uses who, which or that. Arabic uses one of six words, and it must match the noun in gender and number. For a masculine singular noun use الَّذِي. For a feminine singular noun use الَّتِي.

explanations.title: What follows the pronoun
explanations.body: After the pronoun comes a normal clause: a verb, or a prepositional phrase. When the noun is the doer of the verb, the verb agrees with it (يَعْمَل for a man, تَعْمَل for a woman), and you add nothing else.

examples.translation: ar-rajul alladhī yaʿmal hunā muhandis. — The man who works here is an engineer.
al-marʾa allatī taskun bijānibī muʿallima. — The woman who lives next to me is a teacher.

examples.text: الطَّالِب الَّذِي يَدْرُس مَعِي يَتَكَلَّم الرُّوسِيَّة.
examples.translation: aṭ-ṭālib alladhī yadrus maʿī yatakallam ar-rūsiyya. — The student who studies with me speaks Russian.

examples.text: الْمُدَرِّسَة الَّتِي تُدَرِّس الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنْ مِصْر.
examples.translation: al-mudarrisa allatī tudarris al-ʿarabiyya min miṣr. — The teacher who teaches Arabic is from Egypt.
al-kitāb alladhī ʿalā aṭ-ṭāwila jadīd. — The book that is on the table is new.
al-madīna allatī fī ash-shamāl kabīra. — The city that is in the north is big.

exercises.prompt: What does الرَّجُل الَّذِي يَعْمَل هُنَا مُهَنْدِس mean?
options: The man works here as an engineer
The man who works here is an engineer
The engineer who works there is a man

exercises.prompt: What does الْمُدَرِّسَة الَّتِي تُدَرِّس الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنْ مِصْر mean?
options: The teacher who teaches Arabic is from Egypt
The teacher teaches Arabic in Egypt
Arabic is taught by a woman

exercises.promptTranslation: The woman who lives next to me is a teacher.
The student who studies with me speaks Russian.
The book that is on the table is new.

lessons.title: 278. No pronoun for an indefinite noun
lessons.subtitle: رَجُل يَعْمَل هُنَا · الرَّجُل الَّذِي يَعْمَل هُنَا

explanations.title: Definite or indefinite?
explanations.body: Use a relative pronoun only after a definite noun. After an indefinite noun, just put the clause next to it, and English will add “who” or “that” for you.

explanations.title: Same idea, two shapes
explanations.body: A noun with a name counts as definite: مُحَمَّد الَّذِي يَعْمَل هُنَا is “Muhammad, who works here”. These sentences are invented.

examples.translation: ʾaʿrif rajulan yaʿmal fī al-maṭār. — I know a man who works at the airport.

examples.text: أَعْرِف الرَّجُل الَّذِي يَعْمَل فِي الْمَطَار.
examples.translation: ʾaʿrif ar-rajul alladhī yaʿmal fī al-maṭār. — I know the man who works at the airport.
hādhihi ṭāliba tadrus al-ʿarabiyya. — This is a student who studies Arabic.

examples.text: هَذِهِ هِيَ الطَّالِبَة الَّتِي تَدْرُس الْعَرَبِيَّة.
examples.translation: hādhihi hiya aṭ-ṭāliba allatī tadrus al-ʿarabiyya. — This is the student who studies Arabic.
qaraʾtu kitāban ʿani al-jughrāfiyā. — I read a book about geography.

examples.text: سَلْمَى الَّتِي تَعْمَل فِي الْمَكْتَبَة صَدِيقَتِي.
examples.translation: salmā allatī taʿmal fī al-maktaba ṣadīqatī. — Salma, who works in the library, is my friend.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “a woman who works here”?
exercises.explanation: An indefinite noun takes no pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “the woman who works here”?
exercises.explanation: A definite noun takes a pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Is a relative pronoun used after رَجُل (a man)?
What does أَعْرِف رَجُلًا يَعْمَل فِي الْمَطَار mean?
options: I know the man who works at the airport
I know a man who works at the airport

exercises.prompt: What does هَذِهِ هِيَ الطَّالِبَة الَّتِي تَدْرُس الْعَرَبِيَّة mean?
options: This is a student who studies Arabic
This is the student who studies Arabic

exercises.prompt: Is سَلْمَى (a name) definite or indefinite?

exercises.promptTranslation: This is a student who studies Arabic.

exercises.explanation: A definite noun: use a pronoun.
exercises.promptTranslation: I know the man who works at the airport.
Salma, who works in the library, is my friend.

lessons.title: 279. Two of them: اللَّذَان and اللَّتَان
lessons.subtitle: الْمُهَنْدِسَان اللَّذَان يَعْمَلَان هُنَا

explanations.title: Dual pronouns
explanations.body: For two people or things, the relative pronoun is dual too. Masculine: اللَّذَان (nominative) and اللَّذَيْن (accusative and genitive). Feminine: اللَّتَان and اللَّتَيْن. The verb in the clause is also dual: يَعْمَلَان (two men work), تَعْمَلَان (two women work).

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: The pronoun copies the case of the noun it follows: الْمُهَنْدِسَان (subject) takes اللَّذَان; الْمُهَنْدِسَيْن (object) takes اللَّذَيْن.

examples.text: الْمُهَنْدِسَان اللَّذَان يَعْمَلَان هُنَا مِنْ مِصْر.
examples.translation: al-muhandisān alladhān yaʿmalān hunā min miṣr. — The two engineers who work here are from Egypt.

examples.text: الْمُعَلِّمَتَان اللَّتَان تُدَرِّسَان الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنَ الْأُرْدُنّ.
examples.translation: al-muʿallimatān allatān tudarrisān al-ʿarabiyya mina al-ʾurdunn. — The two teachers who teach Arabic are from Jordan.
shāhadtu al-muhandisayn alladhayn yaʿmalān hunā. — I saw the two engineers who work here.

examples.text: تَكَلَّمْتُ مَعَ الْمُعَلِّمَتَيْن اللَّتَيْن تُدَرِّسَان الْعَرَبِيَّة.
examples.translation: takallamtu maʿa al-muʿallimatayn allatayn tudarrisān al-ʿarabiyya. — I spoke with the two teachers who teach Arabic.

examples.text: الصَّدِيقَان اللَّذَان يَدْرُسَان مَعِي طَالِبَان جَيِّدَان.
examples.translation: aṣ-ṣadīqān alladhān yadrusān maʿī ṭālibān jayyidān. — The two friends who study with me are good students.
al-kitābān alladhān ʿalā aṭ-ṭāwila jadīdān. — The two books that are on the table are new.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun goes with الْمُهَنْدِسَان (two engineers, subject)?
Which pronoun goes with الْمُعَلِّمَتَان (two teachers, subject)?
Which pronoun goes with الْمُهَنْدِسَيْن (two engineers, object)?
Which pronoun goes with الْمُعَلِّمَتَيْن after مَعَ?
What does الْكِتَابَان اللَّذَان عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة جَدِيدَان mean?
options: The two books that are on the table are new
The books are on two tables
The book on the table is new

exercises.prompt: What does the verb in the clause look like after اللَّذَان?

exercises.promptTranslation: The two engineers who work here are from Egypt.
I saw the two engineers who work here.
The two teachers who teach Arabic are from Jordan.

lessons.title: 280. Many of them: الَّذِين and اللَّاتِي
lessons.subtitle: الرِّجَال الَّذِين · الْمُعَلِّمَات اللَّاتِي · الْكُتُب الَّتِي

explanations.title: The six pronouns in one chart
explanations.body: For three or more people, men take الَّذِين and women take اللَّاتِي. Some writers also use الَّتِي for women in the plural, but this course teaches اللَّاتِي. For a plural of things, remember the rule you learned earlier: it counts as feminine singular, so use الَّتِي.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: The verb inside the clause agrees with the antecedent: يَعْمَلُون for men, يَعْمَلْنَ for women, تَقَع or تَكُون for things.

examples.text: الرِّجَال الَّذِين يَعْمَلُون هُنَا مِنْ مِصْر.
examples.translation: ar-rijāl alladhīn yaʿmalūn hunā min miṣr. — The men who work here are from Egypt.

examples.text: الْمُعَلِّمَات اللَّاتِي يُدَرِّسْنَ الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنَ الْأُرْدُنّ.
examples.translation: al-muʿallimāt allātī yudarrisna al-ʿarabiyya mina al-ʾurdunn. — The women teachers who teach Arabic are from Jordan.

examples.text: الطُّلَّاب الَّذِين وَصَلُوا أَمْس يَدْرُسُون مَعَنَا.
examples.translation: aṭ-ṭullāb alladhīn waṣalū ʾams yadrusūn maʿanā. — The students who arrived yesterday are studying with us.
al-kutub allatī ʿalā aṭ-ṭāwila qadīma. — The books that are on the table are old.
al-mudun allatī ʿalā as-sāḥil kabīra. — The cities that are on the coast are big.

examples.text: الْبَنَات اللَّاتِي يَلْعَبْنَ فِي الْحَدِيقَة صَغِيرَات.
examples.translation: al-banāt allātī yalʿabna fī al-ḥadīqa ṣaghīrāt. — The girls who are playing in the garden are small.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun goes with الْمُعَلِّمَات (women teachers)?

exercises.explanation: A plural of things counts as feminine singular.

exercises.prompt: What does الطُّلَّاب الَّذِين وَصَلُوا أَمْس يَدْرُسُون مَعَنَا mean?
options: The students who studied arrived yesterday
The students who arrived yesterday are studying with us

exercises.prompt: Which verb fits: الْبَنَات اللَّاتِي ___ فِي الْحَدِيقَة

exercises.promptTranslation: The men who work here are from Egypt.
The books that are on the table are old.
The women teachers who teach Arabic are from Jordan.

lessons.title: 281. A pronoun that points back
lessons.subtitle: الْكِتَاب الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ · الْمَدِينَة الَّتِي أَسْكُن فِيهَا

explanations.title: When the noun is not the doer
explanations.body: In “the man who works here”, the man is the doer and is already the subject of the clause, so nothing more is needed. But in “the book that I read”, the book is the object of the verb, not its subject. Arabic then adds a pronoun inside the clause that points back to the noun: “the book that I read it”. Match it to the noun: ـهُ for a masculine singular, ـهَا for a feminine singular or a plural of things, ـهُمْ for several men.

rows: the city that I live in
the woman that I spoke with

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: Compare these with the lesson on الَّذِي and الَّتِي: there the noun was the doer, so no pronoun was added.

examples.translation: al-kitāb alladhī qaraʾtuhu jamīl. — The book that I read is beautiful.
al-madīna allatī ʾaskun fīhā kabīra. — The city that I live in is big.

examples.text: الرَّجُل الَّذِي رَأَيْتُهُ فِي الْمَطَار مُهَنْدِس.
examples.translation: ar-rajul alladhī raʾaytuhu fī al-maṭār muhandis. — The man whom I saw at the airport is an engineer.
al-marʾa allatī takallamtu maʿahā muʿallima. — The woman I spoke with is a teacher.
al-kutub allatī qaraʾtuhā qadīma. — The books that I read are old.

examples.text: الطُّلَّاب الَّذِين تَكَلَّمْتُ مَعَهُمْ مِنْ مِصْر.
examples.translation: aṭ-ṭullāb alladhīn takallamtu maʿahum min miṣr. — The students I spoke with are from Egypt.

exercises.prompt: In which phrase is no returning pronoun needed?
What does الرَّجُل الَّذِي رَأَيْتُهُ فِي الْمَطَار مُهَنْدِس mean?
options: The engineer works at the airport
The man who saw me is an engineer
The man whom I saw at the airport is an engineer

exercises.explanation: The book is masculine; I read it.
exercises.promptTranslation: The book that I read is beautiful.
The city that I live in is big.
The woman I spoke with is a teacher.

lessons.title: 282. Choosing the right pronoun: practice
lessons.subtitle: الدَّوْلَة الَّتِي تَقَع فِي الشَّمَال · الطُّلَّاب الَّذِين يَدْرُسُون

explanations.title: A four-step check
explanations.body: To pick the right pronoun, ask four questions. (1) Is the noun definite? If not, use no pronoun. (2) Is it masculine or feminine? (3) Is it one, two, or more? (4) Is it a person or a thing? Plural things count as feminine singular. Then decide whether the clause needs a returning pronoun.

explanations.title: Geography and people (invented sentences)
explanations.body: These sentences use most of the pronouns you know.

examples.text: الدَّوْلَة الَّتِي تَقَع فِي شَمَال أَفْرِيقِيَا كَبِيرَة.
examples.translation: ad-dawla allatī taqaʿ fī shamāl ʾafrīqiyā kabīra. — The country that lies in the north of Africa is big.

examples.text: بَعْض الدُّوَل الَّتِي عَلَى الْخَلِيج غَنِيَّة بِالنَّفْط.
examples.translation: baʿḍ ad-duwal allatī ʿalā al-khalīj ghaniyya bin-nafṭ. — Some of the countries on the Gulf are rich in oil.
al-ʿāṣima allatī zurtuhā jamīla. — The capital that I visited is beautiful.

examples.text: الطُّلَّاب الَّذِين يَدْرُسُون مَعِي مِنْ بِلَاد مُخْتَلِفَة.
examples.translation: aṭ-ṭullāb alladhīn yadrusūn maʿī min bilād mukhtalifa. — The students who study with me are from different countries.

examples.text: الْمُدَرِّسَات اللَّاتِي يُدَرِّسْنَ اللُّغَة مِنْ بَلَد عَرَبِيّ.
examples.translation: al-mudarrisāt allātī yudarrisna al-lugha min balad ʿarabiyy. — The women teachers who teach the language are from an Arab country.

examples.text: الْمُهَنْدِسَان اللَّذَان وَصَلَا أَمْس يَعْمَلَان هُنَا.
examples.translation: al-muhandisān alladhān waṣalā ʾams yaʿmalān hunā. — The two engineers who arrived yesterday work here.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun goes with الطُّلَّاب (students, men)?
Which pronoun goes with الطَّالِبَان (two students, subject)?
Which phrase needs a returning pronoun?
exercises.explanation: The capital is what I visited, not the doer.

exercises.prompt: What does بَعْض الدُّوَل الَّتِي عَلَى الْخَلِيج غَنِيَّة بِالنَّفْط mean?
options: The Gulf is rich in countries
Some of the countries on the Gulf are rich in oil
The oil is in one country

exercises.explanation: Feminine pronoun, feminine returning pronoun, definite noun.

exercises.prompt: الدَّوْلَة ___ تَقَع فِي شَمَال أَفْرِيقِيَا كَبِيرَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The country that lies in the north of Africa is big.

exercises.prompt: الطُّلَّاب ___ يَدْرُسُون مَعِي مِنْ بِلَاد مُخْتَلِفَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The students who study with me are from different countries.
The capital that I visited is beautiful.

lessons.title: 283. Active and passive: who did it?
lessons.subtitle: كَتَبَ الْمُدِير الرِّسَالَة ← كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَة

explanations.title: Same event, two angles
explanations.body: In an active sentence the doer is the subject: “the director wrote the letter”. In a passive sentence the thing that receives the action becomes the subject: “the letter was written”, and the doer is usually left out. In Arabic the passive of a Measure I verb is shown by the vowels alone: ḍamma on the first letter and kasra on the second. The one who receives the action becomes the subject (nominative).

explanations.title: Matching the receiver
explanations.body: The passive verb agrees with the receiver, which is now the subject: كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَة (feminine), فُتِحَ الْبَاب (masculine). A plural of things takes the feminine singular, as always.

examples.translation: kataba al-mudīr ar-risāla ʾams. — The director wrote the letter yesterday.
kutibati ar-risāla ʾams. — The letter was written yesterday.
fataḥa al-muwaẓẓaf al-bāb. — The employee opened the door.
futiḥa al-bāb fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The door was opened in the morning.
ḥumilati al-ḥaqāʾib ʾilā aṭ-ṭāʾira. — The bags were carried to the plane.
durisati al-masʾala bidiqqa. — The issue was studied carefully.

exercises.prompt: Which is the passive of فَتَحَ?
In a passive sentence, who becomes the subject?
options: the one who receives the action
the one who does the action
exercises.explanation: The receiver becomes the subject; the doer is usually left out.

exercises.prompt: Why is it كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَة but فُتِحَ الْبَاب؟
options: the verb agrees with the receiver
exercises.explanation: رِسَالَة is feminine; بَاب is masculine.

exercises.promptTranslation: The door was opened in the morning.

exercises.explanation: A plural of things → feminine singular, passive.
exercises.promptTranslation: The bags were carried to the plane.

exercises.explanation: The director is the doer: active.
exercises.promptTranslation: The director wrote the letter yesterday.

lessons.title: 284. The past passive: all third persons
lessons.subtitle: كُتِبَ · كُتِبَتْ · كُتِبَا · كُتِبُوا

explanations.title: Endings are the usual ones
explanations.body: The passive past changes only the inside vowels. The endings stay the ones you know, and, when the receiver comes first, they match it in gender and number.

explanations.title: After the subject, the verb agrees fully
explanations.body: When the receiver comes first, the verb after it agrees in gender and number. Remember that plural things take the feminine singular, so a passive verb after الْكُتُب is كُتِبَتْ.

examples.translation: al-kitāb kutiba fī al-qāhira. — The book was written in Cairo.
al-qiṣṣa kutibat qabl sanawāt. — The story was written years ago.
al-kitābān kutibā fī sana wāḥida. — The two books were written in one year.
al-kutub kutibat bil-ʿarabiyya. — The books were written in Arabic.
futiḥati al-madrasa qabl sana. — The school was opened a year ago.
futiḥati al-madāris fī ʾuktūbar. — The schools were opened in October.

exercises.prompt: The receiver comes first: الْكِتَابَان ___ (the two books were written). Which fits?
Which is the masculine plural passive past of كَتَبَ (they were written)?
What does فُتِحَتِ الْمَدْرَسَة قَبْل سَنَة mean?
options: The school will open next year
The school was opened a year ago

exercises.prompt: What does الْكُتُب كُتِبَتْ بِالْعَرَبِيَّة mean?
options: The books were written in Arabic

exercises.promptTranslation: The book was written in Cairo.
The story was written years ago.
The two books were written in one year.

lessons.title: 285. The present passive: يُكْتَب · يُفْتَح
lessons.subtitle: تُكْتَب الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنَ الْيَمِين إِلَى الْيَسَار

explanations.title: Prefix with ḍamma, middle letter with fatḥa
explanations.body: In the present, the passive has a ḍamma on the prefix and a fatḥa on the second root letter: يَكْتُب (he writes) becomes يُكْتَب (it is written). The endings stay the same.

explanations.title: General facts
explanations.body: The passive present is perfect for facts about how things are done or where things can be found, without naming a doer. These sentences are simple facts.

examples.text: تُكْتَب الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنَ الْيَمِين إِلَى الْيَسَار.
examples.translation: tuktab al-ʿarabiyya mina al-yamīn ʾilā al-yasār. — Arabic is written from right to left.
yuftaḥ al-matḥaf fī at-tāsiʿa ṣabāḥan. — The museum is opened at nine in the morning.
tuqraʾ al-jarīda kull yawm. — The newspaper is read every day.
yusmaʿ aṣ-ṣawt min baʿīd. — The sound is heard from far away.
tuftaḥ al-maḥallāt fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The shops are opened in the morning.
satuktab ar-risāla ghadan. — The letter will be written tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Which is the present passive of يَكْتُب?
Which is the present passive of يَفْتَح?
exercises.explanation: ḍamma on the prefix, fatḥa on the middle.

exercises.prompt: What does تُقْرَأ الْجَرِيدَة كُلّ يَوْم mean?
options: She reads the newspaper every day
The newspaper is read every day

exercises.prompt: What does تُكْتَب الْعَرَبِيَّة مِنَ الْيَمِين إِلَى الْيَسَار mean?
options: Arabic writes from left to right
Arabic is written from right to left
Arabic was written in the north

exercises.prompt: Why is it تُفْتَح الْمَحَلَّات, not يُفْتَح؟
options: a plural of things takes the feminine singular

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is in the future?

exercises.promptTranslation: The museum is opened at nine in the morning.

exercises.explanation: Things in the plural → feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: The shops are opened in the morning.
The sound is heard from far away.

lessons.title: 286. Passive of hollow, defective and assimilated verbs
lessons.subtitle: قِيلَ · بِيعَ · بُنِيَ · وُجِدَ

explanations.title: Verbs with a weak letter follow their own patterns
explanations.body: Hollow verbs (middle و or ي) have a long ī in the passive past: قَالَ becomes قِيلَ, and بَاعَ becomes بِيعَ. In the present they have a long ā: يُقَال, يُبَاع. Defective verbs end in a long ā or a short ī: بَنَى becomes بُنِيَ, يُبْنَى. Assimilated verbs bring back their و: وَجَدَ becomes وُجِدَ and يُوجَد.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: يُوجَد is very common and means “there is” or “there exists”. يُقَال إِنَّ… means “it is said that…”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: yūjad maṭʿam qarīb mina al-funduq. — There is a restaurant close to the hotel.

examples.text: بُنِيَ هَذَا الْمَسْجِد قَبْل مِئَة سَنَة.
examples.translation: buniya hādhā al-masjid qabl miʾa sana. — This mosque was built a hundred years ago.
tubāʿ al-fawākih fī as-sūq. — Fruit is sold in the market.
bīʿa al-bayt al-qadīm ʾams. — The old house was sold yesterday.
wujidati al-ḥaqība fī al-maṭār. — The bag was found at the airport.

examples.text: يُقَال إِنَّ الطَّقْس جَمِيل فِي الرَّبِيع.
examples.translation: yuqāl ʾinna aṭ-ṭaqs jamīl fī ar-rabīʿ. — It is said that the weather is lovely in spring.

exercises.prompt: Which is the passive past of قَالَ?
Which is the passive past of بَاعَ?
Which is the passive present of وَجَدَ?
exercises.explanation: The و returns in the passive.

exercises.prompt: What does يُوجَد مَطْعَم قَرِيب مِنَ الْفُنْدُق mean?
options: There is a restaurant close to the hotel

exercises.prompt: What does بُنِيَ هَذَا الْمَسْجِد قَبْل مِئَة سَنَة mean?
options: This mosque was built a hundred years ago
This mosque will be built soon

exercises.explanation: يُقَال إِنَّ = it is said that.
Things in the plural → feminine singular, passive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Fruit is sold in the market.
This mosque was built a hundred years ago.
The bag was found at the airport.

explanations.title: When Arabic uses the passive
explanations.body: Choose the passive when the doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious, and in news and general descriptions. A few passive verbs are so common that you should learn them as phrases: يُسَمَّى (is called), يُعْرَف بِـ (is known for), يُسْتَخْدَم (is used).

explanations.title: Descriptions
explanations.body: These sentences describe well-known things in a simple way.

examples.translation: tusammā al-qāhira madīna al-ʾalf miʾdhana. — Cairo is called the city of a thousand minarets.
yuʿraf an-nīl biṭūlihi. — The Nile is known for its length.
yustakhdam al-hātif fī kull makān. — The telephone is used everywhere.

examples.text: تُسْتَخْدَم الْعَرَبِيَّة فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْبِلَاد.
examples.translation: tustakhdam al-ʿarabiyya fī kathīr mina al-bilād. — Arabic is used in many countries.
yuʿraf hādhā al-maṭʿam bil-qahwa al-jayyida. — This restaurant is known for good coffee.
yuqāl ʾinna al-madīna qadīma jiddan. — It is said that the city is very old.

exercises.prompt: What does يُعْرَف النِّيل بِطُولِهِ mean?
options: The Nile is known for its length

exercises.prompt: What does تُسْتَخْدَم الْعَرَبِيَّة فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْبِلَاد mean?
options: Arabic is used in many countries

exercises.prompt: When is the passive a good choice?
options: when the doer is unknown or unimportant

exercises.explanation: Cairo is feminine; it receives the name.
exercises.promptTranslation: Cairo is called the city of a thousand minarets.
The Nile is known for its length.
The telephone is used everywhere.

explanations.title: It happened by itself
explanations.body: Measure VII has the pattern اِنْفَعَلَ: add اِنْ before the root. It describes something that happens to a thing without a doer: كَسَرَ (he broke) → اِنْكَسَرَ (it broke). The meaning is a bit like the passive, but the vowels are those of an active verb, not the passive pattern, and no doer is mentioned. The present is يَنْفَعِل.

explanations.title: Compare I and VII
explanations.body: A transitive Measure I verb needs a doer. Measure VII does not: the door simply opened.

examples.translation: fataḥa al-muwaẓẓaf al-bāb. — The employee opened the door.
infataḥa al-bāb. — The door opened.
inkasara az-zujāj. — The glass broke.
inqaṭaʿa aṭ-ṭarīq bisabab al-maṭar. — The road was cut off because of the rain.
inṭalaqati aṭ-ṭāʾira fī al-ʿāshira. — The plane set off at ten.
inqalabati as-sayyāra ʿalā aṭ-ṭarīq. — The car overturned on the road.

exercises.prompt: Which is the Measure VII verb of كَسَرَ?

options: The door was opened by him

exercises.prompt: What does اِنْطَلَقَتِ الطَّائِرَة فِي الْعَاشِرَة mean?
options: The plane set off at ten
The plane was sold at ten

exercises.prompt: Which of these is Measure VII?
What is the present of اِنْكَسَرَ?

exercises.promptTranslation: The glass broke.
The door opened.
The plane set off at ten.

lessons.title: 289. Verbal nouns of Measure VII: اِنْفِعَال
lessons.subtitle: اِنْطِلَاق · اِنْقِطَاع · اِنْفِتَاح · اِنْقِلَاب

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: The verbal noun of Measure VII is اِنْفِعَال: a kasra on the first root letter and a long ā before the last root letter. It names the event: اِنْطَلَقَ (set off) gives اِنْطِلَاق (departure, launch).

explanations.title: Verbal nouns in sentences
explanations.body: Like any verbal noun, these can follow بَعْد or قَبْل, and be the first word of a phrase with another noun after it.

examples.translation: baʿd inṭilāq ar-riḥla qaraʾtu al-jarīda. — After the flight’s departure I read the newspaper.
sabab inqiṭāʿ aṭ-ṭarīq huwa al-maṭar. — The reason the road is cut off is the rain.
infitāḥ al-ʾaswāq muhimm lil-balad. — The opening up of markets is important for the country.
inkisār az-zujāj kāna bisabab ar-rīḥ. — The breaking of the glass was because of the wind.
inqiṭāʿ al-māʾ mushkila kabīra. — A cut in the water supply is a big problem.
qabl inṭilāq aṭ-ṭāʾira nughliq al-ʾabwāb. — Before the plane sets off we close the doors.

exercises.prompt: Which is the verbal noun of اِنْطَلَقَ?
Which is the verbal noun of اِنْقَطَعَ?
Which one is a Measure VII verbal noun?
What does اِنْقِطَاع الْمَاء مُشْكِلَة كَبِيرَة mean?
options: A cut in the water supply is a big problem

exercises.prompt: What does بَعْد اِنْطِلَاق الرِّحْلَة mean?
Which pattern is the Measure VII verbal noun?

exercises.promptTranslation: After the flight’s departure I read the newspaper.
The opening up of markets is important for the country.
Before the plane sets off we close the doors.

lessons.title: 290. Where is it? تَقَع فِي…
lessons.subtitle: تَقَع مِصْر فِي شَمَال شَرْق أَفْرِيقِيَا

explanations.title: Compass words and the verb “lie”
explanations.body: The four directions are شَمَال (north), جَنُوب (south), شَرْق (east) and غَرْب (west). Put two together for a corner: شَمَال شَرْق (north-east). To say where a place lies, use the assimilated verb وَقَعَ: يَقَع (masculine) or تَقَع (feminine), followed by فِي or عَلَى. Many country names are treated as feminine (مِصْر, السُّعُودِيَّة), but some as masculine (الْمَغْرِب, الْيَمَن). Learn each one, or say دَوْلَة + تَقَع.

explanations.title: Where in the Arab world
explanations.body: These are simple, well-known facts about where places lie.

examples.text: تَقَع مِصْر فِي شَمَال شَرْق أَفْرِيقِيَا.
examples.translation: taqaʿ miṣr fī shamāl sharq ʾafrīqiyā. — Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa.

examples.text: يَقَع الْمَغْرِب فِي شَمَال غَرْب أَفْرِيقِيَا.
examples.translation: yaqaʿ al-maghrib fī shamāl gharb ʾafrīqiyā. — Morocco lies in the north-west of Africa.

examples.text: تَقَع السُّعُودِيَّة فِي شِبْه الْجَزِيرَة الْعَرَبِيَّة.
examples.translation: taqaʿ as-suʿūdiyya fī shibh al-jazīra al-ʿarabiyya. — Saudi Arabia lies in the Arabian Peninsula.
taqaʿ al-kuwayt ʿalā al-khalīj al-ʿarabiyy. — Kuwait lies on the Arabian Gulf .
taqaʿ tūnis bayn al-jazāʾir walībiyā. — Tunisia lies between Algeria and Libya.

examples.text: يَقَع الْيَمَن فِي جَنُوب شِبْه الْجَزِيرَة.
examples.translation: yaqaʿ al-yaman fī janūb shibh al-jazīra. — Yemen lies in the south of the peninsula.

exercises.prompt: What does تَقَع تُونِس بَيْن الْجَزَائِر وَلِيبِيَا mean?
options: Tunisia lies between Algeria and Libya
Algeria and Libya border Tunisia’s sea

exercises.prompt: What does the و of وَقَعَ do in يَقَع?
What does تَقَع الْكُوَيْت عَلَى الْخَلِيج الْعَرَبِيّ mean?
options: Kuwait lies on the Arabian Gulf
Kuwait is far from the Gulf

exercises.promptTranslation: Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa.
Tunisia lies between Algeria and Libya.

exercises.explanation: Yemen is at the southern end.
exercises.promptTranslation: Yemen lies in the south of the peninsula.

lessons.title: 291. Seas, rivers, deserts and mountains
lessons.subtitle: الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر · نَهْر النِّيل · الصَّحْرَاء الْكُبْرَى

explanations.title: Landforms and waters
explanations.body: Learn the type of feature first, then its name. A sea is بَحْر, an ocean مُحِيط, a gulf خَلِيج, a river نَهْر, a desert صَحْرَاء, a mountain جَبَل (plural جِبَال), a coast سَاحِل, an island جَزِيرَة and a canal قَنَاة.

explanations.title: Facts about the region
explanations.body: Two familiar verbs appear in descriptions: تَصِل (it connects, from وَصَلَ) and يَمُرّ (it passes, from مَرَّ). All of these are simple, widely known facts.

examples.text: تَصِل قَنَاة السُّوَيْس الْبَحْر الْمُتَوَسِّط بِالْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.
examples.translation: taṣil qanāh as-suways al-baḥr al-mutawassiṭ bil-baḥr al-ʾaḥmar. — The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
yamurr nahr an-nīl fī miṣr. — The Nile flows through Egypt.

examples.text: فِي الْعِرَاق نَهْرَان كَبِيرَان: دِجْلَة وَالْفُرَات.
examples.translation: fī al-ʿirāq nahrān kabīrān: dijla wal-furāt. — In Iraq there are two big rivers: the Tigris and the Euphrates.
aṣ-ṣaḥrāʾ al-kubrā fī shamāl ʾafrīqiyā. — The Sahara is in the north of Africa.

examples.text: الْبَحْر الَّذِي بَيْن أَفْرِيقِيَا وَآسِيَا هُوَ الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.
examples.translation: al-baḥr alladhī bayn ʾafrīqiyā waʾāsiyā huwa al-baḥr al-ʾaḥmar. — The sea that lies between Africa and Asia is the Red Sea.
tūjad jibāl al-ʾaṭlas fī al-maghrib. — The Atlas Mountains are found in Morocco.

exercises.prompt: What does يَمُرّ نَهْر النِّيل فِي مِصْر mean?
options: The Nile is in the sea

exercises.prompt: What does تُوجَد جِبَال الْأَطْلَس فِي الْمَغْرِب mean?
options: The Atlas Mountains are found in Morocco
The mountains are far from Morocco

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun goes with الْبَحْر (the sea)?
تَصِل قَنَاة السُّوَيْس الْبَحْر الْمُتَوَسِّط بِالْبَحْر ___.
exercises.explanation: The canal joins the Mediterranean to the Red Sea.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
The Nile flows through Egypt.

exercises.explanation: The Sahara lies in the north.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Sahara is in the north of Africa.

explanations.title: What a profile tells you
explanations.body: A country profile answers a few questions: Where is it? What is its capital? Which languages are official? What are its main features? Morocco is a good model, because it uses most of the words of the chapter. The facts below are standard reference facts.

explanations.title: The profile in sentences
explanations.body: Notice تَقَع (it lies), تُوجَد (is found) and الَّتِي after a feminine noun.

examples.text: الْمَغْرِب دَوْلَة عَرَبِيَّة تَقَع فِي شَمَال غَرْب أَفْرِيقِيَا.
examples.translation: al-maghrib dawla ʿarabiyya taqaʿ fī shamāl gharb ʾafrīqiyā. — Morocco is an Arab country that lies in the north-west of Africa.

examples.text: لَهَا سَاحِل عَلَى الْمُحِيط الْأَطْلَسِيّ وَسَاحِل عَلَى الْبَحْر الْمُتَوَسِّط.
examples.translation: lahā sāḥil ʿalā al-muḥīṭ al-ʾaṭlasiyy wasāḥil ʿalā al-baḥr al-mutawassiṭ. — It has a coast on the Atlantic Ocean and a coast on the Mediterranean Sea.
ʿāṣima al-maghrib hiya ar-ribāṭ. — The capital of Morocco is Rabat.
al-lughatān ar-rasmiyyatān humā al-ʿarabiyya wal-ʾamāzīghiyya. — The two official languages are Arabic and Amazigh.

examples.text: تُوجَد جِبَال الْأَطْلَس فِي وَسَط الْبِلَاد.
examples.translation: tūjad jibāl al-ʾaṭlas fī wasaṭ al-bilād. — The Atlas Mountains are found in the middle of the country.
al-ʿumla allatī tustakhdam hiya ad-dirham. — The currency that is used is the dirham.

exercises.prompt: What is the capital of Morocco?
Which two languages are official in Morocco?
Which mountains are found in the middle of Morocco?
Which two bodies of water meet Morocco’s coasts?
options: the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea
the Gulf and the Black Sea
the Nile and the Suez Canal
the Red Sea and the Gulf

exercises.prompt: Why is it الْعُمْلَة الَّتِي تُسْتَخْدَم؟
exercises.explanation: الَّتِي for a feminine singular noun.

exercises.prompt: الْمَغْرِب دَوْلَة عَرَبِيَّة ___ فِي شَمَال غَرْب أَفْرِيقِيَا.
exercises.promptTranslation: Morocco is an Arab country that lies in the north-west of Africa.

exercises.explanation: A plural of things: feminine singular, passive.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Atlas Mountains are found in the middle of the country.
The capital of Morocco is Rabat.

lessons.title: 293. Review: pronouns, passive and Measure VII
lessons.subtitle: الْكِتَاب الَّذِي فُتِحَ · الْبَاب الَّذِي اِنْفَتَحَ

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: (1) A definite noun takes a relative pronoun that matches it: الَّذِي, الَّتِي, اللَّذَان, اللَّتَان, الَّذِين, اللَّاتِي; plural things take الَّتِي. (2) If the noun is the object of a verb or preposition inside the clause (not its subject), add a returning pronoun. (3) The passive past has ḍamma and kasra (كُتِبَ); the passive present has ḍamma and fatḥa (يُكْتَب). (4) Measure VII is اِنْفَعَلَ, with no doer, and its verbal noun is اِنْفِعَال.

explanations.title: Mixed sentences
explanations.body: Each of these combines two ideas from the chapter. They are invented.

examples.text: الْمَسْجِد الَّذِي بُنِيَ قَبْل سَنَوَات قَدِيم.
examples.translation: al-masjid alladhī buniya qabl sanawāt qadīm. — The mosque that was built years ago is old.
al-kutub allatī kutibat bil-ʿarabiyya muhimma. — The books that were written in Arabic are important.
az-zujāj alladhī inkasara kāna jadīdan. — The glass that broke was new.

examples.text: الْمَدِينَة الَّتِي زُرْتُهَا تَقَع عَلَى السَّاحِل.
examples.translation: al-madīna allatī zurtuhā taqaʿ ʿalā as-sāḥil. — The city I visited lies on the coast.

examples.text: الْمُهَنْدِسَان اللَّذَان بَنَيَا الْجِسْر مِنْ لُبْنَان.
examples.translation: al-muhandisān alladhān banayā al-jisr min lubnān. — The two engineers who built the bridge are from Lebanon.
baʿd inqiṭāʿ aṭ-ṭarīq taʾakhkharati al-ḥāfilāt. — After the road was cut off, the buses were late.

exercises.prompt: Which fits الْمُهَنْدِسَان (the two engineers, subject)?
What does الزُّجَاج الَّذِي اِنْكَسَرَ كَانَ جَدِيدًا mean?
options: The new glass was broken by him
The glass that broke was new

exercises.prompt: What does the returning pronoun ـهَا do in الْمَدِينَة الَّتِي زُرْتُهَا؟
options: it points back to the city

exercises.promptTranslation: The books that were written in Arabic are important.
The city I visited lies on the coast.
After the road was cut off, the buses were late.

units.title: الْعَادَات وَالتَّقَالِيد: customs, defective verbs and Measures VIII and X

lessons.title: 294. Defective verbs: three families
lessons.subtitle: مَشَى ← يَمْشِي · دَعَا ← يَدْعُو · نَسِيَ ← يَنْسَى

explanations.title: A weak letter at the end
explanations.body: Verbs whose last root letter is weak (و or ي) are called defective. In the past they end in ـَى, ـَا or ـِيَ: مَشَى, دَعَا, نَسِيَ. A few family 3 verbs, such as سَعَى, end in ـَى in the past, like family 1, so always learn a verb together with its present form. To find the present, you need to know the family. There are three main families, and you learn each verb with its present form.

explanations.title: Reading the family from the present
explanations.body: Family 1 ends in ـِي in the present, family 2 in ـُو, family 3 in ـَى. The vowel before the last letter matches: kasra, ḍamma, fatḥa.

examples.translation: yamshī ʾakhī ʾilā al-madrasa. — My brother walks to school.
banā jaddī baytan kabīran. — My grandfather built a big house.
yadʿū ṣadīqī ʾahlahu ʾilā al-ḥafla. — My friend invites his family to the party.
nasiya ar-rākib ḥaqībatahu. — The passenger forgot his bag.
yabqā al-walad fī al-bayt. — The boy stays at home.
laqiya al-muhandis ṣadīqan qadīman. — The engineer met an old friend.

exercises.prompt: Which is the present of مَشَى?
Which is the present of دَعَا?
Which is the present of نَسِيَ?
Which is the present of بَنَى?
What does بَنَى جَدِّي بَيْتًا كَبِيرًا mean?
options: My grandfather forgot a big house
My grandfather built a big house
My grandfather walked to a big house
My grandfather sold a big house

exercises.prompt: What does يَبْقَى الْوَلَد فِي الْبَيْت mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: My brother walks to school.
My friend invites his family to the party.
The boy stays at home.

lessons.title: 295. The past of مَشَى: every person
lessons.subtitle: مَشَى · مَشَتْ · مَشَيْتُ · مَشَوْا

explanations.title: What happens to the last letter
explanations.body: In مَشَى the last letter is a long ā written ى. Before the endings it changes: it disappears before تْ (مَشَتْ), becomes ي before an ending that starts with a consonant (مَشَيْتُ), and becomes و before the plural ـوا (مَشَوْا). The two-person forms keep the ي: مَشَيَا.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: The same changes happen with every verb of family 1, such as بَنَى and رَمَى.

examples.translation: mashaytu ʾilā al-maḥaṭṭa fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — I walked to the station in the morning.
mashati al-bint ʾilā al-madrasa. — The girl walked to school.
mashaw ʾilā al-bayt maʿan. — They walked home together.
mashaynā fī al-ḥadīqa sāʿa. — We walked in the park for an hour.
banaytu baytan ṣaghīran. — I built a small house.
banaw masjidan jadīdan. — They built a new mosque.

exercises.explanation: The ى becomes ي before تُ.

exercises.prompt: What does مَشَوْا إِلَى الْبَيْت مَعًا mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I walked to the station in the morning.
They walked home together.
We walked in the park for an hour.

lessons.title: 296. The past of دَعَا and نَسِيَ
lessons.subtitle: دَعَوْتُ · دَعَوْا · نَسِيتُ · نَسُوا

explanations.title: Two more patterns
explanations.body: Family 2 (دَعَا) keeps a و where family 1 had ي: دَعَوْتُ, دَعَوْا. Family 3 verbs like نَسِيَ end in ـِيَ, and the ي stays long before the endings: نَسِيتُ (a few, like سَعَى, behave like family 1 in the past). Only the plural he-form is special: نَسُوا, with a ḍamma.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Notice that the doer of دَعَا can be followed by a pronoun ending: دَعَانِي means “he invited me”.

examples.translation: daʿawtu ʾaṣdiqāʾī ʾilā al-ḥafla. — I invited my friends to the party.
daʿatnī ṣadīqatī ʾilā baytihā. — My friend invited me to her home.
daʿawnā aḍ-ḍuyūf ʾilā al-ʿashāʾ. — We invited the guests to dinner.
nasītu ismahu. — I forgot his name.
nasū al-mawʿid. — They forgot the appointment.
nasīnā al-ḥaqāʾib fī baytī. — We forgot the bags at my house.

exercises.prompt: What does دَعَتْنِي صَدِيقَتِي إِلَى بَيْتِهَا mean?
options: I invited my friend to her home
My friend invited me to her home

exercises.prompt: What does نَسِينَا الْحَقَائِب فِي بَيْتِي mean?
options: We carried the bags to the car
We forgot the bags at my house

exercises.promptTranslation: I invited my friends to the party.
I forgot his name.
They forgot the appointment.

lessons.title: 297. The present of يَمْشِي: every person
lessons.subtitle: أَمْشِي · تَمْشِين · تَمْشُون · يَمْشُون

explanations.title: Prefixes as usual, endings with a twist
explanations.body: The prefixes are the usual أَ تَ يَ نَ. The last letter ي stays in the singular forms: أَمْشِي, تَمْشِي, يَمْشِي. For they-men and you-men the ي turns into the plural ـُون: يَمْشُون. For you-woman and the two feminine plurals the ending is ـِين: تَمْشِين. Notice that أَنْتِ and أَنْتُنَّ have the same form.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Family 1 verbs such as يَبْنِي and يَرْمِي follow exactly the same pattern.

examples.translation: ʾamshī ʾilā al-ʿamal kull yawm. — I walk to work every day.
hal tamshīn ʾilā al-madrasa? — Do you walk to school? (to a woman)
namshī fī al-masāʾ baʿd al-ʿashāʾ. — We walk in the evening after dinner.
yamshūn ʾilā al-masjid maʿan. — They walk to the mosque together.
yabnī al-ʿummāl baytan jadīdan. — The workers are building a new house.
yarmī al-walad al-kura. — The boy throws the ball.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ تَمْشِين إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة؟ ask?
options: Do you (a woman) walk to school?

exercises.prompt: Which two pronouns share the form تَمْشِين?

exercises.promptTranslation: I walk to work every day.
They walk to the mosque together.
We walk in the evening after dinner.

lessons.title: 298. The present of يَدْعُو and يَنْسَى
lessons.subtitle: أَدْعُو · تَدْعِين · يَنْسَوْن · يَنْسَيْن

explanations.title: Families 2 and 3 side by side
explanations.body: Family 2 (يَدْعُو) keeps ـُو in most forms and changes to ـِين for you-woman. Family 3 (يَنْسَى) has ـَى in most singular forms, ـَوْن for men in the plural, and ـَيْن for you-woman and the feminine plurals. Remember too: لَنْ + present means “will not”. A real quirk of family 2: they-men and they-women look identical, يَدْعُون.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Context tells you who is meant when a form is shared.

examples.translation: ʾadʿū ʾaṣdiqāʾī ʾilā al-ʿashāʾ. — I invite my friends to dinner.
hal tadʿīn ʾummaki ʾilā al-ḥafla? — Do you invite your mother to the party? (to a woman)
yadʿūn aḍ-ḍuyūf ʾilā al-bayt. — They invite the guests to the house.
ʾansā isma al-funduq dāʾiman. — I always forget the name of the hotel.
tansā aṭ-ṭāliba kitābahā ʾaḥyānan. — The student sometimes forgets her book.
lā yansawn mawʿida al-ḥafla. — They do not forget the time of the party.

exercises.prompt: Which form is shared by “they (m.) invite” and “they (f.) invite”?
What does تَنْسَى الطَّالِبَة كِتَابَهَا أَحْيَانًا mean?
options: The student sometimes forgets her book
The student always remembers her book

exercises.promptTranslation: I invite my friends to dinner.
Do you invite your mother to the party? (to a woman)
They do not forget the time of the party.

lessons.title: 299. Defective verbs: future, negation, commands
lessons.subtitle: لَا تَنْسَ! · اِمْشِ · اُدْعُ · لَمْ يَمْشِ

explanations.title: The weak ending shortens
explanations.body: For the future, add سَـ to the present: سَأَمْشِي. After لَمْ, and in the command, the long final vowel drops: لَمْ يَمْشِ (he did not walk), لَمْ يَدْعُ (he did not invite), لَمْ يَنْسَ (he did not forget). The command is the short form without the prefix: اِمْشِ (walk!), اُدْعُ (invite!), اِنْسَ (forget!). For a woman and a group, the long vowel returns: اِمْشِي, اِمْشُوا (family 3 verbs end in ـَيْ and ـَوْا).

explanations.title: Everyday phrases
explanations.body: لَا تَنْسَ is the verb you will hear most: “don’t forget!”.

examples.translation: saʾamshī ʾilā al-madrasa ghadan. — I will walk to school tomorrow.
lam yadʿu ʾakhī aḍ-ḍuyūf. — My brother did not invite the guests.
lā tansa mawʿida al-ḥafla! — Do not forget the time of the party! (to a man)
lā tansay jawāza safariki! — Do not forget your passport! (to a woman)
udʿu ṣadīqaka ʾilā al-bayt. — Invite your friend to the house. (to a man)
imshū bisurʿa! — Walk quickly! (to a group)

exercises.prompt: Which is the command “walk!” to a man?
Which is “do not forget” to a woman?
What does سَأَمْشِي إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة غَدًا mean?
options: I do not walk to school
I will walk to school tomorrow

exercises.explanation: A man: the long vowel drops.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do not forget the time of the party! (to a man)
Invite your friend to the house. (to a man)
Walk quickly! (to a group)

lessons.title: 300. A story with defective verbs: an invitation
lessons.subtitle: دَعَانِي صَدِيقِي إِلَى حَفْلَة

explanations.title: Pronoun endings on defective verbs
explanations.body: A verb can take an object pronoun directly: دَعَانِي (he invited me), دَعَاهُ (he invited him), دَعَاهَا (he invited her). The ending of the verb stays as it was: دَعَا + نِي. For a verb in the تْ form the pattern is دَعَتْنِي (she invited me).

explanations.title: An invitation (an invented practice text)
explanations.body: A person tells what happened. Read it through once, then answer the questions.

examples.text: دَعَانِي صَدِيقِي أَحْمَد إِلَى حَفْلَة فِي بَيْتِهِ.
examples.translation: daʿānī ṣadīqī ʾaḥmad ʾilā ḥafla fī baytihi. — My friend Ahmad invited me to a party at his house.
mashaytu ʾilā baytihi maʿa ʾakhī. — I walked to his house with my brother.
laqiyanā ʾaḥmad ʿinda al-bāb. — Ahmad met us at the door.
nasītu al-hadiyya fī baytī! — I forgot the gift at my house!

examples.text: رَجَعْتُ وَأَخَذْتُهَا، ثُمَّ بَقِينَا فِي الْحَفْلَة حَتَّى الْمَسَاء.
examples.translation: rajaʿtu waʾakhadhtuhā, thumma baqīnā fī al-ḥafla ḥattā al-masāʾ. — I went back and took it, and then we stayed at the party until evening.
lan ʾansā hādhihi al-ḥafla. — I will not forget this party.

exercises.prompt: How did they get to the house?

exercises.promptTranslation: My friend Ahmad invited me to a party.
I forgot the gift at my house!
I will not forget this party.

lessons.title: 301. Measure VIII: اِفْتَعَلَ
lessons.subtitle: جَمَعَ ← اِجْتَمَعَ · نَظَرَ ← اِنْتَظَرَ · سَمِعَ ← اِسْتَمَعَ

explanations.title: A ت tucked in after the first letter
explanations.body: Measure VIII has the pattern اِفْتَعَلَ: an alif with kasra, then the first root letter with sukūn, then a ت with fatḥa, then the other two root letters with fatḥa. Its meaning often shows that the action involves the doer himself, or happens between people: جَمَعَ (he gathered something) → اِجْتَمَعَ (he met, came together).

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Look out for اِسْتَمَعَ: it begins with اِسْتَ like Measure X, but the س is the first root letter, so it is Measure VIII. These sentences are invented.

examples.translation: ijtamaʿa al-mudīr maʿa al-muwaẓẓafīn. — The director met with the employees.
intaẓartu al-ḥāfila sāʿa. — I waited for the bus for an hour.
istamaʿnā ʾilā al-ʾakhbār. — We listened to the news.
irtafaʿa as-siʿr fī al-maṭār. — The price at the airport rose.
ishtaghala ʾabī fī maṣnaʿ. — My father worked in a factory.
ijtamaʿati al-ʿāʾila fī al-bayt. — The family got together at home.

exercises.prompt: Which is the Measure VIII verb from جَمَعَ?
Which letter is inserted after the first root letter in Measure VIII?
Why is اِسْتَمَعَ Measure VIII, not X?
options: the س is the first root letter
exercises.explanation: Its first root letter is س, from سَمِعَ.

exercises.promptTranslation: The director met with the employees.

exercises.explanation: I waited: Measure VIII, past, I.
exercises.promptTranslation: I waited for the bus for an hour.
My father worked in a factory.

explanations.title: Prefix + the Measure VIII stem
explanations.body: The present is the prefix, the first root letter with sukūn, ت with fatḥa, the second root letter with a kasra, and then the last root letter: يَنْتَظِر, يَجْتَمِع, يَسْتَمِع. The same endings are added as for every present verb. The command drops the prefix and puts اِ in front: اِنْتَظِرْ (wait!).

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Other Measure VIII verbs follow the same plan.

examples.translation: ʾantaẓir ṣadīqī fī al-maṭār. — I am waiting for my friend at the airport.
hal tantaẓirīn al-ḥāfila? — Are you waiting for the bus? (to a woman)
yajtamiʿ al-muwaẓẓafūn kull ʾusbūʿ. — The employees meet every week.
nastamiʿ ʾilā al-ʾakhbār fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — We listen to the news in the morning.
intaẓir qalīlan min faḍlik! — Wait a little, please! (to a man)
lā tantaẓirū ṭawīlan. — Do not wait long. (to a group)

exercises.prompt: Which is the command “wait!” to a man?
What does لَا تَنْتَظِرُوا طَوِيلًا mean?
options: Do not wait long (to a group)

exercises.prompt: What does نَسْتَمِع إِلَى الْأَخْبَار mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I am waiting for my friend at the airport.
Wait a little, please! (to a man)
The employees meet every week.

lessons.title: 303. Measure X: اِسْتَفْعَلَ
lessons.subtitle: خَدَمَ ← اِسْتَخْدَمَ · قَبِلَ ← اِسْتَقْبَلَ · عَمِلَ ← اِسْتَعْمَلَ

explanations.title: Adding اِسْتَ
explanations.body: Measure X has the pattern اِسْتَفْعَلَ: put اِسْتَ in front of the three root letters: the first root letter has sukūn, and the second and third have fatḥa. It often means to ask for, to seek or to put something to use: خَدَمَ (he served) → اِسْتَخْدَمَ (he put to service, used).

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Some very common verbs are Measure X with a weak middle letter, such as اِسْتَطَاعَ (he was able). You will meet them as phrases first. These sentences are invented.

examples.translation: istakhdamtu al-hātif fī al-maṭār. — I used the phone at the airport.
istaqbala al-funduq as-suyyāḥ. — The hotel welcomed the tourists.
istaʿmala al-muwaẓẓaf jihāzan jadīdan. — The employee used a new device.
istaqbalatnā al-mudīra bil-qahwa. — The manager welcomed us with coffee.
istarjaʿtu ḥaqībatī baʿd sāʿa. — I got my bag back after an hour.

examples.text: اِسْتَطَاعَ الرَّاكِب أَنْ يَصِل فِي الْوَقْت.
examples.translation: istaṭāʿa ar-rākib ʾan yaṣil fī al-waqt. — The passenger was able to arrive on time.

exercises.prompt: Which is the Measure X verb from خَدَمَ?
What does Measure X often mean?
options: to ask for, seek or put to use

exercises.prompt: What is the pattern of Measure X?

exercises.promptTranslation: The hotel welcomed the tourists.

exercises.explanation: I used: Measure X, past, I.
exercises.promptTranslation: I used the phone at the airport.
The employee used a new device.

explanations.title: Same plan as Measure VIII
explanations.body: The present is the prefix with fatḥa, then سْتَ, the three root letters, and a kasra before the last one: يَسْتَخْدِم, يَسْتَقْبِل, يَسْتَعْمِل. The command drops the prefix and puts اِ in front: اِسْتَخْدِمْ (use!).

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: These sentences use the present of Measure X.

examples.translation: ʾastakhdim al-ḥāsūb kull yawm. — I use the computer every day.
tastaqbil al-fanādiq as-suyyāḥ fī aṣ-ṣayf. — Hotels welcome tourists in the summer.
yastaʿmil ʾakhī hātifī ʾaḥyānan. — My brother sometimes uses my phone.
hal tastakhdimīn al-ḥāfila? — Do you use the bus? (to a woman)
istakhdim hādhihi al-biṭāqa hunā. — Use this card here. (to a man)
lā tastakhdimū al-hātif fī aṭ-ṭāʾira. — Do not use the phone on the plane. (to a group)

exercises.prompt: Which is the command “use!” to a man?
What does لَا تَسْتَخْدِمُوا الْهَاتِف فِي الطَّائِرَة mean?
options: He does not use the phone
Use the phone on the plane
Do not use the phone on the plane (to a group)

exercises.prompt: What does تَسْتَقْبِل الْفَنَادِق السُّيَّاح mean?
Why is it تَسْتَقْبِل الْفَنَادِق, not يَسْتَقْبِل؟
options: a plural of things takes the feminine singular
exercises.explanation: A plural of things (الْفَنَادِق) takes the feminine singular verb.

exercises.promptTranslation: I use the computer every day.

exercises.explanation: Things in the plural: feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: Hotels welcome tourists in the summer.
Use this card here. (to a man)

lessons.title: 305. Verbal nouns of Measure VIII: اِفْتِعَال
lessons.subtitle: اِجْتِمَاع · اِنْتِظَار · اِحْتِفَال · اِرْتِفَاع

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: The verbal noun of Measure VIII is اِفْتِعَال: kasra under the ت, then a long ā before the last root letter. اِجْتَمَعَ gives اِجْتِمَاع (meeting), اِنْتَظَرَ gives اِنْتِظَار (waiting).

explanations.title: In use
explanations.body: The nouns are everyday words: you will see صَالَة اِنْتِظَار (waiting room), اِجْتِمَاع (meeting) and اِرْتِفَاع الْأَسْعَار (the rise in prices).

examples.translation: al-mudīr fī ijtimāʿ al-ʾān. — The director is in a meeting now.
najlis fī ṣāla al-intiẓār. — We sit in the waiting room.
irtifāʿ al-ʾasʿār mushkila kabīra. — The rise in prices is a big problem.
al-istimāʿ ʾilā al-ʾakhbār mufīd. — Listening to the news is useful.
al-iḥtifāl bil-ʿīd fī al-madīna kabīr. — The Eid celebration in the city is big.
maʿa iqtirāb ash-shitāʾ yanzil al-maṭar. — As winter approaches, the rain falls.

exercises.prompt: Which is the verbal noun of اِجْتَمَعَ?
Which is the verbal noun of اِنْتَظَرَ?
Which pattern is the verbal noun of Measure VIII?

exercises.promptTranslation: The director is in a meeting now.
The rise in prices is a big problem.
We sit in the waiting room.

lessons.title: 306. Verbal nouns of Measure X: اِسْتِفْعَال
lessons.subtitle: اِسْتِخْدَام · اِسْتِقْبَال · اِسْتِعْمَال

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: The verbal noun of Measure X is اِسْتِفْعَال: kasra under the ت and a long ā before the last root letter. اِسْتَخْدَمَ gives اِسْتِخْدَام (use), اِسْتَقْبَلَ gives اِسْتِقْبَال (reception, welcome).

explanations.title: Signs and phrases
explanations.body: These nouns appear on signs: مَكْتَب الِاسْتِقْبَال (reception desk), طَرِيقَة الِاسْتِعْمَال (directions for use), اِسْتِخْدَام الْهَاتِف مَمْنُوع (use of the phone is forbidden).

examples.translation: maktab al-istiqbāl fī aṭ-ṭābiq al-ʾawwal. — The reception desk is on the first floor.
ṭarīqa al-istiʿmāl maktūba ʿalā al-ʿulba. — The directions for use are written on the box.
istikhdām al-hātif mamnūʿ fī aṭ-ṭāʾira. — Using the phone is forbidden on the plane.
istiqbāl al-funduq kāna jamīlan. — The hotel’s welcome was lovely.
istirjāʿ al-māl yaʾkhudh ʾusbūʿan. — Getting the money back takes a week.
baʿd istikhdām al-biṭāqa naḥtafiẓ bil-fātūra. — After using the card we keep the receipt.

exercises.prompt: Which is the verbal noun of اِسْتَخْدَمَ?
What does اِسْتِخْدَام الْهَاتِف مَمْنُوع mean?
Which pattern is the verbal noun of Measure X?
What does اِسْتِرْجَاع الْمَال يَأْخُذ أُسْبُوعًا mean?
options: A week is not enough money
The money is a week old
He keeps the money for a week
Getting the money back takes a week

exercises.promptTranslation: Using the phone is forbidden on the plane.
The reception desk is on the first floor.
The directions for use are written on the box.

lessons.title: 307. A map of Measures I to X
lessons.subtitle: كَتَبَ · عَلَّمَ · شَاهَدَ · أَغْلَقَ · تَعَلَّمَ · تَبَادَلَ · اِنْطَلَقَ · اِنْتَظَرَ · اِسْتَخْدَمَ

explanations.title: Nine patterns on one page
explanations.body: Most verbs from three-letter roots are built on one of these patterns, so recognising the measure tells you a lot about a new word. Measure IX is rare: it describes colours and defects, and you can leave it for later. Here are the measures you now know, each with its past, its present and its verbal noun.

explanations.title: Clues in the first letters
explanations.body: Learn to look at the start of a past verb. A doubled middle letter (عَلَّمَ) means II. An ā after the first letter (شَاهَدَ) means III. أَ at the start usually means IV (unless the أ is a root letter, as in أَكَلَ). تَ at the start usually means V or VI. اِنْ often means VII, but check the root: in اِنْتَظَرَ (root ن ظ ر) the ن is a root letter and the ت shows Measure VIII. اِ + a ت after the first root letter means VIII, and اِسْتَ means X.

examples.translation: ʿallama al-mudarris aṭ-ṭullāb. — The teacher taught the students.
shāhadnā al-ʾakhbār. — We watched the news.
ʾaghlaqa al-muwaẓẓaf al-bāb. — The employee closed the door.
taʿallamtu al-ʿarabiyya. — I learned Arabic.
intaẓara ar-rākib aṭ-ṭāʾira. — The passenger waited for the plane.
istakhdamati ash-sharika ṭāʾirāt jadīda. — The company used new planes.

exercises.explanation: An ā after the first letter.
ت after the first root letter.

exercises.promptTranslation: The teacher taught the students.
The passenger waited for the plane.

exercises.explanation: The verbal noun of اِسْتَخْدَمَ (Measure X) is اِسْتِخْدَام.
exercises.promptTranslation: Using the phone in the hall is forbidden.

lessons.title: 308. Hospitality and visiting
lessons.subtitle: يَسْتَقْبِل صَاحِب الْبَيْت الضُّيُوف · تُقَدَّم الْقَهْوَة

explanations.title: Words for visits
explanations.body: A guest is ضَيْف (plural ضُيُوف) and hospitality is ضِيَافَة. The person who owns the house is صَاحِب الْبَيْت. Customs differ from country to country and from family to family, so the sentences below describe what happens in many homes, not in all of them.

explanations.title: In many homes
explanations.body: Notice the verbs from this chapter: the X verb يَسْتَقْبِل, the passive تُقَدَّم, the defective يَبْقَى, and the hollow يَزُور.

examples.text: فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْبُيُوت يَسْتَقْبِل صَاحِب الْبَيْت الضُّيُوف عِنْدَ الْبَاب.
examples.translation: fī kathīr mina al-buyūt yastaqbil ṣāḥib al-bayt aḍ-ḍuyūf ʿinda al-bāb. — In many homes the owner of the house welcomes the guests at the door.
tuqaddam al-qahwa ʾawi al-ʿaṣīr liḍ-ḍayf. — Coffee or juice is served to the guest.
yazūr an-nās ʾaqāribahum fī al-ʾaʿyād. — People visit their relatives at the holidays.
yabqā aḍ-ḍuyūf sāʿa ʾaw sāʿatayn. — The guests stay an hour or two.

examples.text: لَا يَنْسَى الضَّيْف أَنْ يَشْكُر صَاحِب الْبَيْت.
examples.translation: lā yansā aḍ-ḍayf ʾan yashkur ṣāḥib al-bayt. — The guest does not forget to thank the owner of the house.

examples.text: يَدْعُو صَاحِب الْبَيْت الضَّيْف إِلَى الْعَشَاء.
examples.translation: yadʿū ṣāḥib al-bayt aḍ-ḍayf ʾilā al-ʿashāʾ. — The owner of the house invites the guest to dinner.

exercises.prompt: What does تُقَدَّم الْقَهْوَة لِلضَّيْف mean?
options: Coffee is served to the guest

exercises.prompt: What does لَا يَنْسَى الضَّيْف أَنْ يَشْكُر صَاحِب الْبَيْت mean?
options: The guest does not forget to thank the owner

exercises.prompt: Why does the lesson say “in many homes”?
options: customs differ between families and countries

exercises.promptTranslation: The owner of the house welcomes the guests at the door.
The guests stay an hour or two.
People visit their relatives at the holidays.

lessons.title: 309. Holidays and greetings
lessons.subtitle: رَمَضَان · عِيد الْفِطْر · عِيد الْأَضْحَى · كُلّ عَام وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْر

explanations.title: The main holidays
explanations.body: Muslim holidays follow the Hijri lunar calendar, so their dates move about ten or eleven days earlier each year in the Gregorian calendar. رَمَضَان is the month of fasting; عِيد الْفِطْر is the festival that follows it; عِيد الْأَضْحَى is the other major Muslim festival. Christians celebrate عِيد الْمِيلَاد (Christmas) and عِيد الْفِصْح (Easter). Many countries also have a national day.

explanations.title: What people do and say
explanations.body: The verb يَحْتَفِل (celebrates) is Measure VIII and يَصُوم (fasts) is a hollow verb. A common greeting for any festival is «كُلّ عَام وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْر», literally “every year and you are well”.

examples.text: يَصُوم كَثِير مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِين فِي شَهْر رَمَضَان.
examples.translation: yaṣūm kathīr mina al-muslimīn fī shahr ramaḍān. — Many Muslims fast in the month of Ramadan.

examples.text: يَحْتَفِل النَّاس بِعِيد الْفِطْر بَعْد رَمَضَان.
examples.translation: yaḥtafil an-nās biʿīd al-fiṭr baʿd ramaḍān. — People celebrate the festival of Eid al-Fitr after Ramadan.

examples.text: يَحْصُل بَعْض الْأَطْفَال عَلَى هَدَايَا فِي الْعِيد.
examples.translation: yaḥṣul baʿḍ al-ʾaṭfāl ʿalā hadāyā fī al-ʿīd. — Some children get gifts at the festival.
yaḥtafil al-masīḥiyyūn biʿīd al-mīlād. — Christians celebrate Christmas.
naqūl fī al-ʿīd: «ʿīd mubārak!» — At the festival we say: “Blessed festival!”

examples.text: تَتَغَيَّر تَوَارِيخ الْأَعْيَاد الْإِسْلَامِيَّة كُلّ سَنَة.
examples.translation: tataghayyar tawārīkh al-ʾaʿyād al-ʾislāmiyya kull sana. — The dates of the Islamic festivals change every year.

exercises.prompt: Which is the month of fasting?
What does كُلّ عَام وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْر express?
exercises.explanation: A wish for the whole year.

exercises.prompt: Why do the dates of Muslim festivals move through the year?
exercises.explanation: A lunar year is about eleven days shorter than a solar year.

exercises.prompt: What does يَحْتَفِل النَّاس بِعِيد الْفِطْر mean?
___ كَثِير مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِين فِي شَهْر رَمَضَان.
exercises.explanation: A masculine plural people subject takes a singular verb before it.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many Muslims fast in the month of Ramadan.

exercises.explanation: A singular verb before a plural of people.
exercises.promptTranslation: People celebrate the festival of Eid al-Fitr after Ramadan.
At the festival we say: “Blessed festival!”

explanations.title: Names of clothes
explanations.body: Traditional dress differs a great deal from one country to another, and many people today wear modern clothes every day and traditional dress on special occasions. Here are a few well-known pieces. The verb لَبِسَ (he wore) and the Measure VIII verb اِرْتَدَى (he put on) both mean “wear”.

explanations.title: Who wears what, and where
explanations.body: These are broad descriptions. Use بَعْض (some) and كَثِير مِنَ (many of) to avoid saying that everybody does the same.

examples.text: يَلْبَس كَثِير مِنَ الرِّجَال فِي الْخَلِيج ثَوْبًا أَبْيَض.
examples.translation: yalbas kathīr mina ar-rijāl fī al-khalīj thawban ʾabyaḍ. — Many men in the Gulf wear a white thawb.
talbas baʿḍ an-nisāʾ ʿabāʾa sawdāʾ. — Some women wear a black abaya.

examples.text: فِي الْمَغْرِب يَلْبَس كَثِير مِنَ النَّاس جَلَّابِيَّة.
examples.translation: fī al-maghrib yalbas kathīr mina an-nās jallābiyya. — In Morocco many people wear a djellaba.

examples.text: يَرْتَدِي بَعْض الرِّجَال كُوفِيَّة عَلَى رَأْسِهِمْ.
examples.translation: yartadī baʿḍ ar-rijāl kūfiyya ʿalā raʾsihim. — Some men wear a kufiyya on their heads.

examples.text: تَخْتَلِف الْمَلَابِس التَّقْلِيدِيَّة مِنْ بَلَد إِلَى بَلَد.
examples.translation: takhtalif al-malābis at-taqlīdiyya min balad ʾilā balad. — Traditional clothes differ from one country to another.

examples.text: فِي الصَّيْف يَلْبَس النَّاس مَلَابِس خَفِيفَة.
examples.translation: fī aṣ-ṣayf yalbas an-nās malābis khafīfa. — In summer people wear light clothes.

exercises.prompt: What does تَخْتَلِف الْمَلَابِس مِنْ بَلَد إِلَى بَلَد mean?
options: Clothes are expensive in one country
Clothes differ from one country to another

exercises.prompt: Why does the lesson use بَعْض and كَثِير مِنَ?
options: to avoid saying that everyone does the same

exercises.prompt: What does فِي الصَّيْف يَلْبَس النَّاس مَلَابِس خَفِيفَة mean?
options: In summer people wear light clothes

exercises.prompt: يَلْبَس كَثِير مِنَ الرِّجَال فِي الْخَلِيج ___ أَبْيَض.
exercises.explanation: The translation says thawb; a dress is not worn by men, and عَبَاءَة is feminine, so أَبْيَض would not agree.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many men in the Gulf wear a white thawb.
Some women wear a black abaya.

exercises.prompt: تَخْتَلِف الْمَلَابِس ___ مِنْ بَلَد إِلَى بَلَد.
exercises.promptTranslation: Traditional clothes differ from one country to another.

lessons.title: 311. Peoples and religions of the Arab world
lessons.subtitle: مُعْظَم السُّكَّان عَرَب، وَهُنَاك أَيْضًا أَمَازِيغ وَأَكْرَاد

explanations.title: Many communities
explanations.body: The Arab world is home to people of many backgrounds. In most countries the majority are Arabs who speak Arabic, and there are also communities such as الْأَمَازِيغ (the Amazigh, in North Africa) and الْأَكْرَاد (the Kurds). Most people are Muslim, and there are also Christians and other communities. These are broad facts; every country has its own mix.

explanations.title: Describing a population
explanations.body: Use relative clauses, as in chapter 17, to say who speaks what. Notice the returning pronoun in اللُّغَة الَّتِي يَتَكَلَّم بِهَا.

examples.text: فِي مُعْظَم الْبِلَاد الْعَرَبِيَّة الْعَرَب هُمُ الْأَكْثَرِيَّة.
examples.translation: fī muʿẓam al-bilād al-ʿarabiyya al-ʿarab humu al-ʾakthariyya. — In most Arab countries the Arabs are the majority.
yaʿīsh al-ʾamāzīgh fī shamāl ʾafrīqiyā. — The Amazigh live in North Africa.

examples.text: يَعِيش الْأَكْرَاد فِي الْعِرَاق وَسُورِيَا وَتُرْكِيَا وَإِيرَان.
examples.translation: yaʿīsh al-ʾakrād fī al-ʿirāq wasūriyā waturkiyā waʾīrān. — The Kurds live in Iraq, Syria, Turkey and Iran.

examples.text: مُعْظَم السُّكَّان مُسْلِمُون، وَيُوجَد أَيْضًا مَسِيحِيُّون.
examples.translation: muʿẓam as-sukkān muslimūn, wayūjad ʾayḍan masīḥiyyūn. — Most of the people are Muslims, and there are also Christians.

examples.text: الْعَرَبِيَّة هِيَ اللُّغَة الَّتِي يَتَكَلَّم بِهَا مُعْظَم النَّاس فِي الْبِلَاد الْعَرَبِيَّة.
examples.translation: al-ʿarabiyya hiya al-lugha allatī yatakallam bihā muʿẓam an-nās fī al-bilād al-ʿarabiyya. — Arabic is the language that most people in the Arab countries speak.
taḥtafiẓ jamāʿāt kathīra bilughatihā. — Many groups keep their language.

exercises.prompt: What does تَحْتَفِظ جَمَاعَات كَثِيرَة بِلُغَتِهَا mean?
In اللُّغَة الَّتِي يَتَكَلَّم بِهَا, what is the job of بِهَا؟
options: the returning pronoun بِهَا points back to اللُّغَة

exercises.explanation: The Amazigh live in North Africa.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Amazigh live in North Africa.

exercises.prompt: الْعَرَبِيَّة هِيَ اللُّغَة ___ يَتَكَلَّم بِهَا مُعْظَم النَّاس فِي الْبِلَاد الْعَرَبِيَّة.
exercises.promptTranslation: Arabic is the language that most people in the Arab countries speak.
Most of the people are Muslims, and there are also Christians.

explanations.title: Wedding words
explanations.body: A wedding is زِفَاف or عُرْس or زَوَاج. The bride is عَرُوس and the groom is عَرِيس. The congratulation is مَبْرُوك. Wedding customs vary widely: some weddings are a single evening and others last several days, so these sentences stay general.

explanations.title: Going to a wedding
explanations.body: The verbs you know from this chapter fit this topic: دَعَا (invite), حَضَرَ (attend), اِحْتَفَلَ (celebrate). These sentences are invented.

examples.translation: daʿānī ṣadīqī ʾilā zifāfihi. — My friend invited me to his wedding.
yaḥḍur al-ʾahl wal-ʾaṣdiqāʾ ḥafla az-zifāf. — The family and friends attend the wedding party.
talbas al-ʿarūs fustānan jamīlan. — The bride wears a beautiful dress.
yuqaddim aḍ-ḍuyūf hadāyā lil-ʿarūs wal-ʿarīs. — The guests give gifts to the bride and groom.

examples.text: فِي بَعْض الْبِلَاد تَبْقَى الْحَفْلَة عِدَّة أَيَّام.
examples.translation: fī baʿḍ al-bilād tabqā al-ḥafla ʿidda ʾayyām. — In some countries the party lasts several days.
naqūl lil-ʿarīs wal-ʿarūs: «mabrūk!» — We say to the groom and the bride: “Congratulations!”

exercises.prompt: What do you say to a couple?
What does دَعَانِي صَدِيقِي إِلَى زِفَافِهِ mean?
options: My friend invited me to his wedding
I invited my friend to his wedding

exercises.prompt: What does تَبْقَى الْحَفْلَة عِدَّة أَيَّام mean?
Why does the lesson stay general?

exercises.promptTranslation: My friend invited me to his wedding.
The family and friends attend the wedding party.
We say to the groom and the bride: “Congratulations!”

explanations.title: Opening and closing
explanations.body: A friendly email or card has a greeting at the top, the message, and a closing. For a man write عَزِيزِي; for a woman, عَزِيزَتِي. Common closings are مَعَ تَحِيَّاتِي (with my greetings) and مَعَ أَطْيَب التَّمَنِّيَات (with best wishes).

explanations.title: An invented email
explanations.body: A friend answers a wedding invitation. The people and the message are made up.

examples.translation: ʿazīzī khālid, as-salām ʿalayka. — Dear Khalid, peace be upon you.
shukran lidaʿwatika ʾilā ḥafla az-zifāf. — Thank you for your invitation to the wedding party.

examples.text: سَأَحْضُر مَعَ أَخِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه.
examples.translation: saʾaḥḍur maʿa ʾakhī ʾin shāʾa allāh. — I will attend with my brother, God willing.
mabrūk! ʾaṭyab at-tahānī laka walil-ʿarūs. — Congratulations! Warmest congratulations to you and to the bride.
wasaʾursil lakumā hadiyya ṣaghīra. — And I will send you both a small gift.
maʿa ʾaṭyab at-tamanniyāt, yūsuf. — With best wishes, Yusuf.

exercises.prompt: How do you open an email to a man called Khalid?
How do you open a card to a woman?
What does مَعَ أَطْيَب التَّمَنِّيَات mean?
What does سَأَحْضُر مَعَ أَخِي mean?
options: I did not see my brother
I will attend with my brother

exercises.promptTranslation: Dear Khalid, peace be upon you.

exercises.explanation: The translation says congratulations, so the word is التَّهَانِي.
exercises.promptTranslation: Congratulations! Warmest congratulations to you and to the bride.

exercises.explanation: The usual closing starts with مَعَ.
exercises.promptTranslation: With best wishes, Yusuf.

lessons.title: 314. Giving a short talk: Lebanon
lessons.subtitle: سَأَتَحَدَّث الْيَوْم عَنْ لُبْنَان · شُكْرًا عَلَى اِسْتِمَاعِكُمْ

explanations.title: The shape of a talk
explanations.body: A short talk has an opening (سَأَتَحَدَّث عَنْ…, “I will talk about…”), points in order (أَوَّلًا, ثَانِيًا, ثَالِثًا, or ثُمَّ), and a closing (شُكْرًا عَلَى اِسْتِمَاعِكُمْ, “thank you for listening”). Use the structures of the chapter: يَقَع for place, relative clauses for details.

explanations.title: A talk about Lebanon (basic facts)
explanations.body: These facts are standard reference facts, kept simple.

examples.translation: saʾataḥaddath al-yawm ʿan lubnān. — Today I will talk about Lebanon.

examples.text: أَوَّلًا، لُبْنَان دَوْلَة عَرَبِيَّة صَغِيرَة تَقَع عَلَى الْبَحْر الْمُتَوَسِّط.
examples.translation: ʾawwalan, lubnān dawla ʿarabiyya ṣaghīra taqaʿ ʿalā al-baḥr al-mutawassiṭ. — First, Lebanon is a small Arab country that lies on the Mediterranean Sea.
ʿāṣima lubnān hiya bayrūt. — The capital of Lebanon is Beirut.

examples.text: ثَانِيًا، يَعِيش فِي لُبْنَان مُسْلِمُون وَمَسِيحِيُّون.
examples.translation: thāniyan, yaʿīsh fī lubnān muslimūn wamasīḥiyyūn. — Second, Muslims and Christians live in Lebanon.
thālithan, al-lugha ar-rasmiyya hiya al-ʿarabiyya. — Third, the official language is Arabic.
shukran ʿalā istimāʿikum. — Thank you for listening.

exercises.prompt: What is the capital of Lebanon?
What is the official language of Lebanon?
Which sea does Lebanon lie on?
What does شُكْرًا عَلَى اِسْتِمَاعِكُمْ mean?
What is the order of the points?

exercises.promptTranslation: Today I will talk about Lebanon.

exercises.prompt: لُبْنَان دَوْلَة عَرَبِيَّة صَغِيرَة ___ عَلَى الْبَحْر الْمُتَوَسِّط.

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Defective verbs: the present ends in ـِي, ـُو or ـَى (يَمْشِي, يَدْعُو, يَنْسَى), the long vowel drops after لَمْ and in the command (لَا تَنْسَ). Measure VIII is اِفْتَعَلَ (يَنْتَظِر) with the noun اِفْتِعَال; Measure X is اِسْتَفْعَلَ (يَسْتَخْدِم) with the noun اِسْتِفْعَال.

iḥtafala an-nās ḥattā waqt mutaʾakhkhir. — The people celebrated until late.
