units.title: السُّوق وَالْمَقْهَى: shopping, exclamations and double-letter verbs

explanations.title: Meat, kilos and pieces
explanations.body: A butcher is جَزَّار and a small shop is a دُكَّان. Meat is لَحْم; beef is لَحْم الْبَقَر. The word صِنْف means “kind”, and its plural is أَصْنَاف. You ask for an amount with مِنْ: كِيلُو مِنَ اللَّحْم, “a kilo of meat”.

explanations.title: Asking the butcher
explanations.body: Notice أُرِيد (“I want”) with a noun, and هَلْ تُرِيد أَنْ أَقْطَع لَكَ اللَّحْم؟, “Do you want me to cut the meat for you?”. After أَنْ the verb is in the subjunctive; with أَنَا it looks the same as the present: أَقْطَع.

examples.text: عِنْدَ الْجَزَّار أَصْنَاف كَثِيرَة مِنَ اللَّحْم.
examples.translation: ʿinda al-jazzār ʾaṣnāf kathīra mina al-laḥm. — The butcher has many kinds of meat.
ʾurīd kīlū min laḥm al-baqar. — I want a kilo of beef.

examples.text: هَلْ تُرِيد أَنْ أَقْطَع لَكَ اللَّحْم؟
examples.translation: hal turīd ʾan ʾaqṭaʿ laka al-laḥm? — Do you want me to cut the meat for you?
naʿam, ʾurīd sharīḥa kabīra lish-shiwāʾ. — Yes, I want a large cut for grilling.
ʾurīd qiṭaʿ ṣaghīra liṭ-ṭabkh. — I want small pieces for cooking.
hali ad-dajāj ṭāzaj al-yawm? — Is the chicken fresh today?

exercises.prompt: Which word is the singular of أَصْنَاف?
What does أُرِيد كِيلُو مِنْ لَحْم الْبَقَر mean?
options: I sell a kilo of beef
I want a kilo of beef
I want a piece of fish
I want a kilo of chicken

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ تُرِيد أَنْ أَقْطَع لَكَ اللَّحْم؟ mean?
options: Do you want to buy the meat?
Did you cut the meat yesterday?
Do you want me to cut the meat for you?
Will you cook the meat for me?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want a large cut for grilling.

exercises.explanation: Plural of things: feminine singular adjective كَثِيرَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The butcher has many kinds of meat.
Do you want me to cut the meat for you?

lessons.title: 317. Prices and bargaining
lessons.subtitle: كَمْ ثَمَنُهُ؟ · غَالِي · رَخِيص · آخِر سِعْر

explanations.title: Asking and judging the price
explanations.body: ثَمَن and سِعْر both mean “price”. To ask, say كَمْ ثَمَنُهُ؟ (“How much is it?”). A high price is غَالِي and a low one is رَخِيص; the comparatives are أَغْلَى and أَرْخَص. To bargain, ask for the last price: آخِر سِعْر. The word for bargaining is مُسَاوَمَة, and a discount is خَصْم.

explanations.title: A bargaining dialogue (invented)
explanations.body: A customer and a shopkeeper talk. The customer uses أَظُنّ أَنَّ…, “I think that…”. This verb has a doubled letter; you will study it in this unit.

examples.translation: kam thaman hādhā? — How much is this?
thamanuhu ʿashara danānīr. — Its price is ten dinars.
ʾaẓunn ʾanna ath-thaman ghālī. — I think the price is high.
saʾadfaʿ thamāniya danānīr faqaṭ. — I will pay only eight dinars.
hal tadfaʿ naqdan ʾaw bil-biṭāqa? — Do you pay in cash or by card?

examples.text: فِي بَعْض الْأَحْيَاء يَشْتَرِي النَّاس بِالدَّيْن، وَيَدْفَعُون أَوَّل الشَّهْر.
examples.translation: fī baʿḍ al-ʾaḥyāʾ yashtarī an-nās bid-dayn, wayadfaʿūn ʾawwal ash-shahr. — In some neighbourhoods people buy on credit and pay at the beginning of the month.

exercises.prompt: What does أَظُنّ أَنَّ الثَّمَن غَالِي mean?
options: I think the price is high
I know the price is low

exercises.promptTranslation: I will pay only eight dinars.
This shirt is cheaper than that one.
Do you pay in cash or by card?

lessons.title: 318. أَيّ: “which?” and “any”
lessons.subtitle: أَيّ صِنْف تُرِيد؟ · هَلْ عِنْدَكَ أَيّ قَمِيص؟

explanations.title: أَيّ in a question
explanations.body: Put أَيّ in front of a singular noun to ask “which?”. The noun is indefinite and follows directly: أَيّ لَوْن؟ means “which colour?”. A shopkeeper may open with أَيّ خِدْمَة؟, literally “what service?”, that is, “How can I help you?”. This is a common everyday phrase.

explanations.title: أَيّ meaning “any”
explanations.body: In a yes/no question or after “not”, the same word means “any”: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ أَيّ قَمِيص أَزْرَق؟ “Do you have any blue shirts?”. In fixed phrases it also means “whichever” or “at all”.

examples.translation: ʾayy ṣinf turīd? — Which kind do you want?
ʾayy lawn tuḥibb? — Which colour do you like?
fī ʾayy yawm sataʾtī? — On which day will you come?
hal ʿindaka ʾayy qamīṣ ʾazraq? — Do you have any blue shirts?
laysa ʿindī ʾayy mushkila. — I do not have any problems.

examples.text: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَأْتِي فِي أَيّ وَقْت.
examples.translation: yumkinuka ʾan taʾtī fī ʾayy waqt. — You can come at any time.

exercises.prompt: What does أَيّ لَوْن تُحِبّ؟ ask?
What does أَيّ خِدْمَة؟ mean in a shop?
What does هَلْ عِنْدَكَ أَيّ قَمِيص أَزْرَق؟ mean?
options: Do you have any blue shirts?

exercises.prompt: What does لَيْسَ عِنْدِي أَيّ مُشْكِلَة mean?
options: I do not have any problem

exercises.prompt: What does فِي أَيّ وَقْت mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Which kind do you want?
Do you have any blue shirts?
On which day will you come?

explanations.title: Food and containers
explanations.body: A list is قَائِمَة. In a shopping list, you name the amount and then the thing: كِيلُو طَمَاطِم, عُلْبَة جُبْن, زُجَاجَة زَيْت. Mass nouns such as rice and sugar need a container or a weight.

explanations.title: My list
explanations.body: Read this list from the market. The amounts come first.

examples.translation: kīlū ṭamāṭim — a kilo of tomatoes
kīs ʾaruzz — a bag of rice
zujāja zayt — a bottle of oil
ʿulba jubn — a box of cheese
lā ʾansā al-ḥalīb wal-khubz. — I do not forget the milk and the bread.
hādhihi hiya qāʾimatī lis-sūq. — This is my list for the market.

exercises.promptTranslation: a bag of rice
a bottle of oil

exercises.explanation: لَا + present: I do not forget.
exercises.promptTranslation: I do not forget the milk and the bread.

lessons.title: 320. Clothes, colours and materials
lessons.subtitle: قَمِيص · فُسْتَان · سِرْوَال · مِعْطَف · قُطْن · جِلْد

explanations.title: What people wear
explanations.body: The words below are the basic names of clothes. A word for a piece of clothing is placed before its colour or material: قَمِيص أَبْيَض, “a white shirt”; قَمِيص مِنَ الْقُطْن, “a cotton shirt”.

explanations.title: Colours agree with the thing
explanations.body: A colour is an adjective. It follows the noun and agrees with it. For a masculine noun use the masculine form; for a feminine noun use the feminine form. Words such as قُبَّعَة are feminine because of the ـَة ending.

examples.translation: ʾurīd qamīṣ ʾabyaḍ mina al-quṭn. — I want a white cotton shirt.
ʿindahā fustān ʾaḥmar waqubbaʿa sawdāʾ. — She has a red dress and a black hat.
hādhā al-ḥizām mina al-jild. — This belt is made of leather.
ʾuḥibb al-miʿṭaf al-ʾazraq. — I like the blue coat.

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine form of أَبْيَض?
What does هَذَا الْحِزَام مِنَ الْجِلْد mean?
options: This belt is made of leather
This belt is made of cotton

exercises.explanation: The ـَة ending marks it as feminine.
The adjective agrees with the feminine noun قُبَّعَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: She has a black hat.
I want a white cotton shirt.

exercises.explanation: A coat can be made of wool; a belt or a shirt is not a material.
exercises.promptTranslation: This coat is made of wool.

lessons.title: 321. Trying on and exchanging clothes
lessons.subtitle: هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ أُجَرِّب هَذَا الْقَمِيص؟

explanations.title: In the fitting room
explanations.body: To try something on, use the Measure II verb جَرَّبَ. After هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ, the verb is in the present form: أُجَرِّب, “I try on”. To exchange, use بَدَّلَ: أُبَدِّل, “I exchange, change”. Sizes are described with كَبِير, “big”, and صَغِير, “small”; ask for a different one with أَكْبَر or أَصْغَر.

examples.text: هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ أُجَرِّب هَذَا الْقَمِيص؟
examples.translation: hal yumkin ʾan ʾujarrib hādhā al-qamīṣ? — May I try on this shirt?
al-qamīṣ kabīr ʿalayya. — The shirt is big on me.
hal ʿindaka maqās ʾaṣghar? — Do you have a smaller size?
hādhā al-lawn yunāsibuka. — This colour suits you.

examples.text: هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ أُبَدِّل هَذَا الْقَمِيص بِمَقَاس أَكْبَر؟
examples.translation: hal yumkin ʾan ʾubaddil hādhā al-qamīṣ bimaqās ʾakbar? — May I exchange this shirt for a bigger size?
fī al-maḥall takhfīḍāt hādhā al-ʾusbūʿ. — There are sales in the shop this week.
al-khaṣm ʿishrūn bil-miʾa. — The discount is twenty per cent.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ أُجَرِّب هَذَا الْقَمِيص؟ ask?
options: May I try on this shirt?

exercises.prompt: What does الْقَمِيص كَبِير عَلَيَّ mean?
options: The shirt is cheap for me
The shirt is big on me

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ عِنْدَكَ مَقَاس أَصْغَر؟ ask?
options: Do you have a smaller size?
Do you have a bigger size?
Do you have a cheaper shirt?

exercises.prompt: What does هَذَا اللَّوْن يُنَاسِبُكَ mean?

exercises.explanation: After أَنْ, a present verb: أُجَرِّب.
exercises.promptTranslation: May I try on this shirt?

exercises.prompt: هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ ___ هَذَا الْقَمِيص بِمَقَاس أَكْبَر؟
exercises.promptTranslation: May I exchange this shirt for a bigger size?
Do you have a smaller size?

explanations.title: Two kinds of shopping
explanations.body: In many Arab cities you can find an old market, a سُوق, and a modern mall, a مَرْكَز تِجَارِيّ, in the same town. The sentences below describe common patterns, not rules for every place.

explanations.title: What is different
explanations.body: Three places known for their markets and shops are الْقَاهِرَة in Egypt, مَرَّاكُش in Morocco and مَدِينَة الْكُوَيْت, the capital of Kuwait. These sentences are only general pictures.

examples.text: فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْمُدُن الْعَرَبِيَّة أَسْوَاق قَدِيمَة وَمَرَاكِز تِجَارِيَّة حَدِيثَة.
examples.translation: fī kathīr mina al-mudun al-ʿarabiyya ʾaswāq qadīma wamarākiz tijāriyya ḥadītha. — In many Arab cities there are old markets and modern shopping centres.

examples.text: فِي السُّوق الْقَدِيم تَكُون الْمُسَاوَمَة شَائِعَة فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْأَحْيَان.
examples.translation: fī as-sūq al-qadīm takūn al-musāwama shāʾiʿa fī kathīr mina al-ʾaḥyān. — In many cases, bargaining is common in the old market.

examples.text: فِي الْمَرْكَز التِّجَارِيّ تَكُون الْأَسْعَار عَادَةً مَكْتُوبَة.
examples.translation: fī al-markaz at-tijāriyy takūn al-ʾasʿār ʿādatan maktūba. — In the shopping centre the prices are usually written.
yabīʿ al-bāʾiʿ wayadfaʿ az-zabūn. — The seller sells and the customer pays.
al-qāhira madīna fī miṣr. — Cairo is a city in Egypt.
marrākush madīna fī al-maghrib. — Marrakesh is a city in Morocco.
madīna al-kuwayt hiya ʿāṣima al-kuwayt. — Kuwait City is the capital of Kuwait.

exercises.prompt: Where is the city of الْقَاهِرَة?
What is the capital of Kuwait?
فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْمُدُن الْعَرَبِيَّة أَسْوَاق ___

exercises.explanation: The one who pays is the customer.
exercises.promptTranslation: The seller sells and the customer pays.

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: To say “How beautiful …!”, use مَا, then a word of the shape أَفْعَلَ, and then the thing you admire in the accusative. The middle word ends in a fatḥa, and the thing admired ends in ـَ (or ـًا for an indefinite noun). It is built from the adjective: جَمِيل (beautiful) gives مَا أَجْمَلَ, “how beautiful!”. Do not confuse it with the comparative أَجْمَل, “more beautiful”, which has no مَا before it.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: The admired thing is in the accusative: it takes a fatḥa. In this lesson the final vowels are written, because they carry the grammar.

examples.translation: mā ʾajmala hādhā al-fustāna! — How beautiful this dress is!
mā ʾaghlā hādhā al-fustāna! — How expensive this dress is!
mā ʾarkhaṣa hādhā al-ḥidhāʾa! — How cheap this pair of shoes is!
mā ʾakbara hādhā al-maḥalla! — How big this shop is!
mā ʾaladhdha aṭ-ṭaʿāma! — How delicious the food is!
mā ʾasraʿa al-bāʾiʿa! — How fast the seller is!

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذَا الْفُسْتَانَ! express?
What does مَا أَغْلَى هَذَا الْفُسْتَانَ! mean?
What does مَا أَلَذَّ الطَّعَامَ! mean?
What case is the noun after مَا أَجْمَلَ?
exercises.explanation: The admired thing is accusative, with ـَ.

exercises.prompt: Which is the exclamation built from رَخِيص?

exercises.promptTranslation: How beautiful this dress is!
How expensive this dress is!

exercises.explanation: The noun after the exclamation is accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: How delicious the food is!

lessons.title: 324. Exclamations at the market
lessons.subtitle: مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذَا ! · مَا أَغْلَى هَذَا !

explanations.title: Statement, question, exclamation
explanations.body: The same adjective can be used in three ways. A plain statement says what something is: هَذَا الْقَمِيص جَمِيل. A question with مَا asks what something is: مَا ثَمَن هَذَا الْقَمِيص؟ An exclamation shows feeling: مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذَا الْقَمِيصَ! It is built as مَا + a word like أَجْمَلَ + the thing in the accusative. In writing, an exclamation ends with !.

rows: What is the price of this shirt?

explanations.title: Two friends at the market (invented)
explanations.body: Two friends walk through a market and react to what they see.

examples.translation: mā ʾajmala hādhā al-qumāsha! — How beautiful this cloth is!
wamā ʾaghlā hādhā al-qumāsha! — And how expensive this cloth is!
mā ʾakbara hādhā as-sūqa! — How big this market is!
mā ʾasraʿa al-bāʾiʿa fī al-ḥisābi! — How fast the seller is at counting!
mā ʾajmala al-ʾalwāna hunā! — How beautiful the colours are here!
mā ʾarkhaṣa hādhihi al-qubbaʿata! — How cheap this hat is!

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَكْبَرَ هَذَا السُّوقَ! mean?
What does وَمَا أَغْلَى هَذَا الْقُمَاشَ! mean?
options: And how expensive this cloth is!

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَرْخَصَ هَذِهِ الْقُبَّعَةَ! mean?
What does مَا أَجْمَلَ الْأَلْوَانَ هُنَا! mean?
options: How beautiful the colours are here!

exercises.promptTranslation: How beautiful this cloth is!
How big this market is!
How fast the seller is at counting!

lessons.title: 325. Exclamations about weather, crowds and time
lessons.subtitle: مَا أَحَرَّ الْجَوَّ ! · مَا أَكْثَرَ النَّاسَ !

explanations.title: More exclamations
explanations.body: You can use the same pattern for many things: weather, crowds, time, water, food. Some adjectives have a doubled letter, such as حَارّ (hot) and شَدِيد (strong, severe). Their exclamatory forms keep the doubled letter with a shadda: مَا أَحَرَّ and مَا أَشَدَّ. Others are regular: مَا أَبْرَدَ, مَا أَكْثَرَ.

explanations.title: In use
explanations.body: The thing described is again in the accusative.

examples.translation: mā ʾaḥarra al-jawwa al-yawma! — How hot the weather is today!
mā ʾabrada hādhā al-māʾa! — How cold this water is!
mā ʾakthara an-nāsa fī as-sūqi! — How many people there are in the market!
mā ʾasraʿa al-waqta! — How fast time goes!
mā ʾashadda al-ḥarra fī aṣ-ṣayfi! — How severe the heat is in summer!
mā ʾaqalla az-zabāʾina al-yawma! — How few the customers are today!

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَحَرَّ الْجَوَّ الْيَوْمَ! mean?
options: How hot the weather is today!

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَبْرَدَ هَذَا الْمَاءَ! mean?
What does مَا أَكْثَرَ النَّاسَ فِي السُّوقِ! mean?
options: How few people there are in the market!
How many people there are in the market!

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَسْرَعَ الْوَقْتَ! mean?
Which exclamation is written with a shadda?

exercises.promptTranslation: How hot the weather is today!
How cold this water is!

exercises.explanation: The noun after the exclamation is accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: How many people there are in the market!

explanations.title: Drinks and ways to order
explanations.body: A cup of coffee is فِنْجَان قَهْوَة and a glass of juice is كُوب عَصِير. With sugar is بِسُكَّر or مَعَ سُكَّر; without sugar is بِدُون سُكَّر. A drink can be سَاخِن (hot) or بَارِد (cold). Polite words: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (please, to a man), تَفَضَّلْ (here you are), شُكْرًا (thank you).

explanations.title: Ordering, accepting and declining
explanations.body: A waiter may offer; you may accept or politely decline.

examples.text: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، أُرِيد فِنْجَان قَهْوَة بِدُون سُكَّر.
examples.translation: min faḍlika, ʾurīd finjān qahwa bidūn sukkar. — Please, I want a cup of coffee without sugar.
hal turīd ʿaṣīr bārid? — Do you want cold juice?
naʿam, shukran, ʾurīd kūb ʿaṣīr. — Yes, thank you, I want a glass of juice.
lā, shukran, lā ʾurīd ḥalīb. — No, thank you, I do not want milk.
hal turīd shayʾan ʾākhar? — Do you want anything else?
al-ḥisāb min faḍlika. — The bill, please.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ تُرِيد شَيْئًا آخَر؟ ask?
What does لَا، شُكْرًا، لَا أُرِيد حَلِيب mean?
options: Yes, thank you, I want milk
No, thank you, I do not want milk
exercises.explanation: لَا أُرِيد = I do not want.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase asks for the bill?

exercises.explanation: “Without sugar” needs بِدُون; مَعَ would mean “with”.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want a cup of coffee without sugar.
Do you want cold juice?
Please, I want a glass of water.

explanations.title: Menu words
explanations.body: The menu is قَائِمَة الطَّعَام. A dish is طَبَق, and a meal is وَجْبَة. The waiter is نَادِل. Foods that are cooked on a grill are مَشْوِيّ.

explanations.title: Ordering a meal
explanations.body: Use أُرِيد (“I want”) or أُحِبّ أَنْ آكُل (“I like to eat”) for what you want. Ask politely with هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ…؟, “Do you have …?”.

examples.translation: al-qāʾima min faḍlika. — The menu, please.
ʾurīd ṭabaq salaṭa waḥasāʾ. — I want a plate of salad and soup.
hal ʿindakum samak mashwiyy? — Do you have grilled fish?
mādhā tuḥibb ʾan taʾkul? — What do you like to eat?
ʾuḥibb al-ʾaruzz maʿa al-laḥm. — I like rice with meat.

examples.text: الْغَدَاء وَجْبَة كَبِيرَة فِي كَثِير مِنَ الْبُيُوت.
examples.translation: al-ghadāʾ wajba kabīra fī kathīr mina al-buyūt. — Lunch is a large meal in many homes.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ سَمَك مَشْوِيّ؟ ask?
What does مَاذَا تُحِبّ أَنْ تَأْكُل؟ ask?
options: What do you like to eat?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want a plate of salad and soup.

exercises.explanation: To the restaurant staff: Do you (pl.) have …?
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you have grilled fish?
What do you like to eat?

explanations.title: A review card
explanations.body: A review card gives the name, the location, the working hours, the kind of food, the prices and the way to pay. The restaurant below is invented, so use it only to practise the pattern.

explanations.title: Reading the review
explanations.body: Here is a short review of an invented restaurant.

examples.translation: ism al-maṭʿam: maṭʿam al-wāḥa. — Name of the restaurant: the Oasis Restaurant.
yaqaʿ al-maṭʿam fī wasaṭ al-madīna. — The restaurant is in the middle of the city.
yaftaḥ yawmiyyan lil-ghadāʾ wal-ʿashāʾ. — It opens daily for lunch and dinner.
al-qāʿa wāsiʿa wajamīla wal-khidma sarīʿa. — The hall is wide and beautiful and the service is fast.

examples.text: الْأَسْعَار مَعْقُولَة وَالدَّفْع نَقْدًا أَوْ بِالْبِطَاقَة.
examples.translation: al-ʾasʿār maʿqūla wad-dafʿ naqdan ʾaw bil-biṭāqa. — The prices are reasonable and payment is in cash or by card.
ʾanṣaḥ bis-samak al-mashwiyy. — I recommend the grilled fish.

exercises.prompt: What does يَقَع الْمَطْعَم فِي وَسَط الْمَدِينَة mean?
options: The restaurant is far from the city
The restaurant is in the middle of the city
The city is in the restaurant
The prices are written in Arabic

options: Payment is in cash or by card

exercises.explanation: In the middle of the city.

exercises.explanation: Feminine adjective for the feminine الْخِدْمَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The hall is wide and the service is fast.
The prices are reasonable.

lessons.title: 329. Describing a person
lessons.subtitle: طَوِيل · قَصِير · شَعْرُهُ أَسْوَد · يَلْبَس نَظَّارَات

explanations.title: What you can say
explanations.body: To help a friend recognise someone, say how tall the person is, what the hair is like, and what he or she wears. The adjective agrees with the person: طَوِيل for a man, طَوِيلَة for a woman. For the hair, use شَعْر + the pronoun: شَعْرُهُ أَسْوَد (“his hair is black”), شَعْرُهَا طَوِيل (“her hair is long”). The verb يَلْبَس means “wears”.

explanations.title: Finding a friend at the market (invented)
explanations.body: A friend says how to recognise a person.

examples.translation: ṣadīqī ṭawīl washaʿruhu ʾaswad. — My friend is tall and his hair is black.
ʾukhtī qaṣīra washaʿruhā ṭawīl. — My sister is short and her hair is long.
yalbas qamīṣ ʾazraq waḥidhāʾ ʾabyaḍ. — He wears a blue shirt and white shoes.
hiya talbas fustān ʾaḥmar. — She wears a red dress.

examples.text: الرَّجُل الطَّوِيل الَّذِي يَلْبَس نَظَّارَات هُوَ صَدِيقِي.
examples.translation: ar-rajul aṭ-ṭawīl alladhī yalbas naẓẓārāt huwa ṣadīqī. — The tall man who wears glasses is my friend.

examples.text: هَلْ هُوَ شَابّ أَمْ كَبِير فِي السِّنّ؟
examples.translation: hal huwa shābb ʾam kabīr fī as-sinn? — Is he young or old?

exercises.prompt: Which is the feminine form of طَوِيل?
What does الرَّجُل الطَّوِيل الَّذِي يَلْبَس نَظَّارَات هُوَ صَدِيقِي mean?
options: The tall man who wears glasses is my friend
My friend is a short man
The man who is my friend is blue

exercises.prompt: What does كَبِير فِي السِّنّ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: My sister is short and her hair is long.

exercises.prompt: الرَّجُل الطَّوِيل ___ يَلْبَس نَظَّارَات هُوَ صَدِيقِي.
exercises.explanation: The relative pronoun agrees with الرَّجُل (masculine singular).
exercises.promptTranslation: The tall man who wears glasses is my friend.
She wears a red dress.

explanations.title: A verb whose last two root letters are the same
explanations.body: The root of مَرَّ is م ر ر. The second and third letters are the same, so in the dictionary form they are written together with a shadda: مَرَّ, “he passed”. With هُوَ, هِيَ and هُمْ the shadda stays: مَرَّ, مَرَّتْ, مَرُّوا. When the ending begins with a consonant (تُ, تَ, تِ, تُمْ, نَا, نَ), the shadda disappears and the two letters are written one after the other: مَرَرْتُ, “I passed”.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: The rule is the same for other double-letter verbs. You will meet رَدَّ (replied, returned), مَدَّ (extended), عَدَّ (counted) and حَلَّ (solved) in later lessons.

examples.translation: marartu bis-sūq ʾamsi. — I passed by the market yesterday.
hal mararta bil-maḥall? — Did you pass by the shop?
mararnā bil-maqhā fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — We passed by the coffee shop in the morning.
marrat ʾukhtī bil-maḥall. — My sister passed by the shop.
marra al-bāʾiʿ biz-zabāʾin. — The seller passed by the customers.

exercises.prompt: What is the past of مَرَّ with أَنَا?
exercises.explanation: Before تُ the shadda opens: مَرَرْتُ.

exercises.prompt: What is the past of مَرَّ with نَحْنُ?
What is the past of مَرَّ with هِيَ?
What does مَرَرْتُ بِالسُّوق أَمْسِ mean?
options: I will pass by the market tomorrow
I passed by the market yesterday

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ مَرَرْتَ بِالْمَحَلّ؟ ask?
options: Did you pass by the shop?
Did she pass by the shop?
Will you pass by the shop?
Did I pass by the shop?
We passed by the coffee shop
They passed by the coffee shop
I passed by the coffee shop

exercises.promptTranslation: I passed by the market yesterday.
We passed by the coffee shop in the morning.
She passed by the shop.

explanations.title: The present keeps the shadda
explanations.body: In the present, a double-letter verb is built like other verbs: prefix + stem. With أَنَا, أَنْتَ, هُوَ, هِيَ and نَحْنُ the last two letters stay together under a shadda. Before the endings ـِينَ and ـُونَ the shadda carries the vowel: تَمُرِّينَ, تَمُرُّونَ. The stem vowel of مَرَّ is ḍamma: يَمُرّ.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Add سَـ for the future and لَا for “not”.

examples.translation: ʾamurr bis-sūq kull yawm. — I pass by the market every day.
saʾamurr bil-maḥall ghadan. — I will pass by the shop tomorrow.
tamurrīna bil-maqhā baʿda aẓ-ẓuhr. — You (f.) pass by the coffee shop after noon.
yamurrūna bil-maḥall fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — They pass by the shop in the morning.
lā ʾamurr bis-sūq yawm al-jumʿa. — I do not pass by the market on Friday.

exercises.prompt: What is the present of مَرَّ with أَنَا?
What is the present of مَرَّ with نَحْنُ?
What is the present of مَرَّ with أَنْتِ?
What is the present of مَرَّ with هُمْ?
What does سَأَمُرّ بِالْمَحَلّ غَدًا mean?
options: I pass by the shop every day
I will pass by the shop tomorrow
I passed by the shop yesterday

exercises.prompt: What does لَا أَمُرّ بِالسُّوق يَوْم الْجُمْعَة mean?
options: I pass by the market on Friday
I will not buy a market
I do not pass by the market on Friday
I did not pass by the market

exercises.promptTranslation: I pass by the market every day.
They pass by the shop in the morning.
You (f.) pass by the coffee shop after noon.

explanations.title: A double-letter verb of thinking
explanations.body: ظَنَّ يَظُنّ means “to think, to suppose”. It follows the pattern you know: past ظَنَّ, ظَنَّتْ, ظَنُّوا and ظَنَنْتُ, ظَنَنْتَ, ظَنَنْتِ; present أَظُنّ, تَظُنّ, تَظُنِّينَ, تَظُنُّونَ, يَظُنّ. After the verb you usually add أَنَّ, “that”, and a sentence. With a pronoun it becomes أَنَّهُ, أَنَّهَا.

explanations.title: Giving your opinion
explanations.body: This is a common way to give an opinion.

examples.translation: ʾaẓunn ʾanna ath-thaman ghālī. — I think the price is high.

examples.text: هَلْ تَظُنّ أَنَّ هَذَا الْقَمِيص رَخِيص؟
examples.translation: hal taẓunn ʾanna hādhā al-qamīṣ rakhīṣ? — Do you think this shirt is cheap?
naʿam, ʾaẓunn dhālika. — Yes, I think so.
ẓanantu ʾanna al-maḥall maftūḥ. — I thought that the shop was open.
taẓunnīna ʾannahā sataʾtī. — You (f.) think that she will come.
hum yaẓunnūna ʾanna al-ḥidhāʾ kabīr. — They think the shoe is big.

exercises.prompt: What is the past of ظَنَّ with أَنَا?
What is the present of ظَنَّ with أَنْتِ?
What does هَلْ تَظُنّ أَنَّ هَذَا الْقَمِيص رَخِيص؟ ask?
options: Do you think this shirt is cheap?

exercises.prompt: What does ظَنَنْتُ أَنَّ الْمَحَلّ مَفْتُوح mean?
options: The shop thinks I am open
I think the shop is closed
I thought that the shop was open

exercises.prompt: What does نَعَمْ، أَظُنّ ذَلِكَ mean?
options: No, I did not think so

exercises.promptTranslation: I think the price is high.
I thought that the shop was open.
They think the shoe is big.

explanations.title: Five verbs to learn
explanations.body: Each of these verbs follows مَرَّ in the past: the shadda opens before تُ, تَ, تِ, نَا. In the present, the shadda stays: أَرُدّ, أَعُدّ, أَمُدّ, أَحُلّ. The verb ضَلَّ has a kasra in the present: أَضِلّ.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Notice which preposition or object each verb takes.

examples.translation: radadtu al-qamīṣ ʾilā al-maḥall. — I returned the shirt to the shop.
ʿadadtu ad-danānīr thumma dafaʿtu. — I counted the dinars and then I paid.
madadtu yadī ʾilā al-bāʾiʿ. — I stretched out my hand to the seller.
ḥalaltu al-mushkila. — I solved the problem.
ḍalaltu aṭ-ṭarīq fī as-sūq. — I lost my way in the market.
ʾaʿudd an-nuqūd qabla ad-dafʿ. — I count the money before paying.

exercises.prompt: What does رَدَدْتُ الْقَمِيص إِلَى الْمَحَلّ mean?
options: I returned the shirt to the shop
I bought the shirt in the shop

exercises.prompt: Which is the present of عَدَّ with أَنَا?
Which is the past of حَلَّ with أَنَا?

exercises.promptTranslation: I solved the problem.
I stretched out my hand to the seller.

exercises.explanation: Present: ثُمَّ أَدْفَع is also present.

lessons.subtitle: مَرَرْتُ بِالسُّوق · رَدَدْتُ الْقَمِيص · سَأَمُرّ بِالْمَقْهَى

explanations.title: A note on the table
explanations.body: Read this friendly note. It uses the double-letter verbs of this chapter in the past, present and future. The names are invented.

examples.translation: ʿazīzī sāmī, — Dear Sami,

examples.translation: marartu bis-sūq ṣabāḥan thumma ishtaraytu al-khubz wal-ḥalīb. — I passed by the market in the morning, then bought bread and milk.

saʾamurr bil-maqhā baʿda aẓ-ẓuhr. — I will pass by the coffee shop after noon.

maʿa taḥiyyātī, khālid. — With my greetings, Khalid.

lessons.title: 335. Writing an invitation
lessons.subtitle: يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ أَدْعُوَكَ · أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ تَحْضُر

explanations.title: Parts of an invitation
explanations.body: An invitation has a greeting, the invitation itself, the time and place, and a closing wish. The phrase يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ…, “I am pleased to…”, uses the double-letter verb سَرَّ (يَسُرُّ), with the pronoun ـنِي added. The verb دَعَا يَدْعُو, “to invite”, is one of the defective verbs of an earlier chapter.

rows: I am pleased to invite you

explanations.title: An invitation (invented)
explanations.body: Here is a short invitation, line by line.

examples.translation: ʿazīzī khālid, — Dear Khalid,

examples.text: يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ أَدْعُوَكَ إِلَى الْعَشَاء فِي بَيْتِي.
examples.translation: yasurrunī ʾan ʾadʿuwaka ʾilā al-ʿashāʾ fī baytī. — I am pleased to invite you to dinner at my house.

examples.text: الْمَوْعِد: يَوْم الْخَمِيس، السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة مَسَاءً.

ʾatamannā ʾan taḥḍur. — I hope you will attend.
maʿa ʾaṭyab at-taḥiyyāt, yūsuf. — With best regards, Yusuf.

lessons.title: 336. Review: shopping, exclamations and double-letter verbs
lessons.subtitle: أَيّ · مَا أَجْمَلَ · مَرَرْتُ · أَمُرّ · أَظُنّ

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: أَيّ + a singular noun asks “which?” and also means “any”. An exclamation is مَا + أَفْعَلَ + the thing in the accusative: مَا أَجْمَلَ الْقُبَّعَةَ! Double-letter verbs keep the shadda in the he/she/they past (مَرَّ, مَرَّتْ, مَرُّوا) and open it before consonant endings (مَرَرْتُ, مَرَرْنَا). In the present, the shadda stays: أَمُرّ, تَمُرّ, يَمُرُّونَ.

rows: I think the price is high

exercises.prompt: What does أَيّ مَقَاس تُرِيد؟ ask?

lessons.title: 337. Furniture and rooms
lessons.subtitle: أَثَاث · كُرْسِيّ · سَرِير · خِزَانَة · غُرْفَة النَّوْم

explanations.title: Things in a room
explanations.body: The word أَثَاث means “furniture” in general. For one piece, use the specific name. A bedroom is غُرْفَة النَّوْم (“the room of sleep”) and a living room is غُرْفَة الْجُلُوس (“the room of sitting”).

explanations.title: What is in the room
explanations.body: Use فِي + the room, then the things that are there.

examples.translation: fī ghurfa an-nawm sarīr wakhizāna. — In the bedroom there is a bed and a wardrobe.

examples.text: فِي غُرْفَة الْجُلُوس أَرِيكَة وَطَاوِلَة صَغِيرَة.
examples.translation: fī ghurfa al-julūs ʾarīka waṭāwila ṣaghīra. — In the living room there is a sofa and a small table.
al-maktab mina al-khashab. — The desk is made of wood.
ʾajlis ʿalā al-kursiyy. — I sit on the chair.
ʿalā al-ʾarḍ sajjāda jamīla. — On the floor there is a beautiful carpet.

exercises.prompt: What does الْمَكْتَب مِنَ الْخَشَب mean?
options: The desk is made of leather
The desk is made of wood
The desk is in the kitchen

exercises.explanation: The room with a bed is the bedroom.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the bedroom there is a bed and a wardrobe.

exercises.explanation: A living room has a sofa.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the living room there is a sofa and a small table.
I sit on the chair.

explanations.title: Quality and comfort
explanations.body: Use مُرِيح for “comfortable” and عَالِي الْجَوْدَة for “of high quality”. For non-human plurals, the adjective is feminine singular. So كُرْسِيّ مُرِيح is “a comfortable chair”, but كَرَاسِي مُرِيحَة is “comfortable chairs”. To compare, use أَغْلَى مِنْ (“more expensive than”) or أَرْخَص مِنْ (“cheaper than”).

explanations.title: In a showroom
explanations.body: These are typical phrases.

examples.translation: ʾurīd sarīr murīḥ wakabīr. — I want a comfortable, big bed.
ʿindanā karāsī murīḥa mina al-khashab. — We have comfortable wooden chairs.
hādhā al-ʾathāth ʿālī al-jawda. — This furniture is of high quality.

examples.text: الْكُرْسِيّ الْجَدِيد أَغْلَى مِنَ الْكُرْسِيّ الْقَدِيم.
examples.translation: al-kursiyy al-jadīd ʾaghlā mina al-kursiyy al-qadīm. — The new chair is more expensive than the old chair.

examples.text: الْأَرِيكَة الصَّغِيرَة أَرْخَص مِنَ الْأَرِيكَة الْكَبِيرَة.
examples.translation: al-ʾarīka aṣ-ṣaghīra ʾarkhaṣ mina al-ʾarīka al-kabīra. — The small sofa is cheaper than the large sofa.

exercises.explanation: Things in the plural take a feminine singular adjective.

exercises.prompt: What does عِنْدَنَا كَرَاسِي مُرِيحَة مِنَ الْخَشَب mean?
options: I sit on a wooden chair

exercises.prompt: What does الْكُرْسِيّ الْجَدِيد أَغْلَى مِنَ الْكُرْسِيّ الْقَدِيم suggest?
Which sofa is cheaper in the lesson?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want a comfortable, big bed.
We have comfortable chairs.
This furniture is of high quality.

explanations.title: A dialogue (invented)
explanations.body: A couple moving into an apartment talk with a salesman. Read the lines in order. The verb نَحْتَاج إِلَى means “we need” and is followed by إِلَى.

examples.translation: marḥaban, ʾayy khidma? — Welcome, how can I help?
naḥtāj ʾilā ʾathāth lish-shaqqa. — We need furniture for the apartment.

examples.text: عِنْدَنَا أَصْنَاف كَثِيرَة. هَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْأَثَاث الْحَدِيث؟
examples.translation: ʿindanā ʾaṣnāf kathīra. hal tuḥibbūna al-ʾathāth al-ḥadīth? — We have many kinds. Do you like modern furniture?

examples.text: نَعَمْ، لَكِنَّنَا لَا نُرِيد أَنْ نَدْفَع كَثِيرًا.
examples.translation: naʿam, lakinnanā lā nurīd ʾan nadfaʿ kathīran. — Yes, but we do not want to pay a lot.
hādhā as-sarīr rakhīṣ wamurīḥ. — This bed is cheap and comfortable.
kam thamanuhu? — How much is it?

explanations.title: Useful pieces
explanations.body: Ask for what you need with نَحْتَاج إِلَى or أُرِيد, say what you do not want with لَا نُرِيد, and ask the price with كَمْ.

exercises.prompt: What does نَحْتَاج إِلَى أَثَاث لِلشَّقَّة mean?
options: We sell furniture in the apartment
We need furniture for the apartment

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْأَثَاث الْحَدِيث؟ ask?
What does لَا نُرِيد أَنْ نَدْفَع كَثِيرًا mean?
options: We do not want to pay a lot
We want to pay a lot
exercises.explanation: لَا نُرِيد = we do not want.

exercises.prompt: What does the salesman say about the bed?
What does أَيّ خِدْمَة؟ mean here?

exercises.promptTranslation: We need furniture for the apartment.
We do not want to pay a lot.

exercises.explanation: The salesman speaks to the couple (plural).
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you (both) like modern furniture?

lessons.title: 340. Payment plans
lessons.subtitle: دُفْعَة أُولَى · أَقْسَاط شَهْرِيَّة · بِدُون فَوَائِد

explanations.title: Ways to pay
explanations.body: A store may let you pay all at once or in parts. A part is قِسْط, and the plural is أَقْسَاط. The first payment is الدُّفْعَة الْأُولَى. Interest is فَائِدَة (plural فَوَائِد). A cheque is شِيك. The sentences below describe an invented store; real stores have their own rules.

explanations.title: Choosing a plan (invented)
explanations.body: A customer asks, and the clerk answers.

examples.text: هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ أَدْفَع عَلَى أَقْسَاط؟
examples.translation: hal yumkin ʾan ʾadfaʿ ʿalā ʾaqsāṭ? — May I pay in instalments?
naʿam, ad-dufʿa al-ʾūlā ʿishrūn bil-miʾa. — Yes, the first payment is twenty per cent.
watadfaʿ qisṭan kull shahr. — And you pay an instalment every month.
hal hunāka fawāʾid? — Are there any interest charges?
lā, bidūn fawāʾid. — No, without interest.

examples.text: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَدْفَع نَقْدًا أَوْ بِشِيك.
examples.translation: yumkinuka ʾan tadfaʿ naqdan ʾaw bishīk. — You can pay in cash or by cheque.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ يُمْكِن أَنْ أَدْفَع عَلَى أَقْسَاط؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: May I pay in instalments?
And you pay an instalment every month.
No, without interest.

lessons.title: 341. Arranging delivery
lessons.subtitle: يَصِل الْأَثَاث يَوْم الْأَحَد · لَا تَنْسَ الْعُنْوَان

explanations.title: When will it arrive?
explanations.body: Delivery is تَوْصِيل, and free is مَجَّانِيّ. The verb وَصَلَ is an assimilated verb: past وَصَلَ, present يَصِل, imperative صِلْ. Remember the rule from chapter 16: when the subject is a plural thing, the verb is feminine singular, as in وَصَلَتِ الْأَجْهِزَة, “the appliances arrived”.

explanations.title: Talking to the store
explanations.body: Notice the negative command لَا تَنْسَ, “do not forget”, from the defective verb نَسِيَ.

examples.translation: hali at-tawṣīl majjāniyy? — Is delivery free?
naʿam, sayaṣil al-ʾathāth yawm al-ʾaḥad. — Yes, the furniture will arrive on Sunday.
waṣalati al-ʾajhiza al-jadīda ʾamsi. — The new appliances arrived yesterday.
lā tansa al-ʿunwān. — Do not forget the address.
saʾakūn fī al-bayt ṣabāḥan. — I will be at home in the morning.

exercises.prompt: What does سَيَصِل الْأَثَاث يَوْم الْأَحَد mean?
options: The furniture will arrive on Sunday
The furniture is free on Sunday

exercises.prompt: What does وَصَلَتِ الْأَجْهِزَة الْجَدِيدَة أَمْسِ mean?
options: The new appliances will arrive tomorrow

exercises.prompt: What does لَا تَنْسَ الْعُنْوَان mean?
Why is the verb وَصَلَتِ feminine?
options: the verb is in the future
the subject is a plural thing

exercises.promptTranslation: Yes, the furniture will arrive on Sunday.
The new appliances arrived yesterday.

exercises.explanation: After لَا (command), the shortened form: تَنْسَ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do not forget the address.

explanations.title: Words of the store's rules
explanations.body: A receipt is فَاتُورَة. A warranty is كَفَالَة; ضَمَان means “guarantee”. A defect is عَيْب, and repair is إِصْلَاح. The verb رَدَّ يَرُدّ means “to return (something)”; its noun رَدّ means “returning”. Each store has its own rules, and the examples below describe an invented store.

explanations.title: The rules (invented)
explanations.body: Notice the passive لَا يُقْبَل, “is not accepted”, and the double-letter verb تَرُدَّ, “you return”, after أَنْ.

examples.text: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَرُدَّ الْجِهَاز خِلَال سَبْعَة أَيَّام.
examples.translation: yumkinuka ʾan tarudda al-jihāz khilāl sabʿa ʾayyām. — You may return the appliance within seven days.

examples.text: لَا يُقْبَل رَدّ الْجِهَاز بِدُون فَاتُورَة.
examples.translation: lā yuqbal radd al-jihāz bidūn fātūra. — Returning the appliance is not accepted without a receipt.
iḥtafiẓ bil-fātūra. — Keep the receipt.
al-kafāla thalāth sanawāt. — The warranty is three years.
tashmal al-kafāla al-ʾiṣlāḥ al-majjāniyy. — The warranty covers free repair.

exercises.prompt: What does لَا يُقْبَل رَدّ الْجِهَاز بِدُون فَاتُورَة mean?
options: Returning the appliance is not accepted without a receipt
The appliance is free without a receipt

exercises.prompt: What does الْكَفَالَة ثَلَاث سَنَوَات mean?
يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ ___ الْجِهَاز خِلَال سَبْعَة أَيَّام.
exercises.explanation: After أَنْ, a present form with أَنْتَ: تَرُدَّ.
exercises.promptTranslation: You may return the appliance within seven days.
Returning the appliance is not accepted without a receipt.
The warranty covers free repair.

explanations.title: Appliances
explanations.body: An electrical appliance is جِهَاز كَهْرَبَائِيّ, and the plural is أَجْهِزَة كَهْرَبَائِيَّة. Each appliance does a job, and the jobs are verbs you know.

explanations.title: What each one does
explanations.body: The refrigerator is feminine, so its verb has تَـ. The air conditioner is masculine, so its verb has يَـ.

examples.translation: ath-thallāja taḥfaẓ aṭ-ṭaʿām. — The refrigerator keeps the food.
al-ghassāla taghsil ath-thiyāb. — The washing machine washes the clothes.
al-mukayyif yubarrid al-ghurfa. — The air conditioner cools the room.
al-furn yaṭbukh aṭ-ṭaʿām. — The oven cooks the food.
nurīd jihāzan kahrabāʾiyyan jadīdan. — We want a new electrical appliance.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of جِهَاز?

exercises.promptTranslation: The refrigerator keeps the food.
The air conditioner cools the room.
The washing machine washes the clothes.

lessons.title: 344. Choosing an appliance by its features
lessons.subtitle: سَعَة · صَامِت · كَفَالَة ثَلَاث سَنَوَات

explanations.title: Features and warranty
explanations.body: Shoppers compare size (سَعَة, “capacity”), noise (صَامِت, “silent, quiet”) and warranty (كَفَالَة). A warranty is written as كَفَالَة + the length of time in the genitive: كَفَالَة سَنَة, كَفَالَة سَنَتَيْن, كَفَالَة ثَلَاث سَنَوَات. Imagine a shopper who wants appliances with a warranty of at least three years. These ads are invented.

explanations.title: Reading the ads
explanations.body: Read each sentence and decide which appliance matches the shopper's rule.

examples.translation: ath-thallāja saʿatuhā kabīra wakafālatuhā sanatān. — The refrigerator's capacity is large and its warranty is two years.
al-ghassāla ṣāmita wakafālatuhā thalāth sanawāt. — The washing machine is quiet and its warranty is three years.
al-furn ʾabyaḍ wakafālatuhu sana. — The oven is white and its warranty is one year.

examples.text: الْمُكَيِّف يُوَفِّر الطَّاقَة، وَكَفَالَتُهُ خَمْس سَنَوَات.
examples.translation: al-mukayyif yuwaffir aṭ-ṭāqa, wakafālatuhu khams sanawāt. — The air conditioner saves energy, and its warranty is five years.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَجْهِزَة كَفَالَتُهَا ثَلَاث سَنَوَات عَلَى الْأَقَلّ.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾajhiza kafālatuhā thalāth sanawāt ʿalā al-ʾaqall. — I want appliances whose warranty is at least three years.

exercises.prompt: Which appliances have a warranty of at least three years?
options: the washing machine and the air conditioner
exercises.explanation: Three or more: غَسَّالَة (3) and مُكَيِّف (5).

exercises.prompt: According to the ads, which appliance is quiet?
Which appliance has the shortest warranty?

exercises.promptTranslation: a warranty of three years
The refrigerator's capacity is large and its warranty is two years.

exercises.prompt: أُرِيد أَجْهِزَة كَفَالَتُهَا ثَلَاث سَنَوَات عَلَى ___
exercises.promptTranslation: I want appliances whose warranty is at least three years.

explanations.title: Review: who, which, that
explanations.body: A relative pronoun links a clause to a definite noun and agrees with it. For a masculine singular noun: الَّذِي. For a feminine singular noun or a plural thing: الَّتِي. For people in the plural: الَّذِين. For two masculine persons: اللَّذَان.

explanations.title: In store sentences
explanations.body: Find the noun that each pronoun refers to.

examples.text: الزَّبُون الَّذِي دَفَعَ نَقْدًا حَصَلَ عَلَى خَصْم.
examples.translation: az-zabūn alladhī dafaʿa naqdan ḥaṣala ʿalā khaṣm. — The customer who paid in cash got a discount.
ath-thallāja allatī ishtaraytuhā kabīra. — The refrigerator that I bought is big.
al-ʾajhiza allatī waṣalat ʾamsi jadīda. — The appliances that arrived yesterday are new.
az-zabāʾin alladhīn dafaʿū naqdan saʿīdūn. — The customers who paid in cash are happy.

examples.text: الْبَائِعَان اللَّذَان يَعْمَلَان هُنَا مِنْ بَيْرُوت.
examples.translation: al-bāʾiʿān alladhān yaʿmalān hunā min bayrūt. — The two sellers who work here are from Beirut.

exercises.explanation: Plural things take the feminine singular.

exercises.prompt: What does الزَّبُون الَّذِي دَفَعَ نَقْدًا حَصَلَ عَلَى خَصْم mean?
options: The customer who paid in cash got a discount
The customer who got a discount paid by card

exercises.prompt: What does الْأَجْهِزَة الَّتِي وَصَلَتْ أَمْسِ جَدِيدَة mean?
options: The appliances that arrived yesterday are new

exercises.prompt: الزَّبُون ___ دَفَعَ نَقْدًا حَصَلَ عَلَى خَصْم.
exercises.promptTranslation: The customer who paid in cash got a discount.
The appliances that arrived yesterday are new.
The customers who paid in cash are happy.

lessons.title: 346. The apartment: rooms and floors
lessons.subtitle: شَقَّة · مَطْبَخ · حَمَّام · شُرْفَة · طَابِق · مِصْعَد

explanations.title: Parts of an apartment
explanations.body: An apartment is شَقَّة, and the building is عِمَارَة. The floors of a building are طَوَابِق (singular طَابِق). To say “on the third floor”, use فِي الطَّابِق الثَّالِث, with the ordinal after the noun.

explanations.title: Describing where things are
explanations.body: Combine these words with the place words you know.

examples.translation: ash-shaqqa fī aṭ-ṭābiq ath-thālith. — The apartment is on the third floor.
fī al-ʿimāra miṣʿad. — In the building there is an elevator.
al-maṭbakh wāsiʿ wafīhi nāfidha. — The kitchen is wide and has a window.
fī ash-shaqqa ghurfatān waḥammām. — In the apartment there are two rooms and a bathroom.
mina ash-shurfa manẓar jamīl. — From the balcony there is a beautiful view.

exercises.prompt: What does الشَّقَّة فِي الطَّابِق الثَّالِث mean?
options: The apartment is on the third floor

exercises.prompt: What does الْمَطْبَخ وَاسِع وَفِيهِ نَافِذَة mean?
options: The kitchen is wide and has a window
The window is in the bathroom

exercises.explanation: A building can have an elevator.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the building there is an elevator.

exercises.explanation: The ordinal agrees with the masculine noun طَابِق.
exercises.promptTranslation: The apartment is on the third floor.
In the apartment there are two rooms and a bathroom.

explanations.title: Renting words
explanations.body: Rent is إِيجَار, and the owner is مَالِك. A contract is عَقْد. The key is مِفْتَاح. A contract is for a period of time: لِمُدَّة سَنَة, “for a period of one year”. The terms below are examples; every country and every owner has different rules.

rows: for a period of a year

explanations.title: Examples (invented)
explanations.body: A tenant and an owner talk.

examples.translation: kami al-ʾījār ash-shahriyy? — How much is the monthly rent?
ʿaqd al-ʾījār limudda sana. — The rental contract is for one year.
ʾadfaʿ al-ʾījār ʾawwal kull shahr. — I pay the rent at the beginning of every month.
al-mālik yuʿṭīnī al-miftāḥ. — The owner gives me the key.
iqraʾi al-ʿaqd qabla at-tawqīʿ. — Read the contract before signing.

exercises.prompt: What does عَقْد الْإِيجَار لِمُدَّة سَنَة mean?
options: The contract is for a month
The rental contract is for one year
The owner lives for a year

exercises.prompt: What does أَدْفَع الْإِيجَار أَوَّل كُلّ شَهْر mean?
options: I pay the rent at the beginning of every month
I pay the rent at the end of the year
exercises.explanation: أَوَّل كُلّ شَهْر = beginning of each month.

exercises.prompt: What does اِقْرَأِ الْعَقْد قَبْلَ التَّوْقِيع mean?

exercises.explanation: The preposition لِـ with مُدَّة: for a period.
exercises.promptTranslation: The rental contract is for one year.
I pay the rent at the beginning of every month.

exercises.explanation: The one who gives the key is the owner.
exercises.promptTranslation: The owner gives me the key.

lessons.title: 348. Looking at an apartment
lessons.subtitle: هَلِ الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوشَة؟ · كَمْ غُرْفَة فِيهَا؟

explanations.title: Questions and commands
explanations.body: When you visit an apartment, ask short questions and give short commands. A furnished apartment is شَقَّة مَفْرُوشَة. A command to one man drops the present prefix and uses the short (jussive) form; if the stem would start with two consonants, a helping alif is added: اِفْتَحْ, “open!”. Before ال, a final sukūn takes a helping vowel: اِفْتَحِ الْبَاب.

rows: How many rooms are in it?

explanations.title: A visit (invented)
explanations.body: Read what the visitor and the owner say.

examples.translation: hali ash-shaqqa mafrūsha? — Is the apartment furnished?
naʿam, fīhā sarīr wakhizāna waṭāwila. — Yes, it has a bed, a wardrobe and a table.
kam ghurfa fīhā? — How many rooms are in it?
iftaḥi an-nāfidha min faḍlika. — Open the window, please.

examples.text: هَلْ هُنَاكَ مَاء سَاخِن فِي الْحَمَّام؟
examples.translation: hal hunāka māʾ sākhin fī al-ḥammām? — Is there hot water in the bathroom?
al-maṭbakh wāsiʿ, wal-ʾījār munāsib. — The kitchen is wide, and the rent is reasonable.

exercises.prompt: What does كَمْ غُرْفَة فِيهَا؟ ask?
options: How many rooms are in it?

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ هُنَاكَ مَاء سَاخِن؟ ask?
Why does اِفْتَحِ النَّافِذَة have a kasra on ح?
exercises.explanation: Final sukūn + ال takes a helping vowel.

exercises.promptTranslation: Open the window, please.
Is there hot water in the bathroom?

exercises.explanation: After كَمْ in a question: singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: How many rooms are in it?

explanations.title: A real-estate comparison (invented)
explanations.body: An agent describes two apartments. Compare them with the comparative forms you know: أَكْبَر, أَرْخَص, أَقْرَب. The word مِنْ means “than”.

explanations.title: What the agent says
explanations.body: Read the agent's comparisons.

examples.text: الشَّقَّة الْأُولَى أَرْخَص مِنَ الشَّقَّة الثَّانِيَة.
examples.translation: ash-shaqqa al-ʾūlā ʾarkhaṣ mina ash-shaqqa ath-thāniya. — The first apartment is cheaper than the second.

examples.text: الشَّقَّة الثَّانِيَة أَكْبَر وَفِيهَا ثَلَاث غُرَف.
examples.translation: ash-shaqqa ath-thāniya ʾakbar wafīhā thalāth ghuraf. — The second apartment is bigger and has three rooms.
ash-shaqqa al-ʾūlā ʾaqrab ʾilā as-sūq. — The first apartment is closer to the market.
manẓar ash-shaqqa ath-thāniya ʾajmal. — The view from the second apartment is more beautiful.
ʾayy shaqqa tufaḍḍil? — Which apartment do you prefer?

exercises.prompt: Which apartment is closer to the market?
Which apartment has the more beautiful view?
What does أَيّ شَقَّة تُفَضِّل؟ ask?
What does مِنْ mean in أَرْخَص مِنَ الشَّقَّة الثَّانِيَة?

exercises.promptTranslation: The first apartment is cheaper than the second.
The second apartment is bigger and has three rooms.
Which apartment do you prefer?

lessons.title: 350. Moving in: where do I put it?
lessons.subtitle: أَيْنَ أَضَع الْأَرِيكَة؟ · ضَعِ الْكُرْسِيّ هُنَا

explanations.title: Assimilated verbs when you move
explanations.body: وَضَعَ يَضَع means “to put”. It is an assimilated verb: the و drops in the present (أَضَع) and in the command (ضَعْ). Before ال, the command takes a helping vowel: ضَعِ الْكُرْسِيّ. For “do not put”, say لَا تَضَعْ. The verb نَقَلَ يَنْقُل means “to carry, to move (something)”.

explanations.title: Directing the movers
explanations.body: These are typical sentences when furniture is moved.

examples.translation: ʾayna ʾaḍaʿ al-ʾarīka? — Where do I put the sofa?
ḍaʿi al-ʾarīka bijānib an-nāfidha. — Put the sofa next to the window.
ḍaʿī aṭ-ṭāwila fī wasaṭ al-ghurfa. — Put the table in the middle of the room (to a woman).
lā taḍaʿi al-khizāna ʾamāma al-bāb. — Do not put the wardrobe in front of the door.
nanqul al-ʾathāth ʾilā aṭ-ṭābiq ath-thālith. — We carry the furniture to the third floor.
waḍaʿtu al-kursiyy hunā ʾamsi. — I put the chair here yesterday.

exercises.prompt: What does أَيْنَ أَضَع الْأَرِيكَة؟ ask?
options: Where do I put the sofa?

exercises.prompt: What does ضَعِ الْأَرِيكَة بِجَانِب النَّافِذَة mean?
options: Put the sofa next to the window
Open the window near the sofa

exercises.prompt: What does لَا تَضَعِ الْخِزَانَة أَمَامَ الْبَاب mean?
options: The wardrobe is in the door
Do not put the wardrobe in front of the door
Put the wardrobe in front of the door

exercises.prompt: What does نَنْقُل الْأَثَاث إِلَى الطَّابِق الثَّالِث mean?
options: We carry the furniture to the third floor

exercises.prompt: Which is the command to a woman?

exercises.promptTranslation: Put the sofa next to the window.
Do not put the wardrobe in front of the door.
Where do I put the sofa?

lessons.title: 351. Reading a sale flyer
lessons.subtitle: تَبْدَأ التَّخْفِيضَات يَوْم السَّبْت · اِشْتَرِ الْآن

explanations.title: Flyer language
explanations.body: A sale flyer uses short sentences and commands. Remember chapter 16: when the subject is a plural thing such as التَّخْفِيضَات (“the sales”) or أَجْهِزَة (“appliances”), a verb that comes first is feminine singular: تَبْدَأ, تَنْتَهِي, تَصِل. A command with a defective verb loses its final long vowel: اِشْتَرِ (from اِشْتَرَى). A short exclamation uses مَا + أَفْعَلَ + the thing in the accusative: مَا أَرْخَصَ هَذِهِ الْأَسْعَارَ! The flyer below is invented.

explanations.title: Sentences from the flyer
explanations.body: Read the lines in order.

examples.translation: tabdaʾ at-takhfīḍāt yawm as-sabt. — The sales start on Saturday.
tantahī at-takhfīḍāt yawm al-jumʿa. — The sales end on Friday.
taṣil ʾajhiza jadīda kull ʾusbūʿ. — New appliances arrive every week.
ishtari al-ʾān walā tansa al-fātūra. — Buy now and do not forget the receipt.
al-khaṣm ʿalā al-ʾathāth faqaṭ. — The discount is on furniture only.
mā ʾarkhaṣa hādhihi al-ʾasʿāra! — How cheap these prices are!

exercises.prompt: Why is the verb تَبْدَأ feminine in تَبْدَأ التَّخْفِيضَات?
options: the subject is a plural thing
exercises.explanation: Plural things take a feminine singular verb.

exercises.prompt: What does تَنْتَهِي التَّخْفِيضَات يَوْم الْجُمْعَة mean?
options: The sales are free on Friday

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَرْخَصَ هَذِهِ الْأَسْعَارَ! express?

exercises.promptTranslation: The sales start on Saturday.
New appliances arrive every week.
Buy now and do not forget the receipt.

lessons.title: 352. A delivery problem
lessons.subtitle: لَمْ تَصِلِ الْغَسَّالَة · وَجَدْتُ عَيْبًا · سَنَرُدّ لَكَ الْمَبْلَغ

explanations.title: A conversation (invented)
explanations.body: A customer calls the store about a late delivery and a defect. Notice the assimilated verbs وَصَلَ, وَجَدَ, وَعَدَ; the negative past لَمْ تَصِلْ; and the double-letter verb in سَنَرُدّ, “we will return”.

examples.translation: lam taṣili al-ghassāla ʾamsi. — The washing machine did not arrive yesterday.
waʿadanī al-bāʾiʿ bit-tawṣīl ʾamsi. — The seller promised me delivery yesterday.
naʿtadhir, sataṣil al-ghassāla ghadan ṣabāḥan. — We apologise; the washing machine will arrive tomorrow morning.
wajadtu ʿayban fī ath-thallāja. — I found a defect in the refrigerator.
ʾarsil lī al-fātūra min faḍlika. — Send me the receipt, please.
sanarudd laka al-mablagh khilāl ʾusbūʿ. — We will return the amount to you within a week.

exercises.prompt: What does لَمْ تَصِلِ الْغَسَّالَة أَمْسِ mean?
options: The washing machine will not arrive
The washing machine did not arrive yesterday

exercises.prompt: What does وَعَدَنِي الْبَائِع بِالتَّوْصِيل mean?
options: The seller paid me for delivery

exercises.prompt: What does وَجَدْتُ عَيْبًا فِي الثَّلَّاجَة mean?
options: I found a defect in the refrigerator

exercises.prompt: What does سَنَرُدّ لَكَ الْمَبْلَغ mean?
options: We will return the amount to you
We will send you a receipt

exercises.prompt: What does أَرْسِلْ لِي الْفَاتُورَة mean?
exercises.explanation: أَرْسِلْ = send! (to one man); لِي = to me.

exercises.promptTranslation: The washing machine did not arrive yesterday.
I found a defect in the refrigerator.
We will return the amount to you within a week.

lessons.title: 353. A story: buying a bedroom set (invented)
lessons.subtitle: ذَهَبَتْ نَادِيَة وَصَدِيقَتُهَا إِلَى مَحَلّ الْأَثَاث

explanations.title: A short story
explanations.body: This invented story uses everything from the last chapters: a verb before a compound subject, verbs of Measures II, IV, VIII and X, a relative pronoun, a passive, and defective verbs. A bedroom set is طَقْم غُرْفَة النَّوْم. Read it sentence by sentence.

examples.text: ذَهَبَتْ نَادِيَة وَصَدِيقَتُهَا إِلَى مَحَلّ الْأَثَاث.
examples.translation: dhahabat nādiya waṣadīqatuhā ʾilā maḥall al-ʾathāth. — Nadia and her friend went to the furniture shop.
istaqbalahumā al-bāʾiʿ maʿa ibtisāma. — The salesman welcomed them with a smile.

examples.text: أَقْنَعَهُمَا الْبَائِع بِطَقْم غُرْفَة النَّوْم الَّذِي كَفَالَتُهُ ثَلَاث سَنَوَات.
examples.translation: ʾaqnaʿahumā al-bāʾiʿ biṭaqm ghurfa an-nawm alladhī kafālatuhu thalāth sanawāt. — The salesman convinced them to take the bedroom set whose warranty is three years.

examples.text: اِخْتَارَتْ نَادِيَة الدَّفْع عَلَى أَقْسَاط شَهْرِيَّة.
examples.translation: ikhtārat nādiya ad-dafʿ ʿalā ʾaqsāṭ shahriyya. — Nadia chose to pay in monthly instalments.
yusallam al-ʾathāth baʿda yawmayn. — The furniture is delivered after two days.

examples.text: كَانَتْ نَادِيَة سَعِيدَة، وَلَمْ تَنْسَ الْفَاتُورَة.
examples.translation: kānat nādiya saʿīda, walam tansa al-fātūra. — Nadia was happy, and she did not forget the receipt.

exercises.prompt: Where did Nadia and her friend go?
How long is the warranty of the bedroom set?
How did Nadia choose to pay?
Which verb in the story is passive?
What does الَّذِي refer to in the third sentence?
exercises.explanation: الَّذِي agrees with the first noun, masculine طَقْم.
A verb before its subject: feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: Nadia and her friend went to the furniture shop.
Nadia chose to pay in monthly instalments.

exercises.explanation: After لَمْ, the shortened present: تَنْسَ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Nadia was happy, and she did not forget the receipt.

lessons.title: 354. Review: chapters 16–20
lessons.subtitle: plural things · relative pronouns · passive · defective · double-letter

explanations.title: What the unit taught
explanations.body: Look back over the unit. A verb before a plural thing is feminine singular. A relative pronoun agrees with its noun. The passive changes the vowels: يُقْبَل. Defective verbs shorten their last vowel after لَا, لَمْ and in commands. Assimilated verbs drop the و in the present and command. Double-letter verbs open the shadda before consonant endings. An exclamation is built as مَا + a word like أَجْمَلَ + the thing in the accusative.

rows: the washing machine that I bought

exercises.prompt: Which verb fits: ___ الْأَجْهِزَة الْجَدِيدَة أَمْسِ?
What does لَا يُقْبَل رَدّ الْجِهَاز mean?
options: Returning the appliance is not accepted

exercises.prompt: What does ضَعِ الْكُرْسِيّ هُنَا mean?
What does مَا أَجْمَلَ الشُّرْفَةَ! express?
What is the past of مَرَّ with أَنَا?

exercises.promptTranslation: Do not forget the receipt.
The warranty is three years.
I returned the amount to the shop.

units.title: السَّفَر وَالْمَصْرِف: trip planning, conjunctions, security and banking

lessons.title: 355. At the travel agency
lessons.subtitle: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز رِحْلَة · خَصْم لِحَجْز مَجْمُوعَة

explanations.title: Words for booking a trip
explanations.body: A travel agency is وِكَالَة سِيَاحَة and a tour is رِحْلَة سِيَاحِيَّة. To book is حَجَزَ يَحْجِز, and a booking is حَجْز. A booking for a whole group is حَجْز لِمَجْمُوعَة, and a discount is خَصْم. After أُرِيد you can use أَنْ and a present verb: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز, “I want to book”.

explanations.title: At the agency (invented)
explanations.body: A traveller talks to an agent about a holiday for six people.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز رِحْلَة سِيَاحِيَّة لِسِتَّة أَفْرَاد.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾaḥjiz riḥla siyāḥiyya lisitta ʾafrād. — I want to book a tour for six people.
hal hunāka khaṣm liḥajz majmūʿa? — Is there a discount for a group booking?
naʿam, al-khaṣm ʿishrūn bil-miʾa. — Yes, the discount is twenty per cent.
nurīd ʾijāza limudda ʾusbūʿayn. — We want a holiday of two weeks.
sanazūr sūriyā wal-ʾurdunn wamiṣr wal-maghrib. — We will visit Syria, Jordan, Egypt and Morocco.
nurīd fanādiq jayyida bisiʿr munāsib. — We want good hotels at a suitable price.

exercises.prompt: What does أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِز رِحْلَة mean?
options: I want to cancel a trip
I want to book a trip
I will pay for a trip

exercises.prompt: What does سَنَزُور سُورِيَا وَالْأُرْدُنّ mean?
options: We will leave Syria and Jordan
We live in Syria and Jordan
We will visit Syria and Jordan

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to book a trip for six people.

exercises.explanation: A booking can get a discount.
exercises.promptTranslation: Is there a discount for a group booking?

exercises.explanation: After لِمُدَّة a dual noun takes the genitive form: ـَيْن.
exercises.promptTranslation: We want a holiday of two weeks.

lessons.title: 356. Planning the route
lessons.subtitle: سَنَبِيت فِي دِمَشْق لَيْلَتَيْن · نَنْوِي أَنْ نَزُور أَرْبَع دُوَل

explanations.title: Verbs of a journey
explanations.body: These verbs are useful when you plan a route. زَارَ يَزُور (“to visit”) and عَادَ يَعُود (“to return”) are hollow; بَاتَ يَبِيت (“to spend the night”) is hollow too; نَوَى يَنْوِي (“to intend”) is defective. Time words help to order the plan: بِدَايَة الشَّهْر (“the beginning of the month”), مُنْتَصَف الشَّهْر (“the middle of the month”) and نِهَايَة الشَّهْر (“the end of the month”).

explanations.title: A plan for the trip (invented)
explanations.body: Six friends plan a two-week journey.

examples.translation: nanwī ʾan nazūr ʾarbaʿ duwal. — We intend to visit four countries.
sanabīt fī dimashq laylatayn. — We will spend two nights in Damascus.

examples.text: بَعْد ذَلِكَ نُسَافِر بِالْحَافِلَة إِلَى عَمَّان.
examples.translation: baʿd dhālika nusāfir bil-ḥāfila ʾilā ʿammān. — After that we travel by bus to Amman.

examples.text: سَنَصِل إِلَى الْمَغْرِب فِي مُنْتَصَف الشَّهْر.
examples.translation: sanaṣil ʾilā al-maghrib fī muntaṣaf ash-shahr. — We will arrive in Morocco in the middle of the month.

examples.text: وَفِي نِهَايَة الرِّحْلَة نَعُود إِلَى الْكُوَيْت.
examples.translation: wafī nihāya ar-riḥla naʿūd ʾilā al-kuwayt. — And at the end of the trip we return to Kuwait.
khaṭṭaṭnā lir-riḥla mundhu shahr. — We have been planning the trip for a month.

exercises.prompt: What does نَنْوِي أَنْ نَزُور mean?
What does سَنَبِيت فِي دِمَشْق mean?
options: We will spend the night in Damascus
We spent the night in Damascus
exercises.explanation: سَنَبِيت = we will spend the night.

exercises.prompt: What does نَعُود إِلَى الْكُوَيْت mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: We intend to visit four countries.

exercises.explanation: In the middle of the month.
exercises.promptTranslation: We will arrive in Morocco in the middle of the month.
And at the end of the trip we return to Kuwait.

lessons.title: 357. Class, price and what is included
lessons.subtitle: الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى · الدَّرَجَة السِّيَاحِيَّة · هَلِ السِّعْر يَشْمَل الْفُنْدُق؟

explanations.title: First class and economy
explanations.body: A ticket can be in the first class, الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى, or in the tourist class, الدَّرَجَة السِّيَاحِيَّة (“economy”). The verb شَمِلَ is used for “to include” here as يَشْمَل: السِّعْر يَشْمَل التَّذَاكِر, “the price includes the tickets”. To compare, use أَغْلَى مِنْ (“more expensive than”) and أَرْخَص مِنْ (“cheaper than”).

explanations.title: Questions about the price (invented)
explanations.body: These are typical questions and answers at an agency.

examples.translation: hali as-siʿr yashmal al-funduq? — Does the price include the hotel?

examples.text: السِّعْر يَشْمَل التَّذَاكِر وَالْإِقَامَة وَمُرْشِد سِيَاحِيّ.
examples.translation: as-siʿr yashmal at-tadhākir wal-ʾiqāma wamurshid siyāḥiyy. — The price includes the tickets, the stay and a tour guide.

examples.text: تَذْكِرَة الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى أَغْلَى مِنْ تَذْكِرَة الدَّرَجَة السِّيَاحِيَّة.
examples.translation: tadhkira ad-daraja al-ʾūlā ʾaghlā min tadhkira ad-daraja as-siyāḥiyya. — A first-class ticket is more expensive than an economy ticket.
nurīd ad-daraja as-siyāḥiyya. — We want economy class.
hali at-tawṣīl mina al-maṭār majjāniyy? — Is the transfer from the airport free?
naʿam, at-tawṣīl majjāniyy. — Yes, the transfer is free.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلِ السِّعْر يَشْمَل الْفُنْدُق؟ ask?
options: Does the price include the hotel?

exercises.promptTranslation: Does the price include the hotel?

exercises.prompt: تَذْكِرَة الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى ___ مِنْ تَذْكِرَة الدَّرَجَة السِّيَاحِيَّة.
exercises.promptTranslation: A first-class ticket is more expensive than an economy ticket.
Is the transfer from the airport free?

lessons.title: 358. And, and then at once: وَ and فَ
lessons.subtitle: ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَطَار وَرَكِبْنَا الطَّائِرَة · وَصَلْنَا فَرَكِبْنَا الْحَافِلَة

explanations.title: Two small conjunctions
explanations.body: A conjunction joins two words or two clauses. وَ (“and”) simply adds one thing to another. فَ (“and so, and then at once”) joins two actions that follow each other without a break. Both are written as part of the next word: وَرَكِبْنَا, فَرَكِبْنَا.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: In each pair, notice which action follows the other immediately.

examples.translation: dhahabnā ʾilā al-maṭār warakibnā aṭ-ṭāʾira. — We went to the airport and boarded the plane.
waṣalnā farakibnā al-ḥāfila. — We arrived and at once took the bus.
dakhala al-muwaẓẓaf fasallama ʿalaynā. — The employee came in and at once greeted us.

examples.text: سَنَذْهَب إِلَى دِمَشْق فَعَمَّان بِدُون تَوَقُّف.
examples.translation: sanadhhab ʾilā dimashq faʿammān bidūn tawaqquf. — We will go to Damascus and then straight to Amman without stopping.
zurnā al-matḥaf was-sūq wal-funduq. — We visited the museum, the market and the hotel.
katabtu al-biṭāqa waʾarsaltuhā. — I wrote the card and sent it.

exercises.prompt: Which conjunction means “and then at once”?
What does وَصَلْنَا فَرَكِبْنَا الْحَافِلَة mean?
options: We did not take the bus
We took the bus and then arrived
We arrived and at once took the bus

exercises.prompt: In دَخَلَ الْمُوَظَّف فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْنَا, what does فَ show?
options: the greeting came right after he entered
exercises.explanation: فَ links actions that follow without a break.

options: with a space and a dash
exercises.explanation: وَ and فَ are attached to the next word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “We visited the museum and the market”?

exercises.promptTranslation: We went to the airport and boarded the plane.
We visited the museum and the market.
I wrote the card and sent it.

lessons.title: 359. Then, or: ثُمَّ and أَوْ
lessons.subtitle: ثُمَّ نُسَافِر إِلَى الْمَغْرِب · الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى أَوِ السِّيَاحِيَّة

explanations.title: Later: ثُمَّ. A choice: أَوْ
explanations.body: ثُمَّ (“then, after that”) is a separate word. It joins two actions with a gap of time between them, unlike فَ. أَوْ (“or”) gives a choice. Before ال it takes a helping vowel: أَوِ السِّيَاحِيَّة.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Read the sentences and decide: add, at once, later, or choose.

examples.text: سَنَبِيت خَمْسَة أَيَّام ثُمَّ نُسَافِر إِلَى الْمَغْرِب.
examples.translation: sanabīt khamsa ʾayyām thumma nusāfir ʾilā al-maghrib. — We will stay five days and then travel to Morocco.

examples.text: هَلْ تُرِيدُون الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى أَوِ السِّيَاحِيَّة؟
examples.translation: hal turīdūn ad-daraja al-ʾūlā ʾawi as-siyāḥiyya? — Do you want first class or economy?
nadhhab biṭ-ṭāʾira ʾaw bil-ḥāfila. — We go by plane or by bus.

examples.text: زُرْنَا عَمَّان ثُمَّ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْقُدْس.
examples.translation: zurnā ʿammān thumma dhahabnā ʾilā al-quds. — We visited Amman and then went on to Jerusalem.
ishtaraynā at-tadhākir thumma ḥajaznā al-funduq. — We bought the tickets and then booked the hotel.
mādhā tufaḍḍil: al-ʿaṣīr ʾawi al-qahwa? — Which do you prefer: juice or coffee?

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between ثُمَّ and فَ?
options: ثُمَّ leaves a gap of time
exercises.explanation: فَ = at once; ثُمَّ = after a time.

exercises.prompt: What does سَنَبِيت خَمْسَة أَيَّام ثُمَّ نُسَافِر mean?
options: We will travel and then stay
We will stay five days and then travel

exercises.prompt: Why is it أَوِ السِّيَاحِيَّة with a kasra?
options: the sukūn takes a helping vowel before ال
exercises.explanation: A final sukūn before ال takes a helping vowel.

exercises.promptTranslation: We stay five days and then travel.
We go by plane or by bus.

exercises.explanation: Before ال the sukūn takes a helping vowel.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you want first class or economy?

lessons.title: 360. After a conjunction: the same case
lessons.subtitle: رَأَيْتُ الْمُدِيرَ وَالْمُوَظَّفَ · وَصَلَ الْمُدِيرُ وَالْمُوَظَّفُ

explanations.title: The second part follows the first
explanations.body: A conjunction joins two things of the same kind, so the second noun takes the same case as the first. In this lesson the case endings are written out, although in most of the course they are left off: the nominative ends in ḍamma (ـُ), the accusative in fatḥa (ـَ) and the genitive in kasra (ـِ).

rows: The manager and the employee arrived.
I saw the manager and the employee.
I spoke with the manager and the employee.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: Notice that both nouns always end in the same vowel.

examples.translation: waṣala al-mudīru wal-muwaẓẓafu. — The manager and the employee arrived.
raʾaytu al-mudīra wal-muwaẓẓafa. — I saw the manager and the employee.
takallamtu maʿa al-mudīri wal-muwaẓẓafi. — I spoke with the manager and the employee.
al-maṭāru wal-funduqu qarībāni. — The airport and the hotel are near.
zurtu al-matḥafa was-sūqa. — I visited the museum and the market.
dhahabtu ʾilā al-matḥafi was-sūqi. — I went to the museum and the market.

exercises.prompt: Which vowel mark is the accusative ending?
Which vowel mark is the genitive ending?
Which case follows a preposition such as مَعَ or إِلَى?
exercises.explanation: A preposition is followed by the genitive.

exercises.prompt: What is the rule for a conjunction?
options: the second noun is always nominative
the second noun is always genitive
the second noun has the same case as the first
the second noun has no ending

exercises.explanation: Both are accusative: ـَ and ـَ.

exercises.prompt: Why does الْمُوَظَّفِ end in a kasra in تَكَلَّمْتُ مَعَ الْمُدِيرِ وَالْمُوَظَّفِ?
options: it follows the genitive الْمُدِيرِ after مَعَ
exercises.explanation: The second noun copies the case of the first.
The first noun is accusative, so the second is accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I saw the manager and the employee.

exercises.explanation: The first noun is nominative, so the second is nominative.
exercises.promptTranslation: The manager and the employee arrived.

exercises.explanation: The first noun is genitive, so the second is genitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I spoke with the manager and the employee.

lessons.title: 361. Choosing the right conjunction
lessons.subtitle: وَ · فَ · ثُمَّ · أَوْ فِي قِصَّة قَصِيرَة

explanations.title: A short story (invented)
explanations.body: Sara plans a trip. Read the story and notice which conjunction fits each step: addition (وَ), an immediate next step (فَ), a later step (ثُمَّ) or a choice (أَوْ).

examples.text: حَجَزَتْ سَارَة رِحْلَة إِلَى الْمَغْرِب ثُمَّ اِشْتَرَتْ تَذْكِرَتَيْن.
examples.translation: ḥajazat sāra riḥla ʾilā al-maghrib thumma ishtarat tadhkiratayn. — Sara booked a trip to Morocco and then bought two tickets.
waṣalat ʾilā al-maṭār fadakhalat mubāsharatan. — She arrived at the airport and went straight in.

examples.text: هَلْ تُفَضِّلِينَ الْمَقْعَد قُرْب النَّافِذَة أَوْ قُرْب الْبَاب؟
examples.translation: hal tufaḍḍilīna al-maqʿad qurb an-nāfidha ʾaw qurb al-bāb? — Do you prefer a seat near the window or near the door?
rakibati aṭ-ṭāʾira waqaraʾat jarīda. — She boarded the plane and read a newspaper.
baʿd sāʿatayn waṣalati aṭ-ṭāʾira. — After two hours the plane arrived.
nazalat mina aṭ-ṭāʾira fawajadat ʾakhāhā. — She got off the plane and at once found her brother.

exercises.prompt: Which word fits: حَجَزَتْ رِحْلَة ___ اِشْتَرَتْ تَذْكِرَتَيْن (a later step)?
Which conjunction fits: هَلْ تُفَضِّلِينَ النَّافِذَة ___ الْبَاب?
In وَصَلَتْ فَدَخَلَتْ, what does فَ tell us?
Which sentence adds one action to another?
Which sentence means “She got off the plane and at once found her brother”?
options: نَزَلَتْ مِنَ الطَّائِرَة أَوْ وَجَدَتْ أَخَاهَا

exercises.prompt: Which conjunction is a separate word, not joined to the next one?
exercises.explanation: وَ and فَ are attached; ثُمَّ and أَوْ are separate words.

exercises.prompt: حَجَزْتُ التَّذْكِرَة ___ دَفَعْتُ الْمَبْلَغ بَعْد يَوْمَيْن.
exercises.explanation: A gap of two days: then.
exercises.promptTranslation: I booked the ticket and then paid the amount two days later.

exercises.prompt: هَلْ سَتَسْكُنِينَ فِي فُنْدُق ___ فِي شَقَّة؟
exercises.promptTranslation: Will you live in a hotel or in an apartment?

exercises.explanation: Written attached: فَسَلَّمَ. No wait between the two actions.
exercises.promptTranslation: The employee came into the room and at once greeted us.

lessons.title: 362. Security precautions
lessons.subtitle: الْإِجْرَاءَات الْأَمْنِيَّة · جِهَاز كَشْف الْمَعَادِن · أَبْرِزْ جَوَاز السَّفَر

explanations.title: At the security check
explanations.body: Security at an airport is أَمْن, and the security procedures are الْإِجْرَاءَات الْأَمْنِيَّة. A search is تَفْتِيش, and the verb is فَتَّشَ (Measure II). The commands you hear are short: أَبْرِزْ (Measure IV, “show!”), ضَعْ (“put!”), اِمْشِ (“walk!”). Rules differ from one airport to another.

explanations.title: What the officer says (invented)
explanations.body: These are typical lines at a checkpoint.

examples.translation: al-ʾijrāʾāt al-ʾamniyya fī al-maṭārāt mushaddada. — Security procedures at airports are strict.
ʾabriz jawāz as-safar wabiṭāqa aṣ-ṣuʿūd. — Show your passport and boarding pass.
ḍaʿ ḥaqībataka ʿalā al-jihāz. — Put your bag on the machine.

examples.text: اِمْشِ مِنْ خِلَال جِهَاز كَشْف الْمَعَادِن.
examples.translation: imshi min khilāl jihāz kashf al-maʿādin. — Walk through the metal detector.
fattasha al-muwaẓẓaf ḥaqībatī. — The officer searched my bag.
lā tatruk ḥaqībataka waḥdahā. — Do not leave your bag alone.

exercises.prompt: What does أَبْرِزْ جَوَاز السَّفَر mean?
What does لَا تَتْرُكْ حَقِيبَتَكَ وَحْدَهَا mean?
options: Do not leave your bag alone

exercises.prompt: What does مُشَدَّدَة mean in الْإِجْرَاءَات مُشَدَّدَة?
Who does فَتَّشَ الْمُوَظَّف حَقِيبَتِي describe?
options: the officer will search my bag

exercises.explanation: A command to one man (Measure IV): أَبْرِزْ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Show the passport and the boarding pass.
The officer searched my bag.
Walk through the metal detector.

lessons.title: 363. What may you carry?
lessons.subtitle: حَقِيبَة الْيَد · الْأَمْتِعَة · الْحَدّ الْأَقْصَى لِلْوَزْن

explanations.title: Hand luggage and checked bags
explanations.body: Your hand bag is حَقِيبَة الْيَد. The bags you check in are الْأَمْتِعَة الْمُسَجَّلَة. The heaviest weight allowed is الْحَدّ الْأَقْصَى لِلْوَزْن. Something not allowed is مَمْنُوع. Airlines and airports have their own rules, so always read the notice.

explanations.title: A notice (invented)
explanations.body: A notice at the check-in desk of an invented airline.

examples.translation: al-ḥadd al-ʾaqṣā lil-wazn ʿishrūn kīlū. — The maximum weight is twenty kilos.
ḥaqība al-yad tadkhul aṭ-ṭāʾira maʿaka. — The hand bag goes into the plane with you.

examples.text: السَّكَاكِين وَالْمِقَصَّات مَمْنُوعَة فِي حَقِيبَة الْيَد.
examples.translation: as-sakākīn wal-miqaṣṣāt mamnūʿa fī ḥaqība al-yad. — Knives and scissors are not allowed in the hand bag.
as-sawāʾil fī zujājāt kabīra mamnūʿa. — Liquids in large bottles are not allowed.
nusajjil al-ʾamtiʿa ʿinda al-maktab. — We check in the bags at the desk.
qif hunā min faḍlika. — Stand here, please.

exercises.prompt: What does الْحَدّ الْأَقْصَى لِلْوَزْن mean?
Which are forbidden in the notice?
options: knives and scissors in the hand bag

exercises.prompt: Why is it مَمْنُوعَة with ـَة in السَّكَاكِين وَالْمِقَصَّات مَمْنُوعَة?
options: a plural of things takes the feminine singular

exercises.promptTranslation: The maximum weight is twenty kilos.
Knives are not allowed in the hand bag.
We check in the bags at the desk.

lessons.title: 364. At the check-in desk (a dialogue)
lessons.subtitle: جَوَاز سَفَرِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ · هَلْ مَعَكَ حَقِيبَة يَد؟

explanations.title: A conversation (invented)
explanations.body: A passenger and an employee talk at an invented airline desk. Read the lines in order.

examples.translation: jawāz safarika watadhkiratuka min faḍlika. — Your passport and your ticket, please.
tafaḍḍal. — Here you are.
hal maʿaka ḥaqība yad? — Do you have a hand bag with you?
naʿam, ḥaqība ṣaghīra faqaṭ. — Yes, only a small bag.
ḍaʿi al-ḥaqība al-kabīra ʿalā al-mīzān. — Put the big bag on the scale.
waznuhā ithnān waʿishrūn kīlū. — Its weight is twenty-two kilos.
ʾāsif, al-ḥadd al-ʾaqṣā ʿishrūn kīlū. — I am sorry, the maximum is twenty kilos.
riḥla saʿīda, al-bawwāba raqm khamsa. — Have a good trip. Gate number five.

exercises.explanation: تَفَضَّلْ is said when you hand something over.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ مَعَكَ حَقِيبَة يَد؟ ask?
options: How much is the hand bag?
Do you have a hand bag with you?

exercises.prompt: What does the clerk ask for first?
How heavy is the big bag?
What does آسِف، الْحَدّ الْأَقْصَى عِشْرُون كِيلُو mean?
options: I am sorry, the plane is late
I am sorry, the bag is lost
I am sorry, the maximum is twenty kilos
I am happy, the bag is light

exercises.promptTranslation: Your passport, please.
Put the bag on the scale.
Have a good trip.

lessons.title: 365. More crowded, less used: أَكْثَر with a verbal noun
lessons.subtitle: أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا مِنْ · أَقَلّ اِسْتِخْدَامًا مِنْ

explanations.title: When there is no أَفْعَل adjective
explanations.body: You know comparatives such as أَكْبَر مِنْ and أَسْرَع مِنْ. When a quality has no short comparative of that kind, say أَكْثَر (“more”) or أَقَلّ (“less”) followed by a verbal noun with the accusative tanwīn (ـًا or ـَةً): أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا, “more crowded”. The word مِنْ means “than”. The verbal noun is the one of the verb: اِزْدَحَمَ → اِزْدِحَام.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Read the comparisons.

examples.text: الْقِطَار أَسْرَع مِنَ الْحَافِلَة وَأَقَلّ اِزْدِحَامًا.
examples.translation: al-qiṭār ʾasraʿ mina al-ḥāfila waʾaqall izdiḥāman. — The train is faster than the bus and less crowded.

examples.text: هَذَا الطَّرِيق أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا فِي الصَّبَاح.
examples.translation: hādhā aṭ-ṭarīq ʾakthar izdiḥāman fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — This road is more crowded in the morning.

examples.text: هَذَا الْفُنْدُق أَكْثَر رَاحَةً مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفُنْدُق.
examples.translation: hādhā al-funduq ʾakthar rāḥatan min dhālika al-funduq. — This hotel is more comfortable than that hotel.

examples.text: هَذِهِ الشَّرِكَة أَكْثَر نَجَاحًا مِنَ الشَّرِكَة الْأُخْرَى.
examples.translation: hādhihi ash-sharika ʾakthar najāḥan mina ash-sharika al-ʾukhrā. — This company is more successful than the other company.
funduqunā ʾaqall siʿran. — Our hotel is lower in price.

examples.text: الْخِطَابَات أَقَلّ اِسْتِخْدَامًا مِنَ الْبَرِيد الْإِلِكْتْرُونِيّ.
examples.translation: al-khiṭābāt ʾaqall istikhdāman mina al-barīd al-ʾiliktrūniyy. — Letters are used less than email.

exercises.prompt: What does هَذَا الْفُنْدُق أَكْثَر رَاحَةً مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفُنْدُق mean?
options: This hotel is more comfortable than that hotel

exercises.prompt: What ending does the verbal noun take after أَكْثَر?
What does الْقِطَار أَسْرَع مِنَ الْحَافِلَة وَأَقَلّ اِزْدِحَامًا mean?
options: The train is faster than the bus and less crowded
The bus is less crowded than the plane
The train is slower and more crowded
The bus is faster than the train
exercises.explanation: أَسْرَع = faster; أَقَلّ اِزْدِحَامًا = less crowded.
The verbal noun with tanwīn follows أَكْثَر.
exercises.promptTranslation: This road is more crowded in the morning.

exercises.prompt: هَذِهِ الشَّرِكَة أَكْثَر نَجَاحًا ___ الشَّرِكَة الْأُخْرَى.
exercises.promptTranslation: This company is more successful than the other company.

exercises.explanation: A verbal noun with tanwīn: less used.
exercises.promptTranslation: Letters are used less than email.

lessons.title: 366. The most crowded, the cheapest: الْأَكْثَر and الْأَقَلّ
lessons.subtitle: هُوَ الْأَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا · هِيَ الْأَقَلّ سِعْرًا

explanations.title: The superlative with a verbal noun
