explanations.body: To say “the most …”, put ال on أَكْثَر or أَقَلّ and keep the verbal noun with tanwīn: الْأَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا, “the most crowded”. The sentence usually has هُوَ or هِيَ before it. For “most of the …” use أَكْثَر with a plural noun: أَكْثَر السُّيَّاح, “most of the tourists”.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Notice هُوَ for a masculine noun and هِيَ for a feminine noun.

examples.text: هَذَا الشَّارِع هُوَ الْأَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا فِي الْمَدِينَة.
examples.translation: hādhā ash-shāriʿ huwa al-ʾakthar izdiḥāman fī al-madīna. — This street is the most crowded in the city.
ʾayy funduq huwa al-ʾaqall siʿran? — Which hotel is the cheapest?
hādhihi al-ḥāfila hiya al-ʾakthar rāḥatan. — This bus is the most comfortable.
hādhihi ash-sharika hiya al-ʾakthar najāḥan. — This company is the most successful.
ʾakthar as-suyyāḥ yazūrūn as-sūq al-qadīm. — Most of the tourists visit the old market.
al-funduq al-jadīd huwa al-ʾakthar rāḥatan. — The new hotel is the most comfortable.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا and الْأَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا?

exercises.promptTranslation: This bus is the most comfortable.
Which hotel is the cheapest?

exercises.explanation: “most of”: أَكْثَر without ال before a plural.
exercises.promptTranslation: Most of the tourists visit the old market.

lessons.title: 367. A walk through an old market (invented guide)
lessons.subtitle: مِنْ أَشْهَر الْأَسْوَاق · مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذِهِ الْأَقْمِشَةَ!

explanations.title: What the guide says
explanations.body: A guide shows a group around an old market. The phrase مِنْ أَشْهَر الْأَسْوَاق means “one of the most famous markets”: مِنْ is followed by a plural. This text is invented and describes no particular market.

examples.text: هَذَا السُّوق مِنْ أَشْهَر الْأَسْوَاق فِي الْمَدِينَة.
examples.translation: hādhā as-sūq min ʾashhar al-ʾaswāq fī al-madīna. — This market is one of the most famous markets in the city.

examples.text: هُوَ أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا مِنَ الْمَرْكَز التِّجَارِيّ الْحَدِيث.
examples.translation: huwa ʾakthar izdiḥāman mina al-markaz at-tijāriyy al-ḥadīth. — It is more crowded than the modern shopping centre.
al-ʾasʿār hunā ʾarkhaṣ wal-musāwama shāʾiʿa. — The prices here are cheaper and bargaining is common.
mā ʾajmala hādhihi al-ʾaqmishata! — How beautiful these fabrics are!
ʾayna ʾajid hadāyā lil-ʾaṣdiqāʾ? — Where can I find gifts for my friends?
imshū maʿī ʾilā ʾākhir as-sūq. — Walk with me to the end of the market (all of you).

exercises.prompt: What does مِنْ أَشْهَر الْأَسْوَاق mean?
options: one of the most famous markets

exercises.prompt: What does هُوَ أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا مِنَ الْمَرْكَز mean?
options: It is more crowded than the centre
It is cheaper than the centre
It is far from the centre

exercises.prompt: What does مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذِهِ الْأَقْمِشَةَ! express?
What does أَيْنَ أَجِد هَدَايَا؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: This market is one of the most famous markets.
Walk with me to the end of the market.
Where can I find gifts for my friends?

lessons.title: 368. Lost luggage
lessons.subtitle: ضَاعَتْ حَقِيبَتِي · لَمْ تَصِلْ مَعَ الطَّائِرَة

explanations.title: Reporting a lost bag
explanations.body: When your bag does not arrive, you report it at the lost-luggage desk. The verb ضَاعَ يَضِيع means “to be lost”; for a feminine noun: ضَاعَتْ. You describe the bag by its colour (لَوْن), size (حَجْم) and number (رَقْم). The clerk gives you a form (an اِسْتِمَارَة) and promises to call you.

explanations.title: At the desk (invented)
explanations.body: A passenger reports a lost bag.

examples.translation: ḍāʿat ḥaqībatī fī al-maṭār. — My bag was lost at the airport.
lam taṣil ḥaqībatī maʿa aṭ-ṭāʾira. — My bag did not arrive with the plane.
ḥaqībatī kabīra walawnuhā ʾazraq. — My bag is big and its colour is blue.
imlaʾ hādhihi al-istimāra min faḍlika. — Fill in this form, please.
uktub raqm al-ḥaqība waʿunwānaka. — Write the number of the bag and your address.
sanursil al-ḥaqība ʾilā al-funduq. — We will send the bag to the hotel.

exercises.prompt: What does لَمْ تَصِلْ حَقِيبَتِي mean?
options: I did not pack a bag

exercises.prompt: What does اِمْلَأْ هَذِهِ الِاسْتِمَارَة mean?
What does سَنُرْسِل الْحَقِيبَة إِلَى الْفُنْدُق mean?
options: We will send the bag to the hotel
We sent the bag to the hotel
We lost the bag in the hotel
I will pay for the hotel

exercises.prompt: Why is it ضَاعَتْ and not ضَاعَ?

exercises.explanation: The lost thing is a bag.
exercises.promptTranslation: My bag was lost at the airport.

exercises.explanation: “its colour”, for a feminine bag: لَوْنُهَا.
exercises.promptTranslation: My bag is big and its colour is blue.

exercises.explanation: A command from كَتَبَ يَكْتُب: اُكْتُبْ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Write the number of the bag and your address.

lessons.title: 369. At customs: what do you declare?
lessons.subtitle: هَلْ مَعَكَ شَيْء لِلتَّصْرِيح؟ · عُمْلَة أَجْنَبِيَّة

explanations.title: The customs desk
explanations.body: At customs you may be asked whether you have anything to declare. The verb is صَرَّحَ (Measure II) and the noun is التَّصْرِيح. Typical things to declare are foreign currency (عُمْلَة أَجْنَبِيَّة), large sums of money (مَبْلَغ كَبِير), electronic devices (أَجْهِزَة إِلِكْتْرُونِيَّة) and gifts (هَدَايَا). Rules differ from country to country, so these lines are only examples.

explanations.title: The customs officer asks (invented)
explanations.body: An officer and a traveller.

examples.translation: hal maʿaka shayʾ lit-taṣrīḥ? — Do you have anything to declare?
lā, maʿī hadāyā ṣaghīra faqaṭ. — No, I only have small gifts.
hal maʿaka ʿumla ʾajnabiyya? — Do you have foreign currency?
naʿam, maʿī mablagh ṣaghīr bid-dūlār. — Yes, I have a small amount in dollars.
iftaḥ hādhihi al-ḥaqība min faḍlika. — Open this bag, please.
imlaʾ istimāra al-jumruk. — Fill in the customs form.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ مَعَكَ شَيْء لِلتَّصْرِيح؟ ask?
options: Do you have anything to declare?

exercises.prompt: What does اِفْتَحْ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَة mean?
What does مَعِي هَدَايَا صَغِيرَة mean?
options: I have small gifts with me

exercises.promptTranslation: Do you have foreign currency?
Fill in the customs form.

exercises.explanation: Plural of هَدِيَّة (a plural of things → feminine singular adjective صَغِيرَة).
exercises.promptTranslation: I only have small gifts.

lessons.title: 370. At the bank: opening an account
lessons.subtitle: أُرِيد أَنْ أَفْتَح حِسَابًا · بِطَاقَة الصَّرَّاف الْآلِيّ

explanations.title: Accounts and cards
explanations.body: A bank is بَنْك or مَصْرِف. You open an account with the verb فَتَحَ: أَفْتَح حِسَابًا. A savings account is حِسَاب التَّوْفِير and a checking account is الْحِسَاب الْجَارِي. A cash machine is الصَّرَّاف الْآلِيّ, so the card for it is بِطَاقَة الصَّرَّاف الْآلِيّ. Banks have different conditions, so ask before you sign.

explanations.title: At the bank (invented)
explanations.body: A customer talks to a clerk.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أَفْتَح حِسَابًا فِي الْبَنْك.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾaftaḥ ḥisāban fī al-bank. — I want to open an account at the bank.

examples.text: مَا الْفَرْق بَيْن حِسَاب التَّوْفِير وَالْحِسَاب الْجَارِي؟
examples.translation: mā al-farq bayn ḥisāb at-tawfīr wal-ḥisāb al-jārī? — What is the difference between a savings account and a checking account?
ʾurīd biṭāqa liṣ-ṣarrāf al-ʾāliyy. — I want a card for the cash machine.
uktubi ismaka waʿunwānaka fī al-istimāra. — Write your name and address on the form.
taḥtāj ʾilā jawāz as-safar. — You need your passport.
isʾali al-bank ʿan shurūṭ al-ḥisāb. — Ask the bank about the conditions of the account.

exercises.prompt: What does أُرِيد أَنْ أَفْتَح حِسَابًا mean?
options: I want to buy a ticket
I want to pay a bill
I want to open an account
I want to close an account

exercises.prompt: What does تَحْتَاج إِلَى جَوَاز السَّفَر mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to open an account at the bank.

exercises.explanation: The cash machine is الصَّرَّاف الْآلِيّ.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want a card for the cash machine.

exercises.explanation: A command: اُكْتُبِ (a helping kasra before the hamzat al-waṣl of اِسْمَكَ).
exercises.promptTranslation: Write your name and address on the form.

explanations.title: Money and your account
explanations.body: To withdraw money is سَحَبَ يَسْحَب, to transfer is حَوَّلَ يُحَوِّل (Measure II), and the money in your account is رَصِيد (“balance”). A fee is رُسُوم. Interest is فَائِدَة. Some banks that follow Islamic principles do not use interest in the usual way, so it is wise to ask the bank how its accounts work.

explanations.title: Typical sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Customers and a clerk use these lines.

examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾasḥab khamsīn dīnāran. — I want to withdraw fifty dinars.
raṣīdī fī al-ḥisāb qalīl. — My balance in the account is low.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أُحَوِّل الْمَال إِلَى حِسَاب أَخِي.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾuḥawwil al-māl ʾilā ḥisāb ʾakhī. — I want to transfer the money to my brother’s account.
hal yadfaʿ al-bank fāʾida? — Does the bank pay interest?
hunāka rusūm ʿalā kull taḥwīl. — There is a fee on every transfer.
saḥabtu al-māl ʾamsi. — I withdrew the money yesterday.

exercises.explanation: رَصِيد = the amount in the account.

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ يَدْفَع الْبَنْك فَائِدَة؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to withdraw fifty dinars.

exercises.prompt: أُرِيد أَنْ ___ الْمَال إِلَى حِسَاب أَخِي.
exercises.explanation: Measure II after أَنْ with أَنَا: أُحَوِّل.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want to transfer the money to my brother’s account.
There is a fee on every transfer.

lessons.title: 372. A letter of complaint
lessons.subtitle: أَكْتُب إِلَيْكُمْ بِخُصُوص حَقِيبَتِي · أَرْجُو الرَّدّ

explanations.title: The parts of a formal letter
explanations.body: A letter of complaint is formal and polite. It usually has a greeting, the reason for writing, what went wrong, what you ask for, and a closing. Here is an invented letter to an airline about a lost bag.

examples.translation: as-sayyid al-muḥtaram, taḥiyya ṭayyiba wabaʿd, — Dear Sir, kind greetings, and then:

examples.text: أَكْتُب إِلَيْكُمْ بِخُصُوص حَقِيبَتِي الَّتِي ضَاعَتْ.
examples.translation: ʾaktub ʾilaykum bikhuṣūṣ ḥaqībatī allatī ḍāʿat. — I am writing to you about my bag, which was lost.

examples.text: وَصَلْتُ إِلَى الْمَطَار يَوْم الْأَحَد، وَلَمْ تَصِلْ حَقِيبَتِي.
examples.translation: waṣaltu ʾilā al-maṭār yawm al-ʾaḥad, walam taṣil ḥaqībatī. — I arrived at the airport on Sunday, and my bag did not arrive.

examples.text: أَطْلُب مِنْكُمْ تَعْوِيضًا عَنْ هَذِهِ الْمُشْكِلَة.
examples.translation: ʾaṭlub minkum taʿwīḍan ʿan hādhihi al-mushkila. — I ask you for compensation for this problem.
ʾarjū ar-radd fī ʾaqrab waqt. — I hope for a reply as soon as possible.
maʿa ash-shukr, sāmī. — With thanks, Sami.

exercises.prompt: Which closing fits the end of a formal letter?
What does الَّتِي ضَاعَتْ refer to?
exercises.explanation: الَّتِي agrees with the feminine noun حَقِيبَتِي.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am writing to you about my bag.
I ask you for compensation for this problem.
I hope for a reply as soon as possible.

lessons.title: 373. Review: chapter 21
lessons.subtitle: وَ · فَ · ثُمَّ · أَوْ · أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا · الْأَمْن وَالْمَصْرِف

explanations.title: What the unit taught
explanations.body: Conjunctions join equal parts, and the second part copies the case of the first. وَ adds, فَ follows at once, ثُمَّ follows after a gap, and أَوْ gives a choice. Comparatives without a short أَفْعَل adjective use أَكْثَر or أَقَلّ with a verbal noun in the accusative: أَكْثَر اِزْدِحَامًا; with ال they are superlatives.

rows: I want to book a trip
We arrived and at once went in
I want to withdraw the money

explanations.title: A short summary (invented)
explanations.body: Read the lines, which use everything from the unit.

examples.text: حَجَزْنَا الرِّحْلَة ثُمَّ دَفَعْنَا الْمَبْلَغ فِي الْبَنْك.
examples.translation: ḥajaznā ar-riḥla thumma dafaʿnā al-mablagh fī al-bank. — We booked the trip and then paid the amount at the bank.

examples.text: وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْمَطَار فَأَبْرَزْنَا جَوَازَاتِ السَّفَر.
examples.translation: waṣalnā ʾilā al-maṭār faʾabraznā jawāzāti as-safar. — We arrived at the airport and at once showed our passports.
hal tufaḍḍilūna al-qiṭār ʾawi aṭ-ṭāʾira? — Do you prefer the train or the plane?
aṭ-ṭāʾira ʾakthar rāḥatan waʾaqall izdiḥāman. — The plane is more comfortable and less crowded.

examples.text: ضَاعَتْ حَقِيبَتِي فَكَتَبْتُ خِطَابًا إِلَى الشَّرِكَة.
examples.translation: ḍāʿat ḥaqībatī fakatabtu khiṭāban ʾilā ash-sharika. — My bag was lost, so I wrote a letter to the company.
hādhihi ash-sharika hiya al-ʾakthar najāḥan. — This company is the most successful.

exercises.prompt: Which conjunction means “and then at once”?
What does أَبْرِزْ جَوَاز السَّفَر mean?
Why do both nouns in مَعَ الْمُدِيرِ وَالْمُوَظَّفِ end in a kasra?
options: the second noun copies the case of the first

exercises.prompt: وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْمَطَار ___ أَبْرَزْنَا جَوَازَاتِ السَّفَر.
exercises.promptTranslation: We arrived at the airport and at once showed our passports.

exercises.explanation: A choice, with a helping vowel before ال.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you prefer the train or the plane?
The plane is more comfortable and less crowded.

units.title: الْفُنْدُق وَالْحُدُود: hotels, imperatives of derived verbs, historic sites and adverbs of time

lessons.title: 374. Checking in at the hotel
lessons.subtitle: لَدَيَّ حَجْز لِسَالِم · وَقِّعْ هُنَا مِنْ فَضْلِكَ

explanations.title: At the reception desk
explanations.body: The place where guests arrive is مَكْتَب الِاسْتِقْبَال, and the clerk is مُوَظَّف الِاسْتِقْبَال. A room for one person is غُرْفَة مُفْرَدَة and a room for two is غُرْفَة مُزْدَوِجَة. To sign, the clerk says وَقِّعْ (a command from Measure II). The sentences below are an invented conversation.

explanations.title: A conversation (invented)
explanations.body: A guest arrives in the evening.

examples.translation: masāʾ al-khayr, ladayya ḥajz lisālim. — Good evening, I have a booking for Salem.

examples.text: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا، جَوَاز سَفَرِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: ʾahlan wasahlan, jawāz safarika min faḍlika. — Welcome, your passport, please.
ghurfatān muzdawijatān limudda ʾusbūʿ. — Two double rooms for a week.
waqqiʿ hunā min faḍlika. — Sign here, please.

examples.text: هَذَا مِفْتَاحُكَ، وَغُرْفَتُكَ فِي الطَّابِق السَّابِع.
examples.translation: hādhā miftāḥuka, waghurfatuka fī aṭ-ṭābiq as-sābiʿ. — This is your key, and your room is on the seventh floor.
al-miṣʿad ʿalā al-yamīn. — The elevator is on the right.

exercises.prompt: What does لَدَيَّ حَجْز لِسَالِم mean?
options: I have a booking for Salem

exercises.prompt: Which floor is the room on?

exercises.promptTranslation: I have a booking for Salem.

exercises.explanation: A command to one man, Measure II: وَقِّعْ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sign here, please.

exercises.explanation: A dual feminine noun needs a dual adjective.
exercises.promptTranslation: Two double rooms for a week.

lessons.title: 375. A problem with the reservation
lessons.subtitle: لَا أَجِد حَجْزَكَ · هَلْ عِنْدَكَ رَقْم تَأْكِيد؟

explanations.title: When the booking is not found
explanations.body: Sometimes the clerk cannot find a booking. The clerk may ask for the confirmation number, رَقْم تَأْكِيد الْحَجْز, and may offer another room. The verb وَجَدَ gives لَا أَجِد, “I do not find”. A polite apology is أَعْتَذِر عَنْ هَذَا الْخَطَأ, “I apologise for this mistake”. These are invented lines.

examples.text: آسِف، لَا أَجِد حَجْزَكَ فِي الْقَائِمَة.
examples.translation: ʾāsif, lā ʾajid ḥajzaka fī al-qāʾima. — Sorry, I do not find your booking on the list.
hal ʿindaka raqm taʾkīd al-ḥajz? — Do you have the booking confirmation number?

examples.text: الْفُنْدُق مُمْتَلِئ الْيَوْم، لَكِنْ هُنَاكَ غُرْفَة شَاغِرَة وَاحِدَة.
examples.translation: al-funduq mumtaliʾ al-yawm, lākin hunāka ghurfa shāghira wāḥida. — The hotel is full today, but there is one vacant room.
hal yumkinuka ʾan tantaẓir qalīlan? — Can you wait a little?
saʾattaṣil bil-mudīr. — I will call the manager.
ʾaʿtadhir ʿan hādhā al-khaṭaʾ. — I apologise for this mistake.

exercises.prompt: What does لَا أَجِد حَجْزَكَ mean?
options: I do not find your booking

exercises.prompt: What does مُمْتَلِئ mean in الْفُنْدُق مُمْتَلِئ?
What does هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَنْتَظِر قَلِيلًا؟ ask?
What does أَعْتَذِر عَنْ هَذَا الْخَطَأ mean?
options: I thank you for this gift

exercises.promptTranslation: Sorry, I do not find your booking on the list.
Do you have the booking confirmation number?
I will call the manager.

explanations.title: What is in the room?
explanations.body: Hotel rooms usually have a bed (سَرِير), a television (تِلْفَاز), an air conditioner (مُكَيِّف) and a bathroom (حَمَّام). Smaller things are a pillow (وِسَادَة), a blanket (غِطَاء) and a towel (مِنْشَفَة). The dual is used for two beds: سَرِيرَان.

explanations.title: Asking about the room (invented)
explanations.body: A guest asks the clerk.

examples.translation: fī al-ghurfa sarīrān watilfāz wamukayyif. — In the room there are two beds, a television and an air conditioner.
al-ḥammām fīhi māʾ sākhin. — The bathroom has hot water.
ʾurīd wisāda waghiṭāʾ ʾākhar. — I want a pillow and another blanket.
ʾaḥtāj ʾilā minshafa. — I need a towel.

examples.text: الْإِفْطَار مِنَ السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة إِلَى الْعَاشِرَة.
examples.translation: al-ʾifṭār mina as-sāʿa as-sābiʿa ʾilā al-ʿāshira. — Breakfast is from seven to ten.
ʾayna al-maṭʿam? — Where is the restaurant?

exercises.prompt: What does الْحَمَّام فِيهِ مَاء سَاخِن mean?
What does أَحْتَاج إِلَى مِنْشَفَة mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: In the room there are two beds and a television.
I need a towel.
Breakfast is from seven o’clock.

lessons.title: 377. Complaining about the room
lessons.subtitle: الْمُكَيِّف لَا يَعْمَل · الْغُرْفَة غَيْر نَظِيفَة

explanations.title: Saying what is wrong
explanations.body: To say that something does not work, use لَا يَعْمَل (for a masculine thing) or لَا تَعْمَل (for a feminine thing). “Not clean” is غَيْر نَظِيف. Politely ask for a solution: هَلْ يُمْكِن إِصْلَاح …؟, “Can … be repaired?”, or أُرِيد غُرْفَة أُخْرَى, “I want another room”.

examples.translation: al-mukayyif lā yaʿmal. — The air conditioner does not work.
al-ghurfa bārida jiddan. — The room is very cold.

examples.text: لَا يُوجَد مَاء سَاخِن فِي الْحَمَّام.
examples.translation: lā yūjad māʾ sākhin fī al-ḥammām. — There is no hot water in the bathroom.
al-ghurfa ghayr naẓīfa. — The room is not clean.
hunāka ḍajīj fī al-mamarr. — There is noise in the corridor.
hal yumkin ʾiṣlāḥ al-mukayyif? — Can the air conditioner be repaired?
ʾurīd ghurfa ʾukhrā min faḍlika. — I want another room, please.

exercises.prompt: What does الْمُكَيِّف لَا يَعْمَل mean?
options: The air conditioner does not work

exercises.prompt: What does لَا يُوجَد مَاء سَاخِن mean?
What does هَلْ يُمْكِن إِصْلَاح الْمُكَيِّف؟ ask?
options: Can the air conditioner be repaired?

exercises.prompt: Which is correct for the television, which is masculine (تِلْفَاز)?

exercises.promptTranslation: The air conditioner does not work.
The room is not clean.
I want another room, please.

explanations.title: Ways to say sorry
explanations.body: The simplest apology is آسِف (a man) or آسِفَة (a woman). More formally say أَعْتَذِر عَنْ …, “I apologise for …”. To accept an apology say لَا بَأْس or لَا مُشْكِلَة, “no problem”, or أَقْبَل اِعْتِذَارَكَ, “I accept your apology”. A polite answer to a request is بِكُلّ سُرُور, “with pleasure”.

explanations.title: At the desk (invented)
explanations.body: A manager talks to a guest.

examples.translation: ʾaʿtadhir ʿani al-ʾizʿāj. — I apologise for the inconvenience.
lā baʾs, lā mushkila. — It’s all right, no problem.
ʾaqbal iʿtidhāraka, shukran. — I accept your apology, thank you.

examples.text: هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ تَغْيِير الْغُرْفَة؟ بِكُلّ سُرُور.
examples.translation: hal yumkinuka taghyīr al-ghurfa? bikull surūr. — Can you change the room? With pleasure.
ʾāsifa, taʾakhkhartu ʿani al-mawʿid. — Sorry, I was late for the appointment (a woman speaking).
ʾarjū ʾan taqbala iʿtidhārī. — I hope you will accept my apology.

exercises.explanation: أَعْتَذِر عَنْ … is the formal way.

exercises.promptTranslation: I apologise for the inconvenience.
It’s all right.
I accept your apology, thank you.

lessons.title: 379. Suggesting, agreeing, disagreeing
lessons.subtitle: أَقْتَرِح أَنْ نَذْهَب · أَنَا مُوَافِق · لَا أُوَافِق

explanations.title: Giving your view
explanations.body: To make a suggestion say أَقْتَرِح أَنْ …, “I suggest that …”. To agree say أَنَا مُوَافِق; to disagree say لَا أُوَافِق or أَنَا غَيْر مُوَافِق. Give your view with فِي رَأْيِي, “in my opinion”, and speak with confidence with أَنَا وَاثِق مِنْ ذَلِكَ, “I am sure of that”. In a group, say نُوَافِق or لَا نُوَافِق.

explanations.title: A talk between friends (invented)
explanations.body: Friends plan a day.

examples.text: أَقْتَرِح أَنْ نَذْهَب إِلَى الْمَتْحَف أَوَّلًا.
examples.translation: ʾaqtariḥ ʾan nadhhab ʾilā al-matḥaf ʾawwalan. — I suggest that we go to the museum first.
ʾanā muwāfiq, hādhihi fikra jayyida. — I agree, this is a good idea.
lā ʾuwāfiq, al-waqt qaṣīr. — I do not agree, the time is short.
fī raʾyī, al-funduq al-jadīd ʾafḍal. — In my opinion, the new hotel is better.
ʾanā wāthiq min dhālika. — I am sure of that.
hal tuwāfiqūn? naʿam, nuwāfiq. — Do you agree? Yes, we agree.

exercises.prompt: What does أَقْتَرِح أَنْ نَذْهَب mean?
What does أَنَا وَاثِق مِنْ ذَلِكَ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I suggest that we go to the museum.
In my opinion, the new hotel is better.
I do not agree, the time is short.

lessons.title: 380. Commands from Measures II and III
lessons.subtitle: وَقِّعْ · قَدِّمْ · سَاعِدْ · رَاجِعْ

explanations.title: Take off the prefix
explanations.body: To make a command from Measures II and III, start from the present tense. Drop the prefix يُـ, then put a sukūn on the last letter. So يُوَقِّعُ becomes وَقِّعْ, “sign!”, and يُسَاعِدُ becomes سَاعِدْ, “help!”. For a woman add ـِي, for a group add ـُوا. No helping alif is needed, because the verb already starts with a vowel.

explanations.title: To a woman and to a group (invented)
explanations.body: Commands to a man, to a woman and to a group.

examples.translation: qaddim jawāzaka lil-muwaẓẓaf. — Hand your passport to the clerk.
sajjilī al-ḥajz yā salmā. — Register the booking, Salma.
rājiʿū al-ḥisāb qabla al-mughādara. — Check the bill before leaving.
sāʿidū aḍ-ḍuyūf min faḍlikum. — Help the guests, please (to a group).
sāfir bil-qiṭār yā sālim. — Travel by train, Salem.
shāhidī al-madīna mina an-nāfidha. — Watch the city from the window (to a woman).

exercises.prompt: Which is the command from يُسَاعِد?
exercises.explanation: Drop يُـ and add a sukūn.

exercises.prompt: How do you tell a woman to register the booking?

exercises.explanation: سَافَرَ has a long vowel after the first root letter.

exercises.prompt: What do you say to a man?

exercises.explanation: A woman is addressed, so ـِي.
exercises.promptTranslation: Register the booking, Salma.

exercises.explanation: A group is addressed, so ـُوا.
exercises.promptTranslation: Help the guests, please.
Hand your passport to the clerk.
Watch the city from the window (to a woman).

lessons.title: 381. Commands from Measures IV, V and VI
lessons.subtitle: أَرْسِلْ · تَكَلَّمْ · تَقَابَلْ

explanations.title: Measure IV keeps its hamza
explanations.body: In Measure IV the present is يُرْسِلُ. For the command the prefix goes, but the verb starts again with أَ (a hamza with a fatḥa), and the second letter has a kasra: أَرْسِلْ, “send!”. This hamza is always pronounced, so it never loses its sound inside a sentence.

explanations.title: Measures V and VI keep their ت
explanations.body: In Measures V and VI the present is يَتَكَلَّمُ and يَتَقَابَلُ. For the command, drop only the يَـ and keep the تَـ: تَكَلَّمْ, “speak!”, and تَقَابَلْ, “meet!”. The command from these two measures looks like the past tense of the same verb without its ending; the vowels of the last letters tell them apart.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Short orders and requests.

examples.translation: ʾarsil hādhihi ar-risāla al-yawm. — Send this letter today.
ʾakhbiri al-mudīr ʿani al-mawʿid. — Tell the manager about the appointment.
ʾaḥḍirū jawāzātikum ʾilā al-maktab. — Bring your passports to the office.
takallam maʿa al-mudīr. — Speak with the manager.
tadhakkarī mawʿidaki yā hind. — Remember your appointment, Hind.
taqābalū fī al-funduq as-sāʿa al-ʿāshira. — Meet at the hotel at ten o’clock.

exercises.prompt: What is the command from يُرْسِل?
exercises.explanation: Measure IV starts the command with أَ.

exercises.prompt: What is the command from يَتَكَلَّم?
Which command is from Measure VI?
exercises.explanation: Measure VI has the prefix تَ and a long vowel after the first root letter.

exercises.promptTranslation: Send this letter today.
Speak with the manager.
Meet at the hotel at ten o’clock.
Remember your appointment, Hind.

lessons.title: 382. Commands from Measures VII, VIII and X
lessons.subtitle: اِنْتَظِرْ · اِسْتَمِعْ · اِسْتَخْدِمْ

explanations.title: The helping alif returns
explanations.body: Measures VII, VIII and X begin with a helping alif (hamzat wasl) in the past tense. The present has no such alif: يَنْتَظِرُ, يَسْتَخْدِمُ. For the command, drop the prefix يَـ, and a helping alif with a kasra is added: اِنْتَظِرْ, “wait!”, اِسْتَخْدِمْ, “use!”. The alif is pronounced only at the start of a sentence. After another word it is silent: ثُمَّ اِنْتَظِرْ is said thumma ntaẓir.

explanations.title: Before the article (invented)
explanations.body: A command that ends in a consonant takes a helping kasra before الـ: اِسْتَخْدِمِ الْمِصْعَد.

examples.translation: intaẓir fī al-maktab min faḍlika. — Wait in the office, please.
istamiʿ ʾilā al-mudīr. — Listen to the manager.
istakhdimi al-miṣʿad. — Use the elevator.
iqtariḥ mawʿidan ʾākhar. — Suggest another time.
istaqbilū aḍ-ḍuyūf ʿinda al-bāb. — Welcome the guests at the door.
intaqilī ʾilā ghurfa ʾukhrā. — Move to another room (to a woman).

exercises.prompt: Which command is from Measure X?
exercises.explanation: اِسْتَخْدِمْ adds the prefix اِسْتَ to the root خ-د-م.

exercises.prompt: What does اِسْتَمِعْ إِلَى الْمُدِير mean?
What is the helping vowel in اِسْتَخْدِمِ الْمِصْعَد?
exercises.explanation: A final sukūn before الـ takes a helping kasra.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “Welcome the guests” to a group?
Is the alif of اِنْتَظِرْ pronounced after ثُمَّ?
exercises.explanation: A helping alif is silent after another word.

exercises.promptTranslation: Wait in the office, please.

exercises.explanation: The article is needed after a command meaning “use the …”.
exercises.promptTranslation: Use the elevator.
Welcome the guests at the door.
Move to another room (to a woman).

explanations.title: One verb, five commands
explanations.body: Every command has five forms. Here is أَرْسِلْ in all of them. The pair ends in ـَا, and a group of women ends in ـْنَ.

explanations.title: Objects and ‘do not’
explanations.body: A pronoun can be attached to the end of a command: سَاعِدْنِي, “help me”; أَرْسِلْهَا, “send it (f.)”; قَدِّمْهُ, “present it”. To forbid, put لَا before a short present form, which looks like the command with a prefix: لَا تُرْسِلْ, “do not send”; لَا تُوَقِّعْ, “do not sign”.

examples.translation: ʾarsilā al-ḥaqāʾib ʾilā al-ghurfa. — Send the bags to the room (to two people).
ʾarsilna ar-risāla yā banāt. — Send the letter, girls.
sāʿidnī min faḍlika. — Help me, please.
al-fātūra jāhiza, ʾarsilhā ʾilā al-mudīr. — The bill is ready, send it to the manager.
lā tursil hādhihi ar-risāla. — Do not send this letter.
lā tuwaqqiʿ hunā. — Do not sign here.

exercises.prompt: What does لَا تُوَقِّعْ هُنَا mean?
How do you tell a man, “Do not send”?

exercises.promptTranslation: Send the bags to the room.
Send the letter, girls.
The bill is ready, send it to the manager.

exercises.explanation: After لَا, a short present form.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do not send this letter.

explanations.title: At the desk (invented)
explanations.body: A guest leaves the hotel in the morning. Notice the commands.

examples.translation: ṣabāḥ al-khayr, ʾurīd al-mughādara. — Good morning, I want to check out.
intaẓir laḥẓa, ʾuḥḍir laka al-fātūra. — Wait a moment, I will bring you the bill.
rājiʿi al-fātūra thumma waqqiʿ hunā. — Check the bill, then sign here.
saʾadfaʿ bibiṭāqa al-iʾtimān. — I will pay by credit card.
ʾaḥḍirū ḥaqāʾibī mina al-ghurfa. — Bring my bags from the room (to the staff).

examples.text: اُطْلُبْ لِي سَيَّارَة أُجْرَة مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: uṭlub lī sayyāra ʾujra min faḍlika. — Order me a taxi, please.

explanations.title: A thank-you note (invented)
explanations.body: Before leaving, a guest writes to the manager. Letters begin with the address and end with thanks.

examples.translation: ʾilā mudīr al-funduq, taḥiyya ṭayyiba. — To the hotel manager, kind greetings.
ʾashkuruka ʿalā ʾiqāma jamīla. — I thank you for a lovely stay.

examples.text: أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلَ الْفَاتُورَة إِلَى عُنْوَانِي.
examples.translation: ʾarjū ʾan tursila al-fātūra ʾilā ʿunwānī. — Please send the bill to my address.
maʿa ʾaṭyab at-tamanniyāt. — With best wishes.

exercises.explanation: رَاجِعْ = check!, with a helping kasra before الـ.

exercises.prompt: What does سَأَدْفَع بِبِطَاقَة الِائْتِمَان mean?
options: I will pay by credit card

exercises.prompt: Who is addressed in أَحْضِرُوا حَقَائِبِي?
What does مَعَ أَطْيَب التَّمَنِّيَات mean?
exercises.explanation: A closing wish in a letter.

exercises.promptTranslation: Wait a moment, I will bring you the bill.

exercises.explanation: Luggage is brought from a room.
exercises.promptTranslation: Bring my bags from the room.
Order me a taxi, please.
Please send the bill to my address.

explanations.title: Words for old places
explanations.body: A place where ancient remains lie is a مَوْقِع أَثَرِيّ, “archaeological site”. Around it you may find a castle, a temple, a palace, a bridge, a wall or a gate. A guide who explains the place is a دَلِيل, and you need a تَذْكِرَة to enter.

explanations.title: A visit (invented)
explanations.body: A tourist talks to the guide at the entrance.

examples.translation: ʾurīd ziyāra al-mawqiʿ al-ʾathariyy. — I want to visit the archaeological site.
hādhihi al-qalʿa qadīma jiddan. — This castle is very old.
lahā sūr kabīr wabawwābatān. — It has a big wall and two gates.
ad-dalīl yatakallam al-ʿarabiyya wal-ʾinjilīziyya. — The guide speaks Arabic and English.
kam siʿr at-tadhkira? — How much is the ticket?
al-matḥaf maftūḥ mina al-ʿāshira. — The museum is open from ten o’clock.

exercises.prompt: Who explains the place to visitors?
What does لَهَا سُور كَبِير وَبَوَّابَتَان mean?
options: It is near a big wall
It has a small wall and one gate
It has a big wall and two gates
exercises.explanation: لَهَا = it has (f.); بَوَّابَتَان = two gates.

exercises.prompt: Why is it قَدِيمَة in هَذِهِ الْقَلْعَة قَدِيمَة?
exercises.explanation: A feminine noun takes a feminine adjective.
The noun مَوْقِع is masculine and definite.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want to visit the archaeological site.
It has a big wall and two gates.
How much is the ticket?

lessons.title: 386. Petra and an old city
lessons.subtitle: تَقَع فِي الْجَنُوب · بُنِيَتْ مُنْذُ زَمَن بَعِيد

explanations.title: Where it is and how old it is
explanations.body: To say where a place is, use the verb تَقَع, “is situated”, or تُوجَد, “is found”. To say that a city was built long ago, use the passive بُنِيَتْ, “was built”. These short texts are invented and simple. Petra is an ancient city in the south of Jordan, with tombs cut into the mountains. Jerusalem has an old city with walls and gates.

examples.translation: taqaʿ al-batrāʾ fī janūb al-ʾurdunn. — Petra is situated in the south of Jordan.

examples.text: هِيَ مَدِينَة قَدِيمَة بُنِيَتْ مُنْذُ زَمَن بَعِيد.
examples.translation: hiya madīna qadīma buniyat mundhu zaman baʿīd. — It is an ancient city built a long time ago.
fī al-jabal qubūr kathīra. — In the mountain there are many tombs.

examples.text: يَدْخُل الزُّوَّار مِنْ طَرِيق ضَيِّق بَيْنَ جَبَلَيْن.
examples.translation: yadkhul az-zuwwār min ṭarīq ḍayyiq bayna jabalayn. — Visitors enter by a narrow road between two mountains.

examples.text: فِي الْقُدْس مَدِينَة قَدِيمَة لَهَا أَسْوَار وَأَبْوَاب كَثِيرَة.
examples.translation: fī al-quds madīna qadīma lahā ʾaswār waʾabwāb kathīra. — In Jerusalem there is an old city with many walls and gates.
tūjad fīhā masājid wakanāʾis waʾaswāq. — In it there are mosques, churches and markets.

exercises.prompt: What does تَقَع فِي الْجَنُوب mean?
Why is it بُنِيَتْ and not بُنِيَ?
Who enters by a narrow road?
What does تُوجَد فِيهَا مَسَاجِد mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Petra is situated in the south of Jordan.
An ancient city built a long time ago.
In the mountain there are many tombs.

lessons.title: 387. Hiring a car with a driver
lessons.subtitle: كَمِ الْأُجْرَة؟ · تَوَقَّفْ هُنَا

explanations.title: Talking to the driver
explanations.body: When you hire a car or a van, you ask about the price (الْأُجْرَة) and then tell the driver what to do with commands. Two verbs are useful: تَوَقَّفْ, “stop!” (Measure V), and اِنْتَظِرْنَا, “wait for us!” (Measure VIII). The ‘do not’ form is لَا تُسْرِعْ, “do not hurry”.

examples.translation: nurīd sayyāra kabīra lisitta ʾashkhāṣ. — We want a big car for six people.
kami al-ʾujra ʾilā al-ḥudūd? — How much is the fare to the border?
aṭ-ṭarīq ṭawīl, idhhab bisurʿa muʿtadila. — The road is long, go at a moderate speed.
tawaqqaf hunā min faḍlika. — Stop here, please.
intaẓirnā niṣf sāʿa. — Wait for us half an hour.
lā tusriʿ yā sāʾiq. — Do not hurry, driver.

exercises.promptTranslation: We want a big car for six people.
Stop here, please.
Wait for us half an hour.
Do not hurry, driver.

explanations.title: The officer’s questions
explanations.body: At the border an officer asks for your passport, جَوَاز السَّفَر, and checks the visa, التَّأْشِيرَة. The usual questions are about the purpose of the visit, غَرَض الزِّيَارَة, and how long you will stay. The officer stamps the passport with the verb خَتَمَ. This conversation is invented.

examples.translation: jawāz safarika min faḍlika. — Your passport, please.
mā gharaḍ az-ziyāra? — What is the purpose of the visit?
ʾanā sāʾiḥ, jiʾtu lis-siyāḥa. — I am a tourist, I came for tourism.
kam yawman satabqā hunā? — How many days will you stay here?
saʾabqā thalātha ʾayyām. — I will stay three days.
at-taʾshīra ṣāliḥa lishahr. — The visa is valid for a month.
khatama al-muwaẓẓaf al-jawāz. — The officer stamped the passport.

exercises.prompt: What does مَا غَرَض الزِّيَارَة؟ mean?
options: What is the purpose of the visit?

exercises.prompt: Which answer fits ‘What is the purpose?’
What does كَمْ يَوْمًا سَتَبْقَى؟ ask?
What does التَّأْشِيرَة صَالِحَة لِشَهْر mean?
options: The visa is valid for a month
The visa is for a week

exercises.promptTranslation: Your passport, please.

exercises.explanation: Three days: the plural after ثَلَاثَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: I will stay three days.

exercises.explanation: A past verb for the officer.
exercises.promptTranslation: The officer stamped the passport.
The visa is valid for a month.

lessons.title: 389. At customs
lessons.subtitle: اِفْتَحْ حَقِيبَتَكَ · هَلْ مَعَكَ شَيْء لِلتَّصْرِيح؟

explanations.title: The customs officer
explanations.body: After passport control, the customs officer, مُوَظَّف الْجُمْرُك, may inspect your bags. He may ask whether you have anything to declare (شَيْء لِلتَّصْرِيح). A forbidden item is مَمْنُوع, and a tax or fee is ضَرِيبَة. Notice the commands. This conversation is invented.

examples.translation: iftaḥ ḥaqībataka min faḍlika. — Open your bag, please.
hal maʿaka shayʾ lit-taṣrīḥ? — Do you have anything to declare?
lā, maʿī hadāyā faqaṭ. — No, I only have gifts.
fattasha muwaẓẓaf al-jumruk al-ḥaqība. — The customs officer searched the bag.
hādhā mamnūʿ, lā taʾkhudhhu maʿaka. — This is forbidden, do not take it with you.
ʿalayka ʾan tadfaʿa ḍarība. — You must pay a tax.

exercises.prompt: What does لَا تَأْخُذْهُ مَعَكَ mean?
options: do not take it with you

exercises.prompt: What does عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَدْفَعَ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Open your bag, please.
No, I only have gifts.
The customs officer searched the bag.
You must pay a tax.

explanations.title: Waiting and crossing
explanations.body: At the border, buses stop and passengers queue. The guide gives orders: اِنْزِلُوا مِنَ الْحَافِلَة, “get off the bus”, اُعْبُرُوا الْحُدُود, “cross the border”. To warn someone, use لَا تَنْسَ, “do not forget”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: naṣil ʾilā al-ḥudūd baʿda sāʿatayn. — We shall arrive at the border in two hours.
ʾamāmanā ṭābūr ṭawīl. — In front of us is a long queue.
inzilū mina al-ḥāfila min faḍlikum. — Please get off the bus.
uʿburū al-ḥudūd sayran ʿalā al-ʾaqdām. — Cross the border on foot.
lā tansa jawāzaka. — Do not forget your passport.
baʿda al-ʿubūr narkab ḥāfila ʾukhrā. — After the crossing we ride another bus.

exercises.prompt: What does اِنْزِلُوا مِنَ الْحَافِلَة mean?
What does لَا تَنْسَ جَوَازَكَ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: We shall arrive at the border in two hours.
Please get off the bus.

exercises.explanation: After لَا, the short present: تَنْسَ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do not forget your passport.
Cross the border on foot.

explanations.title: When? The accusative ending
explanations.body: An adverb of time answers the question “When?”. Most of these adverbs are in the accusative case, so they end in tanwīn with fatḥa: ـًا, written with an alif. After tā’ marbūṭa the tanwīn sits on the tā’: عَادَةً. After hamza it is written ـءً: مَسَاءً. Adverbs of time are usually free to move: at the start or the end of the sentence.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Daily life of a traveller.

examples.translation: ʾaṣil ʾilā al-maktab mubakkiran. — I arrive at the office early.
nashrab al-qahwa ṣabāḥan. — We drink coffee in the morning.
ʾadhhab ʾilā as-sūq masāʾan. — I go to the market in the evening.
huwa yanām mutaʾakhkhiran dāʾiman. — He always sleeps late.
ʾaḥyānan nazūr al-matḥaf. — Sometimes we visit the museum.
sanaṣil ghadan. — We shall arrive tomorrow.
ʿādatan ʾaskun fī funduq ṣaghīr. — Usually I stay in a small hotel.

exercises.prompt: Which ending marks an adverb of time?
exercises.explanation: Adverbs of time are in the accusative.

exercises.prompt: How is the tanwīn written after tā’ marbūṭa?

exercises.promptTranslation: I arrive at the office early.

exercises.explanation: The verb is in the future.
exercises.promptTranslation: We shall arrive tomorrow.
I go to the market in the evening.
Sometimes we visit the museum.

lessons.title: 392. Time phrases in the accusative
lessons.subtitle: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ · كُلَّ يَوْمٍ · طَوَالَ اللَّيْلِ

explanations.title: Nouns used as adverbs
explanations.body: Besides the one-word adverbs, some nouns answer “When?” in the accusative case and need no preposition: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ, “on Friday”, كُلَّ يَوْمٍ, “every day”, الْيَوْمَ, “today”. This lesson shows the case endings in full on the time phrases, so that you can see the fatḥa (ـَ) on the first word (a noun or كُلّ). In everyday speech they are dropped.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Plans for the week.

examples.translation: nazūr al-matḥaf yawma al-jumuʿati. — We visit the museum on Friday.
ʾaʿmal kulla yawmin. — I work every day.
al-yawma naskun fī al-funduq. — Today we stay in the hotel.
al-laylata nadhhab ʾilā maṭʿam. — Tonight we go to a restaurant.
hādhā al-ʾusbūʿa ʾanā mashghūl. — This week I am busy.
sāfarnā ṭawāla al-layli. — We travelled all night long.

exercises.prompt: What case is the first word of these time phrases in (يَوْمَ، كُلَّ، طَوَالَ)?
exercises.explanation: Time adverbs take the accusative: fatḥa.

exercises.prompt: What does هَذَا الْأُسْبُوعَ أَنَا مَشْغُول mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: We visit the museum on Friday.
I work every day.
Today we stay in the hotel.
We travelled all night long.

explanations.title: Linking words for time
explanations.body: Adverbs of time also organise a story. Start with أَوَّلًا, “first”; continue with ثُمَّ, “then”, and بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ, “after that”; finish with أَخِيرًا, “finally”. Use فِي الْبِدَايَة, “at the beginning”, and فِي النِّهَايَة, “at the end”. The little story is invented.

examples.translation: ʾawwalan naṣil ʾilā al-funduq. — First we arrive at the hotel.
thumma nadhhab ʾilā al-matḥaf. — Then we go to the museum.
baʿda dhālika nataghaddā fī maṭʿam. — After that we have lunch in a restaurant.
qabla dhālika nashtarī tadhākir. — Before that we buy tickets.
ʾakhīran narjiʿ ʾilā al-ghurfa. — Finally we return to the room.
fī an-nihāya ʾanā mutʿab. — In the end I am tired.

Then we go to the museum.

After that we have lunch in a restaurant.

lessons.title: 394. Review: hotel, commands, border and time
lessons.subtitle: مُرَاجَعَة الْوَحْدَة

explanations.title: Commands from every measure
explanations.body: A summary of the commands from this unit. In Measures II and III the prefix goes; in IV the أَ stays; in V and VI the تَـ stays; in VII, VIII and X a helping alif with kasra is added. Commands to a woman end in ـِي and to a group in ـُوا.

exercises.prompt: Which command is from Measure IV?
Which command is from Measure V?

What does خَتَمَ الْمُوَظَّف الْجَوَاز mean?

options: whether you have anything to declare

exercises.promptTranslation: Hand your passport to the clerk.

units.title: جَوْلَة فِي مِصْر: Egypt, the subjunctive, the jussive and the post office

explanations.title: A huge, ancient tomb
explanations.body: A pyramid is a هَرَم, and the plural is أَهْرَام. The most famous pyramids stand at Giza (الْجِيزَة), near Cairo. The biggest one is called الْهَرَم الْأَكْبَر, “the Great Pyramid”. It is often described as the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. The sentences below are simple invented descriptions.

examples.translation: al-haram al-ʾakbar fī al-jīza. — The Great Pyramid is in Giza.
huwa min ʾaqdam ʿajāʾib al-ʿālam. — It is one of the oldest wonders of the world.
banā al-ʿummāl al-haram bil-ḥijāra. — Workers built the pyramid with stones.
buniya al-haram mundhu ʾālāf as-sinīn. — The pyramid was built thousands of years ago.
al-haram ḍakhm waqadīm jiddan. — The pyramid is huge and very old.
yazūr as-suyyāḥ al-ʾahrām kulla yawm. — Tourists visit the pyramids every day.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of هَرَم?
What does بَنَى الْعُمَّال الْهَرَم mean?

exercises.explanation: The great pyramids are at Giza.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Great Pyramid is in Giza.

exercises.explanation: The workers are the doers: an active verb.
exercises.promptTranslation: Workers built the pyramid with stones.

exercises.explanation: No doer is named: the passive.
exercises.promptTranslation: The pyramid was built thousands of years ago.
The pyramid is huge and very old.

lessons.title: 396. The Sphinx and the Hanging Church
lessons.subtitle: رَأْس إِنْسَان وَجِسْم أَسَد · فَوْقَ بُرْجَيْن

explanations.title: Two famous places in and near Cairo
explanations.body: The Sphinx, أَبُو الْهَوْل in Arabic, is a huge statue near the pyramids at Giza. It has the head of a human and the body of a lion (أَسَد). The Hanging Church, الْكَنِيسَة الْمُعَلَّقَة, stands in Old Cairo. It is called ‘hanging’ because it was built on top of two old towers. The sentences are invented and simple.

examples.text: أَبُو الْهَوْل تِمْثَال ضَخْم قَرِيب مِنَ الْأَهْرَام.
examples.translation: ʾabū al-hawl timthāl ḍakhm qarīb mina al-ʾahrām. — The Sphinx is a huge statue near the pyramids.

examples.text: رَأْسُهُ رَأْس إِنْسَان وَجِسْمُهُ جِسْم أَسَد.
examples.translation: raʾsuhu raʾs ʾinsān wajismuhu jism ʾasad. — Its head is a human head and its body is a lion’s body.
al-kanīsa al-muʿallaqa fī al-qāhira al-qadīma. — The Hanging Church is in Old Cairo.
buniyat fawqa burjayn qadīmayn. — It was built above two old towers.
yadkhul az-zāʾirūn min bāb ṣaghīr. — The visitors enter by a small door.
ʾaḥabba as-suyyāḥ al-kanīsa. — The tourists liked the church.

exercises.explanation: The Arabic name of the Sphinx.

exercises.prompt: What has the head of a human?

exercises.explanation: The passive past with a feminine subject.
The Sphinx has a human head.
exercises.promptTranslation: Its head is a human head.
and its body is a lion’s body.
It was built above two old towers.

exercises.explanation: The adjective agrees with a feminine definite noun.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Hanging Church is in Old Cairo.

explanations.title: Parts of a building
explanations.body: To describe a building, name its parts. A mosque may have a dome (قُبَّة) and a tower; an old temple may have columns (أَعْمِدَة) and thick walls (جُدْرَان). The plural of a thing takes a feminine singular adjective: جُدْرَان طَوِيلَة, “tall walls”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: lil-masjid qubba kabīra waburj ʿālin. — The mosque has a big dome and a tall tower.
fī al-maʿbad ʾaʿmida kathīra. — In the temple there are many columns.
judrānuhu ṭawīla wasaqfuhu qadīm. — Its walls are tall and its ceiling is old.
al-mabnā maṣnūʿ mina al-ḥajar. — The building is made of stone.
lahu thalātha ṭawābiq wanawāfidh ṣaghīra. — It has three floors and small windows.

exercises.prompt: What does مَصْنُوع مِنَ الْحَجَر mean?

options: the plural of a thing takes a feminine singular adjective
exercises.explanation: Plural things behave as feminine singular.
A dome is feminine, like كَبِيرَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: The mosque has a big dome.

exercises.explanation: The plural of a thing: feminine singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the temple there are many columns.

exercises.explanation: The plural of a thing: feminine singular.

lessons.title: 398. The Nile and the four directions
lessons.subtitle: شَمَال · جَنُوب · شَرْق · غَرْب

explanations.title: Directions on the map
explanations.body: The four directions are شَمَال, جَنُوب, شَرْق and غَرْب. Add ـِيّ for the adjective: شَمَالِيّ, “northern”, غَرْبِيّ, “western”. The Nile (النِّيل) flows from the south to the north, so Aswan lies in the south of Egypt and Cairo lies in the north. Cities on the river have two banks: الضِّفَّة الْغَرْبِيَّة and الضِّفَّة الشَّرْقِيَّة. The sentences are simple and invented.

examples.text: يَجْرِي النِّيل مِنَ الْجَنُوب إِلَى الشَّمَال.
examples.translation: yajrī an-nīl mina al-janūb ʾilā ash-shamāl. — The Nile flows from the south to the north.

examples.text: تَقَع الْقَاهِرَة فِي الشَّمَال وَأَسْوَان فِي الْجَنُوب.
examples.translation: taqaʿ al-qāhira fī ash-shamāl waʾaswān fī al-janūb. — Cairo is in the north and Aswan is in the south.
funduqunā ʿalā aḍ-ḍiffa ash-sharqiyya. — Our hotel is on the eastern bank.
al-maʿbad ʿalā aḍ-ḍiffa al-gharbiyya. — The temple is on the western bank.
al-matḥaf ʾilā ash-shamāl mina al-funduq. — The museum is to the north of the hotel.

exercises.prompt: Which way does the Nile flow?

exercises.explanation: A feminine noun takes a feminine adjective.
It flows north from the south.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Nile flows from the south to the north.

exercises.explanation: The bank is feminine and definite.
exercises.promptTranslation: The temple is on the western bank.
Cairo is in the north.
The museum is to the north of the hotel.

lessons.title: 399. After the particles: the ending ـَ
lessons.subtitle: أَنْ أَكْتُبَ · لَنْ يَصِلَ · حَتَّى يَصِلَ

explanations.title: The accusative present
explanations.body: A present verb is normally followed by ـُ in careful speech: أَكْتُبُ. After certain particles it changes to ـَ: أَنْ أَكْتُبَ. This is the accusative (also called the subjunctive) of the present tense. You already know the particles أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ and لِـ. A new one is حَتَّى, “until”. The particles do not change the order of the sentence. In this lesson the endings are written in full.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Plans for a trip.

examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾaktuba biṭāqa. — I want to write a card.
lan yaṣila al-qiṭār mubakkiran. — The train will not arrive early.
jiʾtu liʾazūra al-ʾahrām. — I came to visit the pyramids.
sāfarnā kay nazūra al-maʿābid. — We travelled in order to visit the temples.
saʾantaẓir ḥattā yaṣila al-mudīr. — I will wait until the manager arrives.
ʾayna turīd ʾan tajlisa? — Where do you want to sit?

exercises.explanation: After a particle the verb is accusative: ـَ.

exercises.prompt: What does حَتَّى mean in سَأَنْتَظِر حَتَّى يَصِلَ الْمُدِير?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to write a card.
The train will not arrive early.
I will wait until the manager arrives.

lessons.title: 400. Pairs, women and groups: the ن falls away
lessons.subtitle: أَنْ يَكْتُبُوا · أَنْ تَكْتُبِي · أَنْ يَكْتُبَا

explanations.title: Loss of the final ن
explanations.body: Some present forms end in ن: ـُونَ (they), ـِينَ (you, f.), ـَانِ (the pair). After a particle this ن is dropped: يَكْتُبُونَ → أَنْ يَكْتُبُوا. After the group ending ـُوا a silent alif is written. The women’s plural ـْنَ is the exception: it keeps its ن and does not change.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: At the hotel entrance.

examples.translation: yurīd aḍ-ḍuyūf ʾan yadkhulū al-ʾān. — The guests want to enter now.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ تَجْلِسِي هُنَا يَا سَلْمَى.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan tajlisī hunā yā salmā. — I want you to sit here, Salma.
lan yadhhabā ʾilā al-matḥaf. — The two of them will not go to the museum.
al-banāt yuridna ʾan yakhrujna. — The girls want to go out.
lan taktubū ar-risāla al-yawm. — You (pl.) will not write the letter today.
jāʾa aṭ-ṭullāb liyaktubū ad-dars. — The students came to write the lesson.

exercises.prompt: What happens to the ن of يَكْتُبُونَ after أَنْ?
exercises.explanation: The ن of the group ending is dropped.

exercises.prompt: Which ending needs a silent alif?
exercises.explanation: A written alif follows a group و in a verb.

exercises.prompt: Which form keeps its ن after أَنْ?
exercises.explanation: The women’s plural is the exception.

exercises.prompt: Who is addressed in أَنْ تَجْلِسِي?

exercises.explanation: A group, after أَنْ: no ن.
exercises.promptTranslation: The guests want to enter now.

exercises.explanation: A woman, after أَنْ: no ن.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to sit here, Salma.
The two of them will not go to the museum.
The girls want to go out.

lessons.title: 401. Weak verbs after the particles
lessons.subtitle: أَنْ يَمْشِيَ · أَنْ يَدْعُوَ · أَنْ يَقُولَ

explanations.title: Verbs with a long vowel at the end or in the middle
explanations.body: Verbs whose last letter is ي or و (defective verbs) show the accusative ـَ on that letter: يَمْشِي → أَنْ يَمْشِيَ; يَدْعُو → أَنْ يَدْعُوَ. If the last letter is an alif maqṣūra, nothing can show: يَنْسَى → أَنْ يَنْسَى. Hollow and assimilated verbs behave like sound verbs: يَقُولُ → أَنْ يَقُولَ, يَنَامُ → أَنْ يَنَامَ, يَصِلُ → أَنْ يَصِلَ. Groups of defective verbs lose their ن and the long vowel changes: يَمْشُونَ → أَنْ يَمْشُوا.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Plans and wishes.

examples.translation: nurīd ʾan namshiya ʾilā as-sūq. — We want to walk to the market.
ʾurīd ʾan ʾadʿuwa ʾaṣdiqāʾī. — I want to invite my friends.
lan ʾansā hādhihi ar-riḥla. — I will not forget this trip.
yajib ʾan taqūla al-ḥaqīqa. — You must tell the truth.
ʾurīd ʾan ʾanāma mubakkiran. — I want to sleep early.
lan yamshū ʾilā al-maḥaṭṭa. — They will not walk to the station.

exercises.explanation: Defective verbs show ـَ on the last ي.

exercises.prompt: What happens to يَنْسَى after أَنْ?
options: it gets ـَ on the alif
exercises.explanation: Alif maqṣūra cannot carry a vowel.

exercises.promptTranslation: We want to walk to the market.
I want to invite my friends.

exercises.explanation: Hollow verb: ـَ at the end.
exercises.promptTranslation: You must tell the truth.

exercises.explanation: A group: the ن falls away.
exercises.promptTranslation: They will not walk to the station.

lessons.title: 402. Derived verbs after the particles
lessons.subtitle: أَنْ يُسَاعِدَ · أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ · أَنْ يَنْتَظِرَ

explanations.title: The same ending on every measure
explanations.body: The accusative works the same way on the derived measures. Take the present form and put ـَ on the last letter: يُسَاعِدُ → أَنْ يُسَاعِدَ; يَتَكَلَّمُ → أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ; يَنْتَظِرُ → أَنْ يَنْتَظِرَ; يَسْتَخْدِمُ → أَنْ يَسْتَخْدِمَ. There is no helping alif in the present, so nothing is added at the front.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: At the hotel.

examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾuwaqqiʿa hunā. — I want to sign here.
hal turīd ʾan ʾusāʿidaka? — Do you want me to help you?
sanadhhab linursila aṭ-ṭard. — We will go in order to send the parcel.
yajib ʾan tatakallama maʿa al-mudīr. — You must speak with the manager.
lan nantaẓira ṭawīlan. — We will not wait long.
ʾurīd ʾan ʾastakhdima al-hātif. — I want to use the telephone.

exercises.explanation: Put ـَ on the last letter.
Keep the prefix of the present.

exercises.prompt: Is a helping alif added in the present of Measures VIII and X?
exercises.explanation: The alif belongs to the past and the command only.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to sign here.

exercises.explanation: Measure III, with the suffix ـكَ.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you want me to help you?
You must speak with the manager.
I want to use the telephone.

explanations.title: At the ticket window
explanations.body: A one-way ticket is ذَهَاب فَقَط, a return ticket is ذَهَاب وَعَوْدَة. Trains have classes: الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى, “first class”, and الدَّرَجَة الثَّانِيَة, “second class”. You get a seat (مَقْعَد) with a number and a platform (رَصِيف) to wait on. Use the accusative you just learned: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِزَ …. The conversation is invented.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أَحْجِزَ تَذْكِرَتَيْن إِلَى أَسْوَان.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾaḥjiza tadhkiratayn ʾilā ʾaswān. — I want to book two tickets to Aswan.
dhahāb faqaṭ ʾam dhahāb waʿawda? — One way or return?

examples.text: ذَهَاب وَعَوْدَة فِي الدَّرَجَة الْأُولَى مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.translation: dhahāb waʿawda fī ad-daraja al-ʾūlā min faḍlika. — Return, in first class, please.
kam siʿr at-tadhkiratayn? — How much are the two tickets?
yughādir al-qiṭār mina ar-raṣīf ath-thālith. — The train leaves from the third platform.
maqʿaduka raqm ʿishrīn. — Your seat is number twenty.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to book two tickets to Aswan.
One way or return?

exercises.explanation: A train leaves from a platform.
exercises.promptTranslation: The train leaves from the third platform.
How much are the two tickets?

lessons.title: 404. The timetable and delays
lessons.subtitle: مَتَى يُغَادِر الْقِطَار؟ · تَأَخَّرَ نِصْف سَاعَة

explanations.title: Departures and arrivals
explanations.body: The verb غَادَرَ يُغَادِر means “to leave (a place)”, and وَصَلَ يَصِل “to arrive”. Times use the feminine ordinals: السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة, “eight o’clock”. A late train is مُتَأَخِّر, and تَأَخَّرَ means “was late”. These lines are an invented timetable.

examples.translation: matā yughādir al-qiṭār? — When does the train leave?

examples.text: يُغَادِر الْقِطَار الْقَاهِرَة السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة صَبَاحًا.
examples.translation: yughādir al-qiṭār al-qāhira as-sāʿa ath-thāmina ṣabāḥan. — The train leaves Cairo at eight in the morning.

examples.text: وَيَصِل إِلَى أَسْوَان السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً.
examples.translation: wayaṣil ʾilā ʾaswān as-sāʿa at-tāsiʿa masāʾan. — And it arrives at Aswan at nine in the evening.
hali al-qiṭār mutaʾakhkhir? — Is the train late?
taʾakhkhara al-qiṭār niṣf sāʿa. — The train was half an hour late.
lan yughādira al-qiṭār qabla al-ʿāshira. — The train will not leave before ten.

exercises.prompt: What does مَتَى يُغَادِر الْقِطَار؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: The train leaves Cairo at eight in the morning.
It arrives at Aswan at nine in the evening.

exercises.explanation: A past verb for the train.
exercises.promptTranslation: The train was half an hour late.
The train will not leave before ten.

explanations.title: A dam on the Nile
explanations.body: Aswan lies in the south of Egypt. Near the city there is a big dam on the Nile, السَّدّ الْعَالِي, “the High Dam”. It was built in the twentieth century. A large lake lies behind it (بُحَيْرَة). The dam gives electricity (كَهْرَبَاء) and helps to control the flood (فَيَضَان) of the river. The sentences are simple and invented.

examples.translation: taqaʿ ʾaswān fī janūb miṣr. — Aswan is situated in the south of Egypt.

examples.text: السَّدّ الْعَالِي سَدّ كَبِير عَلَى النِّيل.
examples.translation: as-sadd al-ʿālī sadd kabīr ʿalā an-nīl. — The High Dam is a big dam on the Nile.
buniya as-sadd fī al-qarn al-ʿishrīn. — The dam was built in the twentieth century.
khalfa as-sadd buḥayra kabīra. — Behind the dam there is a big lake.
yuntij as-sadd al-kahrabāʾ. — The dam produces electricity.
yamnaʿ as-sadd al-fayaḍān. — The dam prevents flooding.
yurīd as-suyyāḥ ʾan yazūrū as-sadd. — The tourists want to visit the dam.

exercises.prompt: What does يَمْنَع السَّدّ الْفَيَضَان mean?

options: a passive verb with a masculine subject

exercises.promptTranslation: Aswan is situated in the south of Egypt.
The dam produces electricity.

exercises.explanation: A lake is feminine, like كَبِيرَة.
exercises.promptTranslation: Behind the dam there is a big lake.

exercises.explanation: A group after أَنْ: no ن.
exercises.promptTranslation: The tourists want to visit the dam.

explanations.title: A city of ancient remains
explanations.body: Luxor, الْأُقْصُر, is a city on the Nile with many ancient remains. It has two large temples, مَعْبَد الْأُقْصُر and مَعْبَد الْكَرْنَك. A long road with many statues is said to join them. On the western bank there are old tombs. The sentences are simple and invented.

examples.translation: fī al-ʾuqṣur maʿbadān kabīrān. — In Luxor there are two large temples.

examples.text: اِسْمُ الْأَوَّل مَعْبَد الْأُقْصُر وَالثَّانِي مَعْبَد الْكَرْنَك.
examples.translation: ismu al-ʾawwal maʿbad al-ʾuqṣur wath-thānī maʿbad al-karnak. — The first is called the Luxor temple and the second the Karnak temple.
baynahumā ṭarīq fīhi tamāthīl kathīra. — Between them is a road with many statues.
al-maqābir al-qadīma ʿalā aḍ-ḍiffa al-gharbiyya. — The old tombs are on the western bank.
yazūr as-suyyāḥ al-maʿbadayn kulla yawm. — The tourists visit the two temples every day.

examples.text: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى الْكَرْنَك صَبَاحًا لِأَنَّ الْجَوّ حَارّ.
examples.translation: idhhab ʾilā al-karnak ṣabāḥan liʾanna al-jaww ḥārr. — Go to Karnak in the morning because the weather is hot.

options: it is a plural of people
the adjective agrees with a dual noun
exercises.explanation: A dual noun takes a dual adjective.
The oblique dual ends in ـَيْن.

explanations.title: On the river
explanations.body: Many tourists travel on the Nile between Aswan and Luxor by boat, a رِحْلَة نِيلِيَّة, “Nile trip”. The boat is a بَاخِرَة or a سَفِينَة. It stops at a landing place (مَرْسَى) and sails again. Dinner (عَشَاء) is served on board. The timetable below is invented.

lessons.title: 408. The sound and light show
lessons.subtitle: عَرْض الصَّوْت وَالضَّوْء · يَحْكِي قِصَّة الْمَعْبَد

explanations.title: An evening at the temple
explanations.body: In the evening there may be a show of sound and light at a temple, عَرْض الصَّوْت وَالضَّوْء. Voices and lights tell the story of the place (يَحْكِي قِصَّة الْمَعْبَد). The show starts after sunset (بَعْدَ الْغُرُوب). The verb أَعْجَبَ means “to please”: أَعْجَبَنِي الْعَرْض, “the show pleased me”. The sentences are invented.

yaḥkī al-ʿarḍ qiṣṣa al-maʿbad. — The show tells the story of the temple.
ishtaraynā tadhākir lil-ʿarḍ. — We bought tickets for the show.
ʾaʿjabanī al-ʿarḍ kathīran. — I liked the show very much.
ʾaʿjaba al-ʿarḍ zawjatī ʾayḍan. — The show pleased my wife too.

lessons.title: 409. Let us, let him: لِـ with the jussive
lessons.subtitle: لِنَذْهَبْ · لِيَدْخُلِ الضُّيُوف

explanations.title: A command for ‘we’, ‘he’ and ‘she’
explanations.body: The command form exists only for ‘you’. To give an order or a suggestion to ‘we’, ‘he’, ‘she’ or ‘they’, put لِـ before the short present (the jussive): لِنَذْهَبْ, “let us go”; لِيَدْخُلْ, “let him enter”; لِتَجْلِسْ, “let her sit”. The jussive ends in sukūn, like the command. Compare: لِيَكْتُبْ, “let him write”, and لِيَكْتُبَ, “so that he writes” (purpose, accusative). Only the final vowel tells them apart.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: At the post office.

examples.translation: linadhhab ʾilā maktab al-barīd. — Let us go to the post office.
linajlis hunā qalīlan. — Let us sit here a little.
liyadkhuli aḍ-ḍuyūf al-ʾān. — Let the guests enter now.
litajlis salmā hunā. — Let Salma sit here.
liyaktub kull wāḥid ismahu. — Let each one write his name.
jiʾnā linaktuba al-ʿanāwīn. — We came in order to write the addresses.

options: Do not let the guests enter
exercises.explanation: A request about the third person.

exercises.prompt: Which ending does the jussive have?
exercises.explanation: The short present ends in sukūn.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between لِيَكْتُبْ and لِيَكْتُبَ?

explanations.title: Which ending after which word?
explanations.body: A present verb has three moods, and the word before it decides which one you need. With nothing before it, the verb is indicative (ـُ). After أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ, لِـ (purpose) or حَتَّى it is accusative (ـَ). After لَمْ, لَا (a command) or لِـ (a command) it is jussive (ـْ). The group forms lose their ن in the accusative and the jussive, the women’s plural never does.

explanations.title: One verb, many sentences (invented)
explanations.body: The same verb, three moods.

examples.translation: yaṣilu al-qiṭār fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The train arrives in the morning.
ʾurīd ʾan yaṣila al-qiṭār mubakkiran. — I want the train to arrive early.
lan yaṣila al-qiṭār al-yawm. — The train will not arrive today.
lam yaṣili al-qiṭār ʾams. — The train did not arrive yesterday.
lā tadhhab ʾilā al-maḥaṭṭa al-ʾān. — Do not go to the station now.

exercises.explanation: The plain present ends in ـُ.
لَا + jussive in the second person = prohibition.

lessons.title: 411. At the post office: stamps and parcels
lessons.subtitle: طَابِع · ظَرْف · طَرْد · بَرِيد جَوِّيّ

explanations.title: Words for the post
explanations.body: At the post office, مَكْتَب الْبَرِيد, you buy stamps (طَوَابِع), send postcards (بِطَاقَات بَرِيدِيَّة), letters in envelopes (ظُرُوف) and parcels (طُرُود). You can choose ordinary mail, registered mail (بَرِيد مُسَجَّل) or air mail (بَرِيد جَوِّيّ). The clerk weighs the parcel: its weight is its وَزْن. The conversation is invented.

examples.translation: ʾurīd ṭawābiʿ likhams biṭāqāt barīdiyya. — I want stamps for five postcards.
kam wazn hādhā aṭ-ṭard? — How much does this parcel weigh?
waznuhu thalātha kīlū. — Its weight is three kilos.

examples.text: هَلْ تُرِيد بَرِيدًا عَادِيًّا أَمْ مُسَجَّلًا؟
examples.translation: hal turīd barīdan ʿādiyyan ʾam musajjalan? — Do you want ordinary or registered mail?
bil-barīd al-jawwiyy min faḍlika. — By air mail, please.

lessons.title: 414. A postcard from Luxor
lessons.subtitle: أُمِّي الْعَزِيزَة · أَكْتُب لَكِ مِنَ الْأُقْصُر

explanations.title: How to write a postcard
explanations.body: A postcard has a greeting, a short message and a closing. A greeting can be أُمِّي الْعَزِيزَة, “my dear mother”, or أَبِي الْعَزِيز, “my dear father”. The closing can be مَعَ حُبِّي, “with my love”, or إِلَى اللِّقَاء, “until we meet”. The card below is invented.

maʿa ḥubbī, waʾilā al-liqāʾ. — With my love, and until we meet.

explanations.title: When something goes wrong
explanations.body: A clerk may say that the office is closed (مُغْلَق) and will open tomorrow, that the address is wrong (خَطَأ), or that the parcel is too heavy. He may then give a command with a Measure IV or II verb: أَخْرِجْ, “take out”, غَيِّرْ, “change”. Notice the accusative after يَجِب أَنْ. The lines are invented.

yaftaḥ al-maktab ghadan as-sāʿa ath-thāmina. — The office opens tomorrow at eight.
al-ʿunwān khaṭaʾ, yajib ʾan tughayyirahu. — The address is wrong, you must change it.

lessons.title: 416. Review: Egypt, moods and the post office
lessons.subtitle: مُرَاجَعَة الْوَحْدَة

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: After أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ, حَتَّى and purpose لِـ the present is accusative (ـَ). After لَمْ, a command لِـ and a prohibition لَا it is jussive (ـْ). Groups lose their ن, women’s plurals keep it, and defective verbs show ـَ on their last ي or و. Egypt’s sites, trains, ships and the post office give the vocabulary.

lessons.title: 417. Renting a car
lessons.subtitle: أُرِيد أَنْ أَسْتَأْجِرَ سَيَّارَة · صَغِيرَة أَمْ كَبِيرَة؟

explanations.title: At the rental desk
explanations.body: To rent a car you say أُرِيد أَنْ أَسْتَأْجِرَ سَيَّارَة. The verb اِسْتَأْجَرَ (Measure X) means “to rent (for yourself)”. The noun for renting is إِيجَار, “rent, hire”. Cars come in sizes: صَغِيرَة, مُتَوَسِّطَة and كَبِيرَة. The conversation takes place at an airport in Morocco and is invented.

examples.text: أُرِيد أَنْ أَسْتَأْجِرَ سَيَّارَة لِمُدَّة أُسْبُوع.
examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾastaʾjira sayyāra limudda ʾusbūʿ. — I want to rent a car for a week.

examples.text: أَيَّ نَوْع تُرِيد؟ صَغِيرَة أَمْ كَبِيرَة؟
examples.translation: ʾayya nawʿ turīd? ṣaghīra ʾam kabīra? — Which type do you want? Small or large?

examples.text: نُرِيد سَيَّارَة كَبِيرَة لِأَنَّ مَعَنَا حَقَائِب كَثِيرَة.

kam siʿr al-ʾījār fī al-yawm? — How much is the rent per day?
al-ʾījār al-ʾusbūʿiyy ʾarkhaṣ. — The weekly rent is cheaper.
saʾastaʾjir as-sayyāra al-mutawassiṭa. — I will rent the medium car.

lessons.title: 418. Terms and conditions
lessons.subtitle: رُخْصَة الْقِيَادَة · رَسْم إِضَافِيّ · خَزَّان مُمْتَلِئ

explanations.title: What the contract says
explanations.body: A rental brochure lists conditions (شُرُوط). You must show your driving licence (رُخْصَة الْقِيَادَة). The driver must be old enough: عُمْر السَّائِق. A second driver may cost an extra fee (رَسْم إِضَافِيّ). When you return the car (إِعَادَة السَّيَّارَة), the tank should be full (الْخَزَّان مُمْتَلِئ). The terms below are invented.

examples.translation: ʾaḥḍir rukhṣa al-qiyāda min faḍlika. — Bring your driving licence, please.

examples.text: يَجِب أَنْ يَكُونَ عُمْر السَّائِق مُنَاسِبًا.

hunāka rasm ʾiḍāfiyy lis-sāʾiq ath-thānī. — There is an extra fee for a second driver.

explanations.title: Is it included?
explanations.body: A rental agent offers insurance (تَأْمِين). Full insurance is تَأْمِين شَامِل. To ask whether something is included, use يَشْمَل, “includes”: هَلِ السِّعْر يَشْمَل التَّأْمِين؟ Extras are things like a navigation system (نِظَام مِلَاحَة) or a child seat (مَقْعَد لِلْأَطْفَال). The sentences are invented.
