I will not pay another fee.

lessons.title: 420. Parts of the car and its condition
lessons.subtitle: مُحَرِّك · إِطَار · فَرَامِل · بَطَّارِيَّة

explanations.title: Inside and outside
explanations.body: Before you drive away, you read the description of the car’s condition. The parts have names: the engine (مُحَرِّك), the tyres (إِطَارَات), the brakes (فَرَامِل), the battery (بَطَّارِيَّة), the window glass (زُجَاج), the steering wheel (مِقْوَد) and the lights (مَصَابِيح). The plural of things takes a feminine singular adjective: الْإِطَارَات جَدِيدَة. The description is invented.

examples.translation: al-muḥarrik jayyid wal-ʾiṭārāt jadīda. — The engine is good and the tyres are new.
al-farāmil taʿmal jayyidan. — The brakes work well.
zujāj al-bāb al-ʾayman maksūr. — The glass of the right door is broken.
fī al-bāb al-ʾaysar khadsh ṣaghīr. — On the left door there is a small scratch.
al-maṣābīḥ taʿmal wal-khazzān mumtaliʾ bil-binzīn. — The lights work and the tank is full of petrol.

exercises.prompt: What does زُجَاج الْبَاب مَكْسُور mean?

options: the plural of things is feminine singular

exercises.prompt: What does الْفَرَامِل تَعْمَل جَيِّدًا mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: The engine is good and the tyres are new.
The tyres are new.
On the left door there is a small scratch.

exercises.explanation: A tank is full of petrol.
exercises.promptTranslation: The tank is full of petrol.

explanations.title: What went wrong?
explanations.body: On the road something may go wrong. The car breaks down (تَعَطَّلَتِ السَّيَّارَة), the engine overheats (الْمُحَرِّك سَاخِن), a tyre is punctured (مَثْقُوب), the battery is flat (فَارِغَة) or the fuel runs out (نَفِدَ الْوَقُود). A feminine noun like سَيَّارَة takes a feminine verb: تَوَقَّفَتْ. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: taʿaṭṭalati as-sayyāra ʿalā aṭ-ṭarīq. — The car broke down on the road.
al-muḥarrik sākhin wayakhruj minhu dukhān. — The engine is hot and smoke comes out of it.
al-ʾiṭār mathqūb wal-baṭṭāriyya fārigha. — The tyre is punctured and the battery is flat.
nafida al-waqūd fajʾatan. — The fuel ran out suddenly.
tawaqqafati as-sayyāra ʿalā jānib aṭ-ṭarīq. — The car stopped at the side of the road.
mā al-mushkila? — What is the problem?

exercises.promptTranslation: The car broke down on the road.

exercises.explanation: Smoke comes out of an overheated engine.
exercises.promptTranslation: The engine is hot and smoke comes out of it.
The fuel ran out suddenly.
The car stopped at the side of the road.

lessons.title: 422. At the mechanic’s
lessons.subtitle: كَمْ تَكْلِفَة الْإِصْلَاح؟ · سَتَكُون جَاهِزَة غَدًا

explanations.title: Talking about the repair
explanations.body: At the workshop (وَرْشَة), the technician (فَنِّيّ) first examines the car (فَحَصَ). He names the problem, a spare part (قِطْعَة غِيَار), the cost (تَكْلِفَة) and the time. The verb أَصْلَحَ (Measure IV) means “to repair”; the noun is إِصْلَاح. You can bargain politely. The conversation is invented.

examples.translation: mā al-mushkila? — What is the problem?
al-muḥarrik sākhin jiddan. — The engine is very hot.
saʾafḥaṣ as-sayyāra al-ʾān. — I will examine the car now.
naḥtāj ʾilā qiṭʿa ghiyār jadīda. — We need a new spare part.
kam taklifa al-ʾiṣlāḥ? — How much does the repair cost?
as-siʿr murtafiʿ, ʾarjū ʾan tukhaffiḍahu. — The price is high, please lower it.
hal yumkin ʾan tuṣliḥahā al-yawm? — Can you repair it today?
satakūn jāhiza ghadan masāʾan. — It will be ready tomorrow evening.

exercises.prompt: What does كَمْ تَكْلِفَة الْإِصْلَاح؟ ask?
What does سَتَكُون جَاهِزَة غَدًا مَسَاءً mean?
options: It will be ready tomorrow evening

exercises.promptTranslation: We need a new spare part.
How much does the repair cost?
Can you repair it today?
It will be ready tomorrow evening.

lessons.title: 423. Connectors: adding, giving reasons, drawing results
lessons.subtitle: وَ · كَمَا · لِأَنَّ · بِسَبَب · لِذَلِكَ

explanations.title: Joining sentences
explanations.body: To tell a story, join the sentences. For adding information use وَ, “and”, كَمَا, “also, moreover”, أَيْضًا, “also”, and بِالْإِضَافَة إِلَى ذَلِكَ, “in addition to that”. For a reason use لِأَنَّ, “because”, or بِسَبَب, “because of”. For a result use لِذَلِكَ, “therefore”. After لِأَنَّ comes a noun or a pronoun suffix: لِأَنَّهُ, لِأَنَّهَا.

explanations.title: A breakdown story (invented)
explanations.body: A traveller tells what happened.

examples.translation: tawaqqafati as-sayyāra liʾanna al-waqūd nafida. — The car stopped because the fuel ran out.
tawaqqafnā bisabab ad-dukhān. — We stopped because of the smoke.
al-muḥarrik sākhin, lidhālika tawaqqafnā. — The engine is hot, therefore we stopped.
kamā ʾanna aṭ-ṭarīq ṭawīl. — Moreover, the road is long.

examples.text: بِالْإِضَافَة إِلَى ذَلِكَ، الْهَاتِف لَا يَعْمَل.
examples.translation: bil-ʾiḍāfa ʾilā dhālika, al-hātif lā yaʿmal. — In addition to that, the phone does not work.
lam naṣil liʾannahā taʿaṭṭalat. — We did not arrive because it (the car) broke down.

exercises.promptTranslation: The car stopped because the fuel ran out.
The engine is hot, therefore we stopped.

exercises.explanation: A noun follows: because of the smoke.
exercises.promptTranslation: We stopped because of the smoke.
We did not arrive because it broke down.

lessons.title: 424. Connectors: contrast
lessons.subtitle: لَكِنَّ · أَمَّا… فَـ · بَيْنَمَا · رَغْمَ أَنَّ

explanations.title: But, while, although
explanations.body: To set two things against each other use لَكِنَّ, “but”, بَيْنَمَا, “while”, and أَمَّا … فَـ, “as for … ”. To say “although” use رَغْمَ أَنَّ; to say “even so” use مَعَ ذَلِكَ. To correct a statement use بَلْ, “but rather”. After لَكِنَّ and رَغْمَ أَنَّ a noun is accusative or takes a pronoun suffix: لَكِنَّهَا, “but it”.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Comparing two rental cars.

examples.translation: as-sayyāra qadīma lakinnahā qawiyya. — The car is old but it is strong.
ʾammā al-muḥarrik fajayyid. — As for the engine, it is good.
baynamā al-ʾiṭārāt jadīda, al-farāmil qadīma. — While the tyres are new, the brakes are old.

examples.text: رَغْمَ أَنَّ السِّعْر مُرْتَفِع، سَنَسْتَأْجِر السَّيَّارَة.
examples.translation: raghma ʾanna as-siʿr murtafiʿ, sanastaʾjir as-sayyāra. — Although the price is high, we shall rent the car.

examples.text: مَعَ ذَلِكَ، لَمْ نَدْفَع رَسْمًا إِضَافِيًّا.
examples.translation: maʿa dhālika, lam nadfaʿ rasman ʾiḍāfiyyan. — Even so, we did not pay an extra fee.
laysat as-sayyāra ṣaghīra bal kabīra. — The car is not small but large.

exercises.explanation: It sets two things against each other.

exercises.prompt: What does بَلْ do in لَيْسَت صَغِيرَة بَلْ كَبِيرَة?
What does أَمَّا الْمُحَرِّك فَجَيِّد mean?
options: As for the engine, it is good

exercises.promptTranslation: The car is old but it is strong.
While the tyres are new, the brakes are old.
Although the price is high, we shall rent the car.
The car is not small but large.

lessons.title: 425. Connectors: time
lessons.subtitle: عِنْدَمَا · بَعْدَ أَنْ · قَبْلَ أَنْ · أَثْنَاءَ · حَتَّى

explanations.title: When did it happen?
explanations.body: To say when something happened relative to something else, use time connectors. عِنْدَمَا, “when”, and بَعْدَ أَنْ, “after”, are followed by a past verb in a story. قَبْلَ أَنْ, “before”, is followed by the accusative (ـَ). أَثْنَاءَ, “during”, and مُنْذُ, “since, for”, are followed by a noun. حَتَّى, “until”, can be followed by a past verb in a story, or by the accusative when it is still to come. كُلَّمَا means “whenever”.

explanations.title: A journey (invented)
explanations.body: Things happening on a trip to Rabat.

examples.text: عِنْدَمَا وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الرِّبَاط، تَوَقَّفَتِ السَّيَّارَة.
examples.translation: ʿindamā waṣalnā ʾilā ar-ribāṭ, tawaqqafati as-sayyāra. — When we reached Rabat, the car stopped.

examples.text: بَعْدَ أَنْ تَوَقَّفْنَا، نَزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّيَّارَة.
examples.translation: baʿda ʾan tawaqqafnā, nazalnā mina as-sayyāra. — After we stopped, we got out of the car.
qabla ʾan nataḥarraka, faḥaṣnā al-ʾiṭārāt. — Before we set off, we checked the tyres.
ʾathnāʾa ar-riḥla, samiʿnā ṣawtan gharīban. — During the trip, we heard a strange sound.
intaẓarnā ḥattā waṣala al-fanniyy. — We waited until the technician arrived.
mundhu yawmayn was-sayyāra fī al-warsha. — For two days the car has been in the workshop.

exercises.promptTranslation: When we reached Rabat, the car stopped.
Before we set off, we checked the tyres.

exercises.explanation: A noun follows: during the trip.
exercises.promptTranslation: During the trip, we heard a strange sound.
We waited until the technician arrived.

explanations.title: Conditions
explanations.body: Use إِذَا for a condition that may well happen: إِذَا تَعَطَّلَتِ السَّيَّارَة, “if the car breaks down”. The verb after إِذَا is in the past form, even for the future. Use لَوْ for a condition that is unlikely or impossible, and put لَـ before the result: لَوْ كَانَ مَعَنَا وَقُود لَوَصَلْنَا. For ‘if not’ use إِذَا لَمْ with the jussive. The result of a command often starts with فَـ.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Advice on the road.

examples.text: إِذَا تَعَطَّلَتِ السَّيَّارَة، فَتَوَقَّفْ عَلَى الْجَانِب.
examples.translation: ʾidhā taʿaṭṭalati as-sayyāra, fatawaqqaf ʿalā al-jānib. — If the car breaks down, stop at the side.
ʾidhā sakhuna al-muḥarrik, faʾaṭfiʾhu. — If the engine gets hot, switch it off.
law kāna maʿanā waqūd lawaṣalnā. — If we had had fuel, we would have arrived.

examples.text: إِذَا لَمْ يَعْمَلِ الْمُحَرِّك، سَنَنْتَظِر الْفَنِّيّ.
examples.translation: ʾidhā lam yaʿmali al-muḥarrik, sanantaẓir al-fanniyy. — If the engine does not work, we will wait for the technician.

examples.text: سَتَكُون السَّيَّارَة جَاهِزَة غَدًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه.
examples.translation: satakūn as-sayyāra jāhiza ghadan ʾin shāʾa allāh. — The car will be ready tomorrow, God willing.

exercises.prompt: What does لَوْ كَانَ مَعَنَا وَقُود لَوَصَلْنَا mean?
options: If we had had fuel, we would have arrived
If we have fuel, we will arrive
We have fuel, so we arrived

exercises.prompt: What does إِذَا لَمْ يَعْمَلِ الْمُحَرِّك mean?
options: if the engine does not work

exercises.explanation: The past is used for the condition.

exercises.prompt: What does إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه mean?
exercises.explanation: A common phrase about the future.

exercises.prompt: What starts the result in لَوْ … لَوَصَلْنَا?
exercises.explanation: The result of لَوْ takes لَـ.

exercises.promptTranslation: If the car breaks down, stop at the side.
If we had had fuel, we would have arrived.
If the engine does not work, we will wait for the technician.
It will be ready tomorrow, God willing.

explanations.title: A letter about the trip (invented)
explanations.body: Connectors turn single sentences into a story. Read this short letter to a friend and notice each connector: أَوَّلًا, عِنْدَمَا, لَكِنَّ, لِأَنَّ, لِذَلِكَ, بَعْدَ أَنْ, أَخِيرًا.

examples.text: صَدِيقِي الْعَزِيز، سَافَرْنَا مِنْ فَاس إِلَى طَنْجَة بِسَيَّارَة مُسْتَأْجَرَة.
examples.translation: ṣadīqī al-ʿazīz, sāfarnā min fās ʾilā ṭanja bisayyāra mustaʾjara. — My dear friend, we travelled from Fez to Tangier in a rented car.

examples.text: أَوَّلًا حَجَزْنَا السَّيَّارَة مِنْ شَرِكَة صَغِيرَة.
examples.translation: ʾawwalan ḥajaznā as-sayyāra min sharika ṣaghīra. — First we booked the car from a small company.
kāna aṭ-ṭarīq jamīlan lākinnahu ṭawīl. — The road was beautiful but long.

examples.text: عِنْدَمَا وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْجَبَل، سَخُنَ الْمُحَرِّك.
examples.translation: ʿindamā waṣalnā ʾilā al-jabal, sakhuna al-muḥarrik. — When we reached the mountain, the engine got hot.

examples.text: لِذَلِكَ تَوَقَّفْنَا لِأَنَّ الدُّخَان كَانَ كَثِيرًا.
examples.translation: lidhālika tawaqqafnā liʾanna ad-dukhān kāna kathīran. — So we stopped, because there was a lot of smoke.

examples.text: بَعْدَ أَنْ كَلَّمْنَا الشَّرِكَة، وَصَلَ الْفَنِّيّ.
examples.translation: baʿda ʾan kallamnā ash-sharika, waṣala al-fanniyy. — After we spoke to the company, the technician arrived.
ʾakhīran ʾaṣlaḥa al-muḥarrik, wasāfarnā masāʾan. — Finally he repaired the engine, and we travelled in the evening.

exercises.prompt: Which connector gives the result in ‘so we stopped’?
Which connector gives the reason in ‘because there was smoke’?
What does سَافَرْنَا بِسَيَّارَة مُسْتَأْجَرَة mean?
options: We travelled in a rented car
We rented a car for a friend

exercises.promptTranslation: The road was beautiful but long.
When we reached the mountain, the engine got hot.
We stopped because there was a lot of smoke.
Finally the technician repaired the engine, and we travelled in the evening.

explanations.title: The pattern اِفْعَلَّ
explanations.body: Measure IX is used for colours and bodily defects. It means “to become that colour” or “to become more strongly that colour”. The pattern is اِفْعَلَّ: the last two letters are joined with a shadda. From the colour أَحْمَر, “red”, comes اِحْمَرَّ, “turned red”. The present is يَحْمَرُّ.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Things that change colour.

examples.translation: iḥmarra wajhuhu mina al-ghaḍab. — His face turned red with anger.
iṣfarrat ʾawrāq ash-shajara fī al-kharīf. — The leaves of the tree turned yellow in autumn.
ikhḍarra al-ʿushb baʿda al-maṭar. — The grass turned green after the rain.
iswaddati as-samāʾ qabla al-maṭar. — The sky turned dark before the rain.
ibyaḍḍa shaʿruhu. — His hair turned white.

exercises.prompt: What is the pattern of Measure IX?
exercises.explanation: A shadda on the last letter.

exercises.prompt: What is the feminine of أَحْمَر?
exercises.explanation: Colour adjectives use فَعْلَاء for the feminine.

exercises.promptTranslation: His face turned red with anger.

exercises.explanation: Things take a feminine singular verb.
exercises.promptTranslation: The leaves of the tree turned yellow in autumn.
The grass turned green after the rain.
His hair turned white.

explanations.title: Joined and split
explanations.body: Measure IX behaves like other doubled verbs. When the ending begins with a vowel (he, she, they), the last two letters stay joined: اِحْمَرَّ, اِحْمَرَّتْ, اِحْمَرُّوا. When the ending begins with a consonant (I, you, we), the two letters split: اِحْمَرَرْتُ, اِحْمَرَرْنَا. The present is يَحْمَرُّ, تَحْمَرُّ, أَحْمَرُّ, and the women’s plural splits: يَحْمَرِرْنَ.

explanations.title: In sentences (invented)
explanations.body: Faces and skies.

examples.translation: iḥmarartu mina al-khajal. — I turned red with embarrassment.
iḥmarrat wujūh al-ʾaṭfāl. — The children’s faces turned red.
taḥmarru ash-shams ʿinda al-ghurūb. — The sun turns red at sunset.
izraqqa al-baḥr baʿda aṣ-ṣabāḥ. — The sea turned bluer after the morning.
yaṣfarru waraq ash-shajar fī al-kharīf. — The leaves of the trees turn yellow in autumn.

exercises.prompt: Why do the two letters split in اِحْمَرَرْتُ?
options: the ending starts with a consonant

exercises.explanation: A vowel ending: the letters stay joined.

exercises.prompt: What is the present of اِحْمَرَّ (he)?
exercises.explanation: A shadda on the last letter.

exercises.prompt: What does اِحْمَرَرْتُ مِنَ الْخَجَل mean?
Which form is ‘they (f.)’ in the present?

exercises.promptTranslation: I turned red with embarrassment.
The children’s faces turned red.
The sun turns red at sunset.
The sea turned bluer after the morning.

explanations.title: At the police station
explanations.body: If something is stolen, you report it to the police (الشُّرْطَة). The passive سُرِقَتْ, “was stolen”, hides the thief: سُرِقَتْ حَقِيبَتِي. The glass can be broken too: كُسِرَ الزُّجَاج. To report a crime, say أُرِيد أَنْ أُبَلِّغَ عَنْ سَرِقَة. The officer asks when and where it happened. These lines are invented.

examples.translation: ʾurīd ʾan ʾuballigha ʿan sariqa. — I want to report a theft.
suriqat ḥaqībatī mina as-sayyāra. — My bag was stolen from the car.
kusira zujāj as-sayyāra ʾayḍan. — The car’s window was also broken.
matā waʾayna ḥadathati as-sariqa? — When and where did the theft happen?
ḥadathat ʾams masāʾan ʾamāma as-sūq. — It happened yesterday evening in front of the market.
sanaktub taqrīran wanattaṣil bika. — We will write a report and call you.

exercises.prompt: What does أُرِيد أَنْ أُبَلِّغَ عَنْ سَرِقَة mean?
options: I want to see the police
I want to report a theft
I want to sign a form
I want to rent a car

exercises.prompt: What does مَتَى وَأَيْنَ حَدَثَتِ السَّرِقَة؟ ask?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to report a theft.
My bag was stolen from the car.
The car’s window was also broken.

exercises.explanation: The object of a verb: accusative tanwīn.
exercises.promptTranslation: We will write a report and call you.

lessons.title: 431. Describing what was stolen
lessons.subtitle: حَقِيبَة سَوْدَاء · هَاتِف أَسْوَد · اِتَّصِلْ بِالتَّأْمِين

explanations.title: Colour, size, contents
explanations.body: The officer asks you to describe the items. Colours agree with the noun: حَقِيبَة سَوْدَاء (f.), هَاتِف أَسْوَد (m.). Say what was in the bag: فِيهَا, “in it”. Then call the insurance company (شَرِكَة التَّأْمِين) to ask for compensation (تَعْوِيض). This dialogue is invented.

examples.translation: mā lawn al-ḥaqība? — What colour is the bag?
hiya ḥaqība sawdāʾ kabīra. — It is a big black bag.
fīhā hātif ʾaswad wamiḥfaẓa zarqāʾ. — In it are a black phone and a blue wallet.
wafīhā ʾayḍan jawāz safarī. — And in it also is my passport.
ittaṣil bisharika at-taʾmīn ghadan. — Call the insurance company tomorrow.
ʾurīd ʾan ʾaṭluba taʿwīḍan. — I want to ask for compensation.

exercises.prompt: What does مَا لَوْن الْحَقِيبَة؟ ask?
Which is correct for a black bag?
exercises.explanation: A feminine noun takes a feminine colour.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct for a black phone?
What does اِتَّصِلْ بِشَرِكَة التَّأْمِين mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: It is a big black bag.
In it is a black phone.
and a blue wallet.

exercises.explanation: The object of a verb: accusative tanwīn.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want to ask for compensation.

explanations.title: Writing to the insurance company
explanations.body: A formal letter has a greeting, the explanation, a request and a polite ending. Open with تَحِيَّة طَيِّبَة وَبَعْد, “greetings, and now”. State your purpose with أَكْتُب إِلَيْكُمْ لِأَشْرَحَ …, “I am writing to you to explain …”. Tell the story with connectors, ask for what you want with أَرْجُو أَنْ …, and finish with وَشُكْرًا لِتَعَاوُنِكُمْ, “and thank you for your cooperation”. The letter below is invented.

examples.text: إِلَى شَرِكَة التَّأْمِين الْمُحْتَرَمَة، تَحِيَّة طَيِّبَة وَبَعْد،
examples.translation: ʾilā sharika at-taʾmīn al-muḥtarama, taḥiyya ṭayyiba wabaʿd, — To the esteemed insurance company, kind greetings, and now:

examples.text: أَكْتُب إِلَيْكُمْ لِأَشْرَحَ مَا حَدَثَ أَثْنَاءَ رِحْلَتِي.
examples.translation: ʾaktub ʾilaykum liʾashraḥa mā ḥadatha ʾathnāʾa riḥlatī. — I am writing to you to explain what happened during my trip.

examples.text: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ عَلَى الطَّرِيق بَيْنَ الرِّبَاط وَفَاس، تَعَطَّلَتِ السَّيَّارَة.
examples.translation: ʿindamā kuntu ʿalā aṭ-ṭarīq bayna ar-ribāṭ wafās, taʿaṭṭalati as-sayyāra. — When I was on the road between Rabat and Fez, the car broke down.

examples.text: لِذَلِكَ اِتَّصَلْتُ بِالْوَرْشَة، وَأَصْلَحُوهَا فِي يَوْم وَاحِد.
examples.translation: lidhālika ittaṣaltu bil-warsha, waʾaṣlaḥūhā fī yawm wāḥid. — So I called the workshop, and they repaired it in one day.

examples.text: دَفَعْتُ تَكْلِفَة الْإِصْلَاح، وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تُعِيدُوهَا إِلَيَّ.
examples.translation: dafaʿtu taklifa al-ʾiṣlāḥ, waʾarjū ʾan tuʿīdūhā ʾilayya. — I paid the cost of the repair, and I hope you will pay it back to me.
marfaq bihādhihi ar-risāla al-ʾīṣāl. — The receipt is attached to this letter.
washukran litaʿāwunikum, maʿa fāʾiq al-iḥtirām. — And thank you for your cooperation, with the highest respect.

exercises.prompt: What does تَحِيَّة طَيِّبَة وَبَعْد begin?
exercises.explanation: A usual opening of a letter.

exercises.prompt: What does أَكْتُب إِلَيْكُمْ لِأَشْرَحَ mean?
options: I am writing to you to explain

exercises.prompt: What does مَرْفَق بِهَذِهِ الرِّسَالَة الْإِيصَال mean?
options: The receipt is attached to this letter

exercises.prompt: What does أَرْجُو أَنْ تُعِيدُوهَا إِلَيَّ ask?
options: that they give it back to me

exercises.promptTranslation: I am writing to you to explain what happened.
When I was on the road, the car broke down.

exercises.prompt: دَفَعْتُ تَكْلِفَة ___، وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تُعِيدُوهَا إِلَيَّ.
exercises.promptTranslation: I paid the cost of the repair, and I hope you will pay it back to me.
And thank you for your cooperation, with the highest respect.

lessons.title: 433. The repair report form
lessons.subtitle: تَارِيخ الْعُطْل · مَكَان الْعُطْل · تَكْلِفَة الْإِصْلَاح

explanations.title: Fields on the form
explanations.body: When you return a rented car you may have to fill in a form about any repair. The usual boxes are: تَارِيخ الْعُطْل, “date of the breakdown”, مَكَان الْعُطْل, “place of the breakdown”, نَوْع الْعُطْل, “type of fault”, تَكْلِفَة الْإِصْلَاح, “cost of the repair”, مُدَّة الْإِصْلَاح, “duration of the repair”, and التَّوْقِيع, “signature”. The agent gives you commands. The lines are invented.

examples.translation: uktub tārīkh al-ʿuṭl wamakānahu. — Write the date and place of the breakdown.
uktub nawʿ al-ʿuṭl: al-muḥarrik sākhin. — Write the type of fault: the engine is hot.
sajjil taklifa al-ʾiṣlāḥ wamuddatahu. — Record the cost of the repair and its duration.
lā tansa isma al-mustaʾjir. — Do not forget the name of the renter.
waqqiʿ fī al-makān al-munāsib. — Sign in the right place.

exercises.prompt: What does لَا تَنْسَ اِسْمَ الْمُسْتَأْجِر mean?
options: Do not forget the renter’s name

exercises.explanation: Date and place of the fault.
exercises.promptTranslation: Write the date and place of the breakdown.
Record the cost of the repair and its duration.
Do not forget the name of the renter.
Sign in the right place.

lessons.title: 434. Review: cars, connectors, colours and reports
lessons.subtitle: مُرَاجَعَة الْوَحْدَة

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Renting: اِسْتَأْجَرَ, إِيجَار, شُرُوط, تَأْمِين. Problems: تَعَطَّلَتِ السَّيَّارَة, نَفِدَ الْوَقُود, تَكْلِفَة الْإِصْلَاح. Connectors: لِأَنَّ and بِسَبَب (reason), لِذَلِكَ (result), لَكِنَّ and بَيْنَمَا (contrast), عِنْدَمَا and بَعْدَ أَنْ (time), إِذَا and لَوْ (condition). Measure IX: اِحْمَرَّ, اِصْفَرَّ, اِخْضَرَّ, اِزْرَقَّ, اِسْوَدَّ, اِبْيَضَّ.

exercises.promptTranslation: The car stopped because the fuel ran out.
The car is old but it is strong.
If the car breaks down, stop at the side.
The sea turned bluer after the morning.

exercises.explanation: A feminine noun takes a feminine colour.
exercises.promptTranslation: It is a big black bag.
I want to report a theft.

units.title: الْعَوْدَة إِلَى الْكُوَيْت: accidents, health, feelings and review

explanations.title: What happened on the road
explanations.body: A traffic accident is حَادِث سَيْر. You say it happened with وَقَعَ, “occurred”. Cars collide: اِصْطَدَمَتْ بِـ, “crashed into”, or تَصَادَمَتَا, “collided with each other” (Measure VI). When the verb comes first it stays singular: تَصَادَمَتِ السَّيَّارَتَان. When the pair comes first, the verb agrees with the dual: السَّيَّارَتَان تَصَادَمَتَا. The journal lines are invented.

examples.text: وَقَعَ حَادِث سَيْر عَلَى الطَّرِيق السَّرِيع.
examples.translation: waqaʿa ḥādith sayr ʿalā aṭ-ṭarīq as-sarīʿ. — A traffic accident happened on the highway.
iṣṭadamat sayyāratunā bishāḥina. — Our car crashed into a lorry.
kāna as-sāʾiq musriʿan. — The driver was speeding.
lam yatawaqqaf ʿinda al-ʾishāra al-ḥamrāʾ. — He did not stop at the red light.
taṣādamati as-sayyāratān ʿinda al-ʾishāra. — The two cars collided at the light.
as-sayyāratān taṣādamatā biquwwa. — The two cars collided hard.

exercises.prompt: What does اِصْطَدَمَتْ سَيَّارَتُنَا بِشَاحِنَة mean?
options: Our car crashed into a lorry
the two (f.) collided with each other

exercises.prompt: Why is it تَصَادَمَتِ السَّيَّارَتَان, with a singular verb?
exercises.explanation: A verb before its subject stays singular.

exercises.promptTranslation: A traffic accident happened on the highway.
Our car crashed into a lorry.

exercises.explanation: After كَانَ the predicate is accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: The driver was speeding.

exercises.explanation: The pair comes first: a dual verb.
exercises.promptTranslation: The two cars collided hard.

explanations.title: People and cars after the crash
explanations.body: People are injured: the passive جُرِحَ, “was wounded”, أُصِيبَ, “was hurt”. An injury is إِصَابَة, and the injured are الْجَرْحَى. An injury can be بَسِيطَة, “slight”, or خَطِيرَة, “serious”. Cars are damaged: تَضَرَّرَتِ السَّيَّارَة (Measure V). An ambulance is سَيَّارَة إِسْعَاف. The lines are invented.

examples.translation: juriḥa thalātha ʾashkhāṣ fī al-ḥādith. — Three people were wounded in the accident.
kānati al-ʾiṣābāt basīṭa. — The injuries were slight.
lam yujraḥ ʾaḥad. — No one was wounded.
taḍarrarati as-sayyāra kathīran. — The car was badly damaged.

examples.text: وَصَلَتْ سَيَّارَة الْإِسْعَاف بَعْدَ عَشْر دَقَائِق.
examples.translation: waṣalat sayyāra al-ʾisʿāf baʿda ʿashr daqāʾiq. — The ambulance arrived after ten minutes.
nuqila al-jarḥā ʾilā al-mustashfā. — The injured were taken to the hospital.

exercises.prompt: What does جُرِحَ ثَلَاثَة أَشْخَاص mean?
What does لَمْ يُجْرَحْ أَحَد mean?
What does نُقِلَ الْجَرْحَى إِلَى الْمُسْتَشْفَى mean?
options: The injured were taken to the hospital

exercises.promptTranslation: Three people were wounded in the accident.
The injuries were slight.
The car was badly damaged.
The ambulance arrived after ten minutes.

lessons.title: 437. The news report
lessons.subtitle: أَعْلَنَتِ الشُّرْطَة · يُقَال إِنَّ · مَا زَالَ التَّحْقِيق

explanations.title: How a report sounds
explanations.body: News reports use set phrases. أَعْلَنَتِ الشُّرْطَة أَنَّ …, “the police announced that …”; يُقَال إِنَّ …, “it is said that …”; مَا زَالَ التَّحْقِيق مُسْتَمِرًّا, “the investigation is still going on”. The word مَسْؤُولِيَّة means “responsibility”. The two reports below are invented, and they name no real event.

examples.text: أَعْلَنَتِ الشُّرْطَة أَنَّ حَادِثًا وَقَعَ صَبَاحَ الْيَوْم.
examples.translation: ʾaʿlanati ash-shurṭa ʾanna ḥādithan waqaʿa ṣabāḥa al-yawm. — The police announced that an accident happened this morning.
taṣādamat sayyāra washāḥina ʿinda al-ʾishāra. — A car and a lorry collided at the light.
nuqila al-jarḥā ʾilā al-mustashfā. — The injured were taken to the hospital.

examples.text: يُقَال إِنَّ سَائِق الشَّاحِنَة كَانَ مُسْرِعًا.
examples.translation: yuqāl ʾinna sāʾiq ash-shāḥina kāna musriʿan. — It is said that the lorry driver was speeding.
lam tuḥaddidi ash-shurṭa al-masʾūliyya baʿdu. — The police have not yet determined who is responsible.
mā zāla at-taḥqīq mustamirran. — The investigation is still continuing.

exercises.prompt: What does مَا زَالَ التَّحْقِيق مُسْتَمِرًّا mean?
options: The investigation is still going on

exercises.prompt: Why أَعْلَنَتِ with a final تِ?
What does لَمْ تُحَدِّدِ الشُّرْطَة الْمَسْؤُولِيَّة بَعْدُ mean?
options: The police have blamed the driver
The police have not yet determined the responsibility

exercises.promptTranslation: The police announced that an accident happened.
It is said that the lorry driver was speeding.

exercises.explanation: After مَا زَالَ the predicate is accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: The investigation is still continuing.
The police have not yet determined the responsibility.

lessons.title: 438. Telling mishaps in order: وَ، فَ، ثُمَّ، أَوْ
lessons.subtitle: نَزَلَ السَّائِق ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى الْإِطَار

explanations.title: Four small words
explanations.body: Four short conjunctions organise a story. وَ simply joins, “and”. فَ joins with a quick result, “and so, and then at once”. ثُمَّ joins with a pause, “then, after that”. أَوْ gives a choice, “or”. فَ and وَ are written joined to the next word; ثُمَّ and أَوْ are separate words. Before الـ, أَوْ becomes أَوِ. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: ʾawqafa as-sāʾiq as-sayyāra fanazala. — The driver stopped the car and (at once) got out.

examples.text: نَزَلَ السَّائِق ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى الْإِطَار.
examples.translation: nazala as-sāʾiq thumma naẓara ʾilā al-ʾiṭār. — The driver got out, then looked at the tyre.
waṣalati ash-shurṭa fakatabat taqrīran. — The police arrived and wrote a report.
ittaṣala bish-shurṭa thumma bish-sharika. — He called the police, then the company.

examples.text: أَيَّ طَرِيق نَأْخُذ: الْقَدِيم أَوِ الْجَدِيد؟
examples.translation: ʾayya ṭarīq naʾkhudh: al-qadīm ʾawi al-jadīd? — Which road shall we take: the old or the new?

examples.text: سَأَنْتَظِر فِي السَّيَّارَة أَوْ فِي الْمَقْهَى.
examples.translation: saʾantaẓir fī as-sayyāra ʾaw fī al-maqhā. — I will wait in the car or in the café.

exercises.prompt: Which word means ‘then, after a pause’?
What does فَـ add in أَوْقَفَ السَّيَّارَة فَنَزَلَ?

exercises.explanation: A final sukūn before الـ takes a helping vowel.

exercises.prompt: Which word is written joined to the next word?
What does اِتَّصَلَ بِالشُّرْطَة ثُمَّ بِالشَّرِكَة mean?
options: He called the police, then the company
He called the company, then the police

exercises.promptTranslation: The driver stopped the car and got out at once.
The driver got out, then looked at the tyre.
I will wait in the car or in the café.
Which road shall we take: the old or the new?

explanations.title: The أَفْعَل comparative
explanations.body: You know the comparative pattern أَفْعَل, “more …”: أَسْرَع, “faster”, أَبْطَأ, “slower”, أَخْطَر, “more dangerous”, أَخَفّ, “lighter”, أَسْلَم, “safer”. The thing compared follows مِنْ, “than”. A comparative does not change for gender or number. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: as-sayyāra ʾasraʿ mina ash-shāḥina. — The car is faster than the lorry.

examples.text: الطَّرِيق الْقَدِيم أَخْطَر مِنَ الطَّرِيق الْجَدِيد.
examples.translation: aṭ-ṭarīq al-qadīm ʾakhṭar mina aṭ-ṭarīq al-jadīd. — The old road is more dangerous than the new road.
al-qiyāda al-baṭīʾa ʾaslam. — Slow driving is safer.
kānat ʾiṣābatuhu ʾakhaff min ʾiṣābatī. — His injury was lighter than mine.

examples.text: هَذَا الْحَادِث أَقَلّ خَطَرًا مِنَ الْأَوَّل.
examples.translation: hādhā al-ḥādith ʾaqall khaṭaran mina al-ʾawwal. — This accident is less dangerous than the first.

exercises.prompt: What is the comparative of بَطِيء?
What does أَخْطَر مِنَ الطَّرِيق الْجَدِيد mean?
options: as long as the new road
more dangerous than the new road

exercises.prompt: Does a comparative change for a feminine noun?
What does الْقِيَادَة الْبَطِيئَة أَسْلَم mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: The car is faster than the lorry.
The old road is more dangerous than the new road.
His injury was lighter than mine.
Slow driving is safer.

lessons.title: 440. How do you feel? Adjectives
lessons.subtitle: سَعِيد · حَزِين · غَاضِب · خَائِف · قَلِق · مُتْعَب · مُرْتَاح

explanations.title: Feelings are adjectives
explanations.body: To say how you feel, use a noun phrase with no verb: أَنَا سَعِيد, “I am happy”. The adjective agrees with the person: add ـَة for a woman and ـُون for a group of men, ـَات for a group of women. To ask, use كَيْفَ تَشْعُر؟, “How do you feel?” (to a woman كَيْفَ تَشْعُرِين؟). Another way to say it: أَشْعُر بِـ + a noun, “I feel …”, as in أَشْعُر بِالتَّعَب, “I feel tired”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: ʾanā saʿīd al-yawm. — I am happy today.
hiya ḥazīna liʾanna ʾukhtahā sāfarat. — She is sad because her sister travelled.
limādhā ʾanta ghāḍib? — Why are you angry?
hum khāʾifūn mina al-kalb. — They are afraid of the dog.
kayfa tashʿurīn al-ʾān? — How do you (f.) feel now?
ʾashʿur bit-taʿab. — I feel tired.
naḥnu murtāḥūn fī al-funduq. — We are comfortable in the hotel.

exercises.prompt: What does أَنَا سَعِيد الْيَوْم mean?
exercises.explanation: A noun phrase with no verb.

exercises.prompt: How does a woman say “I am sad”?

exercises.explanation: تَشْعُرِين is addressed to a woman.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural, for a group of men, of قَلِق?

exercises.promptTranslation: She is sad because her sister travelled.
Why are you angry?
They are afraid of the dog.
We are comfortable in the hotel.

lessons.title: 441. Feelings as verbs
lessons.subtitle: فَرِحَ بِـ · حَزِنَ عَلَى · غَضِبَ مِنْ · خَافَ مِنْ · قَلِقَ عَلَى

explanations.title: Verbs of feeling and their prepositions
explanations.body: Many feelings have a verb with a fixed preposition. فَرِحَ بِـ, “was glad about”. حَزِنَ عَلَى, “grieved for”. غَضِبَ مِنْ, “got angry at”. خَافَ مِنْ, “was afraid of”. قَلِقَ عَلَى, “worried about”. تَعِبَ, “got tired”, takes no preposition. The verb خَافَ is hollow, so “I was afraid” is خِفْتُ with a short vowel. To calm someone, use a negative command: لَا تَقْلَقْ, “don't worry”, لَا تَحْزَنْ, “don't be sad”, لَا تَخَفْ, “don't be afraid”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: fariḥtu bil-khabar. — I was glad about the news.
ḥazinat ʿalā jaddatihā. — She grieved for her grandmother.
ghaḍiba al-mudīr mina at-taʾkhīr. — The manager got angry at the delay.
khiftu mina as-surʿa. — I was afraid of the speed.
qaliqat ʾummī ʿalayya. — My mother worried about me.
lā taqlaq, kull shayʾ bikhayr. — Don't worry, everything is fine.
lā takhaf. — Don't be afraid.

options: I was glad about the news
I was angry about the news
exercises.explanation: فَرِحَ بِـ = to be glad about.

exercises.prompt: What does غَضِبَ مِنَ التَّأْخِير mean?
options: he was glad about the delay
he got angry at the delay
exercises.explanation: غَضِبَ مِنْ = to get angry at.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I was afraid”?
exercises.explanation: A hollow verb takes a short vowel before the ending.

exercises.prompt: What does قَلِقَتْ أُمِّي عَلَيَّ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I was glad about the news.
She grieved for her grandmother.
The manager got angry at the delay.
Don't worry, everything is fine.

lessons.title: 442. Parts of the body
lessons.subtitle: رَأْس · عَيْن · أُذُن · أَنْف · فَم · يَد · رِجْل · ظَهْر · بَطْن

explanations.title: The body
explanations.body: Learn the body parts with a pronoun ending: رَأْسِي, “my head”, يَدُكَ, “your hand”. Many paired parts are feminine: عَيْن, أُذُن, يَد, رِجْل. A pair is dual: عَيْنَان, “two eyes”, أُذُنَان, “two ears”, يَدَان, “two hands”, رِجْلَان, “two legs”. As the object of a verb, or after a preposition, the dual ends in ـَيْن: اِفْتَحْ عَيْنَيْكَ, “open your eyes”. The word سِنّ, “tooth”, has the plural أَسْنَان, “teeth”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: lil-ʾinsān ʿaynān waʾudhunān wayadān warijlān. — A person has two eyes, two ears, two hands and two legs.
iftaḥ famaka min faḍlik. — Open your mouth, please.
ḍaʿ yadaka ʿalā ṣadrika. — Put your hand on your chest.
ighsil yadayka qabla al-ʾakl. — Wash your hands before eating.
ʾanfuhu kabīr. — His nose is big.
ʾunaẓẓifu ʾasnānī baʿda al-ʾakl. — I brush my teeth after eating.

exercises.explanation: Do not confuse it with the noon prayer time.

exercises.prompt: What is the dual of أُذُن (as a subject)?
Why is it اِغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ, with ـَيْ?
options: the dual as the object of a verb ends in ـَيْن
exercises.explanation: The dual in the accusative: ـَيْن.

exercises.promptTranslation: A person has two eyes and two ears.
Put your hand on your chest.
Open your mouth, please.
I brush my teeth after eating.

lessons.title: 443. Aches and symptoms
lessons.subtitle: عِنْدِي صُدَاع · عِنْدَهُ حُمَّى · أَلَم فِي ظَهْرِي

explanations.title: Saying what is wrong
explanations.body: Arabic says “I have” with عِنْدِي: عِنْدِي صُدَاع, “I have a headache”. The symptoms: صُدَاع, “headache”, حُمَّى, “fever”, سُعَال, “cough”, زُكَام, “a cold”, إِسْهَال, “diarrhoea”, دُوَار, “dizziness”. For a pain in a place: عِنْدِي أَلَم فِي + the part, “I have a pain in …”. “Since” is مُنْذُ + a time: مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْن, “for two days”. To deny: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي حُمَّى, “I have no fever”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: ʿindī ṣudāʿ shadīd. — I have a severe headache.
ʿindahu ḥummā wasuʿāl. — He has a fever and a cough.
ʿindī ʾalam fī ẓahrī. — I have a pain in my back.
ʾanā marīḍ mundhu yawmayn. — I have been ill for two days.
laysa ʿindī ḥummā. — I have no fever.
hal ʿindaki duwār? — Do you (f.) have dizziness?

exercises.prompt: What does عِنْدَهُ حُمَّى وَسُعَال mean?
options: he has a fever and a cough

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I have no fever”?
What does عِنْدِي أَلَم فِي ظَهْرِي mean?
options: I have a pain in my back
I have a pain in my head

exercises.promptTranslation: I have a severe headache.
He has a fever and a cough.
I have been ill for two days.
I have no fever.
Do you (f.) have dizziness?

lessons.title: 444. Asking about someone's health
lessons.subtitle: كَيْفَ صِحَّتُكَ؟ · مَا بِكَ؟ · لَسْتُ بِخَيْر

explanations.title: How is your health?
explanations.body: To ask about health: كَيْفَ صِحَّتُكَ؟, “How is your health?”, or هَلْ أَنْتَ بِخَيْر؟, “Are you well?” A usual answer is الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه, أَنَا بِخَيْر, “Thank God, I'm fine”. If someone looks unwell, ask مَا بِكَ؟, “What is wrong with you?” (to a woman مَا بِكِ؟). To say you are not well: لَسْتُ بِخَيْر, with بِ before the noun. To say you are better: أَنَا أَفْضَل الْيَوْم. Health that improves is تَحَسَّنَتْ صِحَّتُهُ, “his health improved” (Measure V). The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: kayfa ṣiḥḥatuka yā ʾakhī? — How is your health, brother?
hal ʾanti bikhayr? — Are you (f.) well?
mā biki? tabdīna ḥazīna. — What is wrong with you (f.)? You look sad.
lastu bikhayr al-yawm. — I am not well today.
al-ḥamdu lillāh, ʾanā ʾafḍal al-yawm. — Thank God, I am better today.
taḥassanat ṣiḥḥatuhu kathīran. — His health improved a lot.

exercises.prompt: How do you reply that you are fine?

exercises.explanation: The final ـِ marks a woman.

exercises.prompt: What does أَنَا أَفْضَل الْيَوْم mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: How is your health, brother?
Are you (f.) well?
I am not well today.
His health improved a lot.

lessons.title: 445. At the doctor's
lessons.subtitle: مَوْعِد عِنْدَ الطَّبِيب · ضَغْط الدَّم · تَحْلِيل الدَّم

explanations.title: A visit to the clinic
explanations.body: You book an appointment: أُرِيد مَوْعِدًا عِنْدَ الطَّبِيب. In the clinic the doctor checks you: يَفْحَص الطَّبِيب الْمَرِيض. Common checks: ضَغْط الدَّم, “blood pressure”, دَرَجَة الْحَرَارَة, “temperature”, تَحْلِيل الدَّم, “a blood test”. The cost of treatment may be covered by تَأْمِين صِحِّي, “health insurance”. A clinic is عِيَادَة. The dialogue is invented.

examples.translation: ʾurīd mawʿidan ʿinda aṭ-ṭabīb. — I want an appointment with the doctor.
mawʿiduka ghadan fī al-ʿāshira. — Your appointment is tomorrow at ten.
yafḥaṣ aṭ-ṭabīb al-marīḍ. — The doctor examines the patient.
ḍaghṭ ad-dam ʿindaka ṭabīʿiyy. — Your blood pressure is normal.
daraja ḥarāratika murtafiʿa qalīlan. — Your temperature is a little high.
naḥtāj ʾilā taḥlīl ad-dam. — We need a blood test.
hal ʿindaka taʾmīn ṣiḥḥī? — Do you have health insurance?

exercises.prompt: What does أُرِيد مَوْعِدًا عِنْدَ الطَّبِيب mean?
options: I want to be a doctor
I want medicine from the doctor
I want an appointment with the doctor

exercises.prompt: What does يَفْحَص الطَّبِيب الْمَرِيض mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want an appointment with the doctor.
The doctor examines the patient.
We need a blood test.
Your temperature is a little high.

lessons.title: 446. The doctor's advice
lessons.subtitle: اِشْرَبْ مَاءً · نَمْ · لَا تَأْكُلْ · يَجِب أَنْ

explanations.title: Commands and “you must”
explanations.body: Doctors speak in commands. To a man: اِشْرَبْ مَاءً كَثِيرًا, “drink a lot of water”, نَمْ مُبَكِّرًا, “sleep early”. To several people: اِشْرَبُوا. To forbid: لَا تَشْرَبْ, and before الـ the final sukūn takes a helping kasra: لَا تَشْرَبِ الْقَهْوَة. Another way is يَجِب أَنْ + subjunctive, “you must …”: يَجِب أَنْ تَنَامَ، “you must sleep”, or عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحَ, “you should rest”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: ishrab māʾan kathīran. — Drink a lot of water.
nam mubakkiran. — Sleep early.
lā tashrabi al-qahwa. — Don't drink coffee.
ishrabū al-māʾ. — Drink the water (all of you).
yajib ʾan tanāma thamānī sāʿāt. — You must sleep eight hours.
ʿalayka ʾan tastarīḥa fī al-bayt. — You should rest at home.
lā tadhhab ʾilā al-ʿamal ghadan. — Don't go to work tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: What does اِشْرَبْ مَاءً كَثِيرًا mean?
What does لَا تَشْرَبِ الْقَهْوَة mean?
Why the kasra in لَا تَشْرَبِ الْقَهْوَة?
exercises.explanation: A final sukūn before الـ takes a kasra.

exercises.prompt: How do you tell several people to drink?
exercises.explanation: The group imperative ends in ـُوا.

exercises.prompt: What does يَجِب أَنْ تَنَامَ mean?
What does عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَسْتَرِيحَ mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Drink a lot of water.

exercises.explanation: After لَا, jussive with a helping vowel.
exercises.promptTranslation: Don't drink coffee.
You must sleep eight hours.
You should rest at home.

explanations.title: Inside the hospital
explanations.body: A patient enters the hospital: دَخَلَ الْمُسْتَشْفَى. He leaves it: خَرَجَ مِنَ الْمُسْتَشْفَى. In an emergency you go to الطَّوَارِئ, “the emergency department”, and call the ambulance: اِتَّصِلْ بِالْإِسْعَاف. Rooms and beds: غُرْفَة, سَرِير. A nurse is مُمَرِّض (m.) or مُمَرِّضَة (f.). An operation is عَمَلِيَّة. The future uses سَـ: سَيَبْقَى ثَلَاثَة أَيَّام, “he will stay three days”. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: dakhala al-marīḍ al-mustashfā masāʾa ʾamsi. — The patient entered the hospital yesterday evening.
ittaṣil bil-ʾisʿāf fawran. — Call the ambulance at once.
ghurfatuhu fī aṭ-ṭābiq ath-thānī. — His room is on the second floor.
sayabqā fī al-mustashfā thalātha ʾayyām. — He will stay in the hospital for three days.
satakūn al-ʿamaliyya ghadan ṣabāḥan. — The operation will be tomorrow morning.
matā yakhruj mina al-mustashfā? — When will he leave the hospital?

exercises.prompt: What does دَخَلَ الْمَرِيض الْمُسْتَشْفَى mean?
What does اِتَّصِلْ بِالْإِسْعَاف فَوْرًا mean?

exercises.explanation: Ends in ـَة, so a woman.

exercises.prompt: What does سَيَبْقَى ثَلَاثَة أَيَّام mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: The patient entered the hospital yesterday evening.
His room is on the second floor.
He will stay in the hospital for three days.
When will he leave the hospital?

explanations.title: Buying medicine
explanations.body: The pharmacy is صَيْدَلِيَّة and the pharmacist is صَيْدَلِيّ. You ask for medicine: أُرِيد دَوَاءً لِلصُّدَاع, “I want medicine for a headache”. Forms of medicine: قُرْص, “tablet”, شَرَاب, “syrup”. The pharmacist asks about the prescription: هَلْ مَعَكَ وَصْفَة طِبِّيَّة؟ and tells you how often: ثَلَاث مَرَّات فِي الْيَوْم, “three times a day”, بَعْدَ الْأَكْل, “after eating”, قَبْلَ النَّوْم, “before sleep”. The dialogue is invented.

examples.translation: ʾurīd dawāʾan liṣ-ṣudāʿ. — I want medicine for a headache.
hal maʿaka waṣfa ṭibbiyya? — Do you have a prescription?
khudh qurṣan wāḥidan baʿda al-ʾakl. — Take one tablet after eating.
kam marra fī al-yawm? — How many times a day?
thalāth marrāt fī al-yawm. — Three times a day.
hādhā ash-sharāb lis-suʿāl. — This syrup is for a cough.
ishrabhu qabla an-nawm. — Drink it before sleep.

exercises.prompt: What does أُرِيد دَوَاءً لِلصُّدَاع mean?
options: I want medicine for a headache
I want a doctor for a headache

exercises.prompt: What does هَلْ مَعَكَ وَصْفَة؟ ask?
What does ثَلَاث مَرَّات فِي الْيَوْم mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want medicine for a headache.
Do you have a prescription?
How many times a day?
Drink it before sleep.

explanations.title: Label language
explanations.body: A label speaks in the passive and in short phrases. الْجُرْعَة, “the dose”: قُرْص وَاحِد مَرَّتَيْن فِي الْيَوْم. يُؤْخَذ بَعْدَ الْأَكْل, “is taken after eating”. A warning: تَحْذِير. Something forbidden: مَمْنُوع, and “for … it is not allowed”: لَا يُسْتَخْدَم لِلْأَطْفَال. Storage: يُحْفَظ بَعِيدًا عَنِ الْأَطْفَال, “is kept away from children”. Dates: تَارِيخ الِانْتِهَاء, “expiry date”. The passive present has the prefix يُـ and a fatḥa on the second root letter: يُؤْخَذ, يُحْفَظ. The labels are invented.

examples.text: الْجُرْعَة: قُرْص وَاحِد مَرَّتَيْن فِي الْيَوْم.
examples.translation: al-jurʿa: qurṣ wāḥid marratayn fī al-yawm. — Dose: one tablet twice a day.
yuʾkhadh baʿda al-ʾakl. — Take after eating (lit. is taken after eating).
taḥdhīr: lā yustakhdam lil-ʾaṭfāl. — Warning: not to be used for children.
yuḥfaẓ baʿīdan ʿani al-ʾaṭfāl. — Keep away from children.
tārīkh al-intihāʾ maktūb hunā. — The expiry date is written here.
mamnūʿ lil-ḥāmil. — Not allowed for a pregnant woman.

exercises.prompt: What does يُؤْخَذ بَعْدَ الْأَكْل mean?

options: not allowed for a pregnant woman

exercises.prompt: What does يُحْفَظ بَعِيدًا عَنِ الْأَطْفَال mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: Dose: one tablet twice a day.
Take after eating.
Keep away from children.
Warning: not to be used for children.

lessons.title: 450. Get well soon: visiting a patient
lessons.subtitle: سَلَامَتُكَ · شَافَاكَ اللَّه · زُرْنَا صَدِيقَنَا

explanations.title: Wishing someone well
explanations.body: To a sick person people say سَلَامَتُكَ, “your safety”, meaning “get well”, and شَافَاكَ اللَّه, “may God heal you”. A longer wish: أَتَمَنَّى لَكَ الشِّفَاء الْعَاجِل, “I wish you a quick recovery”. When you visit, you say زُرْتُكَ لِأَطْمَئِنَّ عَلَيْكَ, or simply جِئْتُ لِزِيَارَتِكَ, “I came to visit you”. You may bring flowers, زُهُور, or a gift, هَدِيَّة: أَحْضَرْنَا لَهُ زُهُورًا. These phrases are common and polite; wording varies from place to place. The sentences are invented.

examples.translation: salāmatuka yā ṣadīqī! — Get well, my friend!
shāfāka allāh waʿāfāka. — May God heal you and keep you well.
ʾatamannā laka ash-shifāʾ al-ʿājil. — I wish you a quick recovery.
zurnā ṣadīqanā fī al-mustashfā. — We visited our friend in the hospital.
ʾaḥḍarnā lahu zuhūran wahadiyya. — We brought him flowers and a gift.
saʾazūruhu ghadan marra ʾukhrā. — I will visit him again tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: What does سَلَامَتُكَ say to a sick person?

exercises.promptTranslation: Get well, my friend!
I wish you a quick recovery.
We visited our friend in the hospital.
We brought him flowers and a gift.

lessons.title: 451. A surprise party
lessons.subtitle: أَدْعُوكَ إِلَى حَفْلَة · لَا تَقُلْ لِأَحَد · عِيد مِيلَاد سَعِيد

explanations.title: Inviting friends
explanations.body: An invitation is دَعْوَة and to invite is دَعَا, with إِلَى for the event: أَدْعُوكَ إِلَى حَفْلَة. A surprise is مُفَاجَأَة. A birthday is عِيد مِيلَاد, and the greeting is عِيد مِيلَاد سَعِيد. To keep it secret: لَا تَقُلْ لِأَحَد, “don't tell anyone” (hollow verb: لَا تَقُلْ). To say you will attend: سَأَحْضُر. Congratulations is مَبْرُوك. The messages are invented.

examples.translation: ʾadʿūka ʾilā ḥafla mufājaʾa. — I invite you to a surprise party.
satakūn al-ḥafla yawma al-jumuʿa masāʾan. — The party will be on Friday evening.
lā taqul liʾaḥad, fahiya mufājaʾa. — Don't tell anyone, it's a surprise.
saʾaḥḍur wasaʾuḥḍir hadiyya. — I will come and I will bring a gift.
ʿīd mīlād saʿīd yā ʾukhtī! — Happy birthday, sister!
mabrūk! kam ʿumruki al-ʾān? — Congratulations! How old are you now?

exercises.prompt: What does أَدْعُوكَ إِلَى حَفْلَة mean?
options: I thank you for the party
I invite you to a party
I saw you at the party

exercises.explanation: A surprise party is حَفْلَة مُفَاجَأَة.

exercises.prompt: What does لَا تَقُلْ لِأَحَد mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: I invite you to a surprise party.
Don't tell anyone, it's a surprise.
I will come and I will bring a gift.
Happy birthday, sister!

lessons.title: 452. Politely saying no
lessons.subtitle: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة · لَكِنْ لَا أَسْتَطِيع · أَنَا آسِف

explanations.title: A reason and a feeling
explanations.body: A polite refusal has three parts. First, thanks: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة. Then regret: أَنَا آسِف, “I am sorry”. Then the reason, joined with لِأَنَّ, “because”, or وَلِذَلِكَ, “and therefore”. You can add a wish: أَتَمَنَّى لَكُمْ وَقْتًا جَمِيلًا, “I wish you a lovely time”. For “I can't”, use لَا أَسْتَطِيع, followed by the noun الْحُضُور, “attending”, or أَنْ + subjunctive. The messages are invented.

examples.translation: shukran ʿalā ad-daʿwa. — Thank you for the invitation.
ʾanā ʾāsif, lā ʾastaṭīʿ al-ḥuḍūr. — I am sorry, I can't attend.
liʾannanī musāfir ghadan. — Because I am travelling tomorrow.
ʾanā mashghūl, walidhalika lan ʾaḥḍura. — I am busy, therefore I will not come.
ʾatamannā lakum waqtan jamīlan. — I wish you a lovely time.
saʾazūrukum fī al-ʾusbūʿ al-qādim. — I will visit you next week.

exercises.prompt: What does شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة mean?
What does لَا أَسْتَطِيع الْحُضُور mean?
What does أَتَمَنَّى لَكُمْ وَقْتًا جَمِيلًا mean?
options: I wish you a lovely time
I thank you for the time

exercises.promptTranslation: Thank you for the invitation.
I am sorry, I can't attend.
Because I am travelling tomorrow.
I am busy, therefore I will not come.

lessons.title: 453. Remembering the journey
lessons.subtitle: أَوَّلًا · ثُمَّ · بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ · تَذَكَّرْتُ · رَجَعْنَا

explanations.title: Telling a story in order
explanations.body: To tell a trip in order, link past verbs with أَوَّلًا, “first”, ثُمَّ, “then”, بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ, “after that”, and وَأَخِيرًا, “and finally”. The verbs are past: سَافَرْنَا, وَصَلْنَا, تَعَلَّمْنَا, رَجَعْنَا. To say what you remember: تَذَكَّرْتُ, “I remembered”, or ذِكْرَى جَمِيلَة, “a lovely memory”. Superlatives use أَجْمَل, “the most beautiful”, in an idāfa: أَجْمَل ذِكْرَى, “the loveliest memory”. The story is invented.

examples.translation: ʾawwalan sāfarnā ʾilā madīna jamīla. — First we travelled to a lovely city.
thumma waṣalnā ʾilā al-funduq. — Then we arrived at the hotel.
baʿda dhālika taʿallamnā kalimāt jadīda. — After that we learned new words.
waʾakhīran rajaʿnā ʾilā buyūtinā. — And finally we returned to our homes.
tadhakkartu ʾaṣdiqāʾī hunāk. — I remembered my friends there.
kānat ʾajmal dhikrā fī ḥayātī. — It was the loveliest memory of my life.

exercises.prompt: What does تَعَلَّمْنَا كَلِمَات جَدِيدَة mean?

exercises.promptTranslation: First we travelled to a lovely city.
Then we arrived at the hotel.
After that we learned new words.
And finally we returned to our homes.
It was the loveliest memory of my life.

lessons.title: 454. Course review: the verb, the negatives, the sentence
lessons.subtitle: ماضٍ · مُضَارِع · أَمْر · لَمْ · لَنْ · لَا · لَيْسَ

explanations.title: What you can now do
explanations.body: You now have the main tools of Modern Standard Arabic. Past: كَتَبْتُ, “I wrote”. Present: أَكْتُب, “I write”. Future: سَأَكْتُب, “I will write”. Command: اُكْتُبْ, “write!”. Four negatives: لَا + present (لَا أَكْتُب), لَمْ + jussive (لَمْ أَكْتُبْ, “I did not write”), لَنْ + subjunctive (لَنْ أَكْتُبَ, “I will not write”), لَيْسَ + noun or adjective (لَيْسَ كَبِيرًا). Add feelings, health, directions, travel and the news, and you can tell your own story. These last exercises mix all of it.

examples.translation: katabtu risāla ʾilā ṣadīqī. — I wrote a letter to my friend.
lam ʾaktub lahu ʾamsi. — I did not write to him yesterday.
lan ʾansā hādhihi ar-riḥla. — I will not forget this trip.
laysa aṭ-ṭarīq ṭawīlan. — The road is not long.
ishrab māʾan wanam mubakkiran. — Drink water and sleep early.
ʾidhā taʿibta fanam qalīlan. — If you get tired, sleep a little.

exercises.prompt: Which negative goes with a noun or adjective predicate?
What does إِذَا تَعِبْتَ فَنَمْ قَلِيلًا mean?
options: when I sleep, I get tired
you slept, so you got tired
if you get tired, sleep a little
